<dawi>, demon, joined by <le> to <kau>, the harmful spirit of the old Zomi belief: the fixed pair that names all evil spirits together, those feared and appeased in the old religion and driven out at the Khuado festival. Stands as a noun, the object of verbs such as <hawlkhia>, drive out, and <lau>, fear; also written {dawi leh kau}
<dawi>, demon, <leh>, and, <kaute>, witch spirits: the fixed pair that names all harmful spirits of the old Zomi belief together, those driven out of house and village at the Khuado festival

<dawi>, spirit or demon, and <thoihna>, sacrifice: the sacrifice made to the spirits in the old religion of the Zomi, not a sacrifice of a demon; stands before words such as <phual>, place, and <pawi>, feast
spirit-worshipping, from <dawi> spirit and <bia> worship; used in the Bible for the uncircumcised and for those who do not know God
<dawi>, demon or spirit, with <biakna>, worship; {dawibiakna mun} is a pagan shrine and {dawibiakna tau} a pagan altar
<dawibia> with the plural <te>: those who worship spirits, used for the nations who do not know God
<dawi>, spirit, with <gilo>, evil; {dawigilo lut} is to be possessed by an evil spirit
<dawigilo>, evil spirit, with the plural <te>
<dawi>, demon, in the pair {dawihang kauhang}, the demons and harmful spirits that are driven out of house and village at the <Khuado> festival
an evil spirit that takes hold of a person; {dawilawm nei} is to have a demon, to be demon-possessed
said of the heart: be shaken, disturbed or frightened; {a sin a dawilok tuan loh} is that its heart is not disturbed at all
<dawi> evil spirit, <lut> enter, with the noun suffix <na>; before <mipa>, the man possessed by an evil spirit
<dawi> demon with <mang> lord or chief; {dawimang lianpen pa} is the chief ruler of the demons
the devil, chief of the evil spirits; <dawi> evil spirit and <mang> chief, with <pa> for a male person
the devil, literally the chief of the demons; written with a capital letter as a title or at the start of a sentence
<dawi>, demon, and <nupi>, woman, written as one word: a demon woman, said in news reports of a woman who has done something cruel
<dawi>, demon, with the plural <te>; {dawite hawlkhia} is to drive out demons
of or from evil spirits
<dawi>, evil spirit: troubled or held by an evil spirit; {dawivei mi} is a person possessed by a demon
<dawivei> possessed by a demon with the plural <te>, at the start of a sentence
ritually unclean, of a thing that may not be eaten or touched
stand out from a surface or line, said of a tower, a cliff, the end of a staff
in {tuipi dawk} or {tui dawk}, a part of the sea that juts into the land
form of <dawk>, stick out, with the linking suffix <in>; of a crag, stand out toward a place; {mai dawk} is to step forward
<dawk> emerge with <khia> out
<dawk> emerge, <kik> again, <to> upward
<dawk> stick out or show, with <sa> already done and the linking ending <in>: with a part of the body left showing
make something show or stick out, <dawk> with the causative <sak>
<dawk> stick out, with the causative <sak> and the linking ending <in>: holding out the tip of a staff
<dawk> emerge with <to> upward
<dawk> jut out, with <toh> upward: stand up high above the surroundings, said of a mountain
a deck of a ship, one of the storeys of the ark
a floor or storey of a building
one of the levels of a building, counted one above another
a step or rank in a process or an order, not in a building: a stage of a plan or of a trial, as {dawl masa}, the first stage, or a level of government, as {gambup dawl}, the national level

terms: level by level/in stages/step by step
definition: <dawl>, level, said twice: at each level, one level after another; usually {a dawldawl in}
<dawl>, floor, and <khatna>, first, written as one word: the first floor of a building
<dawl> and <nih> written as one word: with two floors, said of a house or a bus; {dawlnih a pha} is that has two storeys
<dawl>, floor, and <nihna>, second, written as one word
<dawl>, floor or level, and <thum>, three, written as one word: of a building, three storeys high; also three levels or classes of people
<dawl>, floor, and <thumna>, third, written as one word
treat with care or mercy, hold back from harming; in oaths {hong dawm kei ta hen} is may he not spare me, and {dawm loin} is without mercy
after <ki>, written as two words for <kidawm>: watch oneself, take care, and with a thing named before it be careful or sparing with it, as in {zu leh za ki dawm}, be careful with drink and tobacco
<dawm> treat with care, with the linking ending <in>: gently, considerately
take a drink; {tui dawn} is to drink water and {zu dawn} to drink wine or beer
go out to meet someone who is coming
the top or tip of something, as in {mual dawn}, mountain top, {ciangkhut dawn}, the tip of a staff, and {vun dawn}, foreskin
give an answer, the form of <dawng> used before <kik>, back: {dawn kik} is answer back, and {dawn kikna} is a reply
<dawn>, top, with the ending <a>, at or on the top of; {mual dawna biakpiakna munte} are the hilltop places of worship, the high places
a spelling of <dawnna>, what is said in reply, set beside <dotna>, question, as in {dotna dawna}, questions and answers; not the top of a hill

terms: on top of/at the top of/atop
definition: <dawn>, top, with the place marker <ah>, placed after the noun
word of songs and elevated speech used before <tuah>, meet: {dawnbang tuah} is to meet one another or come together again; its own sense apart from that phrase is not clear
<dawn>, here the form of <dawng>, answer, with <dan>, manner, written as one word: the way in which someone answers a question or responds
<dawn> drink said twice, for drinking freely or again and again
<dawn>, go to meet or welcome, and <den>, always, written as one word: welcome someone every time he comes
<dawn>, drink, and <den>, always, written as one word: drink something regularly
<dawn>, drink, and <ding> written as one word: that is to be drunk, for drinking; {dawnding tui} is drinking water, and beside <nekding> it means things to eat and to drink
<dawnding>, for drinking, and <tuisiang>, clean water: water that is fit to drink, the usual term in news of disasters, relief work and public supply; often named beside {nekding an}, food to eat
give an answer to a person or to a question
unit name for songs: a song, <la>, is counted as {dawng khat}, one piece or verse; not the verb answer
<dawng>, answer, with the linking <a> written as one word: answered and
<dawng> answer, doubled: go on answering what is asked
form of <dawng> with the linking suffix <in>, answering, usually before the words spoken

a counting word for songs and stanzas and <khat>, one, written as one word after <la>: {la dawngkhat} is one song or one verse of a song; the first part is spelled like <dawng>, answer, but is not that verb
<dawng>, answer, with <kik>, back: give an answer in return
<dawngkik> answer back, with the linking suffix <in>: answered and went on to say
<dawng> and <lo> written as one word: does not answer
<dawng> answer with <thei> can
<dawn>, drink, with the suffix <huai>: worth drinking, right to drink; {dawnhuai lo} is should not be drunk
form of <dawn> with the linking ending <in>, used before a following verb
form of <dawng>, answer, with the linking ending <in>
form of <dawn>, meet, with the linking ending <in>
<dawn> drink with the negative <kei>, used in a prohibition
<dawn> drink with <kha>, which shows that the action comes to happen; with <kei>, never get to drink
<dawn>, drink, and <khat>, one, written as one word: one draught, drinking a thing down at one go
<dawn>, drink, with <khawm>, together; often paired with <nekhawm>, eat together
<dawn> drink, <khawm> together, with the linking suffix <in>
<dawn>, the tip or shoot of a plant, with <khia> out
<dawn> drink with <khop> together; here swallow something along with the water
<dawn>, drink, with <kik>, again
<dawn.4>, the form of <dawng>, answer, with <kik>, back: give an answer in return to a question, a letter or a prayer; not {dawnkik}, drink again
<dawnkik> answer back with the noun suffix <na>
<dawn> drink with <kim> all, every one drinks
<dawn>, drink, and <lo>, not, written as one word
<dawn>, drink, and <loh>, not, written as one word: not drinking, the form used before a following word, as in {zu dawnloh}, not drinking alcohol
the act of drinking, from <dawn> drink; {dawnna hai} is a drinking cup
the act or place of going to meet someone, from <dawn> meet, welcome
what is said or written in reply, from <dawng>, answer; paired with <dotna>, question, as <dotna leh dawnna>, questions and answers; not drinking and not a meeting
plural of <dawnna>, answer; {dotna leh dawnnate} is questions and answers
<dawn> top or tip with <ngeek> tender, the soft topmost shoot of a tree
<dawn> top or tip with <ngek> tender, the soft topmost shoot of a tree
<dawnngek>, the young tender tip of a branch, with the plural <te>
<dawn>, the form of <dawng> answer used before a suffix, with <pah> at once
<dawn>, top or tip, and <pan>, from, written as one word and placed after the thing named: from the top of it
<dawn>, drink, with <pan>, here only then, begin to: drink only after the time named, as in an instruction to drink an hour after eating
named after cucumbers in the list of the foods of Egypt, where the English has melons; with the plural <te>
<dawn>, drink, with the causative <sak>: give someone a drink or make someone drink
<dawn> drink, the causative <sak>, with the linking suffix <in>
<dawn> drink with <sim> secretly; of stolen water in the proverb
<dawn>, the form of <dawng>, answer, used before a suffix, with <suah>, bring out or become: bring about or carry through what <dawng> names; the page lists the form without a meaning
<dawn>, drink, with the plural <te>: those who drink; in {an nek tui dawnte} also the eating and drinking itself
<dawn>, top or tip, with the plural <te>, as in {mual dawnte}, mountain tops, {bil dawnte}, ear lobes, and {khutpi dawnte}, tips of the thumbs
<dawn>, drink, and <theih>, can, written as one word: something that can be drunk, a drink; often paired with <nektheih>, food

terms: ability to answer/being able to answer
definition: <dawn>, the form of <dawng> answer used before a suffix, with <theih> can and the noun suffix <na>
go or come to meet someone; of trouble or death, come upon a person
<dawntuah> with the linking suffix <in>, meeting someone on the way, followed by another verb
<dawntuah> meet, with <pa> marking a man; the one who came to meet him

terms: deserving an answer/fit to be answered
definition: <dawn>, the form of <dawng>, answer, used before a suffix, with <tuak>, be fitting: deserving an answer
<dawn> top with <zang> flat; of an altar, the hearth on its top
<dawnzang> flat top with <teng> all; after <mual>, all the mountaintops
<dawn>, drink, and <zel> written as one word: drink again and again
<dawn>, drink, with <zia>, way, written as one word, often paired with <nekzia>: how one drinks
<dawn>, a form of <dawng>, answer, with <zia>, way, written as one word: how someone answers a question
<dawn> top with <zum> pointed; a mountain with many peaks is called rugged in the English
get in touch with a person or an office about a matter, to ask or to report; {vai dawp} is bring a matter to an office
<dawp>, contact or inquire, with <theih>, be able, written as one word; {dawptheih ni} is the days on which an office may be approached
drive a sword or dagger into someone
<dawt>, stab, with <gawp>, severely, written as one word: stab again and again or stab badly
<dawt>, pierce, with <kha>, happen to: of a sharp thing, come to pierce or prick a part of the body, often by accident
stab right through with a sword
<dawtlet> stab through, with the linking suffix <in>
<dawt> and <liam> written as one word: stab a person so that he is wounded, beside <dawtlum>, stab to death
<dawt>, stab, and <liamgawp>, be badly wounded, written as one word: stab someone so that he is badly wounded
<dawt>, stab, with <lum>: stab a person so that he dies
<dawtlum> with <sa>, already done, written as one word; {aki dawtlumsa in} is having been stabbed to death, said of how a body is found
<dawt>, stab, with <lup>, lie down: stab a person so that the person falls; {dawtlup thuak} is be stabbed
<dawtlup> with the noun ending {-na}: the act or place of stabbing a person down; usually after <ki>, as in {ki dawtlupna}, the stabbing
<dawt>, stab, with <sak> written as one word: stab a person in a named part of the body with a knife
<dawt>, stab, and <suk>, down into, written as one word: drive a knife down into the body
make a lamp or torch give light, as in {datmei de}, shine a torch
<de> light a torch or lamp, with the linking suffix <in>; meaning taken from the context of torches and lanterns
man of the tribe of Gad, father of Eliasaph who led the tribe in the wilderness
a church officer who serves under the pastor and elders; also written without a capital
the last day on which something can be handed in or applied for
opening word of a letter or address, placed before those who are addressed
a formal argument of a question between two sides, as in a parliament; {debate bawl} is hold a debate
Canaanite royal city in the hill country of Judah, earlier called Kiriath Sepher, later given to the Levites; also the name of a king of Eglon
name of two women: the prophetess and judge of Israel, wife of Lappidoth, and the nurse of Rebekah
follows a word for something flat or wide, such as <peek>, <zai> or <kizal>, and stresses how broadly it spreads; {a peek deda} is the wide sheet of Acts 10, {lupna zai deda} a wide bed
after a verb of sound, silence or thought such as <dai> or <lungngai>, shows that the state takes hold fully and lasts unbroken for a while; not {deda} after a word for something flat or wide
son of Raamah in the line of Cush, and also a son of Jokshan, grandson of Abraham and Keturah; his descendants were a trading people of Arabia
placed after <lungngai> think: describes thinking long and hard about something, pondering
light a torch so that it burns, written also <de>, as in <de-in>; {meilah dee-in tawi} is carry a lighted torch
bargain over a thing in order to buy it
hit with something that falls or is thrown, such as a stone or hail; written with an apostrophe before the next word
throw something at a person; {suang tawh deeng} is stone someone
<deeng>, throw at or strike, with the linking ending <in>; {suang tawh deengin} is to stone someone
kill by throwing stones, usually as {suang tawh deenglum}; <deeng> throw at, with <lum>, which shows that the blow kills
strike so that it breaks off, said of hail stripping the trees; <deeng> strike with <tan> cut off
spread over and take in completely, as a stronger people, language or culture does to a weaker one; a Zolai word, not the English word deep, which occurs in the articles only inside English phrases
Hindu festival of lights, a public holiday in Malaysia; {Deepavali pawi} is the Deepavali festival
the amount by which spending is greater than income, or imports greater than exports; set against <sumval>, surplus
statement of what a word or idea means; the English word, used mostly beside <khiatna>
a title given by a university or college to a person who completes a course of study; {degree ngah} is get a degree
a unit for measuring temperature, as in {degree Celsius}
pierce with a sting, said of a scorpion
<deh> sting with <thei> can: have the power to sting
a room of a house or building; {dei tungnung} is an upstairs room
placed after <kha> bitter, to strengthen it: very bitter, as bitter as the venom of snakes
treat people unequally, favouring some over others; {mi deidan} is to show partiality
<deidan>, show favoritism, and <neilo>, not have: treating all alike, without preferring some people over others; with <in> after it, impartially

<deidan>, treat unequally, and <omlo>, there is none: with no difference made between people; placed after what is not to count, as people, church or religion, or after <kuamah>, anyone, and mostly followed by <in>
<deidan>, show favouritism, and <lo>, not, written as one word, mostly before <in>: without treating one differently from another
<deidan> treat people unequally, with the noun suffix <na>; {mi deidanna} is partiality toward people
be fond of or take pleasure in someone or something
wish to have something or wish that something happens; the thing or clause wanted comes before it

terms: as one wishes/at will/just as one likes
definition: <deih>, want, and <bangbangin>, exactly as: in whatever way one wants, at will; the one who wishes stands before it as <na>, <a>, <i> or a name, and the verb follows

terms: as one wishes/according to the will of
definition: <deih>, want, and <bang>, like, written as one word, placed after the one who wants: in the way that person wishes

terms: just as one wishes/whatever one wants/as one pleases
definition: <deih>, want, and <bangbang> written as one word, after the one who wants: exactly as that person likes
<deih>, want, with <bangin>, according to, written as one word: the way someone wants it; {ka deihbangin} is as I wish
<deih>, want, with <bawl>: wish that something may be so for someone, as in greetings, or be well disposed to someone
<deih>, want, and <bek>, only, written as one word: only want, want nothing but
<deih> and <dan> written as one word: the way someone wants a thing to be, what one wishes or prefers; {Pasian deihdan} is the will of God
<deih> want said twice, with <a> before it: the very thing or everything that one wants
<deihdeih>, whatever one wants, with the adverb ending <in>: without limit, as much as anyone wishes
<deihdeih>, what one desires, with the plural <te>: all that is desired
want strongly something that belongs to another or that is not good to want
<deihgawh> covet with the noun suffix <na>: strong desire, in the verses mostly evil desire
plural of <deihgawhna>: strong, mostly sinful desires
<deih> want with <huai>, worthy of: good to have or to look at, giving pleasure
found good enough to be accepted, pleasing to the one who receives it; {deihhuai sa} is to find something pleasing
worth wanting because of beauty or value; with <zaw>, more desirable than something else
<deihhuai> desirable with the suffix <na>: the quality that makes a thing or person wanted
<deihhuai> desirable with the comparative <zaw>; the thing it is compared with takes <sang> or <sangin>, than
<deih> want with the linking ending <in>: wanting something, used before a following verb
<deih>, want, with <kaih>, pull: draw a matter toward what one wants, take or tell it in a one-sided way; in {deihkaih ing} a writer says what he wishes and urges
<deihkaih> with the noun suffix {-na}: pulling a matter toward what one wants, bias or one's own will
<deih>, want, and the negative <kei>, written as one word: do not want
<deih> and <khat> written as one word: a thing that one wants; {na deihkhat} is what you want

terms: all that one wants/everything one wants
definition: <deih>, want, and <khempeuh>, all, written as one word after <na>, <i> or <a>: everything that you, we or they want
<deih> want with <kik> again: want someone or something a second time

terms: that one wants/the fact of wanting
definition: <deih> want with <lam>, which turns the clause into the thing that is known: {ka deihlam} is that I want
<deih> and <leh> written as one word: if someone wants or wishes for something
<deih> and <lo> written as one word: not want, not like
<deih> and <loh> written as one word: not wanting, or what someone does not want; {a deihloh thu} is a thing he does not want, and {deihloh pen in} introduces something one hopes will not happen
<deih> want, <loh> not, with the noun suffix <na>; {Pasian’ deihlohna} is what God does not want, ungodliness
the attitude of not wanting a person, a government or an act, which is named just before {deihlohna}; with <lungphona> it is a protest against that person or thing
<deihlohna>, rejection, and <lungphona>, protest: a public demonstration against a person or thing, which is named before the pair; the verbs are <nei> and <bawl>, hold
<deih>, want, <loh>, not, and <pen>, here most, written as one word: what is wanted least; {deihlohpen in} opens a clause about something bad that may happen, if the worst comes

terms: unwanted things/those who do not want
definition: <deihloh> and the plural <te> written as one word: the things one does not want, or the people who do not want someone
<deihlo>, not want, with the plural <te>: the people who do not want or do not like someone or something

terms: want too much/be greedy for/love excessively
definition: <deih> want with <lua> too much; with <sum>, be a lover of money
form of <deihlua> used before <leh>, <in> and <mahmah> and in dependent clauses; also as a noun, craving
<deihluat> desire too much, with the linking ending <in>: loving something too much
<deih> want, <luat> too much, with the noun suffix <na>: a very strong desire for something; {sum deihluatna} is the love of money
<deihluat> desire excessively, with the noun suffix <na> and the plural <te>

terms: want very much/like very much/be very fond of
definition: <deih>, want or like, with <mahmah>, very, written as one word
<deih>, want, and <man>, because, written as one word, followed by <in>: because one wants the thing named before it
<deih> want with the noun suffix <na>: what someone wants; {Pasian’ deihna} is the will of God and {lungsim deihna} the desire of the heart

terms: according to the will of/as one wishes/as desired
definition: <deihna>, wish or will, and <bangin>, like or accordingly: placed after the person whose wish it is, in the way that person wants
<deihna>, wish or purpose, and <bulpi>, base or main: the main purpose or underlying aim of a person, a group or an action; a possessor stands before it, as in {a deihna bulpi}
plural of <deihna>: the things someone wants; {Pasian’ deihnate} is what God wills

terms: no longer want/not want any more
definition: <deih> and <nawnlo> written as one word: not want someone or something any longer
<deih>, want, and <ngetna>, request, written as one word: what a group wants and asks for from those in authority
<deih> want, with <pa> marking a man: the man who wants something; {thutang a deihpa} is the one who wants justice
in the articles with <ngeingai>, of neighbours or reporters who come crowding to a place at once; the last part is <pah>, immediately, and the first part is not confirmed
<deih>, like or want, with <pen>, most: what someone likes or wants most
<deih>, want, and <peuhpeuh>, whatever, written as one word, after <na>, <ka> or <a>: whatever you, I or they want
meaning taken from the context, set the heart fully on something
want something for another person or want another to do or be something, care for someone’s good; {deihsak-a satna} is beating out of care, discipline

<deihsak>, wish good for, and <thungetna>, prayer: a prayer said for the good of others, a blessing or intercession; used with <nei> or <neihsak>, to offer it, and often named together with <thapiakna>, encouragement

<deihsak>, wish someone well, and <tuam>, separate: caring for one person more than for others, favouritism; mostly denied with <nei> and <lo>, {deihsak tuam nei lo}, show no partiality, and paired with <khentuam> or {it tuam}
<deihsak>, care for, and <diak>, especially, written as one word: show special care or goodwill toward someone, with <tungah>
<deihsak>, want something for someone, with the linking ending <in>: wishing it for them
<deihsak> and <lo> written as one word: not want good for someone, not care for
<deihsak> want for someone, <luat> exceedingly, with the noun suffix <na>; intense concern for someone
<deihsak>, wish someone well, with the noun suffix <na>: favor or goodwill shown to someone
<deihsakna>, goodwill, and <lianpi>, great: with <tawh>, with, it is the closing formula of a letter or notice, {deihsakna lianpi tawh}, with great goodwill, followed by the name of the writer

<deihsakna>, goodwill, and <tawh>, with: with goodwill; a formula that closes a letter, notice or column before the name of the writer, and that goes with an invitation or request, {deihsakna tawh kong zawn uh hi}, we kindly invite you
<deihsak> want for someone, with the noun suffix <na> and the plural <te>; the things one wishes for another
<deihsak> want for someone, with the plural <te>; the things one wishes for another
persons and not wishes: <deihsak>, care for, with the plural <te>; {na deihsakte} are the people you care about, often beside {na itte}, those you love, and {hong deihsakte} are those who care for us
<deihsak>, want something for someone, with the comparative <zaw>: wish one thing for them more than another
<deih> with <tak>, placed before a verb: with full will or force; {deihtak thungen} is pray earnestly
<deih> want with <takin>, which makes an adverb: with real desire, earnestly, or out of care for someone

terms: those who want/those who love/those who desire
definition: <deih> with the plural <te>; after a possessive, the ones someone wants or chooses
<deih>, want, with <teel>, choose: pick what one likes from among others; {deihteel thei} is be able to choose; also as a noun, {ama deihteel}, his own choice
<deihteel>, choose freely, with the noun ending <na>: what a person chooses for himself, his own free choice
choose what one wants, from <deih>, want, with <teel>, choose; {deihtel theihna} is the power or freedom to choose, and the noun is <deihtelna>
<deih>, want, with <teelna>, choosing: the choosing of what one wants, one's own free choice; {mipi deihtelna} is the choice of the people

terms: all that one wants/whatever one wishes
definition: <deih> want with <teng> all; {mi a deihteng} is all the people he wanted
<deih>, want, with <tham>, worth: worth wanting or wishing for
<deih>, want or like, and <theih>, able, written as one word: that can be wanted or liked, a thing one may desire
<deih> want with <thuah> in addition: desire still more on top of what one has

terms: amount wanted/as much as one wants
definition: <deih>, want, and <zah>, amount, written as one word: the amount or number that someone wants

terms: as much as one wants/as many as one wants
definition: <deih>, want, and <zahzah>, as much as, written as one word: whatever amount a person wishes
<deih>, want, with comparative <zaw>; the thing it is compared with takes <sangin>, than
<deihzaw> prefer, in the form {deihzawk}, with the noun suffix <na>: liking one more than another
what divides one space from another; {deina puan} is the dividing curtain of the temple and {deina kulh} a separating wall
<deina>, separation, with <in>: in order to keep the things named before it apart from one another, as names in a series or abbreviated words
<dei>, room or chamber, and <nih>, two, written as one word: the two houses of a parliament, the upper and the lower
<dei> room with <pi> great; {biakinn deipi} is the main hall of the temple

<gaih>, eat up, with <sak> and <mang>, away: eat up all that belongs to someone else
<gai>, conceive, with <kik>, again, and the linking suffix <in>
<gai> and <lo> written as one word after a verb: the action does not reach all of it, not completely
<gai>, conceive, with the noun suffix <na>: what she has conceived
<gai>, conceive, with the causative <sak>
<gaisak>, cause to conceive, with the linking suffix <in>
<gaisak>, cause to conceive, with the noun suffix <na>: the fact of having been made pregnant
<gai> be pregnant, conceive, with the plural <te>; used after <nupi>, women
<gai>, conceive, with <zawh>, after or having finished; {a gaizawh kha guk} is the sixth month after she conceived
<gai>, all, with <zo>, be able: manage the whole of something
tie or fasten one thing onto another, as a belt round the waist, a cord on a turban or rings on the legs of a table
apparently a misprint of <galkapte>, soldiers
<gak>, tie, with <cip>, tightly: bind fast so that there is no getting free, said of ropes, snares, death and sin
noun of <gakcip>, bind fast: a tying down, a rule or arrangement that holds someone fast
<gakcip>, bind fast, with <sak>: have the feet fastened in the stocks
<gak> tie round the waist with the linking ending <in>, tying or having tied a belt or sash
<gak>, tie, with <khawm>, together
<gak>, fasten, with {-na}: the thing used to fasten or bind round, such as a band on a post or the waistband of a garment
plural of <gakna>: the bands that fasten round the posts of the tabernacle court, named beside the hooks
war or battle, fighting between peoples; {gal kido} is to fight a war and {gal sim} to attack in war
one who is against another and seeks to harm him, a single enemy or the enemy in war
the far side of a river, lake or sea, as in {gal khat} across
<gal> written with a capital in the title {Khrih Gal}, the enemy of Christ, the antichrist
<gal> written with a capital in the book title {Topa Gal Laibu}, the Book of the Wars of the Lord

<gal>, war, and <mainawk>, meeting head-on: the front line of the fighting, and also those who fight or serve there; it stands before the name of a force, takes <in> for at the front, and is used in a figure of health workers in an epidemic

terms: the war ends/the war is over
definition: <gal>, war, and the verb <ven.1>, cease: the war comes to an end; in life stories mostly {gal ven ciangin}, when the war was over, after the war; not the sentence-final word <ven.3>

terms: enemy feast/celebration of a slain enemy
definition: in the old Zomi custom, <gal>, enemy, with <ai>: the feast held by one who has killed an enemy; those who held it were believed to be among the leaders in the village of the dead and not under others
form of <gal-ai> before the noun ending <na>, as in the heading {Gal-aih Sa-aih na}
the feast of the old Zomi custom that a man held to celebrate the killing of an enemy, {gal ai}; named together with <sa-aihna>, and the meat of the animals killed at it is shared out by fixed custom
<gal-aihna> with the place marker <ah>: at the feast for a slain enemy
<gal> the far side with the place marker <ah>; follows the name of a river or land, as in {Jordan gun galah}, across the Jordan; {a galah}, to the other side
name of two Levites who lived in Jerusalem after the exile, one of them a son of Jeduthun
a measure of liquid, the gallon; the number follows the word
Roman province in the middle of Asia Minor, where Paul travelled and founded churches
a fragrant gum used in making the holy incense, the foreign name kept as it is
<gal> enemy with <bawl> make: act as an enemy toward someone
<galbawl> be hostile with the noun suffix <na>: acting as an enemy toward someone
<galbawl> be hostile with plural <te>: those who act as enemies toward someone
<gal>, war or enemy, with <daihna>, calm: freedom from enemies and fighting
<gal> war with <dal> shield: what protects in battle; {galdal thep} beside <awmdal>, the breastplate, is the armor worn on the body
something that keeps the enemy out; {galdalna kulhpi} is a fortress and {galdalna inn} a citadel
<galdalna> defence with plural <te>: the pieces of armor a fighter wears
<galdal> with plural <te>: the defensive works of a city, named beside its walls
<gal> enemy with <do> fight; {galdo dingin} is for battle, for war

terms: will wage war/to go to war/to fight
definition: <galdo>, wage war, and <ding> written as one word: will make war on, or with <in> in order to go to war
<galdo>, fight, with the noun suffix <na>: war or a battle; {galdona aw} is the battle cry
plural of <galdona>: wars; {galdonate nei} is to have wars, to be at war

terms: inquire from afar/ask from a distance
definition: <gal>, the far side, with <dot>, ask: ask after someone who is far away, as by telephone; used in songs of a distant loved one, {ka galdot Zolia}
<galdo>, fight a war, with <zia>, manner: how fighting is done, the skills and tactics of combat
name Jacob gave to the heap of stones set up as a witness between him and Laban in the hill country of Gilead

terms: see from afar/look at from a distance
definition: <gal>, the far side, with <et>, form of <en>, look, and the linking suffix <in>
a view of something from a distance, used in titles for a general survey of a subject; from <galet>, look at from afar, with the noun suffix {-na}
<gal>, war, with <gim>, smell

terms: face off/threaten war/be on a war footing
definition: with <ki> before it, of two sides: stand against each other ready for war without yet fighting
<gal> enemy with <gu> steal: an armed robber; {galgu mat bangin} is as if catching a robber, where the NIV has leading a rebellion
in {galgumat bangin}, as if to seize a robber or rebel; apparently <gal>, enemy, <gu>, thief, and <mat>, seize
one who is brave in war, also used to describe a person as valiant
<galhang> warrior with <pa>, which marks a man
plural of <galhang>: warriors, men who are brave in battle
<gal>, war, with <hat>, strong; {a galhat man} is because of his strength in war
<galhat> strong in war with the noun suffix <na>
<gal>, war, with <hiam>, weapon: a weapon or the arms and armor of a fighter; {galhiam tawi} is armed, and {galhiam puapa} an armor-bearer
<galhiam>, weapon, with the marker <in>: as weapons, by way of weapons
plural of <galhiam>: weapons of war
<gal>, war, with <huh>, help: troops or weapons sent to help a force in battle
help a force in battle, as with aircraft or artillery fire
<galhuh>, give military support, with the noun ending <na>: help given to a side in war, troops, weapons or money
region in the north of the land of Israel, west of the lake of the same name, where Jesus grew up and began his work
region in the north of the land of Israel, west of the lake of the same name, where Jesus grew up and began his work
Galilee, the northern region of Israel in the land of Naphtali, taken by Tiglath-Pileser king of Assyria
Galilee, the northern region of Israel, here the home of Judas the Galilean who led a revolt
<gal> with the marker <in>; {galin do} is to fight against, to make war on
go across to the other side of a river, lake or boundary
<galkah> with the linking suffix <in>, crossing over, followed by another verb
<galkah> cross over with <pih>, together with: cross a river with someone, take them across
<galkah>, cross over, with the causative <sak>
on the far side, across; found in {tuipi galkai}, across the ocean, said of Zomi living abroad; compare <galkah>, cross over, and <galkhat>, the other side
a man who serves in an army
a body of soldiers, the whole fighting force of a king or people; {vantung galkap} is the host of heaven
<galkap> written with a capital in {Galkap Inn}, the House of the Heroes in Jerusalem
<galkap>, soldier, and <kumpi>, king or government: a government of the army, used of the military rulers of Myanmar; {galkap kumpi hun} is the time of military rule

<galkap>, soldier or army, and <mangpi>, high officer: a commander or general of an army; stands after the name of the army and before the rank and name of the person, and with <pa> it is the commander-in-chief
<galkap>, soldier or army, and <mangpipa>, the great lord: the highest officer of an armed force, the commander-in-chief; in news of Myanmar the head of the army
<galkap>, soldier, and <phual>, camp, with the augmentative {-pi}: a large army base or headquarters, placed after the name of the town or army it belongs to, not the sense furnace of <phualpi>
<galkap>, soldier, army, and <ukna>, rule: government of a country by its army; {galkap ukna nuai ah} is under military rule
<galkap>, soldier or army, and <vanleng>, aeroplane: an aircraft of the armed forces
commander of a body of soldiers, <galkap>, soldier, with <bu>
plural of <galkapbu>; in these verses the leaders of bodies of soldiers, named beside <galkapte>, the soldiers
<galkap> and <ding> written as one word: a person who is to be a soldier; {galkapding kaikhawm} is recruit soldiers
<galkap> and <khat> written as one word: a soldier, one soldier
<galkap>, soldier, with <lui>, old, written as one word: one who used to be a soldier
<galkap>, soldier, and <mang>, chief: an officer who commands soldiers
<galkapmang>, army officer, with <pa> marking a man
army officers; <galkap> soldier, <mang> chief, with the plural ending <te>
<galkapna>, warfare or battle, with the place marker <ah>
<galkap> soldier with <pa> marking a man
<galkap>, soldier, and <puan>, clothes, written as one word: the uniform of a soldier
plural of <galkap>: soldiers, or all of them together as an army
<galkapte> written with a capital inside a name, as in the valley of the armies of Gog and the Italian Regiment
<galkapte>, soldiers, with the marker <in> shortened and joined, elsewhere written {galkapte'n}: the soldiers as the doers of the action
<galkap> soldier with <teng>, all those of a group
<galkap>, soldier, and <zia>, way, written as one word: the ways and skills of a soldier; {galkapzia sinna} is military training
the side across a lake, river or valley; after a place name, across from or beyond that place
<galkhat> with <ah>, at or to the other side
<gal>, war, with <kidal>, shield oneself, and the noun suffix <na>: what a man wears for protection in battle; the NIV has tunic
<gal>, war, with <kido>, fight each other, also used as a noun, war
<galkido>, be at war, with the noun suffix <na>: war or a battle between two sides
plural of <galkidona>
<gal> and <kikap> written as one word: fighting in which the two sides shoot at each other
<gal>, war, with <kikap>, shoot at each other, and the noun suffix <na>
<gal>, war, with <kisim>, attack each other, and the noun suffix <na>; the NIV has battle standard

terms: go to war/march out/go on campaign
definition: <gal>, war, with <kuan>, set out: go out to fight; also said of the troops that are on the march
<gal>, the other side, with <lam>, direction: the side across from a place

terms: fear of the enemy/dread of war/threat of war
definition: <gal>, enemy or war, with <lau>, fear, and the noun suffix <na>
<gal>, war, with <lel>, be defeated: lose in war

terms: lose a war/be defeated in battle
definition: <gal>, war, and <lelh>, be overcome, written as one word: be losing or be defeated in a fight or war
<gal>, enemy, with <lem>, be reconciled, and the noun suffix <na>: the making of peace between enemies
town in Benjamin north of Jerusalem, the home of Paltiel son of Laish
Roman proconsul of Achaia, before whom the Jews of Corinth brought Paul
measure for water, fuel and other liquids; it stands before the number, as {gallon khat}, one gallon
the head of an enemy taken in war, from <gal>, enemy, and <lu>, head; in former times brought home as a trophy
Saying: the one who fears an enemy head meets an enemy head; a hard thing we do not want comes to us all the same, however we avoid it
<gal>, war, with <mai>, face: the front in a war; {galmai nawk} is to advance at the front, to carry out an offensive
<galmai>, the front in a war, and <nawkna>, onslaught: an advance by an armed force against the positions of the enemy, a military offensive
<gal>, war, with <mat>, seize: a person taken in war; {galmat suak}, go into captivity
<galmat> captive with <in>; in the state of a prisoner of war, with verbs of carrying off or being
plural of <galmat>, people taken in war
<gal>, enemy, with <mi>, person; {galmi et} is look on someone as an enemy, with ill will
safe from enemies and trouble, from <gal>, enemy, and <muang>, trust; paired with <lungmuang>, at ease

terms: see from afar/see at a distance
definition: <gal>, across or far off, with <muh>, see
<galmuh>, see from afar, with the linking suffix <in>

terms: be visible from afar/can be seen from a distance
definition: <galmuh> and <thei> written as one word, usually after <ki>: it can be seen from far away
Going to the house of a dead person to mourn with the family, used in the phrase {si galna}; Ecclesiastes sets it against {pawi simna}, going to a feast.
what is given to the family of a dead person in sympathy, mostly money, as {galna sum}, condolence money, and {galna pia}, give condolence; not the visit itself
<Gal>, enemy, with <nan>, withstand, and the noun suffix <na>: what is used to withstand an enemy, such as armor; {galnan'na kulh} is a stronghold.
<Gal>, enemy, with <nan>, withstand, and the noun suffix <na>: defence against an enemy; {galnanna kulh} is a fortified wall, a stronghold.
<gal>, enemy, with <neih>, have, written as one word: have someone as an enemy; with <ki>, be enemies of each other
<Gal>, enemy, with <neih>, have, and the noun suffix <na>: holding someone as an enemy; {galneihna bangmah nei lo} means having no malice toward someone.
<Gal>, enemy, with <pa>, which marks a man: the enemy, a male foe.
<Gal>, war, with <pan>, take a stand, and the noun suffix <na>: a place where soldiers take up position; {galpan'na mun} is a stronghold and {galpan'na phual} a military camp.
<Gal>, war, with <pan>, take a stand, and <mun>, place: a strong place to fight from.
<Gal>, war, with <pan>, take up a position, and the noun suffix <na>: a place held by soldiers; {galpanna mun} is a stronghold or outpost and {galpanna phual} a military camp.
<Gal>, war, with <phual>, place: the place where the fighting is.
a post where the soldiers of an army are stationed, which is attacked, taken or left; in war news after the name of an army, as {SAC galphual}, and often explained by <Camp>

terms: set up camp/pitch camp/establish a base
definition: <galphual>, military camp, as the object of <sat.2>, set up: troops pitch their camp or set up a base at a place; the place stands before it with <ah>, and <sat> here is neither strike nor decide

terms: to the battle/in battle/on the battlefield
definition: {Galphual}, battlefield, with the place marker <ah>: to or on the battlefield, into battle.
<galphual>, place of battle, with <pi>, great: a large or main military base or camp
plural of <galphual>: in news the camps and positions held by an army
<Gal>, war, with <pi>, great: a great war.
<galpi>, great war, and <khatna>, first: the First World War, also written {Leitung galpi khatna}; the Second World War is <galpi nihna>

<galpi>, great war, and <nihna>, second: the Second World War, 1939 to 1945, often written with capitals; {galpi nihna lai in} is during the Second World War, and the First World War is <galpi khatna>

<galpi>, great war, and <thumna>, third: a third world war, spoken of as a danger to come, often written with capitals and also as {Leitung galpi thumna}; the earlier ones are <galpi khatna> and <galpi nihna>
<galpi>, great war, with <nih>, two, written as one word: the Second World War; {galpinih hunlai in} is at the time of the Second World War
<galpi>, great war, and <nihna>, second, written as one word: the Second World War, often as {leitung galpinihna} or {leitungbup galpinihna}
<Gal>, from far off, with <sap>, call: call out to someone who is at a distance.
<Gal>, war, with <siam>, skilled: trained and able in fighting; {galsiam mi} is a skilled warrior.
<Gal>, enemy or war, with <sim>, attack: go to war, go into battle; also used like a noun for battle, as in {galsim mite}, fighting men.
{Galsim}, go to war, with the linking suffix <in>: going to war, followed by the next action.
{Galsim}, go to war, with the noun suffix <na>: an act or occasion of going out to fight, a raid, battle or campaign.
Plural of <galsimna>: the wars or campaigns that someone has fought.
{Galsim}, go to war, with <pih>, together with: join someone in battle.
{Galsim}, go to war, with the plural <te>: those who go out to attack, raiding parties.
{Galsim}, go to war, with <zia>, manner: the way to fight, the skill of war.
<gal> and <suak.2> written as one word: become war or enmity; the saying <ciamnuih galsuak> is a joke turns into a fight
<Gal>, war, with <sung>, inside: the battle or the war as the place one is in; {galsung pan} is from the battle and {galsung nazatte} are weapons of war.
{Galsung}, battle, with the place ending <a>: in battle; {galsunga site} are those who die in battle.
<Gal>, enemy, with <tai>, flee: a person who flees from an enemy or from war; {galtai-in} means as a fugitive, in flight.
A person who has fled from war to find safety in another place.
used as a verb, often before <uh> or <hi>: flee from fighting or persecution, where the other senses name the person who flees
<galtai>, flee from fighting, and <khia>, out, written as one word: flee out of a place because of war; also those who have fled
<galtai> and <mi> written as one word: a person who has fled from war, a refugee
{Galtai}, flee from the enemy, with the noun suffix <na>: fleeing before enemies.
Plural of <galtai>: people who flee from an enemy or from war.
Plural of <gal>: enemies, those who fight against or hate someone.
<gal>, war, with <vai>, affair: all that has to do with war and armed forces; {galvai tawh kisai} is concerning military matters, and it is paired with <gamvai> in the news sense of political affairs
<Gal>, war, with <van>, goods: the equipment of war, weapons and armor; {galvan koihna} is an armory and {galvan puapa} an armor-bearer.
<galvan>, weapons, and <tawi>, carry: carrying weapons, armed; it stands before the noun it describes, as {galvan tawi galkapte}, armed soldiers, like {thau tawi}, carrying guns
<gal>, war, with <vanleng>, aircraft: an aircraft of an armed force
plural of <galvanleng>
{Galvan} with the plural <te>: the things worn and carried for battle.
{Galvan}, weapons, with <teng>, all: all the weapons of a soldier.

terms: be at peace/fighting dies down/war is over
definition: <gal>, war, and <ven>, cease, written as one word: the war or the fighting is over or has died down; {galven hun} is a time of peace

terms: stand guard/be on guard/be on the alert
definition: keep watch against an enemy, said of armed forces holding a position

terms: the fighting ends/the quarrel is over
definition: <gal>, war or strife, and <veng>, cease, written as one word: a war or a quarrel comes to an end
<Gal>, enemy, with <vil>, watch: one who keeps watch for the enemy; also the act of keeping watch, as in {galvil koih}, post a guard.
used as a verb: keep watch against an enemy or over a place, with verb endings such as <sak> or {zel ni} after it, where the other sense names the watchman
{Galvil}, keep watch, with the noun suffix <na>: keeping watch against an enemy, or the place for it; {galvilna bukno} is a watchtower and {galvilna inndei} a guardroom.
{Galvil}, watch, with <pa>, which marks a man: a man who keeps watch for the enemy.
Plural of <galvil>: watchmen or guards who keep watch for the enemy.
<Gal>, from far off, with <zak>, hear: hear about someone or something that is elsewhere.
<Gal>, war, with <zawh>, the form of <zo>, overcome, used before another word; {galzawh van} is plunder, the goods won in war.
{Galzawh}, win in war, with the noun suffix <na>: victory in battle.

terms: win the war/be victorious in war/conquer
definition: <gal>, war, with <zo>, win, written as one word; also said of the side that has won
<Gal>, war, with <zo>, win, and the plural <te>: those who win a war.
<Gal>, from afar, with <zuih>, follow: follow at a distance; {nung galzuih} is follow behind someone from far off.
A country or region with its people; {mualtung gam} is hill country.
The area of land that belongs to a people, a tribe or a ruler.
The land that a king rules; {kumpi gam} is a kingdom.
Land as the place where people live; after a name it means the land of, as in {Kanaan gam}, the land of Canaan.
{Gam} written with a capital for the kingdom of God or of heaven, as in {Pasian’ Gam} and {Vantung Gam}.
<gam>, country, with <it>, love: loving one’s country, said of leaders and soldiers
<gam>, country, and <khangtote>, the developed ones: the developed countries of the world as a group, mostly followed by <ah> or <sung>
{Gam Kigawm}, united lands, with <Kawlgam> and <Kumpi>: the Union of Burma, so called because independence was gained only when the peoples of the country agreed together
the day of those who died for the country, one of the national days of Myanmar that the page lists
<gam>, the wild, and <ak>, fowl: the wild fowl of the forest; given by the book as a noun joined to a noun
<Gam>, wild country, with <bawngtal>, bull: a wild ox; also written <gambawngtal>.
<Gam> with the ending <a>, which joins the land to the word that follows: of or in that land.
place, of uncertain location, whose men guarded the towers of Tyre
<Gam> with the place marker <ah>: in or to the land of.

terms: in the kingdom/into the kingdom/in the land
definition: <Gam>, the capitalised word for kingdom or land, with <ah>, the marker of place: in or into the Kingdom, as in {Vantung Gamah}, in the kingdom of heaven.
name of two men: the son of Pedahzur, leader of the tribe of Manasseh in the wilderness, and a Pharisee and teacher of the law in Jerusalem
<Gam>, wild country, with <bawngtal>, bull: a wild ox that cannot be made to work.
<gam>, country, with <bel>, take refuge in: a person who seeks shelter in another country, and the status of such a person; named beside <galtai>, one who flees from war; also written <gambel>
<gambeel>, refugee, and <hihna>, the fact of being: the recognised standing of a refugee; mostly before <card>, the refugee card of the UNHCR, or <khensatna>, the decision on refugee status
people who take refuge in a country that is not their own, said of refugees and of immigrants; <gambeel> with the plural <te>
<gam>, country, and <bek>, only, written as one word; {gambek hilo} after a name is not only that country
<gam>, country, with <bel>, take refuge in: a person who has fled to another country and shelters there; often {gambel mi}

<gambel>, one who shelters in another country, and <galtai>, one who flees from war, two words of nearly the same meaning said together as one noun: a refugee; used of the people whose claim the UNHCR examines, and followed by <te> for the plural or <khat> for one
<gambel> and <ding> written as one word: in order to take refuge in another country, to be a refugee there
a person who takes refuge in another country; <gambel> with <mi>, person
<gambel>, refugee, with the plural <te>, written as one word
country in West Africa
<gam>, country, and <biakna>, religion, written as one word: the religion of a country; with <te>, those who hold to it
<gam>, country, and <bitna>, security, written as one word: the security or defence of a country
<gam>, country, and <buai>, be troubled, written as one word: a time when the country is in turmoil, through war or political crisis
<gam>, country, with <buaina>, trouble: the turmoil or crisis of a country
Wild, empty country where no one goes; {lam lianpite gambulak suak} means the highways have become deserted.
<Gam>, land, with <bup>, whole: the whole of a land.
The whole extent of a country or region, from one border to the other.
before a noun, of or for the country as a whole and not one state or town, as in <gambup thukhunpi>, the national constitution, and {gambup dawl}, the national level

<gambup>, the whole country, and <huam>, take in: covering the whole country, nationwide; stands before the noun it describes, or as a verb, reach the whole country; {minambup huam} is the same for a whole people

<gambup>, the whole country, and <huamin>, taking in: covering the whole country, nationwide; stands before the verb or the clause it qualifies, and a name may stand before it, as {ZBCA gambup huamin}, across the whole of ZBCA
<gambup>, the whole land, and <innpi>, great house: the parliament of the whole country, in Myanmar the Union Assembly, as distinct from the assembly of a state; often written with capitals

<gambup>, the whole country, and <kilemna>, peace: the peace of the whole union, the term for the peace process and the nationwide ceasefire agreement in Myanmar; often followed by <maban>, process, or <khawmpi>, conference
<gambup>, the whole country, and <kiteelna>, election: the election held across the whole country for its parliament, a general election; a year often stands before it
<gambup>, the whole country, and <kiteelpi>, a great election: the general election of a country; the year often stands before it
<gambup>, national, and <makaipi>, chief leader: the leader of the whole country, used for a president or head of government as against the leader of one state or party
<gambup>, the whole country, with <ni>, day: Union Day of Myanmar, kept every year on 12 February in memory of the agreement signed at Panglong in 1947
<gambup>, the whole country, with <suahtakna>, freedom: the independence of the whole of Burma from British rule; also listed as the name of a national day
<gambup>, the whole country, and <thukhunpi>, constitution: the constitution of a state, as against the constitution of an organisation; a year before or after it names one, {2008 gambup thukhunpi}

<gambup>, national, and <thuvanpi>, secretary: taken as the head of a parliamentary government, in {gambup thuvanpi makaihna ki-ukna}, parliamentary rule; found in one article title only, and the pair may name the parliament itself
<gambup> and <ah> written as one word: in the whole country

terms: in the whole land/on the whole land
definition: <Gam>, land, with <bup>, whole, the intensifier <pi> and the place marker <ah>: in or upon the whole land.
<gam>, country, and <ciat>, each, written as one word: each one his own country, as in {amau gamciat}, their respective countries
Still and without noise, said of a land at peace or of people who stop speaking; {gamdai takin} is quietly and {gamdai-in om} is keep silent.
Form of <gamdai>, quiet, used before <nading> and <khit>: become quiet, stop making noise.
{Gamdaih}, be quiet, with the noun suffix <na>: quiet country where no one is; often followed by <mun>, place.
the state of being quiet and not a place: the silence between people who do not speak, as in {gamdaihna sukham}, break the silence, or calm in a country, beside <lungmuanna>
{Gamdai}, quiet, with the causative <sak>: make people be quiet.
{Gamdaisak}, make quiet, with the linking suffix <in>: quieting people before going on to speak.
<gamdai> and <tak> written as one word, mostly with <in>: in a quiet and orderly way
{Gamdai}, quiet, with the comparative <zaw>: quieter than before.

<gamdang>, foreign country, with the ending <a>, in: in another country, abroad

definition: {Gamdang}, foreign land, with the place marker <ah>: in or to another land, among other nations.
not a proper name: the word <gamdangah>, in a foreign land, written with a capital at the start of a sentence
{Gamdang}, foreign, with <mi>, person: a person from another country.
<gamdangmi>, foreigner, and <khualzin>, travel: a foreigner who travels in the country, a foreign tourist

<gamdangmi>, foreigner, and <nasemte>, here workers and not servants: people from another country who work in a country, the term of the news for migrant labour
<gamdangmi>, foreigner, and <phalna>, permission: the official document that allows a foreigner to stay or work in a country; often with <neilo>, without valid papers
plural of <gamdangmi>: people from another country
<gamdang> and <pan> written as one word: from a foreign country
{Gamdang}, foreign land, with the intensifier <pi>: a land wholly foreign to a person.
<gamdang> and <sum> written as one word: the money of another country
<gamdang> and <tawh> written as one word: with another country, with foreign lands

<gam>, the land outside the village, with <dawi>, spirit: a spirit of the wild, called on to go home when the spirits are driven out at <Khuado>

terms: as far as the land/down to the realm
definition: <Gam>, land, with <dong>, until: as far as the land or realm of, in the verse the realm of the dead.
<Gam>, land, with <dung>, length; paired with <gamvai>, the breadth of the land.
a game that is played, mostly a video game or a match in sport; {Game kimawl} is to play a game

<gamgi>, border, and <dung>, length, written as one word: the land along a border, along the border

bamboo, <gua>, that grows in the forest, set against <inngua>, the bamboo by the house; the saying {inngua hah lo gamgua hah}, clearing the wild bamboo and not the house bamboo, blames one who sees to others before his own
Land or property that is handed down in a family or tribe; {gamh luah} is to receive an inheritance.

terms: burn the land/set fire to the forest
definition: <gam>, land or wild country, with <hal>, burn
<gam>, country, with <hau>, rich, written as one word: a wealthy country
plural of <gamhau>: the wealthy countries, set against <gamzawngte>, the poor countries

{Gamhluah} with <pa>, which marks a man: the man who inherits.
{Gamhluah} with the plural <te>: those who inherit.
{Gamhluah} with the plural <te>: the shares of land that pass to the heirs.
<Gam>, land, with <hoih>, good: the good land that God promised.
<gamhoih>, good land, with <na>: a place where the land is good, which people head for when they move
treat others roughly and without respect; named together with <pheengtat> and with <totbawl>, provoke
violent or lawless behaviour; probably a spelling of <gamtatna>, conduct, used of bad conduct
Plural of <gamh>: the shares of land handed down in a tribe or family.

<Gam> with the marker <in> written together: as a country, or the land as the subject of the sentence.

<gam>, wild land or forest, with <katna>, burning: a fire that burns over forest or open country

<gam>, land, with <keek>, push out a border: one who seizes the land of others; placed before the name of a colonial power, as in {gamkeek Mikang kumpi}, the colonial British government
take the land of another people and rule it
those who take the land of other peoples and rule it, from <gam>, land, and <keek>, enlarge a border, with the plural <te>; {Mikang gamkeekte} are the British colonial rulers
<Gam>, wild country, with <keel>, goat: a wild goat.
Plural of <gamkeel>: wild goats.
a power that takes and rules the land of others, from <gam>, land; also the taking itself; {gamkek hun} is the colonial period and {gamkek kumpi} a colonial government
<gamkek> with the plural <te>: the colonial powers or rulers
<gamke>, state, with the plural <te>
<Gam>, land, with <keu>, dry: land without water.

<gamkhangto>, developed country, with the plural <te>: the developed countries
<Gam>, land or kingdom, written together with <khat>, one: one kingdom, a kingdom; <gamkhat leh gamkhat> is kingdom against kingdom.

terms: between countries/country and country/from country to country
definition: <gamkhat>, one country, said twice and joined by <leh>: one country and another, countries among themselves. Stands before a noun or verb of mutual dealing, as {gamkhat leh gamkhat kizopna}, relations between countries, and {gamkhat leh gamkhat kido}, country fights country, or before a thing that differs from one country to the next. The same pattern is made with other nouns and <khat>
<gamkhat>, a country or one country, and <in> written as one word: as a country of some kind, or together as one country
<gamkhat>, one country, and <pan>, from, written as one word; {gamkhatpan gamkhat} is from one country to another

<gamkhat>, a country, with <peuh>, any

{Gamkhing}, wasteland, written with a capital as a name given to the land.

The state of a place laid waste; related to <gamkhing>, desolation, and also written <gamkhin'na>.

wild country where no one lives; the land the Israelites crossed after leaving Egypt

terms: in the field/in the wilderness/in the open country

<gamlak> with the place marker <ah>: in or into the field, the open country or the wilderness
<gamlak>, wild country, with <pi>, great: land left wild and empty; {gamlakpi suak} is become a wasteland
<gamlak> with the plural <te>: the wild, uncultivated parts of a land
<gamla>, far, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not far away; {tawh ki gamlalo} is not far from
<gamla>, far, and <lualo>, not very, written as one word; {tawh aki gamlalualo} is not far from

terms: region/part of the world/direction of a country

<gamla>, far, with <pen>, most; {leimong gamlapen} is the farthest end of the earth

form of <gamla> used before another word; {a gamlat mah bangin} is as far as

<gamla>, far, with the comparative <zaw>
<gam>, country, and <leh>, and, written as one word; mostly in {gamleh minam}, country and people

<gamlum>, uproar, with the causative <sak>

<gammang> and <tulak> written as one word: wild forest country far from where people live

<gam>, country, and <min>, name, written as one word

<gammi>, citizen, with <pa> marking a man: after the name of a country, a man of that country

<gammi> with plural <te>, the people who belong to a land or to a ruler

<gamneu>, province, with the plural <te>

<gam> and <taampi> written as one word: thickly forested country

<gamta>, act, with <khial>, err

<gamta>, act, with <lai>, still

terms: cause to walk again/cause to live again
definition: <gamtangsak> with <kik>, again
doubled form of <gamtang>, move: keep moving on

terms: be able to move about/be able to go about

<gamta>, act, with <teng>, all: all those who act so
<gamtat>, behave, with <hoih>, good, written as one word: good behaviour, and also to behave well

<gamtat> with the linking ending {-in}: acting in the way named before it, as in {hai gamtatin}, acting foolishly

<gamtat>, act, with the noun suffix <na>: what a person does, his deeds and way of acting

plural of <gamtatna>: the things a person does, his ways of acting

<gamtatna>, action, with <zia>, manner, and the plural <te>
<gamtat>, act, with <nop>, want
<gamtatnop>, want to do, with the noun suffix <na>
<gamtat>, behave or act, with <pa>, the man who, written as one word: the man who acted so; {agitloh gamtatpa} is the man who did the wicked deed
<gamtat> behave with <pha> good: doing what is good
<gamtat>, act, with <sa>, already done; {gamtatsa bangin} is as someone had done
