after a verb or an adjective it stresses how far a thing goes: {baih hial lo} is not easy at all, and {thong hial} is even so far as that
said of a judge closing a hearing for the time being without giving a decision

bring a meeting, a programme or a planned activity to its end, as in {meeting ki hialbawl}, the meeting was closed; the thing is finished, not put off for a later day as in the first sense; often followed by <ta>
expressive adverb after <omkhawm> or <takhawm> in the picture of twin fawns; paired with <helhel>, it seems to stress being closely together or alike
expressive adverb after a verb of going about such as <vak>, <vakkhawm> or <paikhawm>: moving along in an easy, unhurried way, often said of people strolling together
final particle of an interrogative sentence, collocating with initial particles such as <bang> and <kua>
postpositional marker to indicate objective case
having a keen edge, of a knife or blade; the opposite of <mawl>, blunt

<hiam>, the word that ends a question, and <cihleh>, if one says: closes a question that the speaker then answers; {banghang hiam cihleh}, if one asks why, is because, for, and the answer often ends in {ahih man hi}; after another question word it means as for what or how, it is this

the question word <hiam>, whether or which, with <cihpen>, as for what is said: closes an indirect question and makes it the topic, as to whether or what or who; a verb of knowing, saying or inquiring follows, often negated

the question particle <hiam> with <cih>, saying, written as one word: closes a question that is reported or thought about, what, why or whether something is; {banghang hiamcih leh}, if one asks why, means because
the question particle <hiam> and <cihleh>, if one asks, written as one word after <banghang>, why: if one asks why, that is, because
cruel and violent treatment of people; {hiamgam takin} is violently, {innsung hiamgam} is domestic violence
<hiamgam>, violence, with the noun suffix <na>: being cruel and violent; listed by the book among the abstract nouns
<hiam>, sharp, with the ending <in>; {tat hiamin} and {kitat hiamin} are whet or be whetted until sharp
<hiam>, weapon, with the marker <in>: as a weapon
the question particle <hiam> with <khat>, one, written as one word after a question word or a describing phrase: an amount or thing that is not known exactly, as {bangzah hiamkhat}, some number of
<hiam> and <mahmah> written as one word: very sharp, of a blade or teeth
<hiam>, sharp, with the noun suffix <na>; {seek hiamna} is the forging of a tool to make it sharp again
<hiam> sharp with <sa> already and the ending <in>, in a sharpened state, said of an arrow kept ready for use
<hiam>, sharp, with <sak>, cause: make sharp

terms: with a blade/with a sharp weapon
definition: <hiam>, here a blade or sharp weapon, and <tawh>, with, written as one word
<hiam>, weapon, with <tawi>, carry: bearing weapons; {hiamtawi mite} are the armed men
noun of <hiamtawi>: the carrying or use of weapons, armed means as opposed to words
<hiamtawi> armed with the plural <te>, those who bear weapons
plural of <hiam>, weapon: the arms a man carries, such as sword, spear, bow and quiver
<hiam>, sharp, in the plural after the thing named, as {thaltang hiamte}, sharp arrows, and {namsau hiamte}, sharp swords
<hiam>, sharp, with <van>, goods: a weapon, any tool for wounding or killing; often named together with <galvan>
<hiam>, sharp, with <zaw>, more: sharper, used with <sangin>, than
branch or bough of a tree or vine, also an arm of the lampstand
a part into which a larger whole divides, as a field of knowledge or a group within a religion; a picture taken from the branch of a tree
<hiang>, branch, written with a capital of the promised king from the line of David, the righteous Branch
<hiang>, branch, with the place marker <ah>: on or in the branches, where birds nest and perch
a kind of tree, used in the Bible for the plane tree and the fir; said with <kung> or <sing>, tree
<hiang>, branch, with <pha>, good or plentiful: having many spreading branches, said of a vine
a kind of tree that people plant; the species is not determined from the page
plural of <hiang>: the branches of a tree or vine
<hiang>, branch, with <teng>, all of them: all the branches of a tree
village near Taingen on the road between Kalaymyo and Tedim
after a verb, usually doubled as {hiat-hiat} or <hit-hiat>: in a calm, undisturbed way
draw or press something across a surface; {sam hiat} is comb or dress the hair, and in Lamentations 3:16 the face is rubbed on the ground
follows a verb, often of speaking, to show that the action goes on in a calm, even and unhurried way
<hiathiat> with the adverbial ending <in>; {na sem hiathiatin} is working quietly and steadily
placed after a verb of going, apparently showing that the going is swift and direct, as in {a paikhia hiau hi}, he went straight on his way
expressive word after <nung>, blow: of a wind blowing softly and gently
<hiau> and <lo> written as one word after a verb: not really, hardly or not at all so
<hiau> and <mawk> written as one word after a verb, apparently saying that the action goes straight on or turns out so, often to the surprise of the speaker
<hiau> and <zen> written as one word after a verb: the act is done suddenly and with feeling, at once
a short form of <hih>, this, with <bang>, like, written as one word: like this, of this kind; {hibang in} and {hibang dan in} are in this way
<hih>, this, <bang>, like, and <dan>, manner, written as one word in a shortened spelling: in this way, of this kind; before a noun, such
<hih>, this, and <bangin>, in the way of, written as one word: in this way; before a verb of saying it introduces the words that follow
<hi>, be, with <bek>, only: is only, is nothing more than
<hi>, be, and <beka> written as one word: is only that and nothing more, linked to the clause that follows
<hi>, be, and <beklo>, not only, written as one word: it is not only that, with something more added after it
<hi>, be, with <bilbel>, as it happened, written as one word: it just happened to be so, as things turned out
<hi> be with the emphatic particle <buang>: whatever else may be said, she is a daughter of a king
in the Bible text it stands before a verb and points to the manner just seen or spoken of: like this, in this way, so
<hici>, like this, and <bang>, like: placed before a noun, such a one or this kind of, pointing to what was just described

terms: this far/up to here/to this point
definition: <hi>, here a short form of <hih>, this, with <ciang>, up to: as far as this, to this point or extent; {hiciang tung} is reach this far
<hici>, like this, and <bang>, like, written as one word: of this kind; with <in>, in this way
<hici>, like this, and <banga>, in the manner of, written as one word before a verb: in this way, so suddenly as this
the sentence ending <hi> and <cih> written as one word, closing a statement that is reported, known or thought: that it is so; {om hicih phawk in} is remember that there is
do or be like this; paired with {huacih}, like that
{hih dan} written as one word with the final h dropped: this manner, like this; before a noun, such a, and alone, such a thing
<hidan>, this way, and <in> written as one word: in this manner
one of the mighty warriors of David, from the ravines of Gaash
the third river that flowed out of Eden, running east of Assyria; the Hebrew name of the Tigris
<hi>, be, and <den>, always, written as one word: it is always so, it keeps being so
<hi> and <deuh> written as one word: it is rather so, it is mostly that
<hi> and <diak> written as one word: it is so in particular, above the rest
<hi>, be, and the marker <ding> for what is to come, written as one word: will be, is to be, or is probably

terms: it is said to be likely/is believed to be/reportedly
definition: <hiding>, will be or probably is, and <cihi>, he said or it is said: closes a news sentence and marks what stands before it as the guess of the source, not an established fact
<hiding>, it will be, and <hiven>, it is so after all: closes a clause that gives the speaker's guess at the reason or circumstance of what is told next, it must be that, presumably

terms: is said to be/is believed to be/is thought to be
definition: <hiding>, probably is, and <kici>, be said: closes a news statement that reports what people suppose and is not confirmed, it is said that it probably is; <hi> may follow
<hi> and <dinga> written as one word: it will be so, and; closes one clause about what is to be and links it to the next
<hi>, be, with <dingaa> written as one word: closes a clause about what will be the case and links it to the next, it will be so and
<hi>, <ding> and a second <hi> that ends the sentence, written as one word: it will be; in reports, it is probably so, it must be
<hi>, <ding> and <hiam> written as one word: a question or doubt about what may be so, could it be that, whether it might be; often before {cihpen kitheician nailo hi}, it is not yet known
<hi> and <dingin> written as one word: that it is or will be so, mostly before a verb of believing or supposing such as <um> and <ummawh>
<hi> and <ei> written as one word at the end of a statement in lively speech: it is so, indeed
man of Bethel who rebuilt Jericho in the time of King Ahab, at the cost of his sons Abiram and Segub
city in Asia Minor near Laodicea and Colossae, where Epaphras worked
a main road for fast traffic between towns
<hi>, be, and <gige>, always, written as one word: it is always so, it remains so
points to a person or thing near the speaker or just mentioned; before a noun it means this or these, and {hih bangin} is in this way
<hih>, this, written with a capital at the start of a sentence or of quoted speech
<hih> written in capitals in the inscription on the cross; {HIH PA} is this man
<hi>, be, and <hang>, here the verb ending for we including the hearer, written as one word at the end of a sentence: we are; after <ding>, we shall
<hih> and <bang> written as one word: of this kind; before <in>, in this way
<hih>, <bang> and <aa> written as one word, where <aa> stands for the adverb ending more often written <in>: in this way, like this
<hih>, <bang> and <dan> written as one word: of this kind, in this way; before a noun it means such a
<hih> and <bangin> written as one word: in this way, like this; it points to what has just been told or to the words that follow

terms: to such an extent/as badly as this/even like this
definition: <hihbang>, like this, and <liang>, even, written as one word: to such a degree, said with shock at how far something went
<hihbang>, like this, and the plural <te> written as one word: things of this kind, often before <hangin>, because of

terms: such a matter/a case like this
definition: <hihbang> and <vai> written as one word: a matter or case of this kind
<hih>, this, and <buaina>, trouble, written as one word: this trouble, this incident just reported

terms: this far/to this point/to this extent
definition: <hih>, this, and <ciang>, as far as, written as one word: up to this point or level, often with <tung>, reach, or followed by <dong>
<hih>, this, and <cibang>, of that kind, written as one word: such a thing, a thing like this; before a noun it means this kind of
<hih>, this, with <dan>, manner, written as one word: this way, like this; {hihdan in} introduces what is said or done
<hih> and <ding> written as one word: to be something, or what is to be done; {hihding kisam} is it is necessary to be
<hi>, be, and <hen>, let, written as one word: let it be so, may it be
<hi>, be, and <het>, at all, written as one word and always followed by <lo> or <kei>: {hihet lo hi} is it is not at all so

terms: be not at all/be by no means
definition: <hi>, be, with <hetlo>, not at all, written as one word: it is not that at all
<hih>, this, and <gamsung>, land, written as one word, usually before <ah>: in this country
<hih>, do, with <gawp>, roughly or violently: fall upon someone, treat with violence

terms: because of this/because it is/although it is
definition: <hih> and <hang>, reason, written as one word. {Hihhang in} is because of this; {a hihhang}, with <hih> the form of <hi>, be, is because it is so or although it is so, and alone it opens a sentence as even so
the form <hih> of the verb be with <hangin>, written as one word after <a> or <na>: {a hihhangin} is although it is so, however, and {na hihhangin} is although you are
<hih>, this, and <hun>, time, written as one word; {hihhun sungah} is during this time
<hi>, be, written as one word with the sentence-final <hi> that follows it, after <a>, <ka>, <na> or <i>: {a hihi} is it is, {ka hihi} I am
<hi> and <hiam> written as one word: the verb to be at the end of a question, as in {bang hihiam}, what is it, and {na hihiam}, are you
placed after a verb: do it calmly and without fuss, just do it and nothing more; compare <hithiat> and <hiathiat>
<hih>, do, with the linking ending <in>: doing or by doing, followed by another verb

<hih.1>, this, with the marker <in>, at the start of a sentence: this, as the subject, pointing to what has just been said or shown, {hihin a thupi khat ahi hi} this is an important thing; not the verb do
<hih> with a following word for than, written as one word and followed by <in>: than this, before a comparison
<hih> and <kei> written as one word, <hih> being the form of <hi>, be, used before <leh>: {a hihkei leh} is if it is not so, otherwise, or else
<hih>, be so, with <kei>, not, and <leh>, if, written as one word and used after <a> as {a hihkeileh}: if it is not so, and so or, between two things of which one is chosen
<hih>, do, with <kha>, which marks an act that happens to be done, by mistake or as something that may come about
form of <hihkha> used before another word: do something without meaning to; {na hihkhak loh nadingun}, so that you do not come to do it

terms: happen to be/turn out to be/come to be
definition: form of <hikha> used before another word, from <hi>, be, and not from <hih>, do: come to be a certain kind of person, after a noun or <mi> as in {tuabang mi na hihkhak phialleh}, even if you happen to be such a person
<hih>, do, and <khialh>, wrongly, written as one word: do something wrongly; also the mistake made
<hih>, do, with <khiat>, out; {khut hihkhiat} is to put out the hand against someone
<hih>, this, and <khuasung>, town, written as one word; with <ah>, in this city
<hih>, do, with <kik>, again
<hih>, do, with <kim>, complete: do all of it and leave nothing out
<hih>, this, and <la>, song, written as one word
<hih> this with <lai> place and the place marker <ah>; also written {hih lai-ah}
<hih> and <laibu> written as one word: this book
the fact of being, from <hih> be with <lam>; with <ka>, <na> or <a> before it and <thei> know, <phawk> notice or <um> believe after it, where English says that I am, that you are
<hih>, the form of <hi> be, with <lam> and <tak>: the very fact of being so; {a gelh ka hihlamtak} is that I am indeed one who writes
<hih>, here the form of <hi> before an ending, with <leh>, written as one word after <a>, <na> or <ih>: if it is, if you are; after a noun or pronoun also as for; the same as <ahihleh>
<hih>, do, with the negative <lo> written as one word; {bangmah hihlo} is do nothing
<hih>, do, with <loh>, the form of the negative <lo> used before <nading>, <om> and similar words
<hi>, be, with <loh>: not being, used before <nading> or <hangin>
the fact of not being or not doing, <hih> with <loh> not and <lam>; with <ka>, <na> or <a> before it and <phawk> notice or <thei> know after it, where English says that I am not, that I was not
<hi>, be, with <loh>, not, and the noun suffix <na>: the fact that someone is not something; {ka hihlohna thu}, that I am not

terms: though not done/what one did not do
definition: <hihloh> and <napi> written as one word: although one did not do it, said of a thing one is blamed for without having done it
<hih>, do, with <lum>, dead: do to death, kill
<hih>, here the form of <hi>, be, used before a following word, with emphatic <mah>, written as one word; {a hihmah bangin} is just as it really is, in keeping with what it is

terms: as it indeed is/since it is/being
definition: <hihmah>, indeed be, and <bang.2>, like, here not the question word what: after a clause with <a> or <ka> and usually followed by <in>, it gives the known fact that explains what follows, as it really is so, since it is so

<hih>, here the form of <hi>, be, with <man>, here reason, written as one word; stands after <a>, <i>, <ka> or <na> at the end of a clause, often followed by <in>: because it is, because we are; the same as {ahih manin}
<hih>, here the form of <hi>, be, with <manin>, because, written as one word; stands after <a>, <i>, <ka> or <na> at the end of a clause: because it is, because I am; the same as {ahih manin}
<hih> with <man> reason and <un>, the plural ending with <in>: because you did or are so; also written {na hih manun} in the same verse
used after <lung> heart, {lung hihmawh}; another spelling of <himawh>
<hihmawh>, be anxious, with <huai>, worthy of; {lung hihmawhhuai hi} is it is a thing to be anxious about
used after <lung>, heart, as {lung hihmawhna}: worry or concern about what may happen; <hihmawh> with the noun ending <na>
<hih>, do, and <mawk>, without thought or care, written as one word; {bang hihmawk na hiam} is what on earth are you doing
<hih>, this, and <mun>, place, written as one word: this place; {hihmun ah} is here, at this point
the fact of being, noun form of <hi> be, used where English says that someone is or will do something, as in {Topa ka hihna} that I am the Lord
what someone does, noun form of <hih>, do; {na hihna khempeuh} is all that you do
<hihna>, the fact of being, and <taktak>, real: what a person or a people really is, as against how others see them; it follows a possessor, as in {i hihna taktak}, what we really are
<hih>, be or do, with the first part of <nakleh>, written as one word and followed by <leh>: if indeed it is so, if they do so
<hihna>, deed, with <sa>, already done: the things someone has done
<hih>, do, with <na>, <sa>, already done, and plural <te>: the things someone has done
<hihna>, the fact of being, and <tawh>, with, written as one word: as one who is, in view of being what was just named
plural of <hihna>; the things someone does or has done
<hih>, this, and <natna>, disease, written as one word

terms: have done before/be used to doing
definition: <hih>, do, and <ngei> written as one word: what one has done before or always does, as in {i hihngei dan}, the way we have always done it
<hih>, this, and <ni>, day, written as one word: this day, the day spoken of
<hih>, do, with <nop>, the form of <nuam>, want, used before a noun or <loh>; {na hihnop khempeuh} is all that you want to do
<hihnop>, want to do, with the plural <te>: the things he wants to do

terms: all that one wants to do
definition: <hihnop>, want to do, with <teng>, all of it: everything one wants to do
<hih>, this, with <nu> marking a woman: this woman, she, said of a woman who is present or being spoken about
<hih>, this, with <pa> marking a man: this man, he, said of a man who is present or being spoken about
<hihpa> written in capitals in the inscription on the cross
<hih>, do, and <pah> written as one word: do something right away
<hih>, do, with <pak>, at once, used in commands: {hihpak in}, do it without delay
<hih>, this, and <pawi>, festival, written as one word
<hih>, this, with the topic marker <pen>, written as one word: this, as the thing spoken about
<hih>, this, and <phual>, site, written as one word: this place, the site that is spoken about
<hih>, the form of <hi> be, with <pih> together with; {sila ka hihpih} is the one who is a servant along with me, my fellow servant
<hih>, do, with <sa>, already: what someone has done, placed before the noun it describes or before <khempeuh>, all
<hih>, do, with <sak>: do something for or to another person; with <lo>, not let someone act against another

terms: deed done for someone/what was done for
definition: <hihsak>, do for, with the noun suffix <na>: what one person has done for another
<hih> this with <san> place, used as {hihsan takah}, right here, at this very place
<hih> and <sang> written as one word, <sang> in the sense than: than this, before a comparison with <zaw>
<hih> and <sangin> written as one word: compared with this, usually with <zaw> on the describing word
<hihsa> with plural <te>: what someone has done
<hih>, do or be, and <sawm>, intend, written as one word: set oneself to be or to do what is named before it
<hih>, this, and <sung>, inside, written as one word and followed by <ah>: in this, within this
<hih>, here the form of <hi>, be, and <sung>, during, written as one word after <a>: during the time that someone is or was something, as {kumpi nu a hihsung}, while she was queen
<hih>, this, and <tak>, exactly, written as one word and followed by <ah> or <a>: right here, at this very point of what is said or written
<hih>, be, with <takpi>, truly; {na hihtakpi leh} is if you really are
<hih> and <tawh> written as one word: with this, counting this one; {hihtawh kisai in} is concerning this
<hihte>, these, written with a capital at the start of a sentence or of quoted speech
found as {ih hihteh} after a describing phrase: since we are so, given that we would be so; a form of the verb <hi>, be, with the ending <teh>
<hih>, this, with <teng>, here in its sense of all of, written as one word: all these, the things just named or about to be named
<hih>, do, with <thei>, can
form of <hihthei> used before <nading>, <zah> or <leh>; {ka hihtheih zahin}, as much as I can
<hihtheih>, be able to do, and the negative <kei> written as one word, before <leh>: if one cannot do it
<hihtheih> and <leh> written as one word; {a hihtheihleh} opens advice: if it can be done
<hihtheih>, can do, with the noun suffix <na>: what one is able or allowed to do
<hihtheihna>, ability, and the plural <te> written as one word: the things one is able to do

terms: as much as one can do/best of one's ability
definition: <hihtheih>, can do, and <zah>, amount, written as one word; {ka hihtheihzah in} is as much as I can, to the best of my ability
<hih>, this, and <thu>, matter or word, written as one word: this matter, what has just been told
<hihthu> and the topic marker <pen> written as one word: this matter, as the thing being spoken about
<hih> and <thupiang> written as one word: this incident, what has just been reported
<hih>, this, and <thute>, matters, written as one word: these things, what has just been told

terms: seem to be/appear to be/apparently be/seem
definition: a form of <hi>, be, joined with <tuak> and written as one word at the end of a statement: it seems, it appears that; the writer passes on or infers something without stating it as certain

terms: seem not to be/probably not be
definition: <hihtuak>, seem to be, with <lo>, not, written as one word: it does not seem to be, it is probably not
<hihtuak>, seem to be, with <mawk>, written as one word: it appears that it was so, said of something reported with surprise
<hih>, this, and <vai>, matter, written as one word; {hihvai tawh kisai in} is concerning this matter
<hih>, this, <vai>, matter, and <tawh>, with, written as one word; used in {hihvaitawh kisai in}, concerning this matter
<hih>, this, with <zah>, amount: as many or as great as this; {hihzah tak nalamdangte} is miracles as great as these

terms: to this extent/as much as this/on this scale
definition: <hihzah>, this much, and <liang>, even, written as one word, usually with <in>: to such a degree as this, often of something never seen before
<hihzah>, this much, with <ta>: as many as these; {kampau hihzahta} is so many words as these
<hih>, this, and <zahzah> written as one word before a noun or verb: as much or as many as this, such a great amount
<hih>, do, with <zaw>, more or rather: do more than others, or do one thing rather than another
<hih>, do, with <zawh>, the form of <zo>, be able, used before <ding>, <zah> or <nakleh>: what one has the power to do
<hihzawh>, be able to do, with the noun suffix <na>: what one is able to do; {Pasian’ piak hihzawhna} is a gift given by God
<hih>, do, with <zia>, manner: the way someone does a thing
<hih>, do, with <zo>, be able: succeed in doing; {hihzo kei} means cannot do
<hih> and <zong> written as one word: this as well
in {a hihzong in}, another way of writing {ahih zongin}: however, even so
<hi>, be, and <in> written as one word: being so, is this and, closing one clause and linking it to the next
<hi>, be, with the first person ending <ing>, written as one word at the end of a sentence: I am
smelling stale or rancid, of food that has gone off; {vok-hiing} is the stench of pigs
seize a plane or vehicle by force; used with other words, as {ki Hijack}, be hijacked, and {Hijack bawl}, carry out a hijacking
a louse, the small insect that lives in hair and clothing
the germ or virus that causes a disease; {natna hik} is a disease germ
without feeling, of the body or a limb; {khe hik} is the feet go numb
said of a hand that has grown tired and stiff and stays clenched
<hi>, be, and <kei>, not, written as one word: it is not so; {tua hikei leh} is if not, otherwise
<hi>, be, with <kei>, not, and <leh>, if: if it is not so; usually follows <tua>, that, as <tua hikeileh>, otherwise
<hi>, be, and the first person negative ending, short for {kei ing}, written as one word: I am not, it is not that I

terms: may be/turn out to be/happen to be
definition: <hi>, be, with <kha>, which marks what may happen or turn out; {hikha thei} is may well be
<hikha>, may be, and <ding>, will, written as one word: it is probably so, it must be; a guess of the writer
<hikha>, may be, with <thei>, can: perhaps it is so

terms: to do at ease/will do in peace

<hih>, this, with <thu>, matter, written as one word: this matter, the thing just spoken of

<hi>, <ve> and <ing> written as one word: sentence ending of the first person singular that stresses the statement, I am indeed, I do; {ding hiveng} is I surely will

<hi>, this, with <zah>, amount: this many, as much as this; {mi hizah tak} is so many people as this

terms: what you find good/as you think best

<hoihbek> with <in>: keeping to what is fitting, without pride

<hoih> with the linking suffix {-in}, good and, joined to a following descriptive word

<hoih> and <ta> written as one word: it is good now, it has become good

the line of generations of a family, from the forefathers down to the descendants; {khangkua kizopna} is the relationship between the generations of one line
in the strength of youth; {khanglai mi} is a young man, {humpinelkai khanglai} a young lion
<khang>, rise, and <laiding>, will still, written as one word: said of water that is expected to rise further
<khanglai>, in the growing years, with the plural <te>; {humpinelkai khanglaite}, young lions
the south, the direction opposite <saklam>, north; {khanglam huih} is the south wind
the side that lies lower down
<khanglam>, south, written with a capital at the start of a sentence or in a title such as {Khanglam kumpi}, the king of the South

terms: in the south/on the south side
definition: <khanglam> and <ah> written as one word: in the south, to the south, or on the lower side of a house
<khanglam> south with the plural <te>, which here covers the pair {saklam leh khanglam}, the north and the south
<khang> and <lian> written as one word: grow up from childhood, grow big
wake from sleep; {khanglo in} is the call to wake up
<khanglo> written with a capital in a call to wake up
<khanglo> be awake with the causative <sak>: rouse someone from sleep
of former generations, of long ago; {khanglui ngeina} is the tradition handed down from the elders
the time of former generations, as in {khanglui laipek panin}, from the days of old
the people of former generations themselves, not their time: with <te> and <in> as the subject of a verb of saying or doing, as in {khanglui te in ci hi}, the forebears said
<khanglui> with the plural <te>: the generations of the past
<khanglui>, former age, with the plural suffix <te>, here the people of earlier generations; written with a capital at the start of a sentence
the people living at one time; <khang> generation with <mi> people
<khangmi>, a person of a certain generation, with plural <te>; {tua khangmite} is that generation
young in age, of a child
<khangmoi>, young, with <lai>, the time when: still young, in the time of youth
<khangmoi> with the plural <te>, set against <khanghamte>, the old
<khang> and <nih> written as one word: two generations; {khangkhat khangnih} is one or two generations
young in age; {a khangno lai} is while still young, and {khangno mite} are young people, the opposite of {khangham mite}
the time of being young, as in {khangno lai}

<khangno> young, with <lai>, the time when

<khangno> with <pen>, most
<khangno> young, with <suak>, become
<khangno>, young, with the plural <te>: young people, set against <khanghamte>, the old
<khangno> with <zaw>, more
<khangnozaw> with the plural <te>

<khangsak> with the linking <a> written as one word: makes something grow or increase, and then the sentence goes on
<khangsak>, make grow or increase, with the linking suffix <in>, followed by a second verb

terms: one who makes grow/giver of growth
definition: <khangsak>, make grow, with <pa>, the one who does it: the one who gives growth, said of God
<khangsak>, make grow, with <tawm>, of oneself: make something grow without outside help, as the soil does with seed
<khangsak>, make grow, with <to>, upward or onward: make something greater still
the generations that come after, mostly in songs and solemn speech; paired with <tusawn> as {tusawn khangsawn}
<khang>, generation, with <sawn>, on in turn, and the plural <te>: those of the generation that follows
<khang>, increase, and <semsem>, more and more, written as one word: go on growing or rising, of a number, a feeling, knowledge or water
the counting of generations, from <khang>, generation, and <sim>, count: a family record; {khangsimna ah kiciamteh} is be entered in the genealogy
<khang> in the sense generation or age, with <tangthu>, story, written as one word: the record of what happened in past times; with a capital, {Khangtangthu}, the Bible book of Chronicles
plural of <khang>, generation: the generations of a people; {mai lam khangte} is the generations to come
<khang>, rise, with the plural <te>: of river waters that rise in flood
in {a inn sak a inn khangte}, the people of the houses above and below, that is the neighbours; <khang> is the lower side
<khang>, generation, with <thak>, new: the generation that grows up after the one before has died
belonging to the present age or to the young generation, said of a time, a person or a thing; {khangthak hun} is modern times, against <khanglui>, of the old days
<khangthak>, new generation, with plural <te>
<khang>, grow or rise, and <theilo>, unable, written as one word: not able to grow, said of a child, or not able to rise, said of rank
the account of the generations: the line of a family or the history of a people or country
<khang>, grow, with <to>, upward: become bigger, taller or more; said of a child, a plant, wealth, a people, or rising waters
of a country, a town, a people or a person: make progress in education, wealth and way of life, not grow in size or number; {gam khangto} is a developed country
<khangto>, develop, and <gamte>, countries: the developed countries of the world, as a fixed term; it stands after <a>, as in {a khangto gamte ah}, in the developed countries
<khangto>, grow or develop, and the linking <in>, written as one word: growing or making progress, and so
<khangto>, grow or develop, with <lo>, not, written as one word: not developed, of a people or country
<khangto> with an ending meaning already: that has developed; {a khangtosa gamte} are the developed countries
<khangto>, grow up, with the causative <sak>: make a plant or a person grow, build up a people, or lift up the lowly
<khangto>, grow or develop, with the plural <te>: those that are developed; <gam khangtote> is the developed countries and {mi khangtote} is advanced or civilised people

terms: keep growing/keep rising/increase more and more
definition: <khang>, grow, and <toto>, more and more, written as one word: go on growing, rising or advancing
<khangto>, grow or rise, and <zaw>, more, written as one word: rise by an amount, or be more developed than another
the time when a person is still in full growth and strength; {a khangtung kimlai}, while in the midst of life
people of the same age or generation as oneself
those of the same age or generation as oneself, with the plural <te>
<khang> generation with <un>; {na khang khangun}, through your generations one after another
<khang>, grow, with <zo>, be able: manage to grow, flourish; said of a planted vine
<kha> month with <nih> two; {khasawm leh khanih}, ten months and two, is twelve months

in the old Zomi custom, the animals killed at a death, mithun, cattle, goats, pigs or even horses, which the dead person was believed to take along and keep in the village of the dead; named together with <kawsah>, and also said <hanken>
<khan>, lifetime, and <khat>, one, written as one word: one lifetime, once in a life
<khan>, grow, with <khiat>, out, and the noun suffix <na>: the growing up of a person, and the place or home where one grew up, as in {ka khankhiatna khua}, the village where I grew up
make someone grow up and come forth, as a king from a family line
<khan> lifetime, <khin> finished, with <in>: having lived out the whole of life
<khan> grow, with <khit> finish; {a khankhit ciangin}, when it has grown, {a khankhit ma-in}, before it is grown
<khan> grow with <kik>, again
a thing made for the dead at a funeral, whose makers receive half of the neck each; taken to be the coffin, as <kuang> is a trough or coffin, which is not confirmed
<khan>, lifetime, and <kum>, year, written as one word: the years of one's life, one's age; also in song language

terms: in midlife/in the middle of life
definition: <khan> lifetime, <lai> middle, with <in>
<khan>, grow, with <lam>, which turns it into the thing spoken of: that someone or something grows; listed without a sentence
wake from sleep; {a khanlawh ciangin} is when he woke up
<khanlawh>, wake up, with the noun ending <na>: an awakening, above all a spiritual revival in the church, also the awakening of a people
<khan> grow with <lua>, too much
the place, mostly on a hilltop, where the dead were buried in former times, named beside <khankuang>, the vault of a clan
<khan> grow up, with the noun suffix <na>: where someone was brought up
<khang>, increase, with the noun suffix <na>: the growing or increasing of something, as a church, knowledge or a price; of a river or of water, its rising
found in {tom khano}, a short moment
in {tavuan khanpi}, the one who bears the chief responsibility; known only from this phrase

<khan>, grow, with <pih>, together with: grow along with someone and so make them grow or progress; {hong khanpih ding makai} is a leader who will lift us up, set against {hong kiatpih}, bring us down
one who grew up at the same time as another, a person of the same age group
<khan>, grow, with the causative <sak>: make a plant grow, build up a body of people, raise up a leader
<khansak>, make grow, and the future marker <ding> written as one word: will raise or is to raise an amount, a fee or a level
<khansak> make grow, with the noun suffix <na>: the raising of someone's rank
<khan>, lifetime, with <sau>, long: have a long life; {khansau hen} is the wish long live
<khansau>, live long, with the noun suffix <na>
<khan>, life span, and <sawt>, long, written as one word: live a long life
of a man, bad in character so that no one can reason with him; said of Nabal
<khan>, lifetime, with <sih>, die: have the lifetime cut short, the opposite of <khansau>
<khansih> with the linking suffix <in>: counted as having died young

terms: cut off early/cause to die young
definition: <khansih> die young with the causative <sak>: cut short the life of someone; in Hosea 9:12 take away the children of someone
care for a child until grown
<khansuah>, bring up, with the noun ending {-na}: the bringing up of the young, also growth in faith
those who have raised children to full age; <khan> grow, <suah> bring out, <sa> already done, with the plural <te>
the time that a person lives; <khan> lifetime with <sung> within

the word for room, as in <khaan> and <innkhan>, with <sung>, inside: a room of a house or building, after <lupna> or the name of a building; not the lifetime of a person, which follows <ka>, <na> or <a>
the word for room, as in <innkhan>, with <sungah>, written as one word: inside the room; {lupna khansungah} is in the bedroom
<khan>, lifetime, with <tawn>, go along: through the whole of life, for good; {khantawn thongkia} is imprisoned for life
<khan> lifetime with <tawn> through and <in>; follows a possessive such as <na>, your: through the whole of your life

terms: all your life/as long as you live
definition: <khan> lifetime, <tawn> throughout, with <un> for you, plural
a Burmese loan word for room with the plural <te>: rooms, as in {lupna khante}, bedrooms, and {sai khante}, shops; not <khan>, lifetime
<khan> grow with <theih>, be able; {khantheih nading}, so that it may grow
<khantheih> with the noun suffix <na>: the way a seed is able to grow
<khanto>, a spelling of <khangto>, grow or rise, with <ding>, will, written as one word: will go up, said of pay, a number or a limit
<khan>, grow, with <toh>, upward: develop and prosper; {khantoh nading} is for the progress or advancement of
<khantoh>, progress, and <ding> written as one word: to progress, the progressing that is still to come
<khangto>, progress, develop, in the form used before a suffix, with <huai>, worthy of: worth developing
<khantoh>, progress, with the noun suffix <na>
<khantoh> and <nading> written as one word: for the progress or development of something
<khantoh>, progress, with {-nang}, a short form of <nading>: for development, the cause of development; used like <khantohna>
plural of <khantohna>: the ways in which a place or people has advanced
<khantoh>, progress, with <nopna>, wish: the wish to advance and develop, mostly in {khantohnopna lungsim}, a mind set on progress
<khantoh>, progress, and <pih>, together with, written as one word: make progress by means of or together with something
<khantoh>, progress, and <pihding> written as one word: to help a people progress, to bring them forward
<khangto>, progress, develop, in the form used before a suffix, with <suah>, bring out or become: develop; the page lists the form without a meaning
<khangto>, progress, develop, in the form used before a suffix, with <tuak>, be fitting: deserving advancement
<khantoh>, progress, and <vai>, affair, written as one word: what has to do with progress and development
<khantoh>, progress, with <zia>, manner: the way and the degree in which a country, a town or a people develops
<khan> lifetime with <tom> short
<khanto>, live on or go on growing, with the causative <sak>: cause someone to live long or to go on prospering

<kha> in the sense wing, which the lexicon lacks, and <nuai>, under, written as one word: under the wing of someone as a place of shelter and care, said of God; also under the charge of an organisation

a named cut of a slaughtered animal in the sharing of meat, of which one half, {khanuai phalkhat}, is set apart for the party that takes the bride; probably the part under the foreleg, not stated on the page
<khan>, grow, and <zia>, way, written as one word: the way a person, a plant or the world grows and develops
the measure of a spread hand; after <tong> it adds half a cubit, {tong khat leh khap} is a cubit and a half
give something as security for a loan; {a na khap} is the thing he has pledged
<kha>, happen to do, with <pa>, the man who: after a verb, the man who did it without meaning to; {mi that khapa}, the man who killed someone by accident

terms: back in the month of/as early as the month of
definition: <kha>, month, and <pek>, far back, written as one word after the name of a month: as far back as that month; often followed by <panin> or <akipan>, since
<kha> bitter, with <pen>, most; here of snake venom
set the jaw hard in order to bear or force oneself through something difficult, mostly as {khapet liangin}, with gritted teeth
placed after a verb before {ahi zongin}: even if it should happen that; <kha>, happen to, with <phial>, even
<kha> wing with <phung>; {a khaphung nuai} is under their wings
<kha> moon with <pi> great: the moon as a heavenly body
something given or taken as security for a debt or a promise; {khapna-in la} means take as a pledge
a solemn promise made to someone
<khap> pledge, with <sa> for a completed action; {ka khapsa} is what I have promised
of city walls brought down flat to the dust, with <sak>, cause, and the linking suffix <in>; meaning taken from this one verse
<kha>, reach, touch or happen to, with the causative <sak>: after a verb, let the action fall on someone; alone, let someone reach a place
with <mangpha>, farewell: {mangpha hong khasak} means let me say goodbye

terms: call the spirits of the dead
definition: <kha>, spirit, with <sam>, call: at the <Khuado> festival, call the spirits of dead grandparents and parents to come as guests
<kha> month with <sawm> ten; {khasawm leh khanih}, ten months and two, is twelve months
be troubled or saddened in spirit, from <kha> spirit and <sia> bad
<khasia>, be troubled in spirit, and <lua>, very, written as one word: be very upset or heartbroken
<kha>, spirit, and <siangtho>, holy, written as one word and usually with a capital: the Holy Spirit

feel pity for someone and so spare them; {ka khasiat kei ding hi} is I will not pity

<khasia> and <tak> written as one word and followed by <in>: with sorrow, in grief
<khasiat> pity with <huai>, worthy of: deserving pity; {khasiathuai sa} is feel pity for, be grieved over
<khasia>, be troubled or saddened, with the noun suffix {-na}: sadness, hurt feelings or discouragement
<khasiatna> with the plural {-te}: the things that sadden or hurt someone
<khasiat> pity with <pih>, toward someone
<khasiatpih> pity with the noun suffix <na> and the plural <te>: expressions of sympathy
<khasiat>, be sad, with <sak>, cause: make someone sad; the English has take advantage of
<kha>, month, with <sim>, each
<khasim> with the suffix <in>
said of roots, {zung khasuk}: send roots down into the ground; <suk> is downward, set against <gahto>, bear fruit upward
<kha> month with <sum> money: pay received by the month
<khasum> and <teng> written as one word: all of the monthly pay
<kha>, month, and <sung>, in, written as one word, placed after the name of a month and often followed by <in>: {April khasung in} is in the month of April

terms: in the month of/during the month
definition: <kha> and <sungin> written as one word: placed after the name of a month, in or during that month
the number one; after a noun also a or an, as {mi khat}, a man; {khat leh khat} is one another
first, in counting the days of a month: {ni khat ni} is the first day
<khat> written with a capital at the start of a line of verse, in a name such as {Mi Za Khat Tausang}, Tower of the Hundred, or for the One who judges
<khat>, one, and <pepeuh>, a spoken form of <peuhpeuh>: placed after a noun, any one of that kind, whichever it may be

terms: either one/one or the other/any one
definition: <khat>, one, and <zawzaw>, whichever: one or the other of the things just named; placed after a list of two or more alternatives
<khat> one written together with a following <a>; {gal khata}, on the other side; {lang khata}, on one side or against
<kha>, moon, with <taang>, shining; paired with <nitaang>, sunlight
<khat>, one, with the place ending <ah>: at or to one place; {gal khatah} is on the other side and {lang khatah} is against
<khatah>, at one, and <zong>, also, written as one word after a noun: at one such place too, in another one as well
placed at the end of a clause, usually before <ci>, say or think: it may be so, I wonder whether; a guess of which the speaker is not sure
<kha>, month, and <tampi>, many, written as one word: many months, for a long time counted in months
through the whole month, used in a pair after <kumtawn>, all year, or {nitawn}, all day, for a thing that goes on without end
<khat> and <bang> written as one word: about one of a measure, as {meter khatbang}, about one metre; after a noun for a person, a certain one, someone like

<khat>, one, and <bangin>, like, written as one word after a noun: like a, as one
<khat>, one, and <bangpen> written as one word after a noun: as for one of them, a certain one
<khat>, one, with <beek>, even: with a negative, not even one, none at all
<khat> and <bek> written as one word: only one, one alone
<khat> and <bekbek> written as one word: one and no more

<khat> and <ciang> written as one word, after a noun and often followed by <in>: for each one, per item or per person, said of a price or share
<khat>, one, and <ciangin> written as one word after the thing counted: for each one, giving the price or number that belongs to a single unit
<khat> one with <ciat>, each
plural of <kha>, wing: the wings or feathers of a bird, a cherub or the wind
plural of <kha>, spirit: spirits, also the spirits of the dead
plural of <kha>, month
<kha.4>, happen to, with the plural <te>, placed after a verb: the people to whom it happened or who came to do it, as in {a thuak khate}, the victims, and not a plural of the noun <kha>
<khate> written with a capital; plural of <kha>, spirit or soul
what another person lets fall or leaves over; {mi khateh ngak} is wait for the leavings of others, live on what others give
<khat> one with <guak>, only: one by itself
<khatguak>, alone, and <bek>, only, written as one word: only one single person, all by oneself
<kha>, spirit, and <tha>, strength, written as one word: the spirit and its strength, spiritual life
<kha>, month, and <thak>, new, written as one word: a new month, the beginning of a month
placed after the verb to say that something may well happen or be so, often followed by <ding>
<khathei> and <ding> written as one word after a verb: it may well happen, it is likely to
<kha> spirit and <thu> matter, written as one word: the things of the spirit, set beside {leitung thu}, worldly matters, and {taksa thu}, matters of the body
<kha> month with <thum> three, written as one word
<khat>, one, with <in>: into one, as in make into a woman or shape into another pot
<khat>, one, with <in>: with, on or in a single one, as {zawl khatin}, on a single pole, and {ni khatin}, for one day

<khat>, one, with the marker <in> and <zong>, also, written as one word: after a noun, a certain one also did something; after <pen>, also as one of the most
<khat>, one, doubled and written as one word: some, one here and one there; {mun khatkhat ah} is in some places and {khatkhat te} is some people

terms: one by one/one at a time
definition: <khat>, one, doubled and followed by <in>: one by one, one after another
<khat> one, repeated, with <in>
<khatkhat>, some, and the plural <te> written as one word: some of them, certain ones; {pawl khatkhatte} is some groups
<khat>, one, and <khit>, after, written as one word, in {khatkhit khat}, one after another, literally after one, one
<khat>, <khit> and <khat> written as one word, one after one: each following the last, in turn
one by itself, with no other
<khat> and <kia> written as one word: one of them falls, said of an aircraft that crashes
<khat>, one, and <kiang>, side, written as one word and followed by <ah>: to a certain person, to one of them
<khat>, one, and <kiangah>, to, written as one word, after a noun: to one of them, to a certain person
<khat>, one, and <lai>, time, written as one word, mostly as {hun khatlai in}: once, at one time in the past

<khat> and <lawhna> written as one word: the name by which a set or quantity of things is called as one, as three gongs, {dak thum}, are {bu khat}, one set; heading of the list of such unit names in the book
<khat> and <le> written as one word; {khatle khat} is one another, between one and another, and after a measure, as {Minute khatle alang}, it is one and a half
<khat>, one, and <leh>, and, written as one word: one and, a and, joining a first person or thing to the next; {khatleh khat} is one another
<khat>, <leh> and <nih> written as one word: one or two, a small number
{khat le khat}, one and one, written as one word: each other; used with verbs that carry the reciprocal prefix <ki>
<khatle> and <nih> written as one word: one or two, a very small number
<khat>, one, and <leuleu>, in turn, written as one word: one more of the same kind, placed after the noun or standing alone
<khat>, one, and <liam>, be injured, written as one word in news reports: one person is injured
<khat>, one, and <lobuang>, except, written as one word after the one excepted, often followed by <adang>, the others
<khat> and the emphatic <mah> written as one word: one, a, with emphasis; after a noun, {Actor khatmah ahihi}, he is an actor
<khat>, one, with the ordinal suffix <na>: first; after {sawm-le} it forms eleventh, twenty-first and so on
<khatna>, first, with the place ending <ah>: in the first, as in {laigual khatna-ah}, in the first sentence
<khat>, one, and <nei>, have, written as one word after the thing had: have one of it
<khat> and <ni> written as one word, in {ni khatni}: one day, some day; with <ciangin> of a day still to come
<khat>, one, and <nu>, woman, written as one word, mostly as {numei khatnu}: a woman who is not named
<khat>, one, with <pa> marking a man: one of two men, or the other one
<khat> and <pan> written as one word, after the noun that is counted: from one, from a, as {innkuan khatpan}, from a family
<khat> and <panin> written as one word, after a noun: from a, from one such place or thing
<khatpa>, one man, and the topic marker <pen> written as one word: one of the men, the other man, as the one spoken about
<khat>, one, with the topic marker <pen>, written as one word: one of them, a certain one, as the one spoken about
<khat>, one, with <peuh>, any: anyone, or any one thing; {mi khatpeuh} is any person
<khatpeuh>, any one, with the place ending {-ah}, after a noun of place: in or at any such place; {mun khatpeuhah} means anywhere, wherever
<khatpeuh>, any one, with the time marker <in>: {ni hun khatpeuhin}, on some day and hour or other

<khatpeuh>, any one, with the agent marker <in>: any person or thing of a kind as the doer of the action, alone or after a noun as in {sepna khatpeuhin}, any work; not the time expression of the other sense
<khatpeuh> with <peuh> repeated: any one at all, of people, places or things
<khatpeuh> and <tawh> written as one word, after a noun: with any one of them, with some one or other

terms: anyone at all/any at all/even one
definition: <khatpeuh> and <zong> written as one word: any person or thing whatever, and with a negative not even one
<khat>, one, and <suak>, be born, come out or become, written as one word at the end of a headline: one such person or animal has been born or has come to be
<khat>, one, and <sung>, in, written as one word after a noun: inside one thing, as {mawtaw khatsung ah}, in one car, or within one unit of time, as {Minute khatsung in}, within a minute
<khat>, one, and <sungah>, inside, written as one word after a noun: inside one thing, as {Box khatsungah}, in one box
<khatsung>, in one, and <pan>, from, written as one word after a noun: from within one, as {innkuan khatsungpan}, from one family
<khat>, one, with the distributive ending {-ta}: one for each, one at a time
one person alone, without company; {khattang kisa} is feel lonely
<khat> and <tawh> written as one word, after a noun: with a, with one, by means of one
<khat> with plural {-te}, in {pawl khatte} and {kim khatte}, some people, some of them
<khat> with plural {-te} at the end of a number that counts a group, as {za khatte}, the hundred, and {sawm-le-khatte}, the eleven
<khat>, one, with <teh>, here a spoken form of <ciangin>, written as one word: at or in one, as {nipi khatteh}, in a week, and {hun khatteh}, at one time, after a time
<khat>, one, and <tek>, each, written as one word: one for each person
<khat>, one, with <thu> and the ending <in>: all at one time; {ni khatthu-in} is in one single day
<khat>, one, with <tuak>, each, written as one word after a noun: one for each of them
<khat>, one, with <tung>, on, written as one word and followed by <ah> or <panin>: on one, as {Motorcycle khattung ah}, on one motorcycle; of a person, against one
<khattung>, on one, with the place marker <ah>, written as one word: on one vehicle, or leaning on one person
<khat>, one, and <tungpan>, from, written as one word and placed after a noun: from a person or from on a thing, as {numei khattungpan}, from a woman
<khat> and <val> written as one word: more than one; after a unit, over one of it, as {Million khatval}, over a million
one time, from <khat>, one, and <vei>, time; with <kik> on the verb it means once more, and at the start of a story it means on one occasion

terms: once or twice/a time or two
definition: <khatvei>, once, and <nihvei>, twice, said together without a linking word: once or twice, a few times only; stands before the verb, often followed by <bek>, only
<khatvei>, once, and <bek>, only, written as one word
<khatvei>, once, and the emphatic <mah>, written as one word: one time, with <ngei> once before and with <kik> or <leuleu> once again
<khatvei>, once, with the ending <na>: the first time something is done
<khatvei>, once, with the distributive <ta>, each, written as one word after a period of time: once in every such period, as in {khakhat in khatveita}, once a month
<khatvei> once, with <vei> repeated: now and then
<khatvei> and <zong> written as one word: even once; with a negative verb, never, not a single time
one of two as against the other; mostly {a khatzaw}, the other one, and {khatzaw zaw}, either one of the two

terms: either one/any one/one or the other
definition: <khat>, one, with <zawkzawk>: one of those named, whichever it is; placed after a list or after <lak>, among
<khatzaw> with <pa> for a man, written as one word: the other of two men, mostly as {adang khatzawpa}
<khatzaw>, the other of two, and the topic marker <pen> written as one word: as for the other one
<khat> and <zawzaw> written as one word: whichever one of two
<khat>, one, with <zong>, even; with {om lo} it means there is not even one
in statements that are not negative: one more of the kind as well, as in {Police Officer khatzong liam}, one police officer was also injured; with <ahihi> it is also one of them
a rope, cord, string or thread of any thickness; {khau dum} is a blue cord and {sihna khau} the cords of death
<khau> and <bang> written as one word: like a cord, a simile of songs and poetic speech for what is drawn out, traced or entangled
<khau>, cord, with <dum>, blue: a blue cord or blue thread
<khau>, rope, with <gui>, vine: a climbing or trailing plant with long stems like cords, also used for tying
hard, firm or strong, not giving way; {lung khauh} and {lungsim khauh} mean stubborn or hard-hearted, and {khauh takin} means firmly or severely
<khauh> written with a capital in a heading, {Itna in Sihna Zahin Khauh}, love is as strong as death
<khauh>, hard, with the ending <in>; after <lung> or <lungsim> it means stubbornly, with a hard heart
<khauh>, strong, with <kik>, again: become strong again
<khauh> and <lua> written as one word: very or too strong, said of wind, an earthquake, fire, a smell or speed
<khauh>, strong, and <mahmah>, very, written as one word: very strong, said of wind, a smell, smoke, an illness or a crackdown
<khauh>, hard, with the ending <na>: the quality of being hard or unyielding; {lungsim khauhna} is stubbornness of heart, and in Philippians 3:6 it stands for zeal
<khauh>, hard, with <pa>, the man; {thu khauhpa} is the harsh, fierce man
<khauh> strong, with <pah>, at once
strong and forceful, or growing so: of wind, fighting, trade, feeling or faith strong and intense, of a rule or a leader firm and strict; built on <khauh>, hard or strong
<khauhpai> with the noun suffix <na>: the being strong or intense of an earthquake, fighting and the like; {khauhpaina mun} is the place where it is strongest
<khauh> strong or stiff, <pen> most, with the plural <te>: the stiffest bows
<khauh>, hard or strong, with <sak>, make: make hard or make strong; {lungsim khauhsak} means harden the heart, and {khut khauhsak} means strengthen the hands
<khauhsak>, harden, with the linking suffix <in>
<khauhsak> harden, with <khak>, happen to; of hardening the heart
<khauhsak> with the noun suffix <na>: the act of making weak hands strong
<khauh>, hard or strict, and <semsem>, more and more, written as one word: firmer or stricter than before, said of security and of faith
noodles made from wheat flour; also instant noodles
<khauh> and <tak> written as one word, usually followed by <in>: firmly, strictly or severely; {khauhtak in thu bawl} is deal severely with a case
<khauh>, hard or firm, with <takin>, like English -ly: strongly, firmly or severely; of the Spirit of God coming on someone, powerfully
act in a hard way toward someone
<khauh> hard, strong, with the plural <te>; {lungsim khauhte} are the stout-hearted
of people compared to oak trees
a rope or cord made of twisted strands, used for tying and binding
<khauhual>, rope, with <pi>, large: a thick rope, such as a cart rope
<khauhual>, rope, with the plural <te>
<khauh> hard or strict, with <zaw> more; with <in> it is used as an adverb, more strictly
a cord hung with a weight to test whether a wall stands upright; {khaukhai sikbawk} is the weighted plumb line
<khau>, rope, and <khattawh>, with a, written as one word: with a rope

terms: tie with a rope/tie a rope to
definition: <khau>, rope, and <khih>, tie, written as one word: fasten a rope to something
<khau>, rope, with <khung>, put across: stretch a rope or tape, to close off a place or to hold on to
dense tangle of bushes or creepers, in which the ram was caught by its horns
string of a musical instrument; {khausai lasakna} is an instrument with strings
<khau>, thread, with <san>, red: a red or scarlet thread
<khausan> with the plural <te>; in a list of costly cloth, where the English has scarlet cloth
coarse cloth; {khautang puan} is a garment of sackcloth, worn in mourning or repentance
<khau> and <tawh> written as one word: with or by means of a rope, cord or cable
<khau>, cord, with the plural <te>: cords, ropes, or in lists of cloth, yarn
a whip made of cords, <khau>; the same verse in the other text has <khautep>
a whip made of cords, <khau>; the same verse in the other text has <khauteep>
loop of cord set on the ground to catch something; <khau> is cord
a length of cord used for measuring
the fibre in food, the stringy part of vegetables and grains that helps digestion; said of what is in food, {an sungah}, where the other sense is a cord
cord such as is used to lead an animal; set beside <khauhualpi>, a thick rope
the feathers of a bird; of the great eagle, {khaveng hoih mahmah}, very fine plumage
form of <khua>, village or town, with {-ua} changed to {-aw}, used as the first part of joined words such as <khawpi> and <khawsak>
look out into the distance in hope of something coming
<khawdak> with <dak> repeated, showing that the looking goes on
work a field to grow crops; {lo khawh} is farm a field and {lo khawh hun} is ploughing time
prepare and work land or plants so that they bear a crop
thrust or throw a spear at an animal or a target, with <tei> or <teipi>, spear; {tei khawh} is also a spear contest; not the {khawh} of working a field
thrust a spear through someone so that he is fixed to the wall or the ground
<khawhcip>, pin with a spear, with <sak>; {hong khawhcipsak in}, let me pin him
<khawh>, throw or thrust something at a person, with the linking suffix <in>; a different word from <khawh>, farm
<khawh>, throw or thrust a spear, with <kha>, reach the mark: hit someone with a thrown spear
<khawh> farm with <kik>, again: work the field again for the next crop; {lo khawhkik hun} is the time to plough again

terms: farm as a tenant/work land for hire
definition: work the land of another man for a share of the crop; {lo khawhlawh} is a tenant farmer and {khawhlawh sak} is let land out to tenants
<khawhlawh>, farm as a tenant, with the causative <sak>: give land to others to farm
<khawhlawhsak>, let land out to tenants, with the linking ending <in>: having let it out
<khawhlawh>, one who works land for its owner, with the plural <te>; said after <lo>, field
<khawh> in the sense spear or stab, with <let>, right through: stab so that the weapon goes through
<khawhlet> pierce through with <zo>, be able
<khawh>, work the soil, with the ending {-na}; {lo khawhna tu} is the tool for tilling a field, a plowshare or hoe
in {ngasa khawhna teipi}, a spear for spearing fish, a harpoon
<khawh> farm with <sa>, already done: what one has grown; {khawhsa tawh biakna}, offering of produce
<khawh>, farm or work the land, with <sak>: make an animal or person work the land, or in Luke 17:7 work the land for someone

terms: field workers/those who work the land for
definition: <khawhsak>, work the land for someone, with the plural <te>; the English has the workers who mowed your fields
<khawhsa>, what one has grown, with the plural <te>
keep and not kill, often as {hing khawi}, keep alive; in Ecclesiastes 3:3 it is the opposite of killing
keep and look after an animal or a person in one's charge: {vasa khawi} is a pet bird, {sila-in khawi} is keep as a slave; in Numbers 6:5 of letting the hair grow long
<khawi> keep, with <kik>, again; {sila-in khawikik}, keep as a slave again
<khawi> rear, <le> and, <vulh> feed: the rearing and feeding of young; the English has blessings of the breast and womb
<khawi>, keep alive, with <lo>, not; {hin’ khawilo}, did not keep alive
<khawi>, keep and rear, with the noun suffix <na>: the rearing of animals, or the place where they are kept; <ganhing khawina> is a place where animals are kept, a zoo or farm
<khawi>, keep or rear, with <pa> marking a man; {tuu khawipa} is a man who raises sheep
<khawi>, keep or rear, with <sa>, already done: an animal that one keeps, livestock or a pet; named beside <neihsa> and <khawhsa>
<khawi>, rear or keep animals, with plural {-te}: animals that are kept; {gan khawite} is livestock and {ui khawite} are house dogs
one marked-off part of something longer or larger, as a stretch of wall, a plot of land or a column of writing

a marked-off area of a country or of the work of a church, with its own leaders, such as a county, a state or a church circuit; {khawk makaite} are the area leaders and {khawk le veng} is area and ward
placed after a measure of length it makes the measure of area: <pi khawk> is a square foot and <tai khawk> a square mile
<khawk>, section, and <khat> written as one word, given by the book as the collective word for firewood, {sing khawkkhat}: one stack or lot of wood
plural of <khawk>, a section or enclosed part; {tuu-khawkte} are sheep pens
named beside <ukpite>, the chiefs, as those who ruled the people harshly under British rule; apparently the headman of a village under the chief
<khawkuk> with the plural <te>
stop what one is doing: pause to rest or stay a while on the way, cease an activity, and after <pan>, from, leave a job or office; {khawl sak} is make stop, suspend, and {khawl phot} is stop for now
stop doing something, for a while or for good; {ki khawlbawl} is be discontinued

terms: stand still/stop completely/come to a standstill
definition: <khawl>, stop or rest, with <cip>, firmly: stop completely and stay still, as the sun and moon in the sky or a work that is halted
noun of <khawlcip>, stop completely: a complete stop, or the place where traffic stands still
<khawlcip>, stop completely, with <sak>, cause: make something stop completely, as trains, a terminal or a business; with <ki> before it, be halted
way of behaving, found in the pair <omdan khawldan>, conduct and manners, beside <omdan>
<khawl>, stay or stop, with <dante>, ways: how people stay and behave in a place, paired with {om dan} as {i om dan i khawldante}, the way we live and conduct ourselves
<khawl> and <ding> written as one word, with <khawl> in the sense stop or rest: to stop, of a vehicle, a piece of work or a habit
see <khawlei-uikai>
first part of {Khawlei-uikai}, the constellation of the Bear, also written as two words
see <khawlei-uikai>
the constellation of the Bear, the Great Bear, named in the book of Job
<khawl>, stop or rest, with <hun>, time: the time when work stops, a break
<khawl> with the ending {-in}: stopping, leaving off, before the next action
<khawl> with <khawm>, together: spend time in one another's company; often paired with <tukhawm>, sit together, as {tukhawm khawlkhawm}
<khawl>, rest, and <khop>, together, written as one word; paired with <tutkhop>, sit together, it means meeting and keeping company with others

<khawl>, rest or stay, and <khopna>, being together, written as one word: a time of staying together; paired with <tutkhop> as {tutkhop khawlkhopna}, a gathering where people sit and spend time together
<khawl> in the sense stop, with <kik> back: stop what one was doing, give up before the goal, or come to a halt
<khawl>, stop or rest, and <lai>, while, written as one word: while at rest or stopped; of a vehicle, parked; of work or school, in the time when it has stopped
<khawl>, stop or rest, with <lo>, not, written as one word: not stop; {khawllo in} is without stopping
<khawl> stop or rest, with <mun> place; {teembaw khawlmun} is a place where ships stop
a place where a bus, boat, taxi or car stops for passengers or is parked, often beside the English words bus or stop; a present-day use beside the resting place and the harbour for ships
<khawlmun>, a place to stop and rest, capitalised in place names: {Khawlmun Nuam}, Fair Havens; {Khimham Khawlmun}, Geruth Kimham
<khawlmun>, a place to stop and rest, with the plural <te>; of ships, a harbour
<khawl>, stop or rest, with the ending <na>: the act of stopping, or a place to stop and rest; {teembaw khawlna mun} is a harbour and {teembaw khawlna sikkawi} is an anchor
<khawl> and <nai> written as one word, followed by <lo>: has not yet stopped
<khawlna>, stopping place, with the plural <te>: places where vehicles or people stop, as {bus khawlnate}, bus stops
<khawl>, stop or rest, with <ni>, day: a day on which work stops, as in {nasep khawlni}; also the day on which something is given up

terms: refuse to stop/be unwilling to stop
definition: <khawl>, here stop or halt, with <nuamlo>, not want, written as one word: not be willing to stop, said of a driver told to halt
<khawl> stop with <pah>, at once
<khawl> stop, with <pak>, for a while or promptly: leave off a quarrel

terms: come to a stop/stop only then
definition: <khawl>, here stop or halt, and <pan>, only then, written as one word: of a vehicle or driver, finally come to a stop

terms: stop for a while/pause/stop for now
definition: <khawl>, here stop or rest, with <phot>, for the time being, written as one word: stop what one is doing for a while
<khawl>, stop or rest, with the suffix <pih>, together with: stop or halt at a place together with someone or taking someone along; {ki khawlpih} is keep company with each other
make someone or something stop or rest; <khawl> with <sak>, cause
put an end to a person's work, for good or for a time: after <nasep>, work, or in the passive {ki khawlsak}, be dismissed or suspended from a job

terms: will stop/will be stopped/will be dismissed
definition: <khawlsak>, stop, and <ding> written as one word: will stop or is to be stopped; of work, will be dismissed or laid off
<khawlsak>, make stop or rest, with the linking suffix <in>
<khawlsak>, stop or suspend, with <lo>, not, written as one word: not bring a vehicle to a stop, or not put an end to someone's work
<khawlsak> make stop, with the noun suffix <na>; {teembaw khawlsakna sikkawipi}, the iron hook for stopping a ship, is an anchor

the stopping of a person from his work or office, or the ending of a right, after <nasep> work or <pan> from: {nasep khawlsakna} is dismissal or suspension from a job, and {nasep khawlsakna lai} is the letter that tells it
<khawlsak>, stop or suspend, and <pah>, at once, written as one word: bring a vehicle to a stop right away, or suspend someone from work immediately

terms: suspend/stop for the time being/halt for now
definition: <khawlsak>, make stop, and <phot>, for the time being, written as one word: suspend a person from work or a service from running until a matter is settled; mostly with <ki>, be suspended
<khawlsak>, make stop, and <sawm>, intend or try, written as one word: try to stop a vehicle or a person, said of police and guards

terms: be able to stop/manage to stop
definition: <khawlsak>, make stop, with <thei>, be able, written as one word: manage to bring a vehicle, a person or an act to a stop
<khawl>, stop, with the ending {-san}, leaving behind: stop doing something and leave it, give up or call off what was done or planned
<khawlsan>, stop, with the noun suffix {-na}: the stopping of something; {kikaptuahna khawlsanna} is a ceasefire

terms: not intend to stop/not try to stop
definition: <khawl>, stop, and <sawmlo> written as one word
<khawl>, here stop or rest, and <ta.2> written as one word: has stopped, has given up a work or an office; {apanmun pan khawlta} is has stepped down from his post
<khawlta> and <ding> written as one word: is now going to stop, said of leaving a post or a job; {nasep khawltading} is will retire from work

terms: be able to stop/manage to stop
definition: <khawl>, stop or rest, and <thei>, able, written as one word: be able to stop, come to a stop
<khawl>, stop, with <theilo>, unable, written as one word: of a train, a plane or a craving, be unable to stop

terms: only then stop/finally come to a stop
definition: <khawl>, stop, and <theipan>, only then can, written as one word: only at that point was it able to stop
<khawl>, here stop, with <tuanlo>, not even so, written as one word: not stop in spite of it, carry on regardless
come to a sudden stop, said of a vehicle or of the heart; {lungtang khawlvat-natna} is cardiac arrest
<khawl>, stop or rest, with <zia>, way, written as one word; found in pairs such as {tut leh khawlzia} and {om zia khawlzia}, the way a person sits and stays, his or her bearing and manner of living
after a verb, doing the action together with others or jointly
bring things together into one place or into the hand, as tickets: {ticket te a khawm hi} is he collects the tickets
bring people or things together into one place; the book gives it as the opposite of <thehthang>, scatter
<khawm> with the linking <a>; {ding khawma om}, be standing together with
<khawm> and <ding> written as one word after a verb: will do it together, are to do it jointly
<khawm>, gather, with the linking suffix <in>: gathering people or things together before a following action
<khawm>, together, with the ending <in>, after another verb: doing it together with others
<khawm>, bring together, said twice: keep gathering; set against <kithehthangsak>, scatter
<khawm>, together, said twice after a verb: do the thing together with others, usually as a habit, as {ne khawmkhawm}, eat together, and {om khawmkhawm}, live together
<khawm> gather with <kik>, again or back
<khawmkik> with the linking suffix <in>
<khawm>, together, and <lo>, not, written as one word after a verb: not doing it together
the ornamental top of a pillar; apparently another spelling of <khuamluzepna>, which stands in the same verse
<khawm>, together, with the noun suffix <na>, after a verb: the doing of something together, as {kipawl khawmna}, fellowship, and {gamtat khawmna}, acting together
<khawmna>, doing together, with the plural <te>; {kikhop khawmnate} are the meetings together
<khawm>, together, and the hortative <ni>, let us, written as one word after a verb: let us do it together, as {thu ngetsak khawmni}, let us pray for them together
<khawm> together with <pa>, the man: after a verb, the man who does it together with someone; {nasem khawmpa} is a fellow worker
<khawm> and <pah> written as one word after a verb: doing it together and straight away, at the same time
<khawm>, together, with the augmentative <pi>: a large general meeting of an organisation, a church body or of nations, such as an annual conference

terms: attend a conference/take part in a convention
definition: <khawmpi>, conference, and <kah.3>, attend, not climb: be present at a conference or convention as a participant; before <mi> it names those who attend
<khawm>, together, with <pih>, with someone: after a verb, do it together with someone or share in it; after a noun, a fellow, as in {galkap khawmpih} fellow soldier
<khawmpih>, do together with someone, with <pa>, the man: the man with whom one does it, as the one who dips in the dish with me
<khawmpih>, do together with someone, with the plural <te>: the people with whom one does it; {a tut khawmpihte}, those who sat at table with him, his guests
<khawmpi>, conference, with the plural <te>
<khawm>, together, with <sa>, already done; {lum khawmsa} is having lain together with someone
<khawm>, together, with the causative <sak>: make people or things come together, collect or assemble them
placed after a verb: cause or allow someone to do the action together with others
<khawmsa>, already together, with the plural <te>; {a gawm khawmsate} are those who have been joined together
<khawm>, together, with plural {-te}, placed after a verb: the people who do the action together, as {an ne khawmte}, those eating together
<khawm>, together, and <thei>, able, written as one word after a verb: can do it together; {om khawmthei} is can be together
given by the book as another word for <kheng> in the saying of the monkey that does not see its own: apparently the bare rump of a monkey
placed after a number, a time or an item to make it approximate
ask a high price for goods

terms: and the like/or some such/things like
definition: <khawng>, or so, and <peuh>, any: placed after a noun, a list or a quoted word, it makes it one loose example among others, things like that, or some such, often with a slighting tone
<khawng>, or so, and the like, with <a>: placed after a place, a time or an action to mean in, at or from such a place or about such a time, and things of that kind
<khawng>, thereabouts, with the place marker {-ah}: at or on such places, here and there on, as {inn tung khawngah}, up on the houses
sad and alone like one bereaved
<khawng>, about, and <bek>, only, written as one word after a number or amount: only about that much
<khawng> and <ciangin> written as one word: placed after a time or an amount of time, at about that time, when about that much time has passed
said of water, {tui khawnggawp}: rise and flood with great damage; the first part seems to be a form of <khang>, rise, with <gawp>
<khawng>, approximately, with <in>, placed after a time: at about that time
<khawng>, or so, with the emphatic <mah>, written as one word after a number, a place or a thing: about that, or some such
<khawng> and <pan> written as one word, often followed by <in>: from such places as the one named, or from about the time or amount named

terms: things like/as for the likes of
definition: <khawng>, and the like or thereabouts, with the topic marker <pen> written as one word: marks a loosely named thing or time as the subject
<khawng> and <peuh> written as one word, placed after a noun or a list: that sort of thing, or anything like it

terms: with something like/with or the like/with about
definition: <khawng>, or so, and <tawh>, with, written as one word after a noun or number: with such a thing or something like it, with about that many
<khawng> placed after each item of a list of examples, with the plural <te> after the last item

terms: and the like also/things like that too
definition: <khawng>, or so, and <zong>, also, written as one word after a noun or phrase: such things as this too
given or done without payment; mostly as {a khawnkhong}, free, and {a khawnkhong in}, for free, freely
form of <khawm>, together, used after a verb when another word follows: {tuang khawp} is ride together and {kikaih khawp} is be gathered together
a flash of lightning; {khawphelep bangin tang} is shine like lightning
form of <khuasa>, live one's life, with <khaw> for <khua>, used before <zia>, manner: {khawsak zia} is the way of life
village in the Tonzang area of Chin State, the seat of the chief Hau Cin Khup before Tonzang; also written <Khuavong>
an administrative district of Myanmar, the unit between the township and the state
the wings in motion; {khazap ging} is the sound of beating wings
<khazap>, wing, with the noun suffix <na>: the moving of the wings and its sound
<kha>, bitter, and <zaw>, more, written as one word: more bitter; after a verb the same spelling is the particle <kha> with <zaw>, more likely to happen
placed after a verb, <kha>, happen to, with <zel>, again or in turn: might also come to do
<kha>, happen to, with <zenzen>, by chance; with <leh>, if it should ever happen that
the Christ, the Messiah, title of Jesus as the one anointed by God
<Khazih>, Christ, and <sungah>, inside: in Christ; set alone on a line with a comma and followed by the name of the writer, it is the closing formula of a letter or article by a Christian writer
the foot or the whole leg of a person or an animal; {khe li} is four legs, and the leg of a table is also {khe}
form of the verb <khia>, with {-ia} changed to {-e}, used before <zo> and a negative: {khe zo kei ning} is I cannot bring it down
<khe>, foot, with <bai>, lame, and the plural <te>
<khe>, foot or leg, with <bai>, lame: unable to walk properly; also a lame foot or a lame person
<khebai> lame with <pa>, which marks a man
<khebai>, lame, with the plural <te>
river or canal in Babylonia beside which Ezekiel lived among the exiles and saw his visions
