<lenkip>, hold firmly, and <zolo>, cannot: said of a driver who cannot keep hold of the vehicle, lose control of it; the vehicle stands before the pair, often with <hoihtak>, and the accident follows
<lenkip>, hold firmly, with the linking ending <in>
<lenkip>, hold firmly, with <te>, those who

terms: be able to hold firmly/manage to catch
definition: <lenkip> and <thei> written as one word: be able to hold fast, to keep a firm grip, or to seize and hold a person
a word of songs and poems for youth, the time of being young, and for the young; one writer explains it as <khangno>, the young men and young women
placed after a verb: do only that and nothing more, without care or effort, as in {om lenlan}, just stay there; often said in reproach
<len> hold, doubled for a continued action
<len>, hold or take, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not hold or handle a thing, and of a phone, not answer
<leeng>, fly, with the noun suffix <na>: flying, a flight; {vanleng lenna} is the flight of an aircraft
the place where someone stays or moves about, often in songs: {ka lenna} is the place where I am staying
a scenic place in the land of Kaptel village in the Tedim area of Chin State, mostly written {Lennupa}; the Falam side calls it Buannel and the boundary there is disputed
<len> hold with <pa>, the man who holds; {heina lenpa}, the man who holds the rudder, the pilot or helmsman
of the wind, carry a ship along with it
<len.2>, fly, with {-pih}, together with: of a bird, a spirit or an aircraft, fly carrying someone or flying beside him; not the wind driving a ship
<lenpih>, carry along, with <to> upward and the ending <in>: carrying up into the air

terms: cause to be carried off/make fly
definition: with <huih>, wind: let the wind carry someone away; apparently <leng> fly with <sak> cause
<len>, hold, with <sak>, cause: make or let someone hold a thing, and so give someone a task or an area to look after, as in {transportation lam lensak}; not the {lensak} of making something fly
the Christian season of fasting before Easter; {Lent hun} is the time of Lent
a village or place in the Zomi hills, named as the end of a motor road from Laaitui
a village and ridge in the Tedim area of Chin State, on a road route toward the India border
name of a Zomi clan, written before <beh>
<len>, the form of <leng>, fly, with <theih>, be able, written as one word; {lentheih nading} is so that one can fly
placed after a word of swelling or hollowness, of a surface covered with many small bumps or pits: {pual leplap}, swollen in bumps
placed after a verb, describes a quick movement to and fro or a flickering: {khuadak leplep} is look about with darting eyes, and {phe leplep} is flicker, glint
noun of {lep}, try out and put right: a rehearsal, as {la lepna}, song practice, and the fitting or adjusting of a thing so that it suits
put right a quarrel or a matter that is at odds, bring two sides or two things into agreement
<leptuah>, settle or reconcile, with the noun suffix {-na}: the settling of a dispute between two sides
a woman who is attracted to women; mostly written with a capital letter and often added to explain {numei leh numei}
city in the far north taken by the tribe of Dan and renamed Dan, also called Laish
something learned from an event or from experience; {lesson la} is learn a lesson
English plural of <lesson>: things learned from an event, or classes in a skill
of water, rise and spill over
form of <len>, hold, used in dependent clauses
placed after a verb of stabbing or shooting: so that the weapon passes through the body
turn a text into another language, often with <kik> or with the language and <tawh>: {Zolai tawh let} is translate into Zolai; not {let} of water overflowing and not hold

terms: hold fast/take firm hold of/grasp tightly
definition: <let>, form of <len> hold, with <cip> tightly
placed after a verb: if one does so, should one do so; also used in wishes and polite requests
<lee>, apparently turn over or translate, in the form used before a suffix, with <huai>, worthy of: worth translating
people descended from Dedan, a grandson of Abraham and Keturah
<let> with the linking ending <in>, after a verb of stabbing, so as to go through, {sun letin}, {dawt letin}, run through
after <dim>, full, so full that it runs over
accept or take in what is handed over, such as money or a guest
<let> overflow with <khia>, out: of water rising over its banks
put a text into another language, after the name of the language with <tawh> or <ah>, as {Zolai tawh letkhia}, translate into Zolai; the other sense is of water spilling over
of the wind carrying something off; {huih letkhiat ansi} is chaff the wind blows away
form of <letkhia.2>, translate: put a text or the Bible into another language, after the translator or with <pan>, from a language, and <in>, into it; not the wind blowing a thing away
of the wind, carry clouds off so that they are gone; <mang> is away, lost
the turning of a text into another language, in {Lai Siangtho letkhiatna}, Bible translation
<letkhiat>, blow away, with the causative <sak>: of wind carrying off blossoms
<let>, here turn over, and <kik>, back, written as one word: put a text from another language into Zolai
<let>, form of <len> hold, with <kip> firm
<let>, hold, and <kop>, pair, written as one word: hold two things at once, keep both together
of wind: carry something off out of sight; {huih letmang}, blown away by the wind
a small unit of length in the 1932 text, which gives cubits as <pi> feet and {letmat}; {letmat kua}, nine, stands for a span and {pi nih le letmat thum} for a cubit and a half
a name signed by hand on a document; <letmat thuh> is to sign and {thukimna letmat thuh} is to sign an agreement; not the measure of length
a ticket for a journey, after the word for the vehicle; {vanleng letmat} is an air ticket and {meileng letmat} is a train ticket
<letmat>, signature, a Burmese loan, and <thuh>, press on: sign a letter, a form, an order or an agreement; what is signed stands before it
a ring worn on the hand and used to stamp a seal or signature
<let>, form of <len> hold, with the noun suffix <na>; {kumpi aana a letna}, his hold on the royal power
<let> in the sense of turn into another language, with the noun suffix <na>: the work of translating, after <Laisiangtho>, the Bible, or <kampau>, speech; no holding with the hand is meant
a village in Kalay Township in Sagaing Region of Myanmar
<let>, a form of <len>, hold, with <sak>: take hold of something of another person, such as the hand, or seize a thing from someone
apparently the handle of a plow, the part that is held, in {lokhawhna leeng letsan len}, hold the plow

terms: try to hold back/try to stop
definition: <let>, hold back, with <sawm>, intend: try to hold someone back from what he is about to do
something given to honor or please a person; {letsong pia} is give a gift
<letsong>, gift, with the ending <in>: given or sent as a gift
plural of <letsong>; {apsa letsongte} are things dedicated to God
<lee>, apparently turn over or translate, in the form used before a suffix, with <suah>, bring out or become: bring about or carry through what <lee> names; the page lists the form without a meaning
a carpenter, a man who builds with wood, and also his trade; named together with {pazaan} or {payan}, mason
plural of <lettama>, a carpenter or builder; in the verses the men who build and repair a ship
the printed heading of the paper on which an organisation writes its letters, with its name and logo
join a man and a woman in marriage, perform a wedding; the writers gloss it with English marriage and with <kitengsak>
<let>, rise and overflow, with <to>, up: of flood water, rise up as far as a place; also said of a road that comes up to a place
<lee>, apparently turn over or translate, in the form used before a suffix, with <tuak>, be fitting: fit to be translated
a people descended from Dedan, grandson of Abraham and Keturah
<let> and <zawh> written as one word: manage to translate; one article has the same spelling for being able to hold on to rule, which is another sense of <let>
written twice after a verb, {leu leu}, which is <leuleu> written as two words: again, in turn
<le>, if, the plural <uh> and the ending <cin> written as one word: if you, said to more than one person
<le>, if, and the plural marker <uh> written as one word: if you or they, of several people; often followed by <cin>; at the end of a sentence, if only they would
descriptive word placed after a verb of shaking such as <kising>, said of soft flesh that wobbles to and fro
of skin, a cover or roofing sheets, come away from what it is fixed to; mostly as {ki leukhia}
after <ki>: of roofing sheets, shutters or the outside of a building, be torn or peeled off violently by a storm or a blast; the last part is <gawp>, severely
descriptive word placed after a verb: lying or left there limp and still, said of a body lying on the ground, a part cut off or a vehicle overturned
placed after a verb: once more, another time
placed after a verb: likewise, in turn, as another in a series has already done
<leuleu> and <ding> written as one word after a verb: the action will happen once more, or in its turn
a people descended from Dedan, grandson of Abraham and Keturah
a level in an order of ranks or grades, as of government, of an organisation or of study; mostly after the word that names it, as in {State level}
third son of Jacob and Leah and ancestor of the tribe of Levi, the tribe set apart for the service of the sanctuary; also the tax collector whom Jesus called, and two ancestors of Jesus
the members of the tribe of Levi, who served at the tabernacle and the temple and assisted the priests
a Zomi village, listed with villages of the Tedim and Tonzang area of Chin State; written after the name of a person to show the home village
<le>, if, and <zong>, also, written as one word after the verb of a clause: even if, even though
the number four; it follows the noun it counts, and {sawm-le-li} is fourteen
<li>, four, with the ending <in>: into four, as in {nam li-in kikhen}, be divided into four kinds
an unmarried young woman; the same word is written as the title <Lia> before a name, and the book uses it where English says she
a girl or unmarried young woman, the female counterpart of <taang>; the grammar lessons use {lia} where English has she, and {lia'} before a noun is her
third person singular pronoun for a female person, as the book sets it beside <taang>, he, and <amah>, it; {lia'} is her and <lia a> is hers
an unmarried young woman, named together with <taang>, young man, in the call {lia leh taang te aw}
poetic word for <numei> or <nungak>, used in songs
title written before the name of a girl or an unmarried young woman, as <Tg> is written before the name of a young man
third person singular for a female; the book says that the forefathers sang it in songs and teaches it in place of <amah> where English has she, beside <Taang> for he
<lia>, she, with <a>, the thing owned: hers, said after the thing spoken of
<lia>, the girl, with the possessive <a>: what belongs to her, standing in place of the noun; the lesson form for English hers
<Lia> with the possessive apostrophe and <nik>, skirt: stands for {Lia ii nik}; the word is the title of a girl and may here be a girl's name
come between something and the light, heat or sight, so as to shade, shield or hide it
form of <liak>, lick, used before <bangin>; said of an animal that licks or laps something up
at a wedding, stand beside the bride or the groom as attendant; said after <mo>, <monu> or <mopa>, and distinct from covering or licking
<liah>, cover, hide, with <ah>, at; {mual liahah}, at the hidden or sheltered side of the hill, where the NIV has mountain ravine
<liah> cover with <cip>, tightly, completely; in the verse, of darkness over the eyelids
<liah>, lick, and <ding> written as one word: if or when a thing is to be licked
<liah>, cover, and <ding> written as one word: what is to be covered over in a text, said together with <phiatding>, to be erased
<liah> cover with the ending <in>
<liah>, cover, shade, with <khak>, reach, happen to touch: of a shadow falling on someone
<liah> lick, doubled for a repeated action
<liah>, cover, with the noun suffix <na>: a covering that shades or protects; {liahna puan} is a veil
<liah> cover with the causative <sak>: make a cloud hide the sun
in the verse, of others using up all that a man owns; apparently <liah> lick with <tum>, all up, and <sak>
placed after a verb: to a small degree, by a narrow margin; {nungta liai-liai} is barely alive
placed after a verb: barely, only just, with difficulty; with <suakta>, escape, it means get away with one's life and nothing more
after <khawm>, together, and after verbs of what a group does: pictures many acting closely together, one with another, with no thought of difficulty; {sem khawm liailiai} is working all together
<liailiai>, all together, with the plural <te>, after a verb with <khawm> or of sharing: people who always do it together, as {a nekhawm liailiaite}, those who eat together
take up with the tongue, as a dog licks a sore or laps water
<liak> lick with the ending <in>
<liak>, lick, with <tum>, completely, eat or drink up until nothing is left

terms: be in an uproar/be greatly stirred
definition: in {luum lialua}, of a whole town astir with noise and excitement; perhaps <lia> with <lua>, exceedingly
in {gamlum lialuanate}, the loud commotion made on the hills; <lialua> with the noun suffix <na> and plural <te>
a wounded state; {a liam} is one who is wounded, and {a liam a bai} are the wounded and the maimed
be hurt or wounded in the body; {liam sak} is wound someone
<liam>, be injured, and <ding> written as one word; after a number of people in a report: that many are said or expected to be injured
<liam>, be wounded, with <gawp>, severely
<liamgawp>, be badly wounded, with the noun suffix <na>: an injury, mostly in {bangmah liamgawpna omlo}, without any injury
<liam> and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word: was injured
<liam> with the linking ending <in>, being wounded and
<liam>, be wounded, with <lawh>, as a result: be hurt by what one tries to do
<liamlawh>, get hurt as a result, with <gawp>, severely, written as one word: be injured, often many people at once, in an accident or attack
placed after a verb: the thing does happen, but only just, with nothing to spare; {suakta liamliam} is escape narrowly
<liam>, be injured, with <lo>, not, written as one word; {bangmah liamlo} is not hurt at all
<liam>, be injured, and <luatna>, great degree, written as one word: being badly hurt; mostly with <omlo>, no serious injury
a wound or sore on the body; {liamma dam} is a wound heals
plural of <liamma>, wound
<liam>, be wounded, with the noun suffix <na>: a wound or injury

<liamna>, wound, and <baina>, harm, said as a pair: injury and bodily harm of any kind, as after an accident or an attack; mostly with <om>, there is, or <ngah>, receive, and often denied, {liamna baina om lo}, nobody was hurt
<liamna>, a wound, and <ngah>, get: receive an injury, be wounded in fighting or in an accident; stands after the person or the number of persons hurt, and reports set it beside <si>, die
<liamna>, injury, and <tuak> in the sense meet with: suffer an injury, the usual wording of news reports for the injured, who stand before it with <in>; {liamna tuak mi} is an injured person
plural of <liamna>, wound
be wounded severely; said of the injured in accidents and attacks
<liam>, be wounded, with <sa>, already: in a wounded state
<liam>, be wounded, with the causative <sak>: wound or injure someone
text: an injury to living tissue caused by a cut, blow, or other impact, typically one in which the skin is cut or broken

definition: <liamsak> wound with <gawp>, severely
<liamsak> wound with the linking ending <in>
<liamsak>, injure, and <kha>, happen to, written as one word: injure someone or a part of the body, also without meaning to
<liamsak>, wound, with the noun suffix <na>: the wounding of someone; {liamsakna mun} is the place where someone was wounded and {liamsakna mate} are the wounds inflicted
<liamsak>, wound, with <sa>, already done: {na liamsaksa mi}, the one you have wounded

<liam>, here go out of sight, with <san>, leaving others behind; in {mual hong liamsan}, has gone beyond the hill and left us, a respectful way of saying that someone has died, see <mualliam> and <liamsanta>
<liam>, here go out of sight, with <san>, here leaving others behind, and <ta>, now; in {mual liamsanta}, has gone beyond the hill and left us, a respectful way of saying that someone has died
cause a wound or injury to someone
those who are wounded, <liam> with plural {-te} used as a noun
<liam.2>, be injured, and <tek>, each, written as one word: every one of those named is injured
big in size
great in power, rank or worth
chief or leading among others of its kind, as a leading city or a senior priest
<lian>, exactly, with a following <a>, placed after the word it stresses: {ahi bang liana} is exactly as it is; the same spelling is also part of personal names
<lian> great with <ah>, in or at; {za lianah}, in a great office, where the NIV has a trust committed to someone
<lian>, exactly, with <bek>, only, written as one word, after a noun: that very thing and nothing else
<lian>, great, with <bel>, most: the greatest or most important of all
<lianbel> greatest with the plural <te>

terms: just about to/on the point of
definition: placed after a verb, formed with <ding>, will: on the very point of doing or suffering something; {alenkhia lianding} is just about to take off
shoulder of a person, or the shoulder cut of an animal
placed after a verb to show how far something goes, often with surprise: even, to the point of

terms: to the point of/so much that
definition: <liang>, even, with the linking <a>, written as one word after a verb or clause: to the point of, so far that; {ihmu lo lianga} is to the point of not sleeping
<liang>, even, so much as, with the linking <aa>, written as one word: so much that, to the extent of
<liang>, shoulder, and <ah> written as one word: on the shoulder
<liang>, shoulder, with <bit>, whole: an entire shoulder of the slaughtered animal, the share of the householder when the family that takes a bride shares out meat

terms: to the point of/so much as to
definition: <liang.2>, even, and <ding> written as one word, mostly as {liangding in} after a verb: so far as to do it; {sihlawh liangding} is so as to die of it

terms: to the point of/so much as to
definition: <liangding> and <in> written as one word after a verb: so badly or so far as to, as in {sihlawh liangdingin}, to the point of dying of it
<liang> even, to the point of, and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word at the end of a sentence: it went so far as that, said with surprise or emphasis
placed after a verb phrase to show how far a thing goes: so much that; {ihmu lo liangin}, even going without sleep
<liang> shoulder with <in>; {a phei a liangin}, by leg and shoulder, means limb by limb
in the verses mostly {liangkaih puan}, the shoulder pieces of the priestly ephod
<liangkaih> with the noun suffix <na>; {liangkaihna puan}, the shoulder pieces of the priestly ephod
<liang>, shoulder, and <khat>, one, written as one word: one shoulder of a slaughtered animal as a share of meat
the shoulder of a person, on which loads are carried
of land, the shoulder of a hill or ridge

<liangko>, shoulder, and <kikim>, equal: with shoulders level, an idiom for equality of rank and rights between peoples or between women and men; with <in>, <zahin> or <takaa> after it, on an equal footing
<liangko>, shoulder, and <tungah>, upon: after a person or group, said of a duty, burden or authority that rests on them, with <kisuan> or <tung>, be laid on or fall on
<liangko> shoulder, with the plural <te>
<liang>, shoulder, with <sa>, meat: the meat of the shoulder of a slaughtered animal
<liang>, even, to the point of, and the plural marker <uh> written as one word after a verb whose subject is more than one
poor and helpless; a word of songs and poetic speech
<liangvai>, poor and helpless, with the noun ending {-na}: the state of being poor and helpless, mostly in the pair {gentheih liangvaihna}, suffering and destitution
the beam of a house on which the ceiling beams or rafters rest; apparently <liang>, shoulder, with <zawl>, pole
<lian> with the linking ending <in>, used when another verb follows; {a lianin kikoih} means be exalted, {lungsim lianin} means with a proud heart
<lian> in its meaning exact, with the linking ending <in>: exactly or precisely, after a word of time or manner and not about size; <tu lianin> is right now and {bang lianin} is exactly as
<lian>, great, and <khat>, one, written as one word after a noun: one that is great or important, as in {tavuan liankhat}, a major duty
<lian> great, big, with <kik> again
<lian>, here exactly, with <laitak>, while, written as one word and placed after a verb: at the exact moment when the action happens
<lian>, here just or exactly, and <leh>, when, written as one word after a verb: at the very moment that the action happens
placed after a verb: without missing, every time; of archers who kill whenever they shoot
after <bang>, like, or a word of time: exactly so, to the letter, on the dot; {a kammal bang lianlian} is exactly as the words say, and {a hun lianlian in} is exactly on time
<lianlian> and <in> written as one word: exactly so, to the letter
<lian> and <lo>, not, written as one word after a verb: not exactly, not quite, not really so; <lian> is here the word that stresses exactness, not the word for large
<lian> and <loh>, not, written as one word after a verb: the form of <lianlo> used before <hangin> and before a noun, not exactly, not really so
<lian> great with <lua>, too much; of a burden, too heavy
<lian>, large, and <mahmah>, very, written as one word and placed after the noun: very big, or of a matter or injury very serious
placed after a verb and before <hi>: <lian>, here exactly, with <mawk>, marks what happened or was said as striking, just so and not otherwise
placed after a verb or phrase for emphasis: exactly so, right then; a lengthened spelling of the emphatic adverb usually written with one n, compare <lianlian>
written as one word before <lo> or <loh>, for {lian nai lo}, with <nai>, yet: not yet really so
<lian> great with <pa> marking a male person; after a noun it means the great or the chief, as in {kumpi lianpa} the great king and {siampi lianpa} the high priest
<lianpa> written with a capital in titles: {Vang Lianpa} the Great Power, {Tuucing Lianpa} the great Shepherd
<lian>, here exactly, as in <lianlian>, with <pan>, from, written as one word: from that very point or moment
<lian>, great, with <pen>, most: the greatest, the highest in rank or the most important; <siampi lianpen> is the high priest
<lian> great with <pen> most, written with a capital in titles: {A Lianpen Pasian}, the Most High God, and {Siampi Lianpen}, the High Priest
<lianpen> greatest with the ending <in>, used with verbs of making and thinking
<lianpen> greatest, with <pa> marking a man: the man highest in rank, placed after a title, as {siampi lianpenpa}, chief priest

terms: the very largest/the very greatest/biggest of all
definition: <lian>, large or great, and <penpen>, the very most, written as one word
<lianpen> with plural <te>: the highest in rank or the biggest of their kind
<lianpen> greatest with plural <te>; {Siampi Lianpente} are the high priests
<lian> with the strengthening ending <pi>; {lam lianpi} is a highway and {awging lianpi} a loud voice
<lianpi>, great, and <khat>, one, written as one word after a noun: a big one, a great one
<lianpi> great with the last part doubled, said of several great things or to stress the greatness; placed after the noun
plural form of <lianpipi>, said of several very large things; {inn lianpipite}, great houses, stands for palaces and fortresses
<lianpi>, great, with the strengthening <tak>, written as one word; also as an adverb, greatly
<lianpi>, great, and <tawh>, with, written as one word after a noun: {dahpihna lianpitawh}, with deep sympathy, closes a message of condolence, and {zahtakna lianpitawh} is with great respect
<lianpi> with plural {-te}, used after a noun for several great things; {na lianpite}, great things
<lian> great with <sa>, consider, feel to be, and the ending <in>
<lian> great with the causative <sak>
<liansak>, make great, with the linking ending <in>

terms: one who makes great/one who makes grow
definition: <liansak> make great with <pa>, the male one who does it; in the verse, he who makes the low tree grow tall
<liansak> make great, exalt, with <zo> marking a completed action
form of <lian> after a plural noun; {siampi liante} is the chief priests
word of songs and elevated speech for a young woman or a beloved woman, as in {angkawi lianu}

terms: use lavishly/do on a grand scale
definition: <lian>, great, and <zat>, use, written as one word: do or spend on a grand scale because one is rich
<lian>, big, with <zaw>, more: bigger in size or number
<lian>, great, with <zaw>, more: greater in power, rank or worth; what it is compared with takes <sangin>, than
<lianzaw> greater with the ending <in>: as greater, in a higher place than others
<lianzaw> greater with the causative <sak>
<lianzaw> greater with <te>, those who
a province in the north-east of China; also the name of a Chinese aircraft carrier
be covered or screened off, as a place the sun does not reach: {ni liap na mun} is a shaded place
poetic word for a young unmarried woman in her bloom, from <lia>, maiden, and <paal>, bloom
placed after a verb: in an uneven, untidy or jumbled way, as of things heaped or fastened together carelessly
<liap>, be shaded, with the noun suffix <na>: the being shaded from the sun; {ni a liapna mun} is a place where the sun does not reach
<liap>, be hidden from view, and a following word for leaving behind: with <mual>, hill, or <hanmual>, cemetery, a gentle way of saying that someone has died
form of <lian> great, big, used before <hangin>, <ciangin>, <nading> and <na>; {migilote a liat ciangin}, when the wicked rise to power
<liat>, become big, and <khit>, after, written as one word: {i liatkhit ciangin} is when we have grown up
<liat> be great with <luat> too much, the forms used before <hang> and <hangin>: so great, so much
<liatluat> be very great with the noun suffix <na>; {na mawhna a liatluatna}, the greatness of your sin
<liat>, be great, with the noun suffix <na>: greatness or majesty; also the great extent of something, as of wickedness
<liatna> greatness, with the plural <te>
<liatna>, greatness, with <teng>, all: all the greatness or splendour of something
<liat>, be great, with the causative <sak>: make someone great or honoured
<liatsak>, make great, with the noun suffix <na>: the act of making someone or something great

terms: be able to increase/be able to become great
definition: <liat> be great with <theih> be able, used before <nadingin>: so that it may become great
form of <lianzaw>, greater, used before {mah bangin}
<liatzawk>, be greater, with the noun suffix <na>: the fact that one is greater than others
pay what is owed or imposed, such as a fine, a debt or a tax
<liau> pay with the causative <sak>: make someone pay a sum as a penalty
<liausak>, make pay a fine, and <ding>, will, written as one word; with <ki> before it, will be fined

terms: can be fined/may be made to pay

<nasep>, work, and <khop>, together, written as one word: work together, cooperate; also as a noun, cooperation
<nasep>, work, with <khopna>, doing together: working together, or a body in which people work together

terms: work permit/right to work/permission to work
definition: <nasep>, work, with <khuan.3>, permission: the leave or right to do a job, as given to refugees or held by a person in his post

terms: go to work/set out for work
definition: <nasep>, work, and <kuan>, set out, written as one word: go out to one's work

terms: term of office/working year/year of service
definition: <nasep> and <kum> written as one word: the year or the years for which someone holds an office or does a work
<nasep>, work, and <loh>, not, written as one word: being without work or off duty; {naseploh hunsung} is while off duty
<nasepna> written with a capital at the start of a sentence or in a title; {Solomon’ Nasepna Laibu} is the book of the acts of Solomon
<nasepna>, work, with the place marker <ah>
<nasep> work with the endings <na> and <sa>: the place or thing already worked
plural of <nasepna>: the things someone has done, in the Psalms mostly the mighty works of God
<nasep>, work, and <nei>, have, written as one word: one who has work to give, an employer; also said of people who have a job
<nasep>, work, and <neilo>, not have, written as one word: having no work; also the people who have none
<nasep>, work, and the topic marker <pen> written as one word: the work or job, as the thing spoken about
one who works together with another; <nasep> work with <pih> together with

terms: to be a co-worker/as an employee
definition: <naseppih>, fellow worker, and <ding>, to be, written as one word: for someone to work with, as when an employer calls a worker
plural of <naseppih>, one who works or serves together with another
<nasep> work with <sa>, already done: what one has worked for and produced
<nasep>, work, with <sak>, here doing something on behalf of another; {hong nasepsak}, the work he did for me
<nasep>, work, with the plural <te>: the things done, or the duties of a service
<nasep> work with <teng> all
<nasep> and <thak> written as one word: a new job, newly created work

terms: be able to work/be allowed to work
definition: <nasep> and <theih> written as one word, mostly before <nading>: so as to be able or permitted to work, as with a work permit
<nasep>, work, with <theih>, be able, and the noun suffix <na>: the right to work in a country, or the document that gives it
<nasep>, work, with <theih>, be able, and the noun suffix <na>: what one is able to do in work
<nasep>, work, with <vai>, matter, written as one word: a matter of work, business; {nasepvai tawh} is on business
<nasep>, work, with <za>, title or rank: the name of what a person does for a living, as <siavuanpa>, doctor, and <ngabengpa>, fisherman
<nasep>, work, with <zia>, manner: how work is done, how something works
<nasep>, work, and <zong>, also, written as one word: the work too, jobs as well

city in the state of Tennessee in the United States, home of a Zomi community

very great in a bad or painful way, of famine, sin, grief or punishment; {nasia takin} is severely, bitterly
as an intensifier with no bad meaning, of something done or found on a grand scale: {nasia takin} before a verb is in a big way, and {nasia} before <thupi> is very grand
<nasia>, severe, with <lua>, too much: so severe or terrible, said of a plague

terms: you are skilled/you are good at
definition: <na>, you, and <siam>, skilled, written as one word: you are skilled, you are good at the thing named before it
<nasia>, severe, with <pen>, most: the most severe, the worst of what is suffered
<nasia>, severe, with the causative <sak>: make suffering or trouble more severe
the form of <nasia> severe used before <ma-in> and <lam>; {a nasiat ma-in} is before it grows severe
<nasia> and <tak> written as one word, often followed by <in>: to a very great degree, of bad things and also of effort or celebration
<nasia>, intense, with <takin>, which makes an adverb, written as one word: to a great degree, with great force or effort
<nasiat> and <leh> written as one word: if or when an illness is severe
<nasiat>, intense, with the noun suffix {-na}: how strong or great something is, the thing an adverb of degree shows
<nasia> severe with the comparative <zaw>
used with <lo> not: {nasim lo} is show no respect for, count as nothing; perhaps <na> thing with <sim> count
not the word for respect: <na>, you, written together with <sim>, read, mostly in a request to the reader such as {nasim un}, read it, and {lai nasim}, you read the text
<na>, you, and <simbeh>, read more, written as one word: mostly a request to the reader to read more about a matter, as {nasimbeh in}
<na>, you, and <simnop>, want to read, written as one word: if or what you want to read
<na>, <sim> and <suak> written as one word: you read on, in the request to the reader {nasimsuak vemaw}, do read on
<na> and <sin> written as one word: you learn or study; also you try something
<na> and <suah>, become, written as one word: you become, your becoming
<na>, you, and <suak>, become, written as one word: you become, you turn out to be
<na>, your, and <suan>, descendant, written as one word; mostly in the pair {nasuan nakhak}, your descendants, your children and their children
seen once in {van nasuhte}, the goods you seized from your enemies; apparently <na>, you, with <suh>, seize, and the plural <te>
<na>, your, and <sum>, money, written as one word
<na>, your, and <sungah>, inside, written as one word: within you
<na> and <sunglam> written as one word: the inside of you, your inner being
the verb particle <na> and <sut>, rob, written as one word
form of <na>, be sick or in pain, used before a following word such as <ciangin>, <hun> or <nading>; said of the body, as {ci nat}, be ill, and of the heart

<nat>, be ill, joined by <le> to a rhyming partner that is not used alone in this meaning and is not <sat>, decide: sickness and disease of every kind, said in general and often listed with other troubles such as hunger and hardship. Stands as a noun, the object of <thuak>, suffer, or <tuah>, meet with; also written <nat leh sat>

<nat>, be ill, joined by <leh> to a rhyming partner that is not used alone in this meaning and is not <sat>, decide: sickness and disease of every kind, said in general. Stands as a noun, the subject of <tam>, be many, or the object of <thuak>, suffer; also written <nat le sat>
<na>, your, and <ta>, child, written as one word; {nazi nata} is your wife and children and {natu nata} your grandchildren and children, your descendants
<na>, thing or work, and <tampi>, many, written as one word: many things, a lot of work
<na>, you, and <tang>, abstain from, written as one word; with <un> a command to several people: abstain from it
<na>, your, and <tapa>, son, written as one word
<tapate>, sons, with <na>, your; in the one verse it follows another <na>, so the doubled <na> is probably a misprint
<na> and <tate> written as one word: your children
the noun ending {-na} written apart from its verb and joined to <tawh>: with or by the doing of it; {hanciam natawh} is {hanciamna tawh}, through the effort
<na> and <tawi> written as one word: you hold, what you carry in the hand, as a card or a weapon
<na>, you, and <tawlngasak>, cause to rest, written as one word: you are making them stop work
placed after the word it stresses, marking an extreme or unexpected case; used like <nangawn>
plural of <na>, thing: things, goods or deeds; {a hoih nate} is the good things
plural of <na> in the sense of a part of the body: the parts or members of a body, also said of believers as members of the body of Christ
<na> and <tel> written as one word: you understand; {natel kei leh} is if you do not understand
<nate>, things, and <min>, name, written as one word: the name of a kind of thing
<na> thing with <teng> all; {pasal nateng}, the whole male member
the particle <na> before the verb <teng>, dwell, written as one word: have lived or settled in a place; not {na teng}, all the things
a common illness that passes from person to person, such as influenza
<na>, thing, and <thak>, new, written as one word: something new, a new idea or invention
name of several men, among them the prophet at the court of David and a son of David
disciple of Jesus from Cana in Galilee
official of the king of Judah whose room stood near the entrance to the temple in the days of Josiah
<na.3>, the marker of an earlier action, and <that>, kill, written as one word
<na>, your, and <thau.1>, gun, written as one word: your gun
<na>, you, and <thei>, know, written as one word; {nathei uhhiam} is do you know, to several people
the preverbal <na>, already or as it turned out, and <thei>, know, written as one word: someone other than the hearer knew it already
<na>, you, with <theih>, the form of <thei>, know, written as one word: that you know; {natheih leh} is if you know
<na>, you, and <theihnop>, want to know, written as one word; {natheihnop leh} is if you want to know
<na.3>, the marker of an earlier action, and <thoih>, make an offering to, written as one word
<na>, your, and <thu>, word or matter, written as one word; in prayer and scripture it is the word of God. In {lungdam nathu}, good news, the letters are divided differently: it is {lungdamna thu}
<na>, you, and <thuak>, suffer, written as one word
<thuak>, suffer, with the particle <na> before it, as in <ana>, written as one word: had to bear something, as blows, hardship or blame
<na>, your, and <thute>, matters, written as one word: your matters, what you have to say or settle
devotion to the interests and standing of one's own people or nation; {Zomi Nationalism} is the national feeling of the Zomi
<nat>, <leh> and <sat> written as one word: illness and bodily harm, a case of sickness or injury
sickness, disease or pain of the body; {pul natna} is a plague and {phak natna} a defiling skin disease

<natna>, disease, and <gil>, belly, here the inside or core: a serious or lasting disease that a person carries, such as tuberculosis or cancer; {natna gil neite} are people with an underlying condition
<natna>, disease, and <gilo>, evil: a grave and feared disease such as cancer or an epidemic, not an evil in the moral sense
<natna>, disease, and <kilawhna>, passing from one to another: the spread of a disease among people, or the number of cases of it; often after the name of the disease, as in {Covid-19 natna kilawhna}
<natna>, disease, and <lungno>, worm: the tiny living thing that causes a disease, a germ, virus or bacterium; {natna lungno ngah} is to be infected
<natna>, disease, and <lungnote>, small worms: the microbes that cause disease, such as bacteria and viruses
<natna>, disease, and <ngah>, get: catch a disease, be infected; {natna ngah mi} are the infected persons, the cases counted in a report
<natna>, sickness, with the rhyming <satna>: a paired expression for sickness and bodily suffering of every kind; used like a single noun, often beside <haksatna>, hardship
<natna>, disease, and <nei>, have, written as one word; {natnanei mi} is a person who has a disease
plural form of <natna>; {lungsim natnate} are pains of the heart
the North Atlantic Treaty Organization, a military alliance of North American and European states
<nat>, be ill, with the causative <sak>: make sick, strike with disease
<nat> be ill or in pain with <sak> cause and the noun suffix <na>: a making sick or causing of pain
<nat> sickness with <sia> bad
of a building, a vehicle or a thing: be badly damaged by fire, an accident or an earthquake; mostly as {natsiat mahmah}
also used as a verb, have a fever; often written with an apostrophe

<nattun> fever with <in>: being ill with fever
medicine against <nattun>, fever, here malaria; the articles use it of quinine and chloroquine
seen once of the illness that left Simon's mother-in-law; apparently <nat>, be ill, <tut>, lie down, and the noun suffix <na>
<na>, your, and <tu>, grandchild, written as one word; {natu nata} is your grandchildren and children
<na>, you, and <tu>, sit, written as one word; {Nang, natu in} is you, sit down
<na>, you, and <tuah>, meet with, written as one word: you meet with, said of trouble such as arrest
<na> and <tuak> written as one word: you meet with or go through something, such as trouble or arrest; {natuak leh} is if it happens to you
fluid that comes out of the body; in Leviticus 15 a discharge caused by illness and also an emission of semen
<na>, you, and <tun>, arrive or reach, written as one word: you arrive, you reach, before words such as <ciangin> and <theihna>
<na>, the verb prefix for something that has already happened, written as one word with <tung>, arrive: arrived, got there
<na>, you, and <tung>, arrive, written as one word
<na>, you, and <tuntheih>, be able to reach, written as one word; mostly before <nadingin>, so that you can reach
<na.1> and <tut>, the form of <tu>, sit, written as one word before words such as <ciangin> and <leh>: when or if you sit
<nat> and <veh> written as one word: go to see someone who is ill; also as a noun, a visit to the sick
<nat>, be ill, with <vehna>, visiting: a visit to a sick person, and the money given to the sick or their family on such a visit

<nau>, child, with <bang>, like: in songs and poems said of weeping, as in {naubang kap}, weep like a child
<nau>, child, with <bu>, nest: the womb; {naubu hong}, open the womb, is said of conceiving and of a firstborn
<nau> child with <cil>, first or early; stands beside {ta upa}, eldest child

<nau> child with <cing> look after: a woman who nurses and cares for a baby

<nau>, child, and <dalna>, prevention, written as one word: the prevention of pregnancy, and a device or medicine used for it
<nau>, baby, with <dap>, pad: an absorbent cloth or pad, as worn by a baby
<nau> child with <dom> lift up, hold: one who helps at a birth; followed by <nu>, woman
<naudom>, midwife, with <nu>, woman: a woman who helps at a birth
plural of <naudom>, midwife
<nau>, child, with <gil>, belly: the womb

<nau>, child, with <kem>, look after: a person, usually a woman or girl, who looks after a small child, often as paid work

<nau> and <kepna> written as one word: the minding of small children, and the place where children are minded while the parents work
<nau>, child, with <khak>, shut: stopping the birth of children; named beside <nauhalna>
a hanging or rocking bed for a baby; {nauluai vei} is rock the cradle
<nau>, child, and <milim>, image, written as one word: a toy figure of a person for children to play with
<nau>, child, and <min>, name, written as one word: the name given to a baby, also the name entered for a child on a birth certificate
placed after a verb, of many doing the same thing: all hurrying to do it, eagerly and one after another
<nau>, baby, with <nawi>, milk: the milk a mother gives her baby; {naunawi piak} is to breastfeed
<nau>, baby, with <nei>, have, written as one word: have a baby, become a mother
<nau>, child, and <neih>, have, written as one word; {nauneih theih nading} is in order to be able to have a child
<nau>, child, with <nen>, small: very young children, named after <naupang> or with <nupi>, women
town in the north of Shan State, Myanmar, on the road from Mandalay to Lashio
a baby or very young child, born or unborn; another spelling of <naungek>
plural of <naungeek>, baby
a baby or very young child; {nawi ne naungek} is a baby still at the breast
<naungek>, baby, and <suakthak>, newly born: a baby just born, the term used in news and in registration matters
<naungek>, baby, with the possessive apostrophe and <khe>, foot, written as one word
<naungek>, baby, with the possessive apostrophe and <khete>, feet or legs, written as one word
<naungek>, baby, with <a> written on to it, in {naungeka suak}: be born as a baby
<naungek> with <in>: as a baby, said of being born; also the baby as the one who acts
<naungek>, baby, with <no>, here young or little: a very small baby
<naungek> and the topic marker <pen> written as one word: the baby, as the one spoken about
plural of <naungek>, baby
<nau>, child, with the diminutive <no>: a little child or baby, also the child in the womb; {sangkah nauno} is a young school child
<nau> younger sibling with <nu>, which marks a woman
<nau>, younger sibling, with <pa>, which marks a male: a younger brother
<nau>, child, with <paai>, carry in the womb: be or become pregnant; {numei naupaai} is a pregnant woman
<naupaai>, be pregnant, and <khin>, already, written as one word
<naupaai>, be pregnant, with the plural <te>
be with child, said of a woman, as in {tua numei naupaii hi}; placed before or after <nupi> or before <te> it describes the women who are pregnant, where the other senses name the state itself
<naupaiina> childbearing, pregnancy, with the place marker <ah>
<naupaii>, be with child, with the plural <te>: pregnant women, often as {nupi naupaiite}
<naupaina> childbearing, pregnancy, with the place marker <ah>
<naupai>, pregnant, with the plural <te>: those who are pregnant
form of <naupang>, child, used before another word: {naupan lai} is childhood, the time when one was a child, and {naupan vai} is a childish thing

<naupang>, child, and <kimawlna>, playing or game: what children play at or with, a game, a toy or a place to play; also said of a matter that is not treated seriously, mere child's play
<naupang>, child, with <la>, song: a song or rhyme sung by children; the old ones are sung in three notes
<naupang> child with <in>: in {a numei a naupangin}, women and children alike; also <naupang> followed by the subject marker <in>, written as one word
<naupang>, child, and <khat>, one, written as one word: a child, one child
<naupang>, child, and <lai>, here still, written as one word: be still a child, be very young
<naupang>, child, and <luai>, cradle, written as one word: a hanging seat in which a small child is swung, said of a toddler swing sold by a toy company
<naupang> child with <neu> small
<naupang>, child, with <ngek>, tiny and tender, written as one word: a very young child, a newborn
<naupang> child with <no> small, young
plural of <naupangno>, little child
<naupang>, child, with the female ending {-nu}: a girl child
<naupang> child with <pa>, male: a boy, here a young servant
<naupang>, child, with the topic marker <pen>, written as one word: the child, as the one spoken about
<naupang>, child, and <tawh>, with, written as one word
plural of <naupang>, child
<naupang> and <vai> written as one word: a matter of children, what is childish; {naupangvai takin} is in a childish way
<naupang>, child, and <zong>, also, written as one word: children too, even a child
<nau>, child, with <phiat>, wipe out: the ending of a pregnancy, abortion
<nauphiat>, abortion, with the noun ending {-na}: the act of ending a pregnancy
small island country in the Pacific Ocean
<nau>, younger sibling, with <sawn>, in turn: the brother next in age
<nau> child with <sia> be spoiled: lose a child before birth; also of the woman to whom it happens
<nau>, child, with <suah>, bring out: give birth; also names childbirth, as in {nausuah natna}, birth pains, and {nausuah hun}, the time of delivery
<nausuah> give birth with the noun suffix <na>; {nausuahna tutphah} is the delivery stool
the labour of a woman giving birth; {numei nausuak} is a woman in labour
{nausuak} used as a verb: bear a child, with the mother as subject and often a place before it, as in {lamzikpi tungah nausuak}, give birth on the road
<nau>, baby, and <suakcil>, just born, written as one word; before a noun, having just given birth

terms: be about to give birth/give birth
definition: <nausuak>, childbirth, and <ding>, will, written as one word: about to give birth, in order to give birth; before a noun, for childbirth, as in {nausuakding Operation}
<nausuak>, childbirth, with <lai>, document: the paper that records a birth
<nausuak>, childbirth, with the plural <te>; {numei nausuakte}
{nau suak thak}, a child newly born, written as one word; in the articles it stands in membership fee lists for a child added to a family
{nausuak thak}, newly born child, with the plural <te>, written as one word: children who have just been born
<nausuak>, birth, with <tung> in the sense just now: a child that has just been born

terms: way of giving birth/how the birth happened
definition: <nausuak>, childbirth, with <zia>, way, written as one word: the way in which a woman gave birth

terms: pupil of the eye/apple of the eye
definition: found in {mit nauta}, the pupil of the eye, said of what is guarded as most precious
used after <mi> as {mi nautang}, the people at large as distinct from priests and leaders
<nautang> and the marker <in> written as one word, after <mipi>: the ordinary people, as the doer or as the manner
people without office or rank, often as {mi nautangte}
<nau> and <tawdap> written as one word: the cloth or pad put under the bottom of a baby
<nau>, baby, and <tawi>, hold in the arms, written as one word: have a small child in the arms; {nupi nautawi} is a woman carrying a baby

<nau> in its meaning of younger sibling, with the plural <te>: the younger brothers and sisters, set against <ute>, the older ones; {u le naute} and <ute naute> address brothers and sisters, also fellow believers

terms: all the younger siblings/all the younger ones
definition: <nau>, younger sibling, and <teng>, all, written as one word; {u le nauteng} is all brothers and sisters, all the relatives
the last-born of the brothers; {a nautum pen} is the youngest
the younger of two children or siblings, opposite of <uzaw> the older
<nauzaw> the younger with <pa>, a male
<nauzaw>, the younger, with the plural <te>
<nauzawte> with the marker of the doer <in> shortened to {'n}; {tanu nauzawte'n} is the junior daughters of the house
<na>, your, and <vai>, matter, written as one word: your affair or business, as a case at an office
said of the mind, {lungsim navak}; {lungsim navak lo} is a dull or hardened heart
<navak> quick-witted with the noun suffix <na>; {lungsim navakna} is brightness of mind
<navak>, quick of mind, with the plural <te>; {lungsim navakte}, those with a quick mind
<na> and <van> written as one word: your goods, your belongings
<na>, the marker of an earlier action, with <vawh>, give a name, written as one word: {min navawh} is gave the name
<na>, your, and <veina>, concern, written as one word: the concern or burden that you feel for someone, as for your own people
placed at the end of a clause, usually after <sam>: granted that it is so, though; the speaker admits a point and then goes on to something else
<na> and <vet> written as one word after <gen>: {gen navet om kei} is there is nothing even to say of them, let alone those

terms: in their/at the place where they
definition: the noun ending {-na} written apart from its verb and joined to <vuah>: {athusuah navuah} is in their publication, {atuntun navuah} wherever they arrive
<na>, your, and <vun>, skin, written as one word
the English word navy with the plural <te>: the navy of a country and its men

placed before another verb to say the action is done quickly or in haste, as {nawh pai} go swiftly and {nawh nek} eat in haste; {ma-nawh} is to head for a place
make an animal or people move on or away; {nawh khia} is to drive out
<nawh>, hurry, with <deih>, want: want in a hurry; in job notices <ki nawhdeih> is urgently wanted
<nawh>, hurry or drive, with <delh> pursue
<nawh> hurry with <hawl> drive
<nawh> drive with <keek>, apart
<nawh> drive with <kek>, apart
<nawh>, drive, with <khia>, out: drive or throw people out of a place
form of <nawhkhia> used before {khit ciangin} and other following words
<nawhkhiat>, drive out, with the noun suffix <na>

terms: things that drive away/acts of driving out
definition: <nawhkhiat> drive out with the noun suffix <na> and the plural <te>: the deeds that drive someone away
<nawh> hurry with <len>, fly: said of an eagle swooping on its prey
<nawh>, hurry, with <pai>, go: go in haste, speed along
always as {nawhsa-in}, in haste

after <lung>, mind, as {lung ngaihngaih}: keep turning a thing over in the mind or keep longing, where the other sense is listening with the ears
<ngaih>, long for, with the endearing <no>: the one a person loves, said by lovers of each other
<ngaihno> written with a capital at the start of a line, used to address a lover: {Ngaihno aw}, my beloved

terms: want to listen/be willing to hear
definition: <ngaih>, listen, with <nop>, want; {mi’ ngaihnop dingin pau} is speak so that people like to listen, and {ngaihnop-huai} is pleasant to listen to
<ngaih>, beloved, with <nu> marking a woman: the girl or woman a man loves; mostly {lawm ngaihnu}, girlfriend
<ngaih>, beloved, with <pa> marking a man; used after <lawm> as {lawm ngaihpa}, the man a woman loves, which is also written <lawmngaihpa>
<ngaih>, lovely or beloved, and <pen>, most, written as one word: the most loved; {la ngaihpen} is the best loved or sweetest song
<ngaih>, dear or lovely, with <pen>, most, and plural <te>: the loveliest; {la ngaihpente} is the loveliest of songs, the Song of Songs

terms: love along with/be in love with
definition: <ngaih>, love, with <pih>, together with: love someone as one of one’s own; {ki ngaihpih} is the one a person is in love with
<ngaih>, a form of <ngai>, listen, with <sak>: listen carefully to what someone says
<ngaih.3>, loud, with <sak>: make the voice loud, after <aw>, voice; not the listening of the other sense
use the mind: think about something, consider it, or regard a person or thing in a certain way; {ngaihsun un} is the command to several people
<ngaihsun>, think, with the linking <a>: while thinking about something, or with someone in mind
<ngaihsun>, think, with the linking suffix <in>: having something in mind while doing the next action, or meaning something by what is said

terms: think at the same time/hope meanwhile
definition: <ngaihsun>, think, with <kawm>, while: think or hope something at the same time as doing something else
<ngaihsun>, think, with <kha>: come to think that something is so, often of a mistaken idea; {ngaihsunkha kei un} is do not suppose
<ngaihsun>, think, with <khial>, wrongly: have a mistaken idea
<ngaihsun>, think, and <kik>, again or back, written as one word: think something over again, or think back on what is past
<ngaihsun> and <lo> written as one word: do not think of something, do not consider or intend it
<ngaihsun>, think, with the causative <sak>: let or make someone think; {bangmah ngaihsunsak thei lo} is leave one unable to perceive anything
<ngaihsun>, think, with the last part doubled for thinking again and again: meditate on, ponder
<ngaihsunsun>, keep thinking about, with <in>, linking to the next verb

terms: those who think/those who plan/those who consider
definition: <ngaihsun>, think, with plural <te>: the people who think, plan or consider something; {thusia ngaihsunte} are those who plot evil
<ngaihsun>, think, and <thei>, able, written as one word: be able to think of or imagine something, or to regard it in a certain way
form of <ngaihsun>, think, used before <ciangin>, <ding>, <na>, <theihna> and in dependent clauses

terms: think back on/reflect on/think over again
definition: <ngaihsut>, think, and <kikkik>, again: look back on a thing and think it over; mostly {ka ngaihsut kikkik leh} or with <ciangin>, when I think back on it, before the conclusion the writer draws

<ngaihsut>, think, and <phat>, which after a verb here means well or thoroughly and not praise: think a matter over with care; very often followed by <huai>, {ngaihsut phat huai}, worth thinking over, or by <ding>
<ngaihsut>, thought, and <piakna>, a giving: a suggestion or piece of advice offered to someone; the person advised stands before it with <tungah> or <adingin>
<ngaihsut>, think, with <theihna.2>, the power to understand: the faculty of thinking, the mind's ability to reason; often {thu ngaihsut theihna}
<ngaihsut>, think, and <dan>, way, written as one word: how a person thinks about something
<ngaihsut>, think, and <ding> written as one word: to be thought about, something to consider; {ngaihsutding thu} is a matter to think about
<ngaihsut>, think, and <huai>, worthy of, written as one word: that deserves to be thought about

terms: think about/consider/take to heart/pay attention to
definition: <ngaihsut>, think, with the linking ending <in>; {ngaihsutin nei} is set the mind on something, take it to heart
<ngaihsut>, think, with <kha>, happen to: come to regard something in a certain way; {neu ngaihsutkha} is think little of, show contempt for
form of <ngaihsutkha>, happen to think, come to think, used in dependent clauses
<ngaihsut>, think, with <kik>, again or back, written as one word: think a thing over again, or look back on it
<ngaihsut> and <lo> written as one word, after a describing word: not think it so; {thupi ngaihsutlo} is not consider it important
<ngaihsut> and the negative <loh> written as one word: not think of, not consider; {ngaihsutloh kaalin} is while one is not thinking of it, unnoticed
<ngaihsut>, think, with the noun suffix <na>: what a person thinks, a thought or idea
<ngaihsut>, think, with the noun suffix <na>: what has been thought out, a plan or purpose; also the advice that one gives
<ngaihsutna>, thought, and <khuak>, brain: the brain as the seat of thinking, the mind or intellect; with <nei> also the idea for something
plural of <ngaihsutna>: thoughts or plans, of God or of people

<ngaihsut>, think, and <piakna>, giving, written as one word: a thought offered to others, a suggestion or piece of advice

terms: think about for someone/consider on behalf of/feel for

<ngaihsut>, think, with <sa>, already done: what has already been thought out or decided, a plan or decision
<ngaihsut>, consider, with <sak>: think of something on behalf of another, or regard something in a certain way
<ngaihsut>, think, with <siam>, skilled: good at thinking, discerning; {thu ngaihsutsiam mi} is a capable, sensible man

those who think of or regard something in a certain way; {a thupi ngaihsutte}, those who regard something as important
<ngaihsut>, think, with plural <te>: the things that people think, plan or take to be so

terms: worth considering/fit to be thought about
definition: <ngaihsut>, the form of <ngaihsun>, think, used before a suffix, with <tuak>, be fitting: worth considering
<ngaihsut>, consider, with <zaw>, more; {thupi ngaihsutzaw} is consider more important, value above another
<ngaihsut>, think, with <zawh>, form of <zo>, be able: be able to think through; with {ding hi lo}, beyond understanding
<ngaihsut>, think, with <zia>, manner

<ngaih>, loud, with <takin>, which makes an adverb: loudly; said of singing or shouting for joy
<ngaih>, dear or beloved, with plural <te>; used after <lawm>, friend, as {lawm ngaihte}: lovers, and as a figure for allies
<Ngaihte> with the plural <te>, set off by a hyphen because the name itself ends in that syllable: the people of the Ngaihte clan

terms: all the beloved/all the dear ones
definition: <ngaih>, love, and <teng>, all, written as one word: all those who are dear, used in addressing readers or kin, often {it leh ngaihteng}
<ngaih>, love or long for, with <tham>, worth: worth loving or missing
<ngaih>, loud, with <theithei>, here as much as can be: as loud as possible, said of a sound, {agin ngaihtheithei}

terms: want to listen/be willing to listen
definition: <ngai>, listen, with <nuam>, want
<ngai>, listen or heed, with the causative <sak>: make someone or something obey
<ngai>, listen, with <sim>, secretly: listen in on what others are saying
another spelling of <ngaihsun>, think; {bangci na ngaisun hiam} is what do you think

terms: those who listen/those who heed/those who welcome
definition: <ngai>, listen or heed, with plural <te>: the ones who listen to someone; also of those who welcome a person

terms: those who miss/those who love/loved ones

terms: fall in love at once/take to at once
definition: <ngai>, love, <thei>, can, and <pah>, at once, written as one word: come to love someone straight away, as at first sight

terms: love more/hold dearer/be more attached to

<ngak>, wait, and <kawm>, while, written as one word, usually followed by <in>: while waiting for something
<ngak>, wait, with <kawm>, while, and the linking suffix <in>: while waiting for something

<ngak>, wait, and <kulding>, will have to, written as one word
wait for or want something with impatience, be eager for it; {an ngaklah} is be greedy for food

<ngaklah>, long for, with the linking suffix <in>: longing, while longing

<ngak> wait, with <lai> still, any longer

<ngak>, wait, and <lo>, not, written as one word
<ngak>, rest or lay upon, with the noun suffix <na>: the thing on which something rests, as the stand of a basin; {khe ngakna} is a footstool
<ngak>, wait, with the noun suffix <na>: the act of waiting or the place where one waits, as {Bus ngakna}, a bus stop; not {ngakna} a stand on which a thing rests
punctuation mark, the waiting place, from <ngak>, wait: the colon
plural of <ngakna>: things on which something rests; {ban ngaknate} are armrests, and the {ngaknate} of a basin are its stand
plural of <ngakna> in the sense of waiting: the times one waits patiently, perseverance
<ngak>, wait, doubled to show that the waiting goes on
after a verb of speaking such as <kici> or <cih>, with no thought of waiting: the thing is said or done again and again, as a habit
<ngak> wait, said twice for continued action, with the noun suffix <na> and <in> marking the cause: because of waiting and waiting

terms: wait a long time/wait and wait

<ngak>, rest upon, with the causative <sak>: lay or place on; {khut ngaksak} is lay a hand on a person

<ngaksak>, lay on, with the linking suffix <in>; {lupna ngaksakin} is laying someone on a bed
those on whom something has been laid, here the hands, from <ngak> lay upon, <sa> already and plural <te>
<ngak>, wait, with plural <te>: people who wait for someone or put their hope in him
<ngak> in its meaning keep watch over a place, with plural <te>: the people who mind a place, as in {sumbuk ngakte} shop attendants and {inn ngakte} those who stay to mind the house
<ngak>, wait, with <zaw>, rather: wait instead of doing something else
<ngak>, wait, and <zawh>, finish or be able, written as one word; the form of <ngakzo> used before <ding>, <hangin> and <ciangin>: be able to wait, or have waited a length of time
<ngakzo>, be able to wait, with the noun suffix <na>: the ability to wait, patience

terms: be able to wait/manage to wait/wait through
definition: <ngak> wait, keep watch, with <zo>, be able, manage to
<ngakzo> and <lo> written as one word: not manage to wait

terms: those who wait/those who can wait
definition: <ngakzo>, be able to wait, with the plural {-te}: those who manage to wait, as in the saying that good things come to those who wait
a wild pig that lives in the forest

<nga> and <lo> written as one word: not turned toward something; {ki ngalo} is not depend on
the jointed upper leg above the foot that an insect such as a locust uses for hopping

armour worn on the lower legs, in the verse made of bronze

plural with <te>: small animals of little strength that make their home among the rocks

<ngam>, dare, and <kei>, not, written as one word and placed after the main verb
<ngam>, dare, with <lah>, fail to: not have the courage to do something, hold back from it
<ngam>, dare, and <lel>, just, written as one word after a verb: do it boldly and without hesitation
<ngam>, dare, and <lo>, not, written as one word after a verb: not dare to do it
<ngam> and <loh> written as one word after a verb: that one does not dare to do, as in {gen ngamloh}, that one dare not say

<ngamlo>, dare not, with the plural <te> after a verb: the people who do not dare to do it

<ngam>, dare, with <pa>, the male one: the one who dares to do something
<ngam>, dare, and the particle <ta>, now or already, written as one word after a verb: now dare to, have come to dare

<ngam>, dare, with <zaw>, more or rather; {sum ngamzaw} is be willing rather to lose
<nga>, five, with <na>, which makes an ordinal number: fifth; {sawm-le-ngana} is fifteenth
<nga>, fish, with <neu>, small
placed after a verb of pain, describing a continual throbbing ache; {tum ngangngang} is ache without stopping
<nga> and <ni> written as one word: the fifth day; {Ni ngani}, the fifth day of the week, is the Bible name of Thursday in the book's table

cross water on foot, as at a ford; {ka ngap zo kei hi}, I could not get across
beach and resort on the coast of Rakhine State in Myanmar, near Thandwe
<nga>, fish, with <pi>, big: the great fish that swallowed Jonah
Burmese fermented paste of fish or shrimp, with a strong smell, eaten as a relish
second part of the pair {utkeng ngapkeng}, from <ut>, want, and <ngap>, dare: doing just what one likes and dares, without regard for what is due

terms: not dare/cannot bear to/not be up to
definition: <ngap>, dare or be up to, and <lo>, not, written as one word after a verb: not have the heart or the strength to do it
<ngap> and <loh> written as one word: not having the strength or heart for something; {ngaploh hun} is a time when one is not up to it
<ngap>, dare, doubled: keep daring, do something boldly and without holding back
<ngap> ford, with <tan>, cut across: go through water on foot; with <sak>, lead someone through
<ngaptan> wade through, with <sak>, cause to: take someone across water on foot

terms: be able to wade across/be able to ford
definition: <ngap>, wade across, with <zo>, be able
a fish, as a living creature and as food; {ngasa bengte} are fishermen

<nga>, face or be turned toward, with the causative <sak>: make a thing face a direction; of hands, lay them on someone
<ngasa>, fish, with <lip>, scale
catching fish with a hook; {ngasiahna sikkawi} is a fish hook
put a carried thing down, with <suk>, downward: lower a jar or a sack to the ground
turn a part of the body toward something; {bil ngat} is incline the ear, pay attention, {mai ngat} is set the face toward, and {nung ngat} is turn the back on
stream followed and crossed on the way from <Zangpitam> to <Ciimnuai>

<ngat>, face or turn toward, with the noun suffix <na>; the side or direction toward which a thing is turned
with <to>, upward, and <in>, linking to the next verb: lifting a load up onto the shoulder
<ngat>, face, with the causative <sak>: make something face a certain way
strictly, without exception: <ngat> with <takin>, which makes an adverb; said of a law that must be strictly obeyed

paired with <zawn>, poor, as {zawn leh ngau}: poor and destitute
the state of having nothing; nearly always said together with <zawnna>, poverty, as {zawnna ngauna}, poverty and want
placed after a verb of feeling, asking or saying: with deep and lasting feeling, earnestly and again and again, as in {lunggulh ngaungau}, long for keenly, and {kap ngaungau}, keep whining
<nga>, five, with <vei>, times

written twice, {ngaw ngaw} or {ngaw-ngaw}: at last, only then, after a wait or several attempts
probably a spelling of <ngawng>, neck; {a ngawg kuaitan} is break its neck

placed before or after a verb, harshly or in anger; {ngawh dawn} is answer harshly

<ngawh>, harshly, with <dawn>, answer: give someone a harsh answer

plural of <ngawhna>: the charges laid against someone
<ngawh>, in anger, with <piak>, give: give something in anger

expressive word placed after a verb of going or lining up, as <kigual>: in a long line, many following one after another
placed after a verb: have ever done or been so; with <kei> or <lo> it means never

expressive word after <ot> shout, describing loud ringing shouting

<ngeina>, custom, with the plural <te>: the customs of a people, or the rules laid down for worship
<ngeina>, custom, with <zah>, amount: as much as is usual; {ngeinazah sangin} is more than usual
expressive word placed after a verb, showing that the action goes on in a noisy stir or commotion, often by many people at once
<ngeingai> with the noun ending <na>, placed after a verb: the doing of something in a noisy stir by many people together, as fighting in a brawl or working busily side by side
placed after a verb or phrase to stress that it really is so or will surely be so; with <kei>, certainly not

terms: wife's family/head of the wife's family

<sung> and <khempeuh> written as one word: the whole inside of something, everywhere in it

the organs inside the body of an animal or a person, the entrails

<tam>, many, with a second part meaning all the more: be more than before or more than the others

<tam> many, with <vei>, time or occasion; {tamvei zaw} is more times

form of <tamzaw>, more, used before a following word

the yellowish paste of ground bark that people in Myanmar rub on the face as a cosmetic; {tanakha kinuh} is to put it on
a member of one's own family or clan

<tanau> relative with <pa> marking a man; in Ruth the kinsman who has the right to redeem
<tanau>, relative, with the plural <te>; used also of one relative together with his family
the level or standing of a person beside others; seen with <kim>, as {gual tawh tanbang kim}, be on a level with one's peers, and {tanbang kim sak}, make equal

terms: have a child/bear a child/have young
definition: <ta> and <nei> written as one word: have a child or children; of an animal, have young

<tanei>, have a child, and <lo>, not, written as one word: having no child
<ta> child with <neu> small; in the verses the younger of two sons

keep oneself from something, as from food in <antang>, fast, or from drink and drugs

of the moon or sun: give light, shine; the same word as <taang>, written with one vowel

go without food, in {an tang}: {an tang in thungen} is fast and pray; the book marks this pronunciation <awtom>, <awlai>; compare <antang>

poetic word for <pasal> and <tangval>, used in songs

poetic expression for <cidam>, in good health, used in songs
be caught in a place with no way out, said of people shut in by the desert and of a narrow well
standing by oneself; <mimal tangdin> is an independent candidate or member of parliament, one who belongs to no party

the very young, said of small children and of the young of a flock
<ta>, child, and <ngek>, tender, written as one word: one's own baby or very young child

living without a husband or wife; {tanggawl om} is stay unmarried

measles, also {tangh natna}; used for rubella as well
a solid piece or lump of something; {tangh khat} is one chunk, and {dangka tangh} seems to be pieces of money, coins
dough or cake made of flour; {tangho su} is knead the dough
placed after a verb: keep on doing it, every time or without giving up
emphatic word placed after a verb, before <hi> or <leh>: really, indeed, in fact; {nong sap tangial leh} is if you really call me
<tan>, school class, and <giat>, eight, written as one word: the eighth class of school; {tangiat sang} is a school that teaches up to that class, a middle school

terms: instead of/in place of/on behalf of/for

<tang> with the linking ending <in>: keeping from something or keeping a day, as in {an tangin}, fasting, and {sabbath tangin}, keeping the Sabbath
town and district in the state of Johor, Malaysia, next to Muar
a month of the traditional Zomi calendar, set beside August in the book's table of month names
the crop of a bird, the pouch in its throat, taken out with the feathers when a bird is offered
<tang>, here the counter for small round things such as grains, pills, bullets, eyes and votes, and <khat> written as one word: one of them

take possession of a land again; <kik> is again
make known publicly, announce a message aloud for all to hear

<tangko>, proclaim, with the ending {-pa}: the man who announces a message in public, as a village crier or a herald

<tangko>, proclaim, with the causative <sak>: have something announced or made known to the public, as a warning or alert
<tangko>, proclaim, with the plural <te>, mostly after <a>: those who proclaim or cry out a message
the distant past; before a noun it means ancient, as in {tanglai mite}, the people of old

terms: long ago/in ancient times/from of old
definition: <tanglai>, olden times, and <pek>, far back: very long ago; mostly followed by <panin>, <pana> or {aa kipan}, since ancient times

not moving at all; mostly {tanglo in}, without stirring, standing or lying still

<tangmi>, envoy, with the plural <te>; also written <taangmite>
people chosen by vote to speak for the public in a parliament or council, after <teel>, elect, or {mipi'}, of the people; they are elected, not sent by a ruler as an envoy is
<tang>, here in the sense stir or move, with <nawnlo>, no longer: not moving any more, said of one who lies unconscious or dead
an insect that eats crops, named beside <kauphe>, locust
<tangngol>, grasshopper, with the plural <te>
<tang>, here the counting word for small round things such as eggs, teeth and bullets and for verses, and <nih>, two, written as one word: two of them
a Zomi village near Lamka in Manipur, India

terms: right before/in full view/in broad daylight

only in the saying <Vaphual tangsa va-ak tang>, of one who was a hornbill and turns into a crow; apparently a verb for be or count as, with <sa>, already: having once been

cause light to shine on someone or something; <taang>, shine, here written <tang>, with the causative <sak>

what someone lacks or requires; {bangmah tangsapna nei lo} is lack nothing

the people at large, ordinary citizens; mostly in the pair <tangpi tangta>, the general public, and in texts on war, civilians
in a straight line, without turning aside, and of speech plainly and directly; mostly as {tangtak in}
