the fifth of the appointed positions of a Zomi household: the eldest of the women of the family who have married out, also called <tuitaak> or <haitawi> after her tasks at the household sacrifice; she and the junior one carry all the work of the house and direct the other <tanukhak>

<tanu>, daughter, with {-pi}, chief: the principal one of the married daughters or sisters as a role in the kinship order of a household, also called <tuitaak> or <hai tawi>; her share of meat is the brisket

the first of the tanu of a Zomi household council, a married daughter or sister of the house, also called {Tuitaak}; the younger, <tanu nauzaw>, is also called {Sawlla}; she receives a set share of meat when an animal is killed
<tanupi>, secretary, and <teng>, all, written as one word: all the secretaries, as addressed in a circular letter
<tanu>, daughter, with the plural <te>
the people who carry out the work of an organisation, written after its name, as in {Tongsan Media tanute}, the staff of a news site who sign a report; not daughters
<tanute.1> with the marker of the doer <in> shortened to {'n}: here the married women of the family who hold the position <tanu>
a length of time, found in the question {bang tanvei}, how long
of a place, wide and open; {mun tanzau}, a spacious place
<tanzau>, spacious, with the noun suffix <na>; {a tanzauna mun} is a spacious place, a place of abundance
a part of the body named with <phei> thigh, where the NIV has legs and the KJV joints of thy thighs; with the plural <te>
city in Taiwan near Taipei, with the main international airport of the country
the fireplace of a house; {tap tungah} is on the hearth, and <tapkual> is the hearth and the space around it
take a name from a person or a place; <mintap> is a name taken over in this way, and {a tap sak} is name something after someone
a male child of his parents; after a name, son of that person
the Son, written with a capital in titles of Jesus such as {Mihing Tapa} Son of Man and {David’ Tapa} Son of David
<tapa>, son, and <neihsun>, the only one that a person has: an only son; in church language, mostly written {Tapa neihsun} after <a> or {Ama'}, the only begotten Son of God
<tapa>, son, and <taimang>, run away: the son who ran away, the prodigal son of the parable in Luke 15; used in sermons as a picture of a person who leaves God and returns
{tapa no} written as one word, <tapa>, son, followed by a word for young or little
<ta>, child, with <pasal>, male: a son
<tapa>, son, with the plural <te>
a month of the Burmese calendar in Zolai spelling, set beside February in the book's table of month names
sticky tape for binding or sealing, and the tape that police stretch round a place; {Tape Record} is a tape recorder
two children born at one birth
placed after a verb and before <hen> in a wish: may it indeed be so; apparently <ta> with <peuh>
after a verb and before the command endings <un>, <in> or <ni>, makes an earnest plea, do so or with <kei> do not; not the wish with <hen>
a Christian, a follower of Jesus Christ; also describes a thing as Christian, as in {Tapidaw pawlpi}, a Christian church
{tapidaw}, Christian, and <upna>, faith: the Christian faith, Christianity as a belief, set against <biakna>, religion, and the old <lawki> customs
plural of {tapidaw}, a Christian, literally a disciple
<ta>, child, with <pil>, wise, written as one word at the start of a proverb; set against <tahai>, foolish child
said of the heart, <lungsim>: be broken by grief
in the expression <tapkual han>, bold only at one's own fireside, said of a person who is bold when away and timid face to face; the meaning of the word alone is not shown by the verse
Saying: brave at the hearth, with <tapkual>, the fireside; said of a person who is bold only at home and timid elsewhere; the book lists it among its idiomatic expressions without explaining it
an armed rebel against the government
<tapong> with the plural <te>: armed rebels
name of two towns, one in the lowland of Judah and one on the border of Ephraim and Manasseh, and of a son of Hebron
sound word placed after a verb such as <ging> or <kiho>: with a quick repeated tapping or pattering sound
the place in the house where the cooking fire is kept
a group of the Falam area of Chin State with a speech of its own, named beside the Zangiat, Khualsim and Laizo
town in the territory of Benjamin
son of Micah, a descendant of King Saul through Jonathan
someone or something aimed at or attacked; {Target in nei} is have as a target; the Zolai verb is <ngim>
the paved ground of an airport where planes stand and move
city in Cilicia, the home town of Saul, who became the apostle Paul
spelling of Tarshish used in the Psalms: a distant land or seaport known for its large trading ships
son of Javan; also a distant seaport known for its trading ships, and the name of a Benjaminite and of a Persian noble
city in Cilicia where the apostle Paul was born
idol worshipped by the Avvites who were settled in Samaria
let animals feed in a field
let someone go their own way, leave them to it
with a negative, never be without, never fail to have
after a verb at the end of a clause, often with <zong>, also, earlier in it: marks that something has now come about as well, as in {hoihkik tasam}, has now become good again too; not the verb lack
<tasam> lack with the causative <sak>; with <lo>, not let someone go without, so provide for

terms: the needy/those in need/those who lack
definition: <tasam>, lack, with the plural <te>: people who are short of something, as {neek ding dawn ding tasamte}, those short of food and drink
a month of the Burmese calendar in Zolai spelling, set beside October in the book's table of month names
paired with <tusawn> in {tusawn tasawn}, children's children and those after them, the descendants of a person down the generations
with <leh> after a verb: {om tase leh}, though there are
<tase>, although, strengthened by <mahleh>, even though: placed after the verb of a clause, even though that is so; the main clause follows, often with <veve>, still
said of a woman who cannot bear children
placed after a verb: even though that is so
<tasel>, childless, with <pa> marking a man
<ta>, child, with <suah>, bring forth

terms: as a place of giving birth/as a birthplace
definition: <tasuahna>, giving birth or the place of it, with <in>, as
<ta>, child, with <suak>, come out; {tasuak dinga kisa} is about to give birth
form of <tan> used before a following word such as <ding>, <nop> or <nading>
of a cord or rope, break or be severed; {sat tat} and {su-tat} mean cut through
carry out a penalty on someone, in the phrase {daan tat}, punish
do things or behave in a certain way, mostly as {gam tat}, the two parts of <gamtat> written apart, and before <zia> or <dan>, manner; not the breaking of a cord or the redeeming of the other senses
placed after a descriptive word to pick out those who have the quality most; {a kahsiam tata} are the most skilful at wailing
the distributive <ta>, each, with <tawh>, with, written as one word after an amount: at that much each, at that rate
the established way in which a people or a person acts, often named together with <ngeina>, culture, and <omdan>, way of life
the fathers of one's children, which the book equates with <ei>, we ourselves; the reverse form <pate'tate> names the same generation
the grandfathers of one's children, which the book equates with <pa>; the reverse form <pute'tate> names the same generation
the children of one's children, which the book equates with <tu>
the grandchildren of one's children, which the book equates with <tu sawn>; the reverse form <tute'tate> names the same generation
<tate>, children, and <bel>, as for, written as one word: as for the children
<tate>, children, with the marker <in> shortened to {-n} and written as one word: the children as the ones who do the action
placed after a verb and before <zongin>: even though it really is so, however much; {ahi tateu zongin} is even though it is indeed so
said of a hot iron pressed on the flesh; <tat> with <gawp>, severely
rub a blade until it is sharp, <hiam>; also said of sharpening the mind, and {ki tathiam} is be sharpened
of four creatures moving, each going in one direction without turning
a wrong act or a going wrong, in Numbers 15 one done without intent
<tat> redeem with <khiat> out: set free by paying a price; form used before <ding>, <nading>, <manin> and <mite>
act of setting free by paying a price, or the price paid: {tatkhiatna sum}, ransom money
<tatkhiat> redeem with <sa> already done: whom someone has redeemed
<tatkhiatsa> redeemed with the plural <te>: those whom someone has redeemed
get back by payment what was sold or dedicated; <tat> with <kik> back

terms: be able to redeem/be able to buy back
definition: <tat>, redeem, with <kik>, back, and <zawh>, form of <zo>, be able
the armed forces of Myanmar, under their Burmese name; with <te> also the soldiers of that army
the buying back or setting free of a person or thing; {Tatna' Ni} is the day of redemption
way of acting, after a describing word; {gitloh tatna} doing evil, {va hoih tatna} walking rightly
{ganhing tatna}, land where animals are let out to graze
plural of <tatna>, conduct, way of acting
of an animal, lose its young before birth
<tatolh> with the linking <in>
<tatolh> miscarry with the noun ending <na>; in the verse what bad water caused, where the NIV has unproductive land
<tatolh> miscarry with the causative <sak>
<tat>, redeem, with <sa>, already done; {Topa tatsa mi}, those the Lord has redeemed
<tat>, redeem, with <sak>, do for another: buy a thing back on someone's behalf
in {hai tatsak}, from <haitat>, act foolishly, with <sak>, cause: lead someone into folly
<tat>, here hit, with <sak>, cause: make a thing hit a person, as poison put on the face in {guza tatsak} or a shot in the head in {thau tawh a lu tatsak}; not the redeeming of the other sense
found with <lo>, not: <tatsat loin>, without a break, regularly, continually, always
<tatsat>, break off, and <loin>, without: placed before a verb, the action goes on without stopping; in war news said of shooting and bombing
<tatsat> and <lo> written as one word: without stopping, round the clock
behave badly toward others, oppress; apparently <tat> as in <gamtat>, behave, with <sia>, bad
form of <tatsia> used before <ding>
<tatsia>, act wickedly, with <te>, those who
noun of <tatsiat>: a wicked or destructive act; in 2 Samuel 24:16 the destruction itself
plural of <tatsiatna>
<tat>, whet or sharpen a blade, with <te>, those who
Persian governor of the province beyond the Euphrates in the time of King Darius, who questioned the rebuilding of the temple
<tat>, redeem, with <theih>, can, and the noun suffix <na>
a mark or picture made in the skin with ink
a Buddhist pagoda, as the Shwedagon in Yangon; with <milim>, an idol or shrine that is worshipped
the way a person or a people act and behave; often paired as {omzia tatzia}
plural of <tatzia>, manner of acting
mostly in {biakna tau}, altar of offering
make low sounds of pain or grief, often after {thum in} and beside <kap>, weep; a verb, not the noun {tau}, altar
a raised structure of any kind, of which the altar is one: a stand on which goods are laid out for sale, a shelter built to rest in, and in {nai tau} a clock tower
first part of {tau sangpi}, high tower, written apart and capitalised in the name {Hananel Tau sangpi}, the Tower of Hananel
a metal cooking pot set on the fire; <beel> is pot
small case holding scripture worn by Jews; named beside <baanbuh>, the one on the arm, so apparently the one worn on the forehead
the Burmese name of Friday in Zolai spelling, from the book's table of the days of the week
<tau>, groan, with <khawm>, together
a Zomi village in Chin State, Myanmar; written after the name of a person it says which village the person is from, and {Tauleng Khua Kipawlna} is the association of its people
the sound made by one in pain or grief
<tau>, altar, with <neu>, small; in the verse the altar is too small, {tau neu lua}
the capital city of Shan State in Myanmar
a city of Bago Region in Myanmar, on the road from Yangon to Nay Pyi Taw
a ward of the town of <Kalaymyo>
a quarter of the town of <Kalaymyo>; also in the names of a hotel and a newspaper there
a tall structure; {nai taupi} is a clock tower
tower, capitalised as part of the name of a particular tower
<tausang> tower, with the place marker <ah>
<tausang>, tower, and <dawn.3>, top, written as one word: the top of a tower or high platform; {saihapak tausangdawn} is an ivory tower
<tausang>, tower, with <pi>, great
<tausangpi>, capitalised in the name {Hananel Tausangpi}, the Tower of Hananel
<tausangpi> great tower with the plural <te>; in the verse towers set up round a city under siege
make low sounds of pain or grief
after a verb of doing, as <leng>, <tai>, <pai>, <hanciam> or <za>: the action keeps going without a break; not the groaning of the other sense
the sound made by one in pain or grief
in both verses with a negative: whoever trusts in him will never be put to shame
what a person is answerable for; <tavuan la> is take on a responsibility

<tavuan>, responsibility, and <la>, take: take on the responsibility or the charge of something; the one who takes it stands before with <in>, and a thing or place taken charge of stands directly before the pair
<tavuan> and <la> written as one word: take a responsibility upon oneself
<tavuan>, duty, with <teng>, all
said of the eyes: {mit taw} is blind
<taw>, bottom, with the place marker <ah>: at the bottom or lower end of something
town and district on the south-east coast of Sabah, Malaysia
in {tawbo dawksa-in}, with buttocks bared; <taw> is bottom
<taw> blind with <cip> completely, said of an eye
the cloth put under the bottom of a baby, from <taw.2>, bottom, and <dap.1>, pad; {nau tawdap} is a baby's nappy
what lies beneath something as its base, said of the heart or mind: {lungsim tawdap} is the underlying state of mind
what settles at the bottom of a cup
placed after a noun: together with a person, or by means of a thing or material
with <mei>, fire, as {mei tawh}: make up or tend a fire; whether kindle or stoke is not settled by the page
<tawh>, with, and <akibang>, that is alike: placed after a noun and before another noun, which is like or resembles the first; before <ahi> <hi>, is the same as
<tawh>, with, and <kibang>, alike: placed after a noun, be like it or the same as it; with <lo> it is be unlike

terms: like/in the same way as/together with
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kibangin>, alike: placed after a noun or pronoun, like it or in the same way as it; in messages of condolence, sharing the grief of the people named before it

terms: be far from/be distant from/keep away from
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kigamla>, be far apart: the place or person from which there is distance stands before <tawh>, where English says from; with <lo> it means not far from, near
<tawh>, with, and <kikop>, be joined as a pair: to be joined with someone or something, placed after the partner; <tawh kikop in> before another verb is together with, in cooperation with

terms: together with/jointly with/in cooperation with/in partnership with
definition: <tawh.2>, with, <kikop>, be paired or allied, and the adverbial ending <in>: placed after the name of a person or organisation and before the main verb, it says that the action is done jointly with that partner

<tawh>, with, and <kimemat>, be connected: placed after a noun or a clause, in connection with it, about it; mostly followed by <in>, and before a noun such as <thute> it means the matters that have to do with it
<tawh>, with, and <kimuhna>, here the noun of <kimu>, meet one another: placed after the name of a person or group, a meeting or interview with them; common as the heading of a report
<tawh>, with, and <kinai>, be near: placed after a noun, be near that place or close to that person; where English says near to, Zolai says near with
<tawh>, with, and <kipawl>, form one group: placed after the name of a person, group or body, join forces with it, be its ally or partner

terms: be free from/escape from/keep away from/be apart from
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kipelh>, escape or keep away: the thing that is avoided or escaped stands before <tawh>, where English says from and not with

<tawh>, with, and <kisaiin>, being related: placed after a noun or noun phrase, about or concerning it; the form with <in> joins the phrase to the verb that follows, while {tawh kisai} stands before a noun or as a heading

terms: be measured by/be compared with/be judged by
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kiteh>, be measured: placed after a noun that names the standard, be measured, valued or judged by it

terms: keep company with/associate with/work together with
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kithuah>, be joined: placed after the name of a person or group, be together with them, as a companion or a partner in work; of things, be fitted with
<tawh>, with, and <kituak>, agree: placed after a noun, agree with it, fit it or be in keeping with it

terms: in accordance with/according to/in keeping with/in proportion to
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kituakin>, fitting: placed after a noun, in a way that fits or matches it, as a law, a custom, a position or an amount

terms: in line with/in accordance with/along with
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kizawi>, go side by side: placed after a noun and nearly always followed by <tawn> or <tawnin>, {tawh kizawi tawnin}, in line with it, in accordance with it, going together with it; {tua tawh kizawi tawn in} is in line with that

terms: be connected with/be linked to/contact/keep in touch with
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kizom>, be joined: placed after a noun, be linked to or bound up with it; of persons, be in touch with someone, and as a command, {tawh kizom in}, get in touch with, in notices that give a name or a telephone number; {tawh kizom in} after a matter also means in connection with it

terms: be in contact with/connect with/be linked to
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kizop>, be joined: placed after a noun for a person or body, keep in touch or have dealings with it; {tawh kizop ding} is to get in contact with

terms: in accordance with/according to/in keeping with
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kizuiin>, following: placed after a noun or <tua>, in keeping with it, as a result of it; also written {tawh kizui in}
<tawh>, with, and <kopin>, jointly: placed after a noun or a name, together with that person or thing, of two parties who do one thing as partners or of two things that go together

<tawh>, with, and <tehna>, measuring: placed after a noun or a number and usually followed by <in>, {tawh tehna in}, compared with that thing; what follows says how the subject differs, often with <zaw>, more
<tawh>, with, and the linking ending <a> written long and joined to it: with or by something, and so
keys, <tawh>, kept together in a bunch, <bom>; inferred from the parts of the word
a lock, opened with a <tawhtang>, key
the form of <to>, dig, that is used before endings, with <ding> written as one word: that is still to be dug, said of a pit or of a new road
<to>, dig, in the form used before a suffix, with <huai>, worthy of: worth digging
<tawh>, kindle a fire, with the linking ending <in>; {mei tawhin}, kindling a fire and then
<tawh.2>, with, and the ending {-in}, after a noun or after <dan> and <hang>: with, by means of or through; not the kindling of a fire
<tawh> and <kisai> written as one word, placed after a noun: concerning it, to do with it

terms: fit/be in keeping with/be in line with
definition: <tawh>, with, and <kituak>, be suitable, written as one word after the thing matched: be in keeping with it
<tawh> and <kizui> written as one word after a noun: in keeping with it, according to it
with <mei>, fire, make a fire flare up; <kuang> is burn
<tawhkuang>, kindle, with <sa>, already done; of a fire that has been kindled
<tawh>, with, and <lo>, not, written as one word and placed after a noun: without it
<tawh>, form of <to>, dig, with <na>: the act or place of digging a pit or well, or of cutting stone from the ground; {kan tawhna} is a siege ramp
with the linking <in>, resting; apparently the word <tawlnga>, rest, written with h
<tawh>, form of <to>, dig, with <sa>, already: placed before a noun, the pit or well that someone has dug
<to>, dig, in the form used before a suffix, with <suah>, bring out or become: bring about or carry through what <to> names; the page lists the form without a meaning
<tawhtang>, key, with the plural <te>; in Matthew 16:19 the keys of the kingdom of heaven
<to>, dig, in the form used before a suffix, with <tuak>, be fitting: fit to be dug
dig a way through rock or a wall so that there is an opening; {kulh tawhvang} is dig through a wall
<tawh>, with, and <zong>, also, written as one word after a noun: with that too, or even with that
hold or carry in the hand or arms
draw water from a well or spring; {tui tawi dingin pai} is go to fetch water
a unit of weight used for money and gold, the mina of the parable in Luke 19; {sum tawi khat} is one mina
a Myanmar measure of weight of a hundred ticals, {tikal 100}, about 1.6 kilograms, by which goods are sold in the market; {tawi khat} is one viss
<tawi>, hold in the hand, with the linking suffix <in>: holding, with something in the hand
<tawi> and <ding> written as one word: to be held or carried, something to carry, will carry
<tawi>, hold, and <kawm>, while, written as one word: holding or carrying something in the hand or arms while doing something else
<tawi>, hold, with <kawmin>, while: holding something in the hand while doing something else
<tawikawm>, while holding, and <sa> written as one word, followed by <in>: with the thing still held in the hand while doing something else
<tawi>, hold or carry, and the particle <kha> written as one word: happen to have a thing in hand, end up carrying it
find the weight of something on scales; also weigh out money in payment, and of God weighing a person or his deeds
<tawikhai>, weigh, with the noun ending <na>: the instrument for weighing; {tawikhaina man} is honest scales, {tawikhaina man lo} dishonest scales
<tawi>, hold in the hand, and <khat>, one, written as one word: one thing that is held or carried in the hand
<tawi>, hold or carry, with <khawm>, together: hold or carry several things together
<tawi>, draw water, with <khia>, out: draw water out of a well
<tawi>, viss, and <lang>, half, written as one word: half a viss, fifty ticals
<tawilang>, half a viss, with <lang>, half: half of a half viss, a quarter of a viss, 25 ticals
<tawi>, hold or carry, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not carrying something, without it in hand, as {permit tawilo}, holding no permit

<tawi>, hold or carry, with the noun suffix <na>: the carrying or bearing of something, as in {thau tawina}, the bearing of arms; in {pah tawina} it is the second half of <pahtawina>, honor, written apart
<tawi> and <neilo> written as one word: have nothing of the kind in hand, as a document or permit
<tawi>, hold or carry, with <pa>, the man who: the man who holds or carries something, as {thal tawipa}, an archer
<tawi>, draw water, with <sa>, already done: of water that has been drawn
<tawi>, hold in the hand, with <sa>, already done: having a thing in the hand, such as a knife, a weapon or a card, mostly as {tawisa in}, holding; not the drawing of water
<tawi>, draw water, with <sak>, do for another: draw water for someone or for his animals

terms: make hold/have carry/put in the hand
definition: <tawi>, hold or carry, with the causative <sak>: put a thing in someone's hand or have someone carry it; {hiam a tawisak tangvalpa} is an armor-bearer

terms: will make hold/will have carry/will issue
definition: <tawisak> and <ding> written as one word: will have someone hold or carry a thing, as a card or paper
<tawisak> draw water for someone with the linking ending <in>: having drawn water for someone, and then
<tawisak> draw water for someone with the plural <te>: the people who draw water for others
<tawi>, hold, with <sang>, high: hold high, raise the standing of a people, a faith or a way of life
<tawisang>, lift up, with the noun ending <na>: the act of raising the standing of someone; {minam tawisangna} is the uplifting of the nation
<tawi>, hold or wield, with <siam>, skilled; {thal tawisiam}, skilled with the bow
stone used as a weight on scales; {tawisuang man} is an honest weight, {tawisuang nam nih} two differing weights
<tawi>, hold or carry, said twice and written as one word: keep carrying, carry about with one
<tawi>, hold or carry, with the plural <te>: those who carry or wield something; {thal tawite} are archers, {galhiam tawite} armor-bearers, {tui tawite} water carriers
find the weight of something; <tawi>, hold, with <teh>, measure
<tawiteh>, weigh, with the linking <in>; weighing out, by weight
<tawiteh>, weigh, with the noun ending <na>: the instrument for weighing or measuring goods; {tawitehna man lo} is dishonest scales
plural of <tawitehna>

terms: bring in addition/bring along as well
definition: <tawi>, carry, with <thuah>, add, and the linking <in>
<tawi>, hold, with <zawh>, form of <zo>, be able: {khut sunga tawizawh} is that can be held in the hand
reach all through something, as yeast through dough or wine over lips and teeth
the bare rump of a monkey, in the saying that the monkey does not see its own {tawkheng} but points at that of its friends, said of one who blames others for a fault of his own
<tawk>, spread all through, with <sak>, cause; of yeast working through a whole batch of dough, and of arrows made drunk with blood
a stretch of time, in {tawl khat}, a while; {tawl khat sung} is for a while, {tawl khat khit ciangin} after some time
become tired from effort; paired with <gim>, be tired, and in the verses mostly with <lo>, not
<taw>, bottom, with <lam>, side: the rear part of a boat or ship
first in a list of unclean lizards, where the NIV has gecko and the KJV ferret
be relieved of tiredness or worry; {lungsim tawldam} is be refreshed in heart, and with <sak> it means refresh someone
<tawldam>, be rested, with the noun ending <na>: rest or relief from work, trouble or weariness
<tawldam>, be rested, with the causative <sak>: give rest to someone, ease a trouble
<tawldam> and <tak> written as one word, followed by <in>: in a rested and relaxed way
an opening in the wall of a house or ship for light and air; {tawlet panin} is from or through the window
<tawlet>, window, with the plural <te>; {vantung tawlette}, the windows of heaven, where the English has floodgates
<tawl>, a while, with <khat>, one: for a short time; {tawlkhat sung} is for a while, {tawlkhat khit ciangin} after a little while
<tawlkhat>, a little while, and <khit>, after: always followed by <ciangin> or <teh>, and placed at the head of a sentence in a story, after a short time
<tawlkhat>, a little while, with <khat> repeated
<tawlkhat> and <sung> written as one word: for a short time, during a while
<tawl>, be tired, and <lo>, not, written as one word
<tawl>, be weary, with <lua>, too much
<tawl> and <mahmah> written as one word, the first word here in the meaning be tired: be very tired
<tawl>, be tired, and the question word <maw>, written as one word: tired, is it; in {tawlmaw tawllo}, whether tired or not
<tawl>, be weary, with the noun ending <na>; used in the pair {gimna tawlna}, suffering and hardship
stop working or moving in order to recover strength
be at ease, free from work or trouble

<thawh>, rise, with <khiat>, out: come up out of something, as out of the water; the form used before <khit> and <ciangin>

terms: rise again/rise from the dead/be raised
definition: <thawh>, rise, with <kik>, again: rise again, especially from death; the form used before <khit>, <ciangin> and <nading>
<thawhkik>, rise again, with the noun suffix <na>: rising again from death, resurrection
<thawhkik>, rise again, with <ni>, day: the day of the resurrection of Jesus, Easter Sunday
<thawhkik>, rise again, with the causative <sak>: make someone rise again from death
<thawhkiksak>, raise again, with the noun suffix <na>: the fact of having raised someone from death
<thawhkiksak>, raise again, with <pa> marking a man: in the verse, the man whom Jesus raised from the dead
<thawh>, rise, with <lam>: the fact or moment of getting up, paired with <luplam>, lying down
<tho>, rise, in the form used before a suffix, with the noun suffix <na>: the act of rising or getting up, as in <thawhkikna>, resurrection
<thawh>, get up, and <pan>, from, written as one word: from the time one gets up

terms: just get up/as soon as one gets up
definition: <thawh>, get up, with <phet>, just, written as one word: the moment of getting up from sleep; {zingsang na thawhphet in} is as soon as you get up in the morning
<thawh>, rise, with the causative <sak>: make someone rise, especially from death

terms: raise again/raise up/bring back to life
definition: <thawhsak>, make rise, with <kik>, again: raise someone from death
<thawhsakkik>, raise again, with the noun suffix <na>: the raising of someone from death
<thawh>, the form of <tho>, rise, get up, used before a suffix, with <suah>, bring out or become: raise up; the page lists the form without a meaning
<thawh>, rise, with <toh>, upward: come up, as out of the water; the form used before {lai takin}
<thawhtoh>, rise up, with the noun suffix <na>: the act of rising up
<thawh>, the form of <tho>, rise, get up, used before a suffix, with <tuak>, be fitting: fit to rise
<thawh>, rise, with <zawh>, a form of <zo>, be able: be able to get up again after an injury

written after a detached <ki>: {ki thawithawi} is <kithawithawi>, be busy getting ready, be about to
container for liquids such as water, oil or wine; {savun thawl} is a wineskin, and {thawl khat} also renders the liquid measure hin
have room to go through a gap or between things without being held back, unlike the noun {thawl}, a bottle; often followed by <thei> or <zawh>
<thawl>, bottle, and <hawm>, empty, written as one word: an empty bottle, as collected and sold again
<thawl>, bottle or jar, with <khat>, one, written as one word
<thawl>, bottle, and <neu>, small, written as one word
<thawl>, bottle, and <nih>, two, written as one word, after the name of the liquid
<thawl>, jar, with <pi>, big: a large jar; in Haggai a measure of wine
a container of the <thawl> kind, here one filled with perfume; the part <san> is not explained by the verse
<thawl>, bottle, and <sung>, in, written as one word, usually followed by <ah>: inside a bottle
feeling alone and without company; {thawmhau kisa} is feel lonely
<thawmhau>, lonely, with the noun suffix <na>: the state of feeling alone or empty
shake or ring with a loud noise, said of the ground or the shore
strike with a loud noise so as to throw into panic
<thawn>, shake, written as one word with <kham>: of the ground, shake and ring with the noise of a crowd
town and district on the Irrawaddy in Magway Region of Myanmar; those living as far as the Thayet area are called <Asho>
<tha>, strength, with the first part of <zatui>, medicine: something taken to build up strength, a tonic or vitamin
<tha>, strength, with <zaw>, weak: have no strength left, said of eyes, hands and courage; {thazaw sak} is weaken or discourage
<tha>, strength, with <zawh>, overcome: be stronger than someone and overpower him, or have strength enough for a heavy task
<tha>, strength, with <zawm>, weak: faint and worn out, as with hunger
<thazawm>, weak, and <cip>, completely, written as one word: be completely without strength
<thazawm>, weak, with the noun ending <na>: lack of strength, of body or of mind
<thazawm>, weak, with the causing <sak>: make a person, a body or a power weak
having little strength, weak; said of the body and of people
<tha>, strength, with <zawngkhal>, weak, written as one word: without strength, powerless
<thazawng>, weak, with the plural <te>: the weak, people who are weak
<thazaw>, be weak, with the causative <sak>: take away strength or courage; of hands, let them hang limp
a town and district in <Mandalay> Region of Myanmar
Burmese name, that of an orchid; a ward of the town of Kalaymyo, and part of the name of the bus line Shwe Thazin
said of the root of the olive tree whose sap feeds the branches; {thazung tui} is its sap
chief city of Upper Egypt on the Nile, against which the prophets announced judgment
town near Shechem where Abimelek son of Gideon was killed by a millstone a woman dropped on him
said of heads of grain that are poor and empty; which of the three English words it answers to is not certain
<theem>, thin, with the causative <sak>: of the east wind, make ears of grain thin and dried up
<theemsak> cause to shrivel with the connective <in>; said of the east wind blasting ears of grain
throw a liquid in drops over something, as blood on the altar or oil before the Lord
<theh>, sprinkle, with the linking ending <in>: sprinkling, before the next action in the sentence
<theh>, sprinkle, with <khia>, out, written as one word: send out in a spray or cloud, as a volcano its ash or a flower its scent; with <ki>, be thrown out
<theh> sprinkle with the noun suffix <na>: the act of sprinkling blood
throw or drive apart in all directions: scatter a people among the nations, or scatter things such as frost and arrows
with <ki.2>, as {ki thehthang}: of a photo, a video or news, spread quickly among many people, above all on social media
<thehthang> with <gawp>, written as one word after <ki.2>: of people or broken glass, be scattered in all directions; of a photo or a video, spread all over social media
<thehthang>, scatter, with the linking ending <in>: scattering, before the next action in the sentence
noun of <thehthang>, scatter; before <gam> or with <panin> it names the place to which people were scattered, as {note kong thehthangna gamte}, the lands where I scattered you
<thehthang> scatter with <pa> marking a male person: he who scattered them
<thehthang>, scatter, and <pah>, at once, written as one word; with <ki>, of news or a video: spread quickly everywhere
<thehthang> scatter with <zo> marking that the act is completed
scatter or spread over a wide area; mostly with <ki> as {ki thehzak}, the same as <kithehzak>: be scattered about, and of a video or a piece of news, be spread widely
<thehzak>, scatter, with <gawp>, thoroughly; with the prefix <ki>, mostly written apart, be spread everywhere, said of a video or photo that goes viral on social media; compare <kithehzak>
written after <ki>, as {ki thehzakpah}: <kithehzak>, be scattered, with <pah>, at once; of a photo, video or piece of news, spread quickly and widely on social media
<thehzak>, scatter, and the causative <sak> written as one word: cause news or a message to spread among people; mostly after <ki>, be spread about
know a person, a fact or a way; {thei kei} is not know
placed after a verb: able to do it, can; {thei lo} is unable
the fig; {thei gah} is the fruit, {thei kung} the tree and {thei moh} a cake of pressed figs
<thei>, know, written with a capital at the start of a sentence or of quoted speech; {thei in} is the command know, often translated see or look

<thei>, know or be able, and <keng>, here not the verb carry but the negative <kei> run together with <ing>, the ending of the first person: I do not know, closing a sentence, often after a question clause; after another verb, I cannot
the sycamore-fig tree, common in the foothills; said as {theiba sing} or {theiba kung}
<thei>, know, with <baih>, soon or quickly, written as one word: come to know or understand a thing quickly or early
<thei>, able, and <bek>, only, written as one word after a verb: can only do that, it is possible in that way alone
<thei>, know, with <cian>, clearly: know exactly; {ki theician nailo} is it is not yet known for certain
<thei>, know, <cian>, clearly, and <lo>, not, written as one word; in news reports {ki theicianlo hi} is it is not known for certain

terms: want to know for certain/want to know exactly
definition: <theician>, know for certain, and <nuam>, want, written as one word; with <ki>, people want to know for certain

terms: be able to know for certain/manage to identify
definition: <theician>, know exactly, and <zo>, be able, written as one word; mostly with <ki> before and <nailo> or <nawnlo> after: it cannot yet be known for certain
<thei>, know, and <ciat>, each, written as one word: each one knows; {i theiciat hi} is we all know
<thei>, be able, and <dan>, way, written as one word after a verb: the way in which something can be done
<thei> and <den> written as one word, placed after a verb: always able to do it, can at any time
<thei> and <ding> written as one word: after a verb, will be able to, so as to be able to; alone, will know
<thei>, able, and <dinghi> written as one word at the end of a sentence, after a verb: will be able to, may well

terms: so as to be able to/in order that it can
definition: <thei> and <dingin> written as one word, placed after a verb: so that one is able to do it
the fruit of the fig tree
<theigah>, fig, with the plural <te>; in a list of crops it also stands for the fig trees
form of <thei>, know or be able, used before words such as <ni>, <ma-in>, <loh>, <ding> and <nading>; <theih nadingin> is so that one may

terms: so that ... can/in order to be able to
definition: <theih>, be able, and <nadinga>, in order to: placed after a verb to form a clause of purpose, so that the action can be done; a variant of <theih nadingin>

terms: so that it may be possible/in order to be able to
definition: <theih>, be able, and <nadingin>, in order to: placed after a verb, so that it can be done, in order to be able to do it; by itself after an object, so that it may be known

terms: so that they can/so that they may know
definition: <theih>, know or be able, and <nadingun>, in order that, with a plural subject: placed after a verb it closes a clause of purpose, so that they can do it; after a noun as object, so that they may know it

terms: so that one can/in order to be able to
definition: <theih>, be able, with <nangin>, here a short form of <nadingin>, in order to, and not the pronoun you: placed after a verb, so that the action can be done; the same as <theih nadingin>

terms: as much as possible/to the utmost/as best one can
definition: <theih>, be able, and <tawp>, the limit: placed after a verb or describing word and followed by <in> or <un>, it says that the thing is done to the furthest degree possible; {a hat theih tawp un} is as fast as they could

terms: as much as possible/to the best of one's ability/as far as one can
definition: <theih>, be able, and <tawpin>, to the utmost: placed after a verb, to the limit of what can be done; {ka hih theih tawpin} is as much as I can do, and {hanciam theih tawpin} trying as hard as possible
<theih>, know, and <ban>, reach, written as one word; {theihban zawhloh} is what knowledge cannot reach, unknown or beyond understanding
<theih>, <ban> and <loh> written as one word: what one's knowing does not reach, be beyond one's knowledge
<theih>, know, with <bat>, reach, written as one word: as far as knowledge reaches; {ka theihbat tanh} is as far as I know, and {theihbat loh} is what is beyond one's knowledge
<theih>, know, with the ending {-beh}, more, in addition: come to know more; {theihbeh nop a om leh} is if anyone wishes to know more
<theihbeh>, know more, and <huai>, worthy of, written as one word: that is worth knowing in addition; {theihbehhuai aomte} is further things worth knowing
<theihnop>, want to know, and {theih beh}, know further, written as one word: wish to know more about a matter
<theih>, know, and <cian>, clearly, written as one word: know a thing exactly and for certain; {ki theihcian} is be found out for certain
<theihcian> and <ding> written as one word: what is to be known clearly, or in order that someone knows it for certain
<theih> and <ciang> written as one word: as far as is known, what one knows, or when it became known
<theih> and <ciangin> written as one word: when someone comes to know something, or after another verb when it could be done
noun of <theihcian>: knowing a thing clearly and for certain; {theihcianna om lo} is nothing is known for certain
<theih>, know, with <ciat>, each, written as one word: known to each one; {i theihciat} is what we all know
<theih> and <cil> written as one word: the first knowing of a thing, when it is first noticed; {ka theihcil akipan} is since I first knew, as long as I remember
<theih>, know, and <dan>, way, written as one word: the way someone knows or understands a thing, what one knows of it; {ka theihdan} is as far as I know
<theih> and <ding> written as one word: what is to be known, things one should know; after another verb, so as to be able to

terms: for the information of/so as to know
definition: <theih>, know, and <dingin>, in order to, written as one word: so that someone may know, placed after those who are to know
<theih>, know, with <hak>, hard: difficult to know or understand, said of a saying or riddle
<theih>, know, and <huai>, worthy of, written as one word: that ought to be known; {a theihhuai} is the things worth knowing
<theihhuai>, worth knowing, with <sa>, consider: find that something ought to be known and therefore tell it
<thei>, able, and the sentence-final <hi> written as one word after a verb: closes a statement that something can be done or may happen
<thei>, can, and the question particle <hiam> written as one word: could it, how could it; closes an indirect question, as in {banghangin puakkham theihiam}, why it could explode

terms: before/in the presence of/with the knowledge of
definition: <theih>, know, with the ending <in>, placed after a possessive: with that person knowing, in the hearing or sight of; {mite’ theihin} is before people, openly
<theih>, be able, and the negative <kei> written as one word, after a verb and mostly before <leh>, if: {theihkei leh} is if one cannot
<theih>, know, with <khak>, happen to: come to know or learn something
<theih>, know, and <khialh.2>, wrongly, written as one word: understand wrongly; {ka theihkhialh kei leh} is if I am not mistaken
<theih>, know, with <khiat>, out: come to know by searching; the form used before a noun or <zawh>
<theihkhiat>, find out, with the noun suffix <na>: the act of finding out or coming to know something

terms: have come to know/know fully/finish learning
definition: <theih>, know, with <khit>, finished: {theihkhit ciangin} is after one has come to know, {theihkhit phetin} as soon as one knows

terms: have been able to/have managed to
definition: after another verb, <theih>, form of <thei>, can, with <khit>, finished: the action has been achieved, as in {aphelh theihkhit uhciangin}, after they were able to put it out; not the verb know of the other sense
<theihkhit> have come to know, with the noun suffix <na>: the fact of already knowing
<theih>, know, with <khol>, beforehand: know in advance
<theih>, know, with <kholh>, beforehand; {theihkholh lohin}, without knowing beforehand, means unexpectedly, suddenly
<theihkholh> know beforehand with the noun suffix <na>
<theih> able with <kik> again and the noun suffix <na>; {khua muh theihkikna} is the regaining of sight
<theih>, know, with <kim>, all: known to everyone, well known or in common use
<theih>, know, with <kim>, all: of everyone, come to know; also be known by all
<theih> know or able with <lam> way, manner; in the verse, that someone is able to know all mysteries

terms: come to know/get to know/learn of
definition: <theih>, know, with <lawh>, here gain as a result: come to know something through an event or through someone; {ki theihlawh} is get acquainted with one another
<theih> and <leh> written as one word: if one can; {ahih theihleh} is if possible
<theih> know and <lo> not written as one word: not knowing, not known, without someone knowing
<theih> and <loh> written as one word, the form of {thei lo} used before a noun or <ding>: after a verb, that cannot be done; alone, not knowing or what is not known
<theihloh>, not knowing, and <kalin>, while: while one does not know or notice, unawares; stands at the head of a clause or after a subject marker, as in {i theihloh kalin}, without our noticing

terms: so that it is not possible/to prevent from/lest
definition: <theihloh>, cannot, and <nadingin>, in order to: placed after a verb, so that the action cannot be done, to keep someone from doing it; the clause it closes gives the purpose of the main verb that follows; the negative of <theih nadingin>

terms: so as not to know/so as not to be able
definition: <theihloh> and <ding> written as one word after a verb: so that it is not known or cannot be done, as in {amuh theihlohding in}, so that he or she could not see
<theih>, know, <loh>, not, and <kal>, interval, written as one word: while someone does not know or notice; after a possessive and before <in>, as in {na theihlohkal in}, without your noticing

terms: because of not knowing/out of ignorance
definition: <theih> and <lohman> written as one word: because one does not know, or what comes only from not knowing
<theih>, know, with <loh>, not, and the noun suffix <na>: not knowing, ignorance; {theihlohna hangin} is through ignorance, unintentionally
after a verb, where <theih> means can and not know: not being able to do what that verb says, as <ihmut theihlohna>, being unable to sleep, and {lungkim theihlohna}, being unable to be content
plural of <theihlohna>; after a verb it names the things one is not able to do, as {na hih theihlohnate}, the things you cannot do
<theih>, know or be able, and <luat>, so very, written as one word: know something only too well; in some sentences be very possible
<theih> able with <ma> before, placed after a verb: before one could do it

<theih>, know, with the noun suffix <na>: what one knows, knowledge
the power to think and understand; {thu ngaihsut theihna} is good sense or discretion
<thei>, can, with the noun ending, after another verb: being able to do it; {theihna ding} or <theihna dingin> is so that it can be done, and {theihna lampi} is a way to do it

terms: so that it may be possible/in order to be able to
definition: <theihna>, here being able, and <dingin>, in order to: placed after a verb, so that it can be done; another way of writing <theih nadingin>

terms: so that they can/in order that they may
definition: <theihna>, here not knowledge but <thei>, be able, with <na>, and <dingun>, for them to: placed after a verb with <a> before it, so that they may be able to do it

terms: so as to be able to/in order to know
definition: <theih> and <nading> written as one word: after a verb, so that it can be done, in order to be able to; after a noun, in order to know it

terms: so that it can/in order to be able to
definition: <theihnading> and <in> written as one word after a verb: so that the action can be done

terms: so that one can/in order to be able
definition: <theih>, be able, with <nang>, a short form of <nading>, written as one word after a verb: so that it can be done, in order to be able to
plural of <theihna>, the things one knows; also the way one came to know something

after a verb, <theih> in its meaning can: the things one is able to do, or the possibility of doing them, as {hih theihnate}, what one can do, and {sepkhop theihnate}, being able to work together; not what one knows
<theih> know with <ngei> ever; with {nai lo}, have never yet known
<theihngei>, have ever known, with <loh>, not, written as one word before a noun: that one has never known
<theih> know, with <nop> want; the form used before a noun, as in {theihnop thu}, a thing someone wants to know
<theihnop>, want to know, and <leh>, if, written as one word; mostly {na theihnopleh}, if you want to know

terms: not want to know/unwillingness to know
definition: <theihnop> and <loh> written as one word: not wanting to know, set against <theihloh>, not knowing
<theihnop> want to know with the noun suffix <na>
<theihnop> want to know with the plural <te>; {thu theihnopte} are the matters people want to learn by inquiring
<theih> able with <pah> at once, placed after a verb: can do it right away
<theih> in its meaning know, not able, with <pah> at once: understand a thing immediately; the thing known stands before it, often ending in <lam>, and no other verb comes directly before {theihpah}

terms: know right away/be able right away
definition: <theih>, know or be able, and <pak>, quickly, written as one word: know offhand, or be able to do at once
<theih>, be able or know, and the topic marker <pen> written as one word: the fact of being able to do something, or what one knows, taken as the topic

terms: as soon as known/the moment it is known
definition: <theih>, know, and <phet>, as soon as, written as one word: {aki theihphet in} is as soon as it became known
know about a matter together with someone, so as to be a witness to it; {a theihpih mite} are the witnesses, and {theihpih lohin} is without the knowledge of
in the phrase {kisak theihpih}: be proud of something, boast in it
of a government or other authority: accept a body or a person as lawful and registered; {kumpi theihpih} before a noun is recognized by the government
<theihpih> and <lo>, not, written as one word: not know a matter along with someone, not understand what a person feels or does
<theihpih>, know of or recognize, with <loh>, not, written as one word: not known of or not recognized by the one named before it, as in {kumpi theihpihloh}, not recognized by the government
<theihpih> with the noun suffix {-na}: official recognition or acknowledgement, as given by a government
<theih>, know, with <sa>, which marks something already done: what one already knows or has come to know
in grammar, of a word that is not spoken or written because the hearer knows it already, as {kei in} in spoken style
in grammar, a subject that is not said because it is taken as known, as <Nang>, you, in the command {Hong tum ve}, come in; also called <nusiat a sempa>

terms: as we all know/known to everyone
definition: <theihsa>, already known, and <ciat>, each one: a thing that every one of us already knows; it follows <i> or <ih>, we, and closes a statement with {ahi hi}, or opens one as {ih theihsa ciat mah bang in}, just as we all know

terms: as we all know/known to everyone
definition: <theihsa>, already known, and <tek>, each one: what each of us already knows; stands after <i> or <ih>, we, and mostly before {mah bangin} or <mahbangin>, just as, to open a statement with a fact the reader knows
<theih>, know, with the causative <sak>: cause someone to know, make known, reveal or warn
<theihsak>, make known, and <ding> written as one word: to inform, that someone is to be told, often before <kisam>, it is necessary
<theihsak>, make known, with <na>: something that gives notice, such as a trumpet blast or a smoke signal; {theihsakna lim} is a sign

terms: want to make known/choose to reveal
definition: <theihsak>, make known, with <nop>, want: wish to make something known to someone; the form used before a noun

terms: wish to inform/intention to make known
definition: <theihsaknop>, want to make known, with the noun suffix <na>: the purpose of letting people know
<theih>, know, with <sasa>, already, written as one word: what or who was already known before

terms: try to know/seek to understand/find out
definition: <theih> and <sawm>, intend, written as one word: make an effort to know or learn about something
<theih>, know, with <siam>, skilled: grasp a matter rightly, or understand a person's situation with sympathy
<theih>, know, with <siam>, skilled, and the noun suffix <na>: the skill of knowing well, good judgment
<theih>, the form of <thei>, know, used before a suffix, with <suah>, bring out or become: make known; the page lists the form without a meaning

terms: as far as one knows/what one knows
definition: <theih>, know, with the ending {-sun}, the full extent, after <ka>, <na> or a pronoun: all that one knows, as far as one knows; {ka theihsun tawm} is the little that I know

terms: know by oneself/find out on one's own
definition: <theih>, know, with <tawm>, by oneself: come to know something by one’s own effort, without being told
<theihtawm> know by oneself, with the noun suffix <na>
<theih> with plural <te> after a verb: the things that can be so used; {tum theihte} instruments that are played, {nek theihte} things that can be eaten
in {mel theihte}, those known by face
<theih>, know, with plural <te>, after <a> or <ka> and not after another verb: the things or the people that someone knows or has learned, where {nek theihte} is of what can be done
<theih>, know, and <tek>, each, written as one word: each one knows, every one of us knows
<theih>, know, with <tel>, clearly: know thoroughly; also used as a noun, full knowledge
<theihtel> understand with <hak> hard
clear and full knowing of a matter
plural of <theihtelna>
<theihtel> understand with <nop> want
<theih> know with <teng> all, the whole of
<theih>, know, and <thamloh> written as one word, followed by <in>: without the other person noticing it
in the verse the horns that scattered Judah; probably a misprint of <thehthang> scatter
<theih>, know, with <theih>, be able
after a descriptive word: as much as possible; {hunsau theihtheih} is as long a time as possible
<theih>, know, said twice: know as a matter of common knowledge, not be able to know; {i theihtheih sa} is what we all know already

terms: so that it may somehow be possible/in order to be able to know
definition: <theihtheih>, <theih> said twice, and <nadingin>, in order to: placed after a verb, so that the action may by any means become possible, said of repeated effort or coaxing toward that end; after an object without another verb, in order to be able to know it
the ability to know
after a descriptive word, a way of being so as far as possible; {hun sau theihtheihna}, a means of making the time as long as can be

terms: so that it may be possible/so as to be able
definition: <theihtheihna>, here being able as far as can be, and <dingin>, in order to: placed after a verb, so that the act may be possible by whatever means, as {ngah theihtheihna dingin}, so as to be able to get
<theihtheih> with <sa> already done: what one has come to know

terms: worth knowing/that ought to be known

<thei>, fig or fruit tree, with {nah}, leaf: the leaf of the tree
<thei>, able, and <nai>, yet, written as one word and followed by <kei> or <lo>: not yet able to, cannot yet

terms: not yet know/not yet be able

<thei> and <nawn> written as one word, followed by a negative such as <lo> or <kei>: can no longer, or no longer know

terms: not know at once/not be able right away

<thumna>, third, written with a capital at the start of a sentence and in the place name {Ansai Thumna}, given in the NIV as Three Taverns
<thum> and <ni> written as one word: the third day; {Ni thumni}, the third day of the week, is the Bible name of Tuesday in the book's table
<thum>, beg, with <nop>, want; {kong thumnop thu} is the thing I wish to plead for, my petition
<thu>, matter, with <mong>, end: what a person comes to in the end, the outcome of a life
<thumong>, the end a matter comes to, with the plural <te>
<thum>, beg, with <sak>, do for another: ask or pray on behalf of someone

<thum> and <sung> written as one word after a word of time: for three hours, days or the like
<thum>, three, with the strengthening <tak> written as one word after a noun: three of them, as many as three
<thum>, three, with the plural marker <te>: a group of three already known
<thum>, three, with <teng>, here all of: all three of the ones just named, placed after the noun
<thum>, beg, doubled to show that the asking is repeated or urgent

<thumu>, seer, capitalised as a title with <pa> before a name: {Thumu pa Iddo}, Iddo the seer
<thu>, matter, with <muh>, see: seeing into matters, insight; used before <nading>
<thu> matter, <muh> see, <kholh> beforehand, with the noun suffix <na>: seeing matters ahead of time
<thumuh>, seeing into matters, with the noun suffix <na>: insight, understanding
<thumuhna>, what one sees or perceives of a matter, with plural <te>; of a prophet, the things seen in a vision
<thum> three with <un>, the plural ending on those who act: the three of them
<thumu>, seer, with the plural <te>
<Thumu>, seer, with the plural <te>; in the title of a book of records of the seers
<thum>, three, with <vei>, time; also the third time
<thumvei>, three times, with the ordinal suffix <na>: the third time, for the third time
<thumvei>, three times, with <ta>; {nisimin thumveita} is three times every day
put a liquid or other thing into a container such as a skin, a jar or a horn; used with <sungah>, into
put money into an account, a machine or a phone balance, after <sum>, money; {sum thunna} is the place where money is paid in, and the first sense is putting a thing into a container
put the ball into the goal in football, after <goal>; {goal tam a thun pen} is the one who has scored the most goals
<thu>, matter, with <nawngkai>, be troubled, written as one word: a troublesome matter, a problem, disturbance or incident that causes difficulty

terms: to refill/to top up/to put more in
definition: <thun>, put in, with a middle part meaning in addition as in {thun beh}, and <ding>, to, written as one word: in order to put more money into a cash machine
<thun> and <ding> written as one word: in order to put in, of fuel into a vehicle or money into a machine
<thun>, put in, and <dingin>, in order to, written as one word: in order to put in; {datsi thundingin} is to fill up with fuel
a matter that someone has against another, brought to be judged; <thu>, matter, with <nei>, have
a person who holds authority in a government, the police, an armed group or an institution, after words such as <kumpi> and <palik>; with <te> the authorities; not a matter brought to be judged
<thu>, word, with <neih>, have; {thuneih theihna} is power or authority

plural of <thuneihna>, authority
<thuneih>, have authority, and <nop>, want, written as one word; {thuneihnop luatna} is too great a desire for power

terms: have a dispute with/be at law with
definition: <thuneih>, have a case, with <pih>, together with; {na thuneihpih} is the one you have a dispute with
{thunei}, one who holds authority, compare <thuneite>, with <khat>, one, written as one word: an official or person in charge, of the police or another body
the man who holds authority over something; <palik thuneipa> is a police official or spokesman, and with {tung a} before it, the one who has power over something
{thunei}, one who has authority, with {-pi}, great or chief: the person who holds the highest authority in a country, an army, a hospital or an organisation
<thuneipi>, chief authority, with <pa> for a man: the man at the head, as {palik thuneipipa}, police chief; of God, sovereign
those who hold authority, from <thu> matter and <nei> have, with <te> plural; {ukna thuneite}, the governing authorities
those who have a matter or case, such as the two sides of a dispute
<thuneite>, the authorities, with the agent marker <in> shortened to <n>: the authorities as the ones who act or speak, as in {thuneiten gen hi}, the authorities said
<thu>, word, with <nem>, soft; {thunem tawh} and {thunem zangin} are gently
<thunem>, gentleness, with the linking ending <in>: gently
<thu>, matter, with <neu>, small: something of little weight or difficulty; {thuneu sa} is think it a small thing
<thuneu>, small matter, with the plural <te>
a bag carried on a journey or by a shepherd, named beside {dangka-ip}, the money bag
<thu>, word, with <ngai>, listen: listen to what is said and do it; {thungai lo} is disobedient
listen to a sermon or a speech as one of the audience, without the idea of obeying; {thungai mite} and {thungai dingte} are the listeners, as in <thungaite>
form of <thungai>, obey or listen, used before <ding>, <nading> and <lohna>; {thungaih lohna} is disobedience
<thungaih>, obey or listen, with the noun suffix <na>: obedience; {thungaihna ngah} is be heard
think matters over; {thungaihsun theite}, those able to think things through, are the discerning
thought given to a matter; {thungaihsut theihna}, the ability to think a matter through, is good judgment, discretion or understanding
<thungaihsut>, think a matter over, with the noun suffix <na>: a plan or purpose, planning
<thungaihsut>, thinking, and <zia>, manner, written as one word: the way a person thinks about things
<thungai>, listen to what is said, with the plural <te>: those who listen to the word
<thu> matter with <ngeek> infant, tender: the first and basic things; {leitung thungeek} is the elemental things of the world
<thu>, word, with <ngen>, ask: speak to God in prayer; {thungen ding} is to pray
<thungen>, pray, with the linking <a> written on to it: prayed and, praying
<thungen>, pray, and <ding> written as one word: to pray, going to pray
<thungen>, pray, with the linking suffix <in>: praying, or prayed and then
<thungen>, pray, with the noun suffix {-na}: a prayer, or the prayer as a part of a meeting; the same as <thungetna>
the things said, here by the seers; apparently <thu> word and <gen> speak with <nate>, written as one word

terms: those who pray/those who call on
definition: <thungen> pray with the plural <te>; {tua min tawh thungente} is those who pray in that name
<thu> word, <gen> speak, <teh> compare, with the noun suffix <na>: a saying told as a comparison
form of <thungen>, pray, used in dependent clauses and before endings; also as a noun, praying
<thunget>, pray, and <khopna>, doing together: prayer by several people together, a prayer meeting; often the object of <nei>, hold
<thunget>, pray, with the noun suffix <na>: a prayer, what is asked of God

terms: prayer is held/a prayer meeting is held
definition: <thungetna>, prayer, and <kinei>, here the passive of <nei>, have or hold: prayer is held, a prayer meeting takes place; the place with <ah> and the purpose with <adingin> stand before it
<thungetna>, prayer, with the plural <te>
<thu> and <ngetpih> written as one word: pray for someone or pray together with someone; also of the people one prays with
<thunget>, pray, with <sak>, do for another person: pray for someone
<thungetsak>, pray for someone, with the linking ending <in>
<thungetsak>, pray for someone, with the noun suffix <na>
<thunget> praying with the plural <te>: the things prayed; the NIV has what you are saying
<thunget>, pray, with <zia>, manner: the way to pray
a bag carried on a journey or by a shepherd
a bag worn on a strap over the shoulder; in the articles it glosses sling bag, backpack and handbag; compare <thung-ip> and <kuah>, strap on
<thu>, word or order, with <nial>, refuse, written as one word: refuse what one is told, defy an authority; also of one who is quick to contradict
<thu> and <nih> written as one word: two matters, two points
<thunih>, two matters, with the plural marker <te>: the two things spoken of
<thun>, put into a container, with the linking ending <in>; {a dimtakin thunin} is having filled it full
<thun>, put in, and <laitak>, while, written as one word: at the very time of putting in, as fuel into a vehicle
<thun>, put in or fill, and <man>, price, written as one word: the price paid for filling something, as a gas cylinder; in one article the word seems to be a misspelling of <thuman>

terms: filling/place for filling/thing for putting in
definition: <thun>, put into or fill, with the noun ending {-na}: the act, place or device of putting something in; {datsi thunna} is a petrol station and {sum thunna} a place for paying in money
<thu>, word or order, with <nolh>, refuse, and the noun ending {-na}: refusing to obey; {tangpi' thunolhna} is civil disobedience, the Zolai wording for CDM
<thun>, put into, and <sak.1> written as one word: put something into a container, or pay money into an account or fund, for someone or at their request
<thun> put into with <thuah>, add: fill a vessel with something, here oil into a lamp

terms: keep putting in/put in again and again
definition: <thun>, put into, said twice: go on putting or pouring something in, as water into a pot or money into a bank or a phone
<thu>, word or authority, and <nuai>, under, written as one word and followed by <ah>: under the rule, command or control of the one named before it
peace or good terms between people or with God; {thunuam gen} is proclaim peace and {thunuam-a biakna} is the fellowship or peace offering

terms: be good to/be kind to/be favourable to/be gracious to
definition: used with <tungah> for the person who is treated kindly
of a person's character, pleasant and easy to deal with, as in {mi thunuam}, a good-natured person, often with <mahmah>; a lasting quality, not kindness shown to one person with <tungah>
<thunuam> with the linking suffix <a>, describing the next noun; {thunuama biakna} is the fellowship or peace offering

what comes after a matter, from <thu> and <nung>; mostly in the pair <thunung thuma>, what follows a matter and what goes before it, all its ins and outs

<thunung>, what comes after a matter, and <thuma>, what comes before it: all that hangs on a matter, its consequences and further questions; {thunung thuma om loin} is without any more to it, without conditions
<thu>, matter, with <pai>, go: how a matter proceeds, mostly as {thupai zia} or {thupai dan}, the way things work; in some articles also a phrase or expression beside <laimal>, a word
<thu>, matter, and <paizia>, way of going, written as one word: how a matter proceeds, the proper order in which it is dealt with

<thu>, matter, with <patna>, beginning: the opening part of an article, sermon or speech
<thu>, matter, and <pawlkhat>, some, written as one word: some matters, a number of things to say or to know

<thu>, matter, with <phamawh>, serious, written as one word: a serious or urgent matter

<thupha> and <piakna> written as one word: the giving of a blessing, the benediction in a service

form of <thupi>, important, used before words such as <lam>, <sak>, <ngaihsut> and <luatna>; {a thupit lam} is how important it is

<thupitak> with <in>, written as one word: in a grand, solemn or important way

<thupi>, great or important, with the comparative <zaw>: greater, worth more; the thing compared is marked by <sangin>, than
<thu>, matter, and <poimawh>, important, written as one word
<thu> with <pom>, hold fast: what a person or a church holds to be true, a doctrine or conviction
the way a matter is held, from <thu>, <pom>, hold fast, and <zia>, manner: what a person or a church believes about something
<thupomzia>, belief or view, with the plural <te>: the beliefs or views a person holds
<thu>, word, with <puak>, carry or send: a message or news brought to someone, also an order sent; {thupuak pa} is a messenger
<thupuak>, message, with the noun ending {-na}: the sending of a message, or the message or statement sent out
<thupuak>, word that is carried, with the plural <te>: those who bring the message
<thu>, word, with <pulak>, make known: announce something to a gathering or to the public; in a programme also the heading for the one who makes the announcements; <thupulakna> is the announcement
<thu>, word, with <pulakna>, announcement: a public statement by an organisation or office; <thupulakna nei> is issue a statement

count something as a matter that counts; {ama thu bek thusa} is to regard only his own matter as important
a role in Zo custom: the person appointed to speak and advise for a household or clan in its affairs; <beh thusa> is the one of a clan
<thusa>, the spokesman of a household, and <geel>, both, written as one word: the two holders of that position taken together

plural of <thusa.2>: the persons who speak and arrange matters on behalf of a household in Zo custom
<thusate>, the spokesmen of the household, with the marker of the doer <in> shortened to {'n}
<thu>, matter, with <sau>, long, written as one word: a matter that is long or reaches far ahead; {thusau khual} is taking the long view
<thu>, word or matter, and <saupi>, very long, written as one word: a long thing to tell or think about; before another noun, long-term
<thu>, matter, with <seel>, argue: quarrel or dispute; {thuseel lo} stands where the NIV has will not quarrel; also written <thusel>

<thu>, matter, with <sia>, bad: evil that is planned, spoken or done; {thusia bawl} is do evil and {thusia geel} is plot evil

<thusia>, a bad matter, doubled with {lasia}, bad song, after the pair {thu le la}, word and song: bad things of every kind, evil happenings, wrongdoing and bad news; the opposite is {thu hoih la hoih}

<thusia>, evil matter, with <pi>, great: a grievous or bitter thing; here the bitter things sought against someone
<thusia>, bad matter, with the plural <te>: bad news, words that bring distress
<thu>, matter, with <sim>, count: pay regard to a person or thing, look on with favor; {thusim lo} is disregard or show contempt for

<thusim>, secret, with <nei>, have: one who keeps hidden motives, a hypocrite
<thusim nei>, hypocrite, with the plural <te>

<thusim>, regard, with <loh>, not, and the noun suffix <na>: contempt, treating someone with no respect

<thusim>, pay regard, with <sak>: give regard to a person or to what he does or says; {thusimsak lo} is take no account of

<thusim>, hidden matter, with <teng>, all of

<thusinna>, lesson or study, with the plural <te>

question a person who is held, as the police or soldiers do, sometimes with beating; {thusit thudotna} is an interrogation and {thusit thuak} is be interrogated, where the first sense is a trial in court
<thusit> and <ding> written as one word: in order to question someone or examine a case

<tong> cubit with <kua> nine, written as one word
village in Manipur in India
<tong> cubit with <li> four, written as one word

<ton>, draw together in folds, with the linking ending <in>; said of cloth

<tonkhawm>, go together, and <in> written as one word, after <tawh>: going along together with, in company with
<tonkhawm>, go together, with the plural <te>: those who travel along with someone

terms: go together with/accompany/keep in step with

<ton>, draw together in folds, with the noun suffix <na>; {sa tonna} is a wrinkle of the skin

have someone with oneself on a journey, take along; the person taken is the object
<tonpih>, take along, with the linking ending <in>
<tonpih>, go with, with <pa> marking a man: the man who is with someone
<tonpih> go with, with plural <te>: the people who are with one on the way
<ton>, accompany, with the causative <sak>: send someone along with others
<ton>, draw in, with the causative <sak>; with <kik>, back, it is draw a stretched-out hand back to the body
<tonsak>, draw in, with <kik> back: bring a stretched-out hand back to the body
Zolai name of Champhai, a town in Mizoram, India, near the border of Myanmar
<to>, lord or master, with <nu> marking a woman: a woman who is head of a household or has servants; also a queen, and a polite word for a lady
<tonu>, lady or mistress, written with a capital: the lady to whom 2 John is addressed, and Babylon speaking of herself as queen
<Tonzang> with the plural <te>: Tonzang and places like it, or the people of Tonzang
the English word tools used in Zolai sentences for implements and equipment, usually written with a capital
pick up things left lying: of grain, glean; of food, gather up what is left over; {van top} is take plunder
the English word top, written before a number for the best few in a contest or a list, as in {Top 5 teng}, the top five; not the verb pick up

<Topa>, Lord, and <Jesu>, Jesus: the title and name together, the Lord Jesus; {i Topa Jesu} is our Lord Jesus
<Topa>, Lord, and <Jesuh>, Jesus: the title and name by which Jesus is spoken of in sermons and church writing, often {i Topa Jesuh}, our Lord Jesus, and {Topa Jesuh Khrist}

terms: the Lord's favour/the Lord's face/God's grace

<Topa>, Lord, as a title before <Zeisu>, Jesus: the Lord Jesus, the usual way to name him in church writing
<Topa>, the Lord, with the possessive ending {'a}: belonging to the Lord
<to>, upward, and <pah>, at once, written as one word after a verb: the step up is made straight away
<Topa> with the subject marker <in> shortened to {-n}: the Lord as the one who acts, common in blessings

terms: the Lord bless/may the Lord bless
definition: <Topan>, the Lord as the one who acts, and <thupha>, blessing: opens the closing wish of a letter, article or speech, {Topan thupha hong pia ta hen}, may the Lord bless you; the one blessed stands before it
<topa> with the plural <te>; in the verses always in the title Lord of lords
a precious stone, the English name; one of the stones of the breastpiece of the high priest, where the NIV has chrysolite
<topaz>, a precious stone, capitalised in the text
the subject of a talk, a discussion or a paper
<top> glean with <sa>, already done: what has been gleaned
a violent whirling wind; often written with <huihpi>, storm, as {Tornado huihpi}
the largest city of Canada, in the province of Ontario
make strong and firm, said of the bars of a city gate
<to> upward with the causative <sak>, after a verb of movement: {paikhia tosak} is make someone go up out of a place
<to> dig with <suk>, downward, and the linking ending <in>
walk along a path or road, and so follow a way of life; the form of <tawn> used before a noun or <ding>, as in {tot lampi}, the path walked
wear an ornament stuck into the hair or headdress, such as a feather, <vamul>, or a flower, <tukpak>; not the verb walk
unit name for cotton: one roll of cotton, {pat hual khat}, is {tot khat}; what the word means apart from this is not clear from the page; not the verb walk
<to>, onward, and <ta>, here now or already, written as one word after a verb: the action has gone on and has now come to this point
<to> up with <tai> run; {a suktai a totai kawikawi} is running down and up, here and there
<to>, dig, with <tawm>, by oneself or for oneself: {tuikhuk totawm} is dig cisterns of their own

terms: pick on/pick a quarrel with/treat harshly
definition: speak or act in a quarrelsome way toward someone, named beside <neubawl>, belittle, and <kobawl>; compare <kitot>, quarrel
plural of <to>, master or lord: the masters of slaves or servants; {ka tote aw} is the polite address my lords, sirs
<to>, dig, with <te>, the people who dig
<to>, lord, with <thum>, three: the three persons of the one God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit
<tot>, walk along, with the noun suffix <na>: the act of treading or walking; {a totna mun} is the place where the foot treads, and {lampi totna} is walking in the ways of someone
<to>, upward, said twice and placed after a verb to show that an action or state goes on and increases
<toto>, onward, and the future marker <ding> written as one word; after a verb: will go on doing it, will keep doing it more and more
<toto> and <lai>, here still, written as one word after a verb: the action is still going on and increasing
<toto>, continually, and <laiding>, will still, written as one word after a verb: the action will be carried on further

terms: let us keep on/let us go on
definition: <toto>, on and on, with the ending {-ni}, let us, written as one word after a verb: let us keep doing it; at the end of a news item {Update totoni} is let us keep updating
<toto> and <thei> written as one word after a verb: the action can go on further; {ki behlap totothei} is may go on increasing

terms: walk with/lead along/take along a way
definition: <tot> and <pih> written as one word: walk a road together with someone, take someone along a path
<tot> with <sa>, already done: describes land or a path on which someone has walked
<tot>, walk a path, with the causative <sak>: make or let someone walk a path, used of bringing up children; {lampi maan totsak} is lead along the right path
<tot> walk along with the plural <te>: the paths one has walked, one's conduct
the business of receiving visitors who travel for pleasure; found mostly in headlines and in the names of ministries
a foreign visitor who travels for pleasure; mostly before another noun, as in {Tourist Bus}
the English plural used in Zolai news for people who travel for pleasure, often after <gamdangmi>, foreigner
a sports competition of several teams
<to> dig with <vang> hole: dig a hole through a wall
dig up the soil around a plant, with the connective ending <in>
an administrative division of Myanmar below the state or region, a town with the villages around it
English plural of township, the administrative division below the district in Myanmar, used in Zolai text without the plural <te>
<township> with the plural <te>, written as one word: the townships, the administrative districts of a state
a Japanese make of car
endure or go on longer than another; from one sentence and a dictionary entry

terms: on and on/as time goes on/onward
definition: <to> and <zel> written as one word after a verb: going on further and further; {hunpai tozel in} is as time went on
the movement of vehicles on a road; also short for the traffic lights, as in {Traffic khawlna}, the stop at the lights
a large goods lorry that pulls a trailer, also {Trailer mawtaw}
{trailer}, the English word, and <mawtawpi>, truck: a large truck that draws a long trailer; the usual name of this vehicle in reports of road accidents
a course of training for a job, a skill or military service

region south of Damascus and east of Galilee, ruled by the tetrarch Philip
Dutch airline; {Transavia Airlines}, {Transavia vanleng}

passing through a country or an airport on the way to another place; {Transit ding} is to pass through and {Transit Visa} a visa for passing through
the English verb used in Zolai sentences, often with <bawl> or <sak>: put a text into another language; writers also gloss {kaleh} and {kiteisawn} with it
openness of a government or an organisation about what it does, so that the public can see it
the carrying of people and goods, and the vehicles and roads for it; mostly in {public transportation}
a flat tray, in the articles the trays on which a shop lays out jewellery
medical care given to a sick or injured person, used beside {zatui bawl}
the testing of a medicine or vaccine on people
the hearing of a case in a court of law
a tribe, especially as an officially recognised group in India
Christian woman in Rome whom Paul greets as a worker in the Lord, named together with Tryphosa
Christian woman in Rome whom Paul greets as a worker in the Lord, named together with Tryphena
the number one million million, mostly of sums of money
the Christian teaching that God is one in three persons, in Zolai {tothum gawm khat}
state in the north-east of India
port city on the north-west coast of Asia Minor, where Paul saw the vision of the man of Macedonia
Christian from Ephesus who travelled with Paul to Jerusalem and was later left sick at Miletus
Christian woman in Rome whom Paul greets as a worker in the Lord, named together with Tryphena
a cart on wheels pushed by hand, for goods in a shop or bags at an airport
soldiers of an army, mostly written beside or in place of <galkap>
a cup or other prize object given to the winner of a competition
a large motor vehicle that carries goods, often written before <mawtawpi>
a great sea wave that floods the coast, usually after an earthquake; also explained as {tuipi zinlin} and <tuihualpi>
written abbreviation of <tangte>, verses
