<busa>, settle, with the prefix <ki>: of people who have moved, settle down and live in a place
<a> and <piasa> written as one word: the ones who have already given, in lists of donors
<ka> and <lam> written as one word: mostly in {kalam en}, I expect, where <lamen> is split by the writer; also I built, and my way or my direction

terms: not at all/by no means/not really
definition: emphatic negative placed after a verb, most often <hi>: it is by no means so, not really so, written {saamlo} or with a hyphen before the ending
<mai>, front, with the place ending <a> written on the word: in front of, in the presence of, ahead of
<suut>, go through point by point, with the prefix <ki>: of a history, a genealogy or a subject, be traced, set out or analysed
<keel>, goat, written short, with <sa>, meat: the meat of a goat
take or bring a person along to a place, lead the way for someone; {zi pui} is bring home a wife; in the articles also a part of personal names
<hausa>, chief, with the ending {-pi}, great: the principal chief or headman of a village, town or ward
a strongly scented garden herb whose leaves season soup, meat and fish and are taken as a home medicine; the English name of the plant is not settled by the articles
in songs and poetic prose with <kai>: the haze that draws across the hills in the dry season
said after <innsung> or <inn>: the circle of relatives who hold the customary roles in the affairs of a household, the family and its kin as an organised body
through the whole of life or through all generations, for ever, set against <khangkhat>, one lifetime; also written <khantawn>
<hizah>, this much, with the linking <a>, written as one word before a describing word or a verb: so, to such an extent as this
<Vuandok> with <pa>, man: the township officer as a person, a title of office
of a bomb, a grenade or a building: go off or be blown apart with a blast; {puaktam sak} is blow up
the hunt that the men of a village go on together on the morning after the Tual sacrifice of the <Sialsawm> festival, a custom of the old religion
town on the <Chindwin> in <Sagaing> Region of Myanmar, under British rule the seat of the Deputy Commissioner of the Upper Chindwin district
written iZomi: Zomi R&B and hip hop music group of three young men, formed in 2010 and based in <Tulsa> in the United States

<na> and <sung> written as one word: within you, inside you; in other sentences the noun ending {-na} of the verb before it is written onto <sung>, as {a om nasung pan}, from among those that there are
<pah>, at once, and the linking <a>, and, written as one word after a verb: does it at once, and then the next clause follows
<si>, blood, with <sitna>, test: a blood test, and the medical check that refugees and migrants take before resettlement
<hong> and <pang> written as one word; mostly in {ma hongpang}, which is <mapang>, contribute, with <hong> inside it: came forward to help with money or effort
<a> and <pawlten> written as one word: he or it and those on the same side as the doers of the action, as {US leh apawlten}, the US and its allies
putting into practice what has been said, planned or promised, action as against words
plural of <pawlmi>: the members of a group, association or church
<na> and <mit> written as one word: your eye, your eyes
<a> and <hampha> written as one word: the fortunate one, is fortunate
word of songs and poetry for <khut>, the hand or arm; {banzaal len} is hold hands
<uum>, surround, with <khawm>, together: sit together around one dish or table and eat from it, as in {ankuang uumkhawm}
the short line that joins two words or parts of a word in writing
the side where the sun rises, the east; {suahlam Zogam} is eastern Zogam
do what has been planned or agreed until it is done, carry it through
<palikte>, the police, with the subject marker <in> shortened and written as one word: the police, as the doer of the action
<hopsawn>, share and pass on, with the noun ending {-na}: the passing on to others of what one has learned or gone through, as an experience or good news
a number written as a figure, also the number of an item in a list or on a jersey
<khaak>, happen to, and <leh>, if, written as one word after a verb: if it should happen that, in case; with <ci-in> it gives the reason for a precaution
a body of ideas or the way a matter runs: writers gloss it as theory and, in {Pasian thuluan}, as theology; {thuluan zia} is the way a matter or a text runs
the comfort shown to a bereaved family by a group or its members, in words or as money; {gaalna sum} is condolence money
village of the Paite in the east of Mizoram, India, near Mimbung and <Hiangmun>
village in the east of Mizoram, India, between <Teikhang> and Mimbung
found only in the pair {vuihtheih khamtheih}, drugs and intoxicants, where it stands in the place of <guihtheih>
<teng>, dwell, with <den>, always: live in a place for good; in teaching on the Holy Spirit, dwell within the believer
<na> and <sinna> written as one word: your studies, what you learn
the raised open platform, <tau>, of the <innka> at the front of a traditional house, where people sit and talk
word of Paite and related speech for a thing or matter, where Tedim says <na> or <thu>; found in articles written in Paite
word of Paite speech for leaders, <heutu> with the plural <te>, where Tedim says <makaite>
the life a person or a people lives; {khotang hinkhua} is social life
country in West Africa
<kisai>, concern, with <a> written on to it: after <tawh>, {tawh kisaia} is concerning, that has to do with
<dah>, mourn, with <khawm>, together: share the grief of others; <tawh> marks those one mourns with
<vanlam>, the air, and <tawh>, with, written as one word: by air, said in war news of attacks made from aircraft
the English plural of <bishop>, used as written, often with the plural <te> after it
town in the north of Syria on the border with Turkey, fought over in 2014 and 2015
the cast of mind that a person or a people carries: {khuapimi lungpuak} is a civic mind and {minam lungpuak} the spirit of a people
apparently a verb for be worn out or spent, not the number <tul>, with <ta>, now: has become worn out, said of land that no longer bears and of strength; frequent in songs with <gam>, land
<hong> and <hilhna> written as one word: what it teaches us, the teaching of the church or of Scripture
expressive word placed after a verb such as <om> or <kizuak>, showing that there is a great deal of something or that it is found in large numbers
the traditional woven skirt, <nik>, of Zomi women, named beside <Zopuan>
<khasia>, be troubled in spirit, with the prefix <ki>: feel hurt or saddened by what has happened; {kikhasia sak} is upset someone

terms: as it is/as it really is
definition: <a>, <hi> and <bang> written as one word: as it is, in the way a thing really is, often followed by <in> or <lian>
word of songs, apparently the children of others, people not one's own: {singta gam} is a foreign land, the land of others
city and prefecture in the north-east of Japan, known for the nuclear power plant damaged in 2011

terms: be able to love/manage to love
definition: <it>, love, and <zo>, be able, written as one word: be able to love, go on loving; with <nawnlo> or <hetlo>, be unable to love
<i> and <mu> written as one word: we see, we find
<khaam>, forbid or hold back, with the noun ending {-na}: a prohibition or a thing that holds back; {nat khaamna zatui} is medicine that prevents illness
<a> and <kisuun> written as one word, after <tawh>, with: that which resembles, similar to
form of <tangsam>, lack, mostly written after a separate <ki> as {ki tangsap}, the same as <kitangsap>: be needed, what one needs
word of songs for <khuang>, the drum, named with the gong and the cloth of the forefathers; one writer derives it from <len> with {lensialki} and {lenpuan}
<Aizawl> and <ah> written as one word: in Aizawl, to Aizawl
<nong> and <hawh> written as one word: you visit us, you come to see us; found only in the closing line of one news site

terms: regard as good/look on with favour
definition: <hoih>, good, with <muh>, see: take a thing to be good; one writer sets it against {a hoihna mu}, see the good that is in a thing, and uses it of calling good what is not
coffee, the plant and its beans; {kaphi kung} is the coffee tree and {kaphi tang} the coffee bean
a gourd grown in the fields beside <mai.5>, the pumpkin, and eaten as a vegetable; when ripe its skin is covered with a white powder
a young unmarried woman, paired with <tangval>, young man; the same as <nungak>
<thumaan> and <thutak> written as one word: the truth, what is true and right

word of songs placed before <zuun> or <zom>, as {giabang zuun}, put a land or a people in order again, build it up; a comparison with <bang>, like, whose first part {gia} is not explained by the sentences
a town in the state of Assam in India, the seat of Eastern Theological College
the Mormon church, the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, and its members
<theih> and <tawp.4> written as one word: the most that can be done; {ka theihtawp in} is as best I can, and after a describing word, as {a manlang theihtawp in}, as quickly as possible
a city in Germany, the capital of West Germany from 1949
word of songs for <mual>, the hills and ridges on the skyline where the sun rises and sets; {lenmual dawn} is the hilltops
word of songs for <singkung>, a tree, as a list of song words explains it; {tulsing dawn} is the top of a tree
put things, goods or ideas of several people together in one place or into one whole
<Yangon> and <ah> written as one word: in Yangon, to Yangon
<si.2>, blood, with <sit.2>, examine: a test of the blood; of people leaving for another country, the medical examination before the journey
<simlei>, the world, with <vai.2>, affair: the affairs of the world, which writers explain as politics; also written {SimleiVai}
<a> and <liim> written as one word: its shadow or shade; in news writing more often its picture or image, set beside <athu>, the text
a bridge over a river or a gorge; {sikkhau leidawh} is a suspension bridge; also the name of a place in the Tedim area
<i> and <na.3> written as one word before a verb: we, with the particle that sets the action in an earlier time, as {ina om hi}, we were
<cih.2> and <peen> written as one word after a statement or question: as for the matter that, marking the whole clause before it as the topic
the planet Saturn; also the Roman god after whom Saturday is named, and a kind of American space rocket
<ka> and <om> written as one word: I am, I stay; before a noun, where I am

terms: long for/miss/want more/be loath to part
definition: feel that one has not had enough of a person or of a good time: miss someone, long for more, be unwilling to stop or leave; paired with <iplah> and <ngaklah>
word of songs for <sum> and <dangka>, money, as a list of song words explains it; {sesum minthang} is wealth and fame
placed after a verb of shining, rising or seeing: bright and clear to the eye, as the sun that rises or glows red, or an aim seen plainly
a village of the Tedim area, in the Tungzang village tract
a village and village tract in the Simzang area of the Tedim region, named after its first headman
the act or place of rolling up or gathering together; {kha hualna} is the rite of calling and binding the souls of a married couple at the Ton feast, and {kithu hualna} is agreement
an exclamation of dismay, pity, longing or surprise, a fuller form of <kalai>
to fly away to another place, as a bird does; commonly said of people who leave to resettle in another country
a lit torch carried at night, and the carrying of it; {khuahaang meide} or {khuasia meide} is a will-o'-the-wisp, a ghost light

terms: in the long run/after a long time/eventually
definition: usually as {a sawtteh}: as time goes on, in the end
one who teaches or preaches, chiefly a teacher of religious doctrine
plural of <laisiam>: those who are educated or good at study

terms: pleasant to talk with/enjoyable in conversation
definition: pleasant to talk with; also said of people talking happily together

terms: act separately/go one's own way/stand apart
definition: to act apart from the group instead of together with it

terms: all the siblings/all the relatives/brothers and sisters
definition: <sanggam> with <teng>, all: the whole circle of brothers, sisters and relatives
<i> and <suah> written as one word: we become, we turn into
a region of South Asia, a state of India and a province of Pakistan
adverb of small degree or size, as in {neu ciuciau}, tiny, and {hi ciuciau lel}, to be merely
to have the advantage or benefit of something
<a> and <kidang> written as one word: that is different, that differs
the charismatic revival movement that came from Mizoram, Mizo hlimsang, and its followers, found within several churches, marked by ecstatic dancing in worship
plural of <minampih>
to be poisoned by something eaten or drunk, or to be poisonous
the people who come from Dim village, {Dim Khua}, and their descendants

terms: driving out of evil spirits/spirit chasing
definition: the driving of evil spirits out of house and village with torches and noise at the Khuado festival
taking part in or attending another's occasion in support; {ki uapna} is attending one another's feasts and funerals
the large valued bead of the traditional Zomi necklace, counted as {khipi tang}, a bead, and {khipi gui}, a string
the Korean autumn harvest festival, compared in the articles to the Zomi Khuado festival
a village, in English spelling usually Khuangleng, whose warriors fought the Laaitui people in the nineteenth century
those who were among the first to do something
a bird; the form of <vasa> with its parts in the other order, said in the articles to be the usage of Mizo and other dialects
a higher or further step, an advance; mostly in {kalsang suan}, to take a step forward
word of songs and poetry, literally like salt, used with <dah> for deep grief and with <mang> for being lost
to clap the hands, and the clapping itself
<lut> and the particle <ta> written as one word: has now entered, has joined
to manage the use of time; at a meeting or programme, to act as moderator or master of ceremonies, and the person who does so
<hi>, be, and the particle <tazen> written as one word, placed after a verb or describing word and before <hi> or <uh>: it really is so, it actually is so, said with surprise or reproach
plural of <gualzawhna>: victories, and the things a person has achieved
<ci>, say, and <giap>, outright, written as one word after the words quoted: say it firmly and without holding back
<en>, look, and the ending <lehang>, if we, written as one word: if we look at, when we consider, used to bring in an example or a point of view
<om>, be, and the emphatic particle <se> written as one word, mostly before <lo>: {omse lo} is there is none at all, there is no such thing
the air force of a country, named beside the army and the navy
<tu>, this, and <hunteh>, at the time, written as one word: at this time, nowadays, often set against <nidang>, formerly
<a> and <kaang> written as one word: white, the white one; {avom akaang}, the black and the white, is said of all kinds without distinction and of how a matter really stands
<la>, song, with <dawng>, the counting word for songs: a single song or poem as one composed piece
name of a Zomi news magazine published at Aizawl in Mizoram, taken from the name of the bird
a bird of the Zo hills whose loud repeated call is heard in the dry season and towards evening, named beside {tangawm} or <tawlawk>; the species is not determined
of a person or a way of thinking: like someone from a remote village, unpolished, narrow and behind the times; also such a person
<gam>, country, with <seh>, part: one of the states or provinces into which a country is divided, as Shan State or Queensland; a word of a few writers for what is mostly called state
a thorough overturning of the order and way of thinking of a society, the word one writer uses for English revolution; its last part is <lumleh>, turn over, with the noun ending {-na}
<lah>, show, and <pakding>, to do briefly, written as one word and mostly followed by {-in}: to show it briefly, for example; a word of one writer, who also shortens it to {lpd}
<tangko>, proclaim, with <pih>: make a message or a cause known to people, speak up publicly for it; {a tangkopih pawl} are those who campaign for something
<tonkhop>, go together with, with the noun ending {-na}: going along together with someone, as in {Pasian tawh tonkhopna}, walking with God
town and district in the Magway Region of central Myanmar, on the Ayeyarwady river
name of a Linux operating system for computers, made by the company Canonical

<taang>, millet, with <tang>, seed: a single grain of millet; the saying {taangtang phelhawm}, split a grain of millet and share it, from the tale of Thang Ho and Lian Do, stands for sharing even the least thing in love
a dictionary, mostly as {tongdot bu} with <bu>, book; in old songs the word is also found of spoken words
<beh>, clan, and <khat>, one, written as one word: one single clan, people of the same clan or kin; also said of things that are of one kind
plural of <Kuki>: the Kuki people
<minam>, people, with <neu>, small: a people that is small in number within a country, an ethnic minority
city near Tokyo in Japan and the international airport of Tokyo that lies there
a traditional Zomi woven cloth with its own pattern, worn by men and given as a mark of honour, named beside <Puanlaisan> and {Tualpuan}; also shirts and coats sewn from it
a traditional Zomi feast of several days in the old religion at which much <zu>, beer, is drunk, named beside the {Ton} feast and the feasts {gal aih} and {sa aih}
<thum>, three, with <gawm>, join: three joined in one, said of God as Father, Son and Holy Spirit, {thumgawm Pasian}, the triune God; alone it stands for the Trinity
help given to those in need, above all money or goods given as aid; it is used as <huhna> is and may be the same word in another spelling
after the name of a pest or of what is guarded: keeping birds, insects or mosquitoes away, or a means of doing so, as {vasa hunna}, something against birds, and {lo hunna}, the guarding of a field
the sugar cane plant and its sweet stalk; {kawltu tui} is cane juice
city in the Philippines, named for the seminaries where Zomi pastors studied

word of the custom {ngawk sat} of the Khuado feast, for which the young men gather at their youth house at midday and then wrestle, and of the call {ngawk ngawk e} that the elders of the house raise first; what the word itself names is not clear from the texts
city in Libya, in the news of the war against IS
a frog, written beside <uiphuk> as another word for it
word of songs and love poems for the heart or mind as the seat of longing and thought, from <lung>, heart
the separate gate or opening of a traditional Zomi house by which the mithun and cattle go into their pen under the house, from <sial>, mithun, and <kong>, door
placed after a verb: after sit, ride or set on top, up high where all can see; after say or record, openly and plainly
<nasep>, work, with the ending {-pi}, great or chief: the main work or chief task of a person or body
<kikum> and <ding> written as one word: will discuss, are to confer about
<tam> and <simsim> written as one word: quite many, a considerable number
{a zat beh toh} written as one word: use a thing further, go on using it beyond the time first agreed; it begins with <azat> and ends with <toh>
silk thread and what is made of it, from <khau>, thread; in the notices {Zodial naikhau} is a Zomi scarf of silk
<gam> and <ten> written as one word: the countries, as the doer of the action

terms: go one's own way/stand apart/be self-willed
definition: keep to one's own way or opinion apart from the others and not join in with them; {thu tangpek} is one who is self-willed in a matter

terms: not at all/nowhere near/by no means
definition: <deksuai> and <lo> written as one word, after a verb or describing word: not at all, far from it
a level or flat piece of land among the hills, from <mun>, place
<kik> and <lo> written as one word, after a verb: not again, not back; {nung kiklo} is not turning back and {dawng kiklo} is not answering
<ki> with <zik>: of a road, a path or the site of a village, be laid out and made
<lo>, field, and <bang>, like, written as one word, a comparison of songs and sayings: {lobang tul} is grow old and worn out like a used field, and {lobang khual} is care for as for a field
<a> and <lianbel> written as one word: the greatest, the highest; {Alianbel Siampipa} is the High Priest and is also said of the Pope
only in the pair {sanpi sanno}, illness great and small, which the texts explain as {natpi natneu}; see <sanno>
<san>, red, with the ending {-pi}, great: of a robe or garment, deep red; apart from this the word is a personal name
<zaw>, more, and <a>, and, written as one word at the end of a clause that another clause follows
{Kawl galkap} written as one word and with long vowels: the army of Myanmar or its soldiers
ending of colloquial speech placed after the verb at the end of a statement, giving it emphasis or feeling; it holds the word <cia> of the same use
the bank of earth that stands above a road on its uphill side, where the road is cut into a slope; from <lam>, road, and <phung>, bank
<palai>, envoy, with the ending {-pi}, chief, written with long vowels: the ambassador of a country, also the chief representative of a state or body
a Zomi village of the Tedim area, named with Dimpi, Dimlo and Suangpi and written after the names of people who come from it
live or act at the side of others and in dependence on them, as a small people does in the land or the party of another; also one who so depends; from <pang>, side, and <bel>, cling to
<hel> and <loh> written as one word: not mixed in, not included, left out; {tui helloh} is undiluted, pure
<hong> and <kihel> written as one word: come and take part, join in
<nih>, <leh> and <thum> written as one word: two or three, a few
<nga>, fish, and <bang>, like, written as one word, a comparison of songs: {ngabang leng} is live and play happily together like fish in the water
<pom>, hold, with <siam>, skilled: know how to accept a thing and take it in good part, whether criticism, a loss or a chance
<in>, placed after the doer or after a verb, and the following <hong> written as one word
exclamation of colloquial speech: at the start, hey or oh; written after the last word of a statement with a hyphen, it gives the statement feeling
<kinaih> with the ending {-na}: the state of being close or akin, of persons, peoples or languages
a cool gentle wind, from <huih>, wind, and <dam>, cool
poetic word of songs and laments for the face or looks of a loved person, as in {na sakmel muh ding}, to see your face
<kisin>, practise or learn, with its last part said twice: go on practising or learning over a length of time
<a>, its, and <tong> written as one word, the second word of the pair {azia atong}: the ways and character of a person or a thing
<a> with <tong>, here a form of the verb for holding the traditional feast of merit: one who has held the feast, {atong lote} those who have not
word of traditional songs for a bamboo that grows in clumps at the edge of the village, a picture of people growing and thriving together, the last part is <gua>, bamboo
poetic word of songs for a young person or the time of youth, mostly in {seino gual}, young companions, and {ka seino lai}, when I was young
<i>, we, and <siam>, be skilled, written as one word: we know how to, we are good at
the English word used in Zolai articles for the movement and thinking that seeks equal standing for women, explained as {numei lapsangna}
<bual>, bathe or wallow, with the ending {-na}: the place of bathing or wallowing, {tui bualna} is a swimming pool or bathing place
poetic word of songs for the many people, the whole company, often after <mi>

terms: up to standard/on a par/abreast of others
definition: <gual>, peers, with <ban>, reach: reaching the level of others, up to the standard of the time, said of work, music, a town or a way of thinking
<gelhsak>, have something written, and <nop>, want, written as one word: want a letter or paper to be written for one
<nun>, life, with <lui>, old: the life one lived before, former ways, the days gone by, {nunlui sial} is recall the past
<kau>, the harmful spirit of the old belief, and <nei>, have, written as one word: a person or family said to keep such a spirit, feared and avoided in marriage
<ma>, front, with the <bang> of song language, before verbs of striving and beginning such as <pang>: go forward, press on or make a beginning together
word of song language placed before <khang>, grow, with the comparing <bang>, like: {kilbang khang} is grow up well, thrive and increase, said of children, a people or a land
<gawmkhawm>, put together into one, with the linking <in>: joining or combining things, and so doing what follows
<simsim>, rather or fairly, with the plural <te>, after a describing word: those who are fairly so, as {gol simsimte}, the rather large ones
<sim>, read, said twice, with the plural <te>, after <lai>: those who read much or keep on reading
<zah>, amount, and <tek>, each, written as one word after a verb: as much as each one wants or is able
the people of a village or a people as a body and their common life, {khuatang nuntakzia} is social life and {khuatang kipawlna} civil society
<neih>, have, with an ending that means leaving behind: take another wife, husband or lover and so leave the one that one had, after {zi dang}, {pasal dang} or {lawmnu dang}
<guai>, the word of address to equals, with the plural <te>: friends, said at the end of a sentence or as {guaite aw}
former province of China east of Tibet, the region of Kham, named in an article on where the Zomi came from as the Sikang-Tibetan Plateau
the English title of the person who calls and leads a committee, written before or after a name in lists of office bearers
<na>, you, and <san>, the form of <sang>, receive, written as one word: you receive or accept, as {thupha nasan}, you receive blessing
placed after a noun to mark an extreme or unexpected case, the same as <nangawn>
the Burmese word for politics, the affairs of state and party, set against the work of the church in the articles
a village in the township of Kalaymyo, one of the places that received rice after the floods
<tui>, water, with a second part that means go under: covered by flood water, said of houses, villages and valleys, {tuitup cip} is completely under water

the yearly rite of the old religion in which the village honours its guardian spirit at the <tual>, also called {Tualbia}, kept with a village taboo and at the same time as <Sialsawm>, {Tualbawl kha} is the month in which it falls
<upa>, leader, with <phual>, place: the office of an organisation or of the authorities, a word of some writers who gloss it with English office

terms: opening day/first day of a feast
definition: the day on which a traditional feast begins, as the first day of <Khuado> and the day the mithun is killed at a feast of merit, said as {pansik ni}
a traditional Zomi garment of plain cotton worn by men, named with <Puanlaisan> among the cloths of the people
<dawi>, demon, and <lut>, enter, written as one word: the state of being possessed by a spirit, or a person in that state
cook grain soft, alone or with meat, and the dish so made, as {taksih nganhuan}, the grain dish eaten with meat at the old feasts, and {aksa nganhuan} with chicken
be at ease in spirit, feel safe and content, often as {khalum tuam}, feel relieved, and {khalumna} is comfort
in news reports after a number of people: lose their lives, be killed, set beside <liam>, be injured

<lawm>, friend or companion, and <ding>, to be, written as one word: one who is to be a friend or companion, {khansung lawmding} and {khantawn lawmding} are a partner for life, a future husband or wife
<panmunlen>, office bearer, with the plural <te>: the people who hold the offices of an organisation
rank of an officer of the army, police or civil service shown by two pips, a lieutenant, the step below <bawkthum>
the Japanese form of wrestling, in {sumo kimawlte}, sumo wrestlers, and {sumo kibuan}, wrestle sumo; a Japanese word

terms: make a living/earn a living/seek a livelihood
definition: seek what one eats, from <nek>, food to eat, and <zong>, seek: work for a living, or the living so made
<khin>, finished or already, and the linking <a> written as one word: stands after a verb, the action is already done, and the sentence goes on
plural of <tangta>, in the pair {tangpi tangtate}, the general public

a small bird that comes in the cold season and is known for its bobbing, dancing walk, named in songs as a sign of winter; probably the wagtail; Lailen is also the name of a village in the story of Liando
of the weather, fine and clear, without cloud or rain; said when the rain clouds have gone, the opposite of <khuasia>; Khuapha is also the name of a village
<hong> and <sat> written as one word: found a village or pitch a camp, strike or beat; of the sun, beat down, and of the clock, strike the hour
<ong> and <nei> written as one word: come to have, as children or land, or hold, as a speech or a wedding
<na> and <lungsim> written as one word: your heart, your mind
plural of <zinmang>: the invited guests of a festival or conference
<ong> and <kipan> written as one word: begin, set out from
<a> and <dikna> written as one word: his righteousness, or what is right in something; known from the verse on seeking the kingdom of God and his righteousness
<nui>, laugh, with the prefix {ki-}: people laugh, a company laughs together, often followed by a word painting the sound such as <ziahziah>
said with the prefix {ki-} and <tawh>, with: be contrary to, go against, be at odds with; apparently a picture from <keel> <ki>, the horns of a goat, which point apart
<nei> and <in> written as one word and shortened: having, and with that; the same as <neiin>
word of songs for the people in their hundreds, the multitude, from <mi>, people, and <za> in its meaning hundred; Miza is also the name of a village with a school
a village and quarter of Lamka, Churachandpur, in Manipur, India, and the stream of the same name
<tulaitak>, now, with the linking <a> that joins it to the following word: the present, the one of now
<nitumna>, west, and <lam>, side or direction, written as one word: the west, the western side of a place
stands after a describing word: thin, sparse or of little account, as hair growing thinly, land lying bare, or a place that is only a tiny village, {khuano thilthel}
word painting the manner of something small or of one who acts alone and quietly: {neu keukeu} is very small, {tai keukeu} is scamper along, {om keukeu} is stay all by oneself
<kikeuh>, at all, and <lo>, not, written as one word: stands after a verb, not in the least
plural of <Vaphual>, the great hornbill, emblem of the Zomi
being old or senior, the form of <upa> used before another word: {upat khit ciangin} is after growing old, {kum upat} is advancing age, and {upat bawlna} is treating someone as an elder, respect
<mah> and <tek> written as one word, after <kua>: {a kua matek} is each and every one, everyone without exception, common in greetings and appeals
<hilel>, be only, and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word: ends a statement, it is just that and nothing more
<gal>, <le> and <sa> written as one word: enemies and wild animals, the two dangers of life in the old villages
<mun>, place, with <lui.2>, old: the place where a village or building once stood, as {khua munlui}, an old village site
act in a film or play, perform a scene; from the Burmese word for show, which is also the first part of {piah-ta-na}, problem, and {piahzat}, a play
<khia>, out, and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word: ends a statement after a verb of saying, coming forth or beginning, as {pulak khiahi}, announced
<hi>, be, and <leltak>, merely, written as one word: it is just that, it is simply so, said with some feeling

terms: since the time of/from the generation of
definition: <khang.3>, generation, and <pan>, from, written as one word: {pupa khangpan} is since the days of the forefathers
in the night just past, from <zan>, night; often {zantak in}
in {zantak an}, the staple food, the food that a household mainly lives on, such as maize or millet
island country in the Atlantic Ocean, north of Cuba
<sa>, here already done, with the emphatic <mah>, written as one word after a verb: just as already said, hoped or done, and with <in> all the while doing so
<denciang>, later, with the marker <in>, written as one word: later on, in time to come
<kamkum>, talk over, with the noun suffix {-na}: a talking over of a matter, a conversation, or formal talks between parties
the people of Nepal and those of that descent living in India and elsewhere, and their language
a wide stretch of worked fields, <lo>, field, with <zau>, spread wide; with the name of a crop before it, land planted with that crop
make a matter or a people greater, better, wider or more important than it was, bring it forward
<ka>, I, with <seh>, set or assign, written as one word: I count someone or something as such, after a phrase ending in {-in}; with <uh> also we have appointed
<sun>, here take after or be a copy of, with the linking <a>, written as one word after {lim leh mel}, image and likeness: bearing the image of, made after the likeness of
<sun>, daytime, with the place marker <a>, written as one word: during the day
<hong>, toward the speaker or the place spoken of, with <kuan>, set out, written as one word: set out and come for a task
<ahih>, its being so, with <ban>, what comes on top, written as one word and followed by <ah>: besides being that, on top of being that
the milk of a goat, {kel}, goat, with <nawi>, milk; compare <bawngnawi>
<khangkhia>, arise or grow up, with the causative <sak>: make a leader arise for a people, or bring a child up
the highest part of something, as the ridge of a roof or the top of the world; also the name of a mountain and a stream near Saizang
go to another village or land to get food in a time of want, as the brothers of Joseph went to Egypt; also said of the people who go
name of several cities in the United States, among them the capital of Illinois, the home of Abraham Lincoln
do a thing in deed and bring it to completion, not only speak or plan; {a semsuah makai} is a leader who gets the work done with his people
leaning to one side like a scale that tips, said of a teaching, a belief or a way of seeing that holds only one side of a matter
<zuun>, tend and put in order, with <ding>, to or for, written as one word: to be maintained, for putting in order
<Tedim> and <khuapi>, town, written as one word: the town of Tedim
<tai>, run, and <kidemna>, competition, written as one word: a running race
<pu>, grandfather, <leh>, and, and <pate>, fathers, written as one word: the forefathers of a people
country on the west coast of South America
a kind of <khi>, necklace, of the Zomi, a costly ornament and heirloom named beside <khipi>
the prefix <a> with <madawk>, at the front, written as one word: the one out in front, a leading or pioneering person or thing
<khang>, grow, to the full: of a child, come of age; of a believer, grow to maturity, beside <picing>; of a disease, reach its full stage

terms: think of for/be considerate toward/look out for
definition: <khual>, be considerate of, with <sak>, for another: keep the good or the future of someone in mind and act for it
<khutlet>, take by the hand in greeting, with the prefix {ki-}, each other: shake hands with one another
word of songs and poetry, <mu>, here hawk or kite, with <bang>, like: mostly before <ngai>, long for, of deep longing for parents, home or a loved one
the opening at the bottom of the body; also a hole in the bottom of a thing, see the second sense

terms: with a hole in the bottom/holed
definition: placed after the name of a pot, a container or trousers: having a hole in its bottom or seat
a village of the Tedim area, named in a list of Zomi villages and after the names of people from it
the clear, wholesome water of the Zo land, a word of songs; also the brand name of bottled drinking water made by Zomi in Kalay
<mi>, people, and <lakah>, among, written as one word: among other people, in public
the head of a government department, of a state government or of an army, a title placed after the name of the state, department or army
of a shirt or jacket, having short sleeves, the opposite of <bansau>, long-sleeved
<hong> and <kisang> written as one word: be accepted, said by the side that receives
<sap>, call, and <man>, price, written as one word: what is paid for a telephone call
after <inn>, house: the money paid each month for a rented house or room
<kaal>, week or interval, and <sung>, in, written as one word: within a week, as {tu kaalsung}, this week, or during a span of time

terms: make known to us/let us know/reveal
definition: <hong> and <theisak> written as one word: make something known to the speaker or to us
<kihel>, be mixed, and <zau>, spread wide, written as one word: mix freely with one another, said of peoples, languages and good and bad things
the country of Egypt, in the spelling of older Bible translations
<kham>, gold, and <khuk>, pit, written as one word: a gold mine, also said of the mines in Burma where young men went to work
<a> and <tatak> written as one word: the real thing, and with <in> after it, in truth, actually
<ki>, horn, and <li>, four, written as one word, in the folk tale name {sial kili nei}, the mithun that has four horns
a town in Texas, USA, where a Zomi community lives
<zek>, spend, with the prefix {ki-}: of money, be spent or paid out for a purpose
<tuambawl>, treat differently, with the prefix {ki-}: treat one another as different, keep apart from others, or of a thing be made separately
the particle <na> before a verb and <muak>, welcome, written as one word: welcomed, came out to meet
a team ball game played indoors, in which Zomi youth teams take part in Asian championships
meat or vegetables boiled plain in water in the Zo way, without oil; {aksa Zohuan} is chicken cooked so

terms: stretching out/in a wide view/spread out
definition: placed after a verb of seeing or appearing: of a land, haze or cloud seen spread out far and wide, or of a thing seen clearly before the eyes
<va>, go and, and <kihel>, be among, written as one word: go and take part in a meeting or event
<van>, goods, and <thak>, new, written as one word: newly bought or newly made things
<van>, heaven, and <thak>, new, written as one word: the new heaven, said together with the new earth
<pua>, carry, and <zo>, be able, written as one word: be able to carry a load, or to bear wealth, poverty or fame
a place where a stream falls over a cliff; {tui zeu} is the falling water
<dat>, substance, with the plural <te>: the substances that a food, the body or the soil contains
the act of pushing a person or group aside as worthless, or the state of being so rejected

terms: the way it is/how it is/that it is
definition: <ahih>, its being, and <dan>, manner, written as one word: how something is, or the fact that it is so, after a clause that states it
the pressing of a way of thinking into the minds of people by a ruling power, glossed in the articles as brainwashing
the place where a person was born and grew up; {a lamkiatna gam} is his native land
<ten>, the plural with the marker of the doer, and <bel>, as for, written as one word: placed after a noun to say what that group for its part says or does, often in contrast
<thukhenmang>, judge, with the male ending {-pa}: the judge of a court
<a> and <tenna> written as one word: his, her or their dwelling place, the place where they live
a rocket or shell fired in war, in news of fighting
a solid piece of iron for a smith to forge; also said of the fuel rods of a nuclear reactor
<i>, our, and <pawlpi>, church, written as one word
<anneek>, eating, with the noun ending {-na}: the eating of a meal, or the food eaten; {anneekna khan} is a dining room
<tenkhop>, live together, with the noun ending {-na}: the living together of people in one house, or of different peoples in one town or country
<zawl>, sweetheart, and <lui>, old, written as one word: the person one used to court
<pai>, go or come, and <teh>, when, written as one word: when someone goes or comes

terms: be put on/be printed on/be included/be given a ride
definition: <tuangsak>, put on, with the prefix {ki-}: of words or a picture, be placed on a book, banknote or page, or be included in a law; of people, be let ride in a vehicle
<pom>, embrace, and <cip>, tightly, written as one word: hold a person tight in the arms; also hold fast to a name or an idea
<ankam>, mustard, of the kind that forms a round head: cabbage; the articles also use it for the cabbage family as a whole, with broccoli and cauliflower
a country in South America
<kong>, door, and <mai>, front, written as one word: the place in front of the door of a house, church or hall
<na>, you, and <sap> written as one word: you call or summon someone; with a room, a house or a helper, you rent or hire
the Korean dish of salted and soured cabbage, eaten with rice
the people of <Sihzang>, the name with the plural <te>
<kikhen>, be separated, and <kik>, again, written as one word: of people, part from one another again; of a thing, be divided further
<kikhen> in its meaning be printed, and <kik>, again: of a book, be printed again
the name of a Zomi restaurant in Malaysia, below the office of the Zomi Association of Malaysia; the name is also used in writing as a poetic word and as the title of a series
<a> and <theihlawh>, come to know, written as one word: he, she or they get to know something as a result
a village in Champhai district of Mizoram, India, where speakers of Tedim live
<masuan>, head for, with the prefix <ki>: set one's course and go forward, on a road or toward an aim in life
placed after a verb, <taleh>, even if, in the form for we, compare <lehang>, if we: even if we do so, wherever or however much we do
<kai>, pull, with the prefix <ki>, written with a long vowel: of tax, be levied; {kikaai khawm} is be gathered together and {kikaai awk} is be caught up or entangled
the English word agency with the Zolai plural <te>: agencies, as those that resettle refugees or that send workers abroad, and news agencies
a village and border market beside <Tamu> in Sagaing Region, Myanmar, at the crossing to Moreh in India
<khet>, print, and <sak> written as one word: print a book for someone, or have it printed
a group of people chosen to deal with a matter, the English word in Zolai spelling
<puah>, repair, and <to>, upward, written as one word: mend a thing and make it better than before, said of customs, a way of life, software or a person
<biang>, cheek, and <ah>, at, written as one word: on the cheek, mostly of tears; after a word for a door or gate, at its side
<na> and <huh>, help, written as one word: you help; with <na> in its meaning of an earlier action, he, she or they helped
the <Sialkal> hill range in the north-east of Mizoram, India, home of the Tedim and Paite speaking people of that state
a traditional food of <taang>, millet, cooked for feasts such as the Khuado festival, pressed into lumps with the hand and eaten with meat; cooking it is {taksih nganhuan}
the reading of a text before printing to find and correct its mistakes
the English pop group of the 1960s
<dawilawm>, demon, and <nei>, have, written as one word: a person who is said to have a spirit as companion
<taang>, millet, boiled soft as a porridge, often together with chicken or pork; {vaimim ciim} is the same dish made of maize
<siat>, thrust, and <in> written as one word: sticking a thing into or onto something, as a torch on the tip of a bamboo or a tree
a camp and place at the front in France where the men of the Chin Labour Corps arrived in August 1917, in the spelling of the articles
form of <luikhia> used before endings and before the noun it describes: bring a matter, a piece of writing or food out before others
word of songs for the moon, <solkha> with {-pi}, great; {tung solkhapi} is the moon above
placed after a describing word or a verb and before the closing word, it seems to strengthen it in a lively way: {lum heha} is nice and warm, {nam heha} smells strongly
word of songs, <thei>, fruit, with <bang>, like: {theibang sen} is red like ripe fruit, said of youth, and {min theibang lo} is call a name, as one plucks fruit
<a> and <hive> written as one word: it is so indeed, often followed by <maw>

the basic rule or statement on which a body, a system or a piece of teaching rests: the constitution of an organisation, named beside <thumeilet>, by-laws, the principle of a system, or the key verse of a sermon
<vua> and <leh> written as one word: if, said after a verb when several persons are meant, if you all or if they

terms: be concerned with/be involved in/relate to/pertain
definition: <kisai>, concern, with <pih>, together with: have to do with a matter; {a kisaipih} is the one concerned, the relevant person or side
<ni>, sun, with <lum>, warm: the pleasant warmth of the sun; {nilum awi} is bask in the sun, sunbathe
dance at a feast, as the young people do in the courtyard; found mostly in songs
after the name of a field of work, those who run it or deal in it: {meileng lamsai} is a railway man
<nino> and <ni> written as one word: Saturday, the day before <Nipini>, Sunday
title of Pau Cin Hau as the man through whom a script came into being, <Laipian> with <pa>, man
<a> and <kiteng> written as one word: the ones who marry, or they marry
<theihsiam>, understand, with <pih>, together with: understand another person's situation, thoughts or hardship with sympathy
<lei> and <thak> written as one word: new land, and beside {van thak}, new heaven, the new earth
<lei>, buy, and <thak> written as one word: buy something new, or one who has newly bought
<kaal> and <nih> written as one word: two weeks
word of songs and speeches, found almost only in {maciang suan}, go forward, strive ahead together

terms: pass out of sight/pass away/be gone
definition: in {mual hong khupsan}, go down behind the hill out of sight: said of a year or a time that is ending or is forgotten
placed after <ci>, say, or <hi>, be, and before the closing word; it seems to stress that the thing was really said or is really so
pour water into or over something; {zu leih} is pour water into the beer pot so that the beer can be drunk
one kind of traditional Zo song with its own tune, named beside <laphei>, <lapi> and <zawlla>
<hi> and <lam> written as one word: the fact that something is so, said after <a>, <na> or <i> and before a verb of knowing or seeing
{hih lam} said short: this direction, this side, set against {hualam}, that way
affectionate word of address used by a parent or an older person to a boy or a young man
stick out or turn upward, as the bottom or a turned-up nose; {del liangin} with a verb of running is said of making off in a hurry
<thu>, matter, with <kituahna>, meeting: a coming to one mind, an accord; {Mang Thukituahna} is the accord of the chiefs at Tedim
<it> and <loh> written as one word: not love, and one who is not loved
<ih> and <thei> written as one word: we know, we come to know
plural of <puaisa>: the agents who arrange work, papers or travel for others, also those who smuggle people
a Zomi village in the Tedim area of Chin State, Myanmar
<siam>, skilled, with <nel>, fine: skilled to a fine degree, thoroughly proficient in something learned
sound written for a pause while thinking, doubting or sighing, before or after what is said
after a place name: the country from that place southward or down toward the plains, <khang> as in <khanglam> with <siah>, and beyond
something to eat, a bare living; {neektawm zong} is seek a living
at a later time, after a while, said of what will happen or be done later
the seeds of the bean plant <ga>, shelled from the pod: beans as food, also burned and ground in making gunpowder
in {gatang kai}, literally draw the beans: weigh a matter point by point and settle it, reach a compromise
a thick, soft and warm cloth woven of cotton, used as a blanket and spread as a covering, one of the traditional cloths of the Zomi
<ding> and <ciang> written as one word after a verb: when about to do it, or only as far as doing it

terms: slaughter an animal/kill for a feast
definition: <sa> and <go> written as one word: kill an animal for a feast or a rite; {sago teng} are those who provide the animals killed
a traditional festival of the <Zomi> that some keep as the new year, another name of <Sialsawm>
a kind of <zusa>, rat, with a white breast, that multiplies in the fields after the rice harvest and is caught for food
a Zomi village in <Manipur>, India
the earning and handling of money as a field of life, the economy, glossed economic in the articles; also trade carried on for gain
<luang>, body, with <man>, price: money paid to the family of a person who has died, by a government for its servant or soldier, or by the one at fault
a Zomi village in the <Tonzang> area of Chin State, Myanmar

terms: be particular to/be directed at/focus on
definition: with {-a} or {-in} after a noun: with particular regard to it, directed at it or based on it
word of songs and love letters for the one a person loves and longs for
<khuasa>, live, with the prefix <ki>: of people, live their life or earn a living in a place or by some means
<siam>, skilled, with <zia>, manner: the way of doing something skilfully, how to do it well

terms: not even a penny/even one kyat
definition: <pekkhat> and <zong> written as one word: even a single coin, with a negative verb not even a penny
word of songs: lie down or rest, as in the arms of a loved one or in the bosom of God
<kua>, who, with <ta>: who, mostly in questions that expect the answer no one; {kuatu kuata} is anyone at all
<lim> and <sak> written as one word: make food taste good; also find something tasty, enjoy eating it
<lo>, the form of <lawh>, call a name, said twice: keep calling a name, go on using it
<ta> and <teng> written as one word: all the children of someone
title of a headmaster or senior teacher, <Sya> with <pi>, great, written before the name; the Burmese sayagyi
organisation and website that publishes leaked secret documents of governments
<hongtung> and <khin> written as one word: has already arrived at the place spoken of
a district in the east of <Singapore>
breathe noisily through the nose while asleep, from <nak>, nose
<England> with the plural <te>: the people or the government of England, the British
<deih>, want, with <zia>, manner: what a person wants and the way he wants it
<mit>, eye, with <na.4>, be in pain: a disease or soreness of the eyes
<thu>, matter, with <muhzia>, way of seeing: how a person looks at and understands matters
the ethnic nationalities of Myanmar, the native peoples other than the Burman majority, as a group in national politics
<ngawng>, neck, with <khauh>, stiff: unwilling to yield or obey although one knows what is right
the ailment of a neck so stiff that the head cannot be turned; one article uses it as a picture of rigid thinking
split into two or more branches, as a tree, a horn, a tail or a line of thought; also the fork or branch itself
<i> and <kisam> written as one word: we need, it is necessary for us
<bawm>, basket, with <pua>, carry on the back: one who carries a basket on the back; an article gives it as the meaning of the name Chin
<gankhawi> with the noun suffix {-na}: the keeping and rearing of animals, or the place where they are kept, often named with <lokhawhna>, farming
<deuh> and <ta> written as one word after a describing word or verb: has now become somewhat more so
<huam> and <lo> written as one word: does not cover, does not include
{a ci} written as one word in the spelling of neighbouring dialects, with {chi} for <ci>: he or she says, they call it
plural of <Zolia>: the young unmarried women of the Zomi
<gelh>, write, with <pih>, do together with or for someone: write something for or with another person
placed after a verb: in a limp, drooping or half-hearted way, without strength or firmness
<galte>, enemies, with the subject marker <in> shortened and written as one word: the enemies as the doers of the action
placed after a verb of shaking, sounding or speaking: with force and without stopping, as {ling kangkang}, tremble violently
<kipat> and <ding> written as one word: will begin, that is to be started
in songs and sayings, <sial.4>, mithun, and <bang.2>, like, written as one word: like a mithun, said of what grows great and strong
<lung>, heart or mind, with <puakzia>, way of carrying: the attitude of mind that a person or a people holds
<kilom>, in one mass, with <khawm>, together: come together and hold together as one group or people
<teel>, choose, with the ending {-pi}, great: a general election for parliament, also written <kiteelpi>
a city in the state of Haryana, India, next to Delhi
<pai> and <leng.1> written as one word: if I or we go, when one goes
the capital city of the state of Nagaland in northeast India
a traditional Zomi cloth for men, in former times worn by those honoured for bravery in war or hunting; usually {Tangcing puan}
<an>, food, with <tawi>, carry: cooked food carried as a gift to relatives by custom, as at a feast or for a newborn child in {nau antawi}
<khak.4>, send, and <thei>, can, written as one word: can send; with <ki> before it, can be sent
a Zomi village in the Tedim area of Chin State, Myanmar; {Simzang gam} is the tract around it
<meidet>, torch, with the noun suffix {-na}: the lighting and carrying of torches at the Khuado festival
in the history of a village church, leave the old religion and become a Christian, entered with its date before <innphiat>, the cleansing of the house
a Zomi village in the Tedim area of Chin State, Myanmar
<pau>, speak, with <dan>, way: how a person speaks, and the form of speech of a place, as {Laitui paudan}

terms: to and fro/over and over/again and again
definition: placed after a verb of turning, shaking or showing: with a repeated movement back and forth or one time after another
form of <phuankhia>, found, used before words such as <ding> and <uh> and in clauses that describe a noun: {a phuatkhiat uh kipawlna} is the association they founded
<zan>, night, with <mang.2>, dream: a dream of the night, paired with <sunmang>, a dream of the day, for all that one dreams and longs for
placed after a verb: the action or state goes on steadily or to a strong degree; {thuak teitai} is endure steadily, and {mai san teitai} is said of a face that flushes deep red
<cian>, here clearly or exactly as in <kician>, and <lo> written as one word after a verb: not clearly, not for certain; {kithei cianlo} is it is not known for certain
<sak.3>, consider, and <diak>, especially, written as one word after a word of quality: {thupi sakdiak} is regard as especially important
after the name of a place: a little to the north or upper side of it, from <sak>, here north, and <diak>; whether north or simply close by is not settled by the sentences
<Shillong> and <ah> written as one word: in Shillong
<na>, <mu> and <ding> written as one word: you will see, you will find
placed after a verb: the thing happens again and again in quick succession, as of people arriving or grains falling out one after another

terms: his full name/her full name/its full name
definition: <a> and <minpi> written as one word: his or her real, full name
<a> and <zawngpen> written as one word: the poorest, the one that is poorest
placed after a verb: do the thing just like that, at once and without waiting to be asked or holding back; with a prohibition it warns against being forward

terms: make much of/give great weight to/emphasise/promote
definition: <uang>, go to great lengths, with <bawl>, make: treat a matter as very important and put much effort into it, close to <thupibawl>
<mualtung> and <gam> written as one word: hill country, the land in the hills as against the plains

terms: be eaten as a dish/be had with the meal
definition: <meh>, the dish eaten with the staple, used as a verb with the prefix <ki>: of meat or vegetables, be eaten as the dish that goes with the rice or grain
<kita> and <lo> written as one word: there is no room for it, it does not fit in or through

terms: in order to take/to take on
definition: <la.3>, take, and <dingin> written as one word: in order to take or fetch; {tavuan ladingin} is to take on a responsibility
<naak>, here greatly as in <naakpi>, with <liam>, be wounded: be badly hurt; the usual word of news reports for the seriously injured, set against those lightly hurt
a Chin people of the southern part of Chin State in Myanmar and their language, named in lists with Zotung, Zophei, Mara and Senthang
of love, a marriage or a purpose: it does not hold out to the end; {tullo itna} in song titles is a love that did not last
<mi> and <nuai> written as one word: the place below other people; {minuai ah om} is be behind others, rank lower than others
the embassy of a country in another country, glossed embassy by the articles themselves
<sia>, bad, said twice: after a verb it means in a bad way and again and again, {gen siasia} is keep speaking ill of; {a siasia} is getting worse and worse

terms: near the town/vicinity of the town
definition: <khua> and <kiang> written as one word after the name of a town: the place near that town

terms: in the Burmese plains/to the Burmese plains
definition: <Kawlzang> and <ah> written as one word: in or to the Burmese plains
<ngaihsun> and <leng> written as one word: if we think of it, if one considers
<Zosuan> and <tate> written as one word: the children of the Zo line, all the Zo peoples
the game of jumping over a raised bar or cord, and the bar itself; with <kan.4>, step over, as {kanteh kan}, do the high jump

terms: from one side/from another point of view/in another way
definition: <lamkhat> and <pan> written as one word: from one side; {lamkhatpan in genleng} is to put it another way
a table for eating, reading or setting things on; two articles add <sabuai> to explain it
sticky rice or sticky millet, steamed for feasts such as Khuado and for the visit to the graves; mostly spelled <taksih>, and {taksih nganhuan} is to steam it

terms: that he founded/which was set up
definition: <a> and <phuh> written as one word: that he founded or set up, said of a church, a village or a post
<a> and <huan.1>, garden, written as one word: his, her or their garden
<a> and <huan.3>, cook, written as one word: the one who cooks, or he or she cooks
<tui> and <nuai> written as one word: the place under the water; before a noun it means underwater, as in an underwater drone
<siangtho> and <pumpi> written as one word: the holy body of Jesus given in the Lord's Supper
<zong.5>, seek, and <lo> written as one word: not seek, without looking for
of two things, views or parties: be contrary to each other, go against each other, with <tawh> for the other side
<duang>, figure, with <cing.3>, be complete: having a fine, well-formed body, said with <melhoih> of good-looking women and men; {duangcing kidemna} is a contest of physique

terms: be short of/not have enough/be hard-pressed
definition: <kicing>, enough, with <lah>, here lacking: of money, goods or a person, fall short, not have enough for what is needed
of a person who acts as if never having enough: be greedy for a share, or push in where it is not one's place
<taam> and <ding> written as one word: will stay, in order to stay for a time
<a> and <beina> written as one word: the end of it, its coming to an end
<kaam>, luck, with <sinna>, a trying: a draw of numbered tickets sold to raise money, in which the winners get prizes
<lam>, road, with <khak>, shut: a roadblock where police or soldiers stop travellers, and anything that bars the way
hold something to be important or dear, give it the first place, said beside <thupisak>
reach over and take in the whole of something, as {leitung bup huap}, cover the whole world; said beside <huam>
placed after a verb of sinking, lessening, easing or growing dark: it happens bit by bit and keeps on

terms: out again and again/down one after another
definition: <khiat> said twice, after a verb or as the verb itself: the taking out or dropping is done again and again, one after another
the man of a village who deals with the <dawi>, the spirits, in the old religion, named together with the <siampu> or <siampi>, priest
<a> and <nun>, life, written as one word, the first part of {anun tak} and {anun takna}, his or her living, way of life, which is otherwise written with <nuntak> and <nuntakna>
<a> and <nun>, blow, written as one word, said of the wind or a storm
New York, the largest city of the United States, written as one word
moving pictures recorded and shown on a screen, a common spelling of the English word video
<khua>, village, and <tuam>, separate, written as one word: a village of its own, or a different village, as <gamtuam> is a different country
the people of the <Tawmging> clan, who held the chieftainship of Saizang
<minvawh>, give a name, with the noun suffix <na>: the name given to a people, a group or a thing, and the giving of it
a quarter, {Botung veng}, of the town of <Tedim>; the name is also found at Vangteh
<kikup> and <ding> written as one word: will talk a matter over together, something to be discussed
a thing that a smith forges of iron, wanted by young women and given as a gift; taken here as the pipe for smoking tobacco
<pak>, for a moment, and <leng>, if I or we, written as one word after a verb: if we do it briefly, used by writers to say let us briefly look at or mention something
<ka> and <phat> written as one word: I praise, I give thanks for
<i> and <sisan> written as one word: our blood, the common descent of a people
<nuam>, want, and <ten>, the plural with the marker of the doer, written as one word after a verb: those who want to do it, as the ones who act

terms: upper part of a village/above the village
definition: <khua>, village or town, and <tung>, above, written as one word: the upper side of a village or the place over a town; also part of village names such as Mualnuam Khuatung
<a> and <vaak> written as one word: go about from place to place, the one who goes about; in lists of caring for children or sheep it is <vaak> in its sense of feeding
<mai>, just, and <mah> written as one word after a verb at the end of a sentence, in writing from Manipur: it simply is so
<mai>, face, and <mah> written as one word: the face itself
placed after <bang>, like, or after a noun: exactly so, just the same, as {tua bang ngeiingeii in}, in just that way; after a verb, surely; it may be the same word as <ngeingei>

terms: those who will enter/those to go in
definition: <lutding> with the plural <te>: the people who are to go in, as to an interview
<hong> and <piakhia> written as one word: give out to us, donate to the speaker or his group
<na> and <piaknop> written as one word: you want to give, mostly before <leh>, if
<kamphen>, interpreter, with <pa> for a man: the man who interprets for a speaker
<mawng>, banyan, with <pi>, great: a large banyan tree; with a capital also the name of a hill and a name of persons
<det> said twice, after a verb: keeping on steadily, as tears that keep falling, or going into a matter thoroughly, as {ngaihsun detdet}, think it through, and {sui detdet}, examine closely
stir or push into action; {han thot na} is a word of exhortation at a meeting, and one writer explains the word as impact
<hong> and <bang> written as one word: come to be like something, or seem so to the speaker
<khan> in the sense of a room, as in <innkhan>, with <ah> written as one word: in the room, as {lupna khanah}, in the bedroom; not the word for lifetime
<sa>, meat, with <kal>, kidney: the kidney of an animal as meat, named with <salung> among the choice parts given to the elders
Astaka sports complex in Petaling Jaya, Malaysia, where the Zomi football tournaments are played
move a thing or oneself from its place, compare <kikhin>: {nung khiin} is draw back, {nawl khiin} is push aside or abolish, and {ki khiin} is be moved

terms: social skill/ability to get along with people
definition: <kikholh>, keep company with, and <siamna>, skill: being good at mixing and getting along with other people
<sem>, work or serve, spelled with a long vowel, and <ding> written as one word: will serve, to hold an office or do a work
<dawn>, drink, with the ending <pih>: drink together with someone, or give someone tea, beer or another drink as a host
<panpih>, help, and <theih>, be able, written as one word, the form of <panpihthei> used before <nading> and before a noun: that can be helped, so as to be able to help
<hel>, include, and <ding> written as one word, mostly after <ki>: will be included, will take part, to join in
<zom>, continue or join, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not going on with something, and after <ki> not joined to it
the village in the hill country, <khamtung>, that a person or family comes from, given in profiles of people who now live elsewhere
<lai>, writing, with <gelhdan>, way of writing: how a language is written and spelled
a village named as the home village of Zomi people and of a village association, {Chantagyi Khua Kipawlna}; the Burmese name suggests the plains of Myanmar
<a> and <kipuah> written as one word: that has been repaired, improved or put in order; {akipuah toto} is improved again and again
<nam>, people, with <phung>, clan: a tribe, a division of a people larger than a <beh>, clan, and smaller than the <minam>, nation; the articles gloss it with English tribe
the prefix <ki> and <semzo>, be able to do, written as one word: can be done, gets done

<taang>, millet, with <za>, hundred: a harvest of a hundred measures of millet, the mark of a wealthy household, named together with <mimza>; {taangza aih} is the traditional feast of the <Zomi> that celebrates it
the heavy metal used as fuel for nuclear power and in atomic bombs
the folder of an email account where incoming messages arrive
the English plural of <sponsor> used as a noun: the people who pay for an event, or the support they give, as in {sponsors hongpia teng}, those who gave sponsorship

terms: at the time of/in the days of/when
definition: <hunlai>, time or period, and <in> written as one word: at that time, in the days of the person or state named before; {tua hunlaiin} is at that time

<tuamtuam>, various, written as one word with <na>, thing, or with the noun ending {-na} of the word before it: various things, or the various ones of what the word before names, as in {kipawl natuamtuam}, the various organisations
<ngeilo>, never, and <ding> written as one word, after a verb: will never do or be so

terms: be free from/be exempt from/keep out of
definition: <peng>, be exempt, with the prefix <ki>: be clear of or stand apart from something, which is marked by <tawh>; {kipeng thei lo} is cannot be free of it or cannot stay out of it
the particle <hong>, spelled without its first letter, and <huh>, help, written as one word: help towards the speaker, help us or help me

terms: happen to be/there happen to be
definition: <a> and <omkhak>, happen to be, written as one word with a long vowel in the last syllable; {khialhna aomkhaak aleh} is if there should happen to be a mistake, a closing formula of news writers
<tun>, arrive, and <sawm>, intend, written as one word: make sure to be there, used in notices that tell people to come before a set hour
<thu>, word or matter, with <zasak>, make hear: let someone know a matter, report it to an office, or give notice or an order
<tuambawlna>, unequal treatment, with the prefix <ki>: people of one group treating one another as separate, forming sides and favouring their own
<zak>, hear, and <teh>, when, written as one word: when someone hears or heard it
<i>, our, and <pau>, language, written as one word: our language, said of the speech of the Zomi
a village or quarter at <Kalaymyo> in the plains of Myanmar where Zomi live; {Sanpya lampi} is Sanpya road
<an>, food, with the ending <pi>, main or great: the food a people mainly lives on, or the main dish of a meal
<bawl>, make, and <pawl>, group, written as one word after what is made: the group of people who make or carry it out, as in {thukhun bawlpawl}, the makers of the law
<bek>, only, and <ding> written as one word, after a verb: will only do or be that and nothing more
<tual>, the communal ground of a village, with <biak>, worship: the sacrifice of the old Zomi religion made by a whole village, the same as <tualbiakna>; {Tualbiak-pawi} is its festival
a bird of the hills whose call is heard through the dry season, also called {lawkta}
word of songs and formal wishes for what lies ahead of a person or a people, often paired with <masuan> as {masuan mazap}
Mount Popa, a volcanic mountain in central Myanmar near Bagan, named in accounts of where the Zomi once lived and also written {Pupa}
<loding> and the sentence-final <hi> written as one word after a verb: closes a statement that something will not happen
<cidamna> and <lam> written as one word: the side of health, matters of health and medicine
a place where books are kept for people to read, from <laibu>, book
<lungngaih> and <huai> written as one word: that calls for careful thought, that one ought to think over
the government of India or of one of its states, in the writing of Zomi in India; elsewhere <kumpi>
a woven container of the farming household in which goods and food such as taro are kept, named beside <lawhpi>; in a few sentences the same spelling stands for <lawhcing>, successful
<nam>, kind, and <sawm>, ten, written as one word after a noun: ten of them, ten kinds; {Thukham namsawm} is the Ten Commandments
in {sum dipkikna}, the payment by which the members of a mutual aid fund fill the fund up again after money has been paid out of it
<gam>, country, with <pawl>, group: a group or union of countries, as in {EU gampawl} and {NATO gampawl}
<bal>, taro, with <pi>, great: the taro plant and its large tuber, a common food crop of the Zomi hills, named beside {balke}
port city in the south of France, where the Zomi labour companies landed in 1917
the moon when it is full, and the day of the month on which it is full, {khaliik ni}; set against <khadet>, the new moon
<tui>, water, with <khuat>, dig: dig out the water source of a new village, said together with <khuasat>, found a village, of the first settlers
narrow in extent or in outlook, set against <zaii>, the same writer's spelling of <zai>, wide; {toii sa} is find something narrow
<na>, the marker of something done earlier or elsewhere, and <ciamteh> written as one word: has noted or recorded it, and after <in>, has regarded it as
<i>, we, and <tel>, understand, written as one word: we understand, we grasp

the land and villages on the far side as seen from where one stands, <gal>, other side, with <khua>: {galkhua dak} is look out over it, and in songs {galkhua don} is gaze toward the far land with longing
town in central Myanmar, now part of Naypyidaw, known for its agricultural college and university
<gen>, say, and <suk>, down, written as one word: go on to speak of what follows, or what has been said in the lines above
a person who represents a people, a party or an organization, above all an elected member of parliament, {Hluttaw kosale}; the Zolai words are <palai> and <taangmi>
noun of <kizem>: the adorning of oneself with clothes and ornaments, the decoration of a house or room, and the things used for it
<muh>, see, with <sawm>: form a picture of something before seeing it; {ka muhsawm dan sangin} is more than I had imagined
after <ki>, plan to see one another, arrange a meeting
noun of <ven>: the coming to an end of a war, a trouble or a dispute; {gal venna} is the end of a war and {buaina venna} the settling of a conflict
a heap or setting of stones raised as a memorial to a person, from <suang>, stone, and <phuh>, set up; also part of place names
expressive word placed after a verb or a describing word for something big and bulky that stands, lies or is held in plain view, as in {gol bembam}, great and bulky
word of songs for <kiangah>, to or beside a person: {na siangah} is to your side
<lung>, heart, and the place marker <ah> written as one word: in the heart or mind, mostly in songs

terms: at the time of/in the days of
definition: <hunlai> and <a> written as one word after a date, a name or a clause: in or of the time when that was so
{Kawl}, Burmese, with the Burmese word for country: Burma, as the land is named in one series of comic dialogues; the usual word is <Kawlgam>
<laih>, replace, with <to>, onward: one thing takes the place of another in turn, as a new model or name replaces the old; {laihsuk laihto} is change back and forth
<a> and <danin> written as one word: in the manner of what is named before it, as in {hih anuai adanin}, as shown below, and {abeisa adanin}, as in the past
<na> and <tup> written as one word: what you aim at or intend, often paired with {na ngimna} and {na sawmna}
placed after a verb: the action is all that is done or goes on being done, merely, single-mindedly, as in {buaipih lunglung}, be taken up with nothing else
<tum>, set, and <ta> written as one word: of the sun or of the days of a life, has now gone down, is coming to an end
<tum>, play an instrument, and <ta> written as one word: has come to play, began playing

terms: be rejected/be cast aside/reject one another
definition: <pampaih>, cast aside, with the prefix <ki>: be left aside as of no account, or reject one another; {kipampaih thei lo} is cannot be set aside
<la>, song, with <pu>: in {Zogam Lapu}, a title of honour given to a senior Zomi songwriter
<kipatcil>, first beginning, with the noun suffix <na>: the very beginning of something, or the place and time where it began
plural of <siampu>: the priests of the traditional religion; {zato siampute} are physicians
town in the south of the Manipur valley in India, near the hills where Zomi villages lie
<koici>, how, and <dan>, manner, written as one word: in what way, of what sort
<dot>, ask, and <behnop>, want to add, written as one word: wishing to ask something more; {dotbehnop a om leh} in a notice is if there is anything further to ask
<nop> and <dan>, manner, written as one word: after <a> how pleasant a place is, after a verb how much someone wants to do it, as in {ka theih nopdan}, how I long to know
<tut>, sit, and <khawl>, rest, written as one word: sit down for a rest, stop and sit; paired with <dinkhawl>, stand still
second part of the name Sierra Leone, a country in West Africa
<tawn>, follow a path, with <zia>, manner: the ways a people follows and hands down, as in {pupa tawnzia}, the customs of the forefathers; often beside <ngeina>
<hong> and <sung> as a verb, pour out, written as one word: set out a view or account before the readers, as in {ka muhna hongsung nuam-ing}, I wish to present my view; not the word for in
placed after a verb: in a big or showy way, as in {minpua lianluan}, bear a title grandly, and {kilam lianluan}, be built on a grand scale
city in the state of Missouri in the United States, in the news in 2014 for unrest after a police shooting; also an English surname
<min>, name, with <san>, from <saang>, receive: the taking down of names, said of refugees being registered by the UNHCR
short form of <khuaphelep>: electric power, mostly as {khuaphe mei}, electric light or supply, and {khuaphe meiset}, electric generator
a flash of lightning, compare <khuaphia>
<sa>, game, with {ben}, from <beng>, hunt: the hunting of wild animals; {saben in ben} is hunt down, said also of pursuing wanted men
<nawh>, hurry, with <tak>: in haste, as a matter of urgency
<bua>, pour out, and <sa> written as one word: already spilled; known from the proverb {tui buasa kiluak kik thei lo}, spilled water cannot be scooped up again
placed after a verb: the action goes on briskly and without letting up, as in {buai citcit}, be in a great stir, and of birds {ham citcit}, keep chirping
<tuisawp>, baptism, with the noun suffix <na>: the rite of baptism; {tuisawpna pia} is baptize and {tuisawpna ngah} is be baptized
a large bag carried on the back or shoulder for one's things on a journey or to the field, compare <thung-ip>
open footwear, slippers or sandals, as against closed shoes
placed after a noun: of every kind, as in {paak namcih}, all kinds of flowers; in songs also every people, all nations
words of power spoken by a priest or a man with such knowledge; mostly in {phui sam}, say an incantation, see <phuisam>; also said as an exclamation of scorn
only in {mat leh zet} and {kimat zet}: one following close on another without a break, as vehicles passing or people talking
<mi> and <gen> written as one word: what others say, people talking; {migen za} is hear people say
<dang>, throat, with <keu>, dry: be thirsty, or thirst; {dangkeu pha sak} is quench the thirst
<a> and <siahuai> written as one word: that which is bad or terrible; {asiahuai bangmah omlo} is there is nothing wrong
<akhak>, send, and <nuam>, want, written as one word: {akhaknuam te} are those who wish to send something
placed after a verb or noun: exactly so, in the strict sense, as in {kituak liinlian}, fit exactly, and {akibang liinlian}, exactly the same
<ih>, we, and <suak>, become, written as one word: we become, we turn out to be
a city on the Irrawaddy in Bago Region, Myanmar, formerly called Prome, and the seat of a Catholic diocese
<ih> and <pate> written as one word: our fathers, mostly in the pair {ihpu ihpate}, our forefathers

terms: those who base on/those who rely on
definition: those who make something their foundation or main concern, <bulphuh> with plural {-te}, after <a>
worth having or owning, <neih> with the ending {-huai}, worthy of
<ham.2> and <zaw> written as one word: older in age than another, with <sang> for than
<ngai.2> and <in> written as one word: missing or longing for a person or thing, said of what one does meanwhile
<hong> and <tu.2> written as one word: come and sit or settle at a place, land there, or of a duty come to rest on someone
strikingly fine or bright, said of dress, of a day and of a literature; {mei vam} is glowing embers
the man who found or discovered something, <mukhia> with the ending {-pa}
a principle or policy that a group holds and follows; {thulet bulpi} is a basic principle
<siam> and <dan> written as one word: the way or degree in which one is skilled at something
a dark-skinned foreigner, such as an Indian, mostly paired with {mangkang}, a white foreigner: {mangvom mangkang} is foreigners of every kind
<veng.2> and <nuai> written as one word: the lower quarter of a town or village, also used as the name of such a quarter
<khang> and <masate> written as one word: the people of earlier generations
plural of <Indian>; in the articles mostly the native peoples of America, also {Red Indiante}
<ciau> and <tui> written as one word: the water of a river, a word of songs
<na> and <nau> written as one word: your younger brother or sister, or your baby
bearing much seed or many offspring, said of plants, animals and people; also to multiply in this way

terms: all the good ones/the good part
definition: <hoih> and <teng.3> written as one word: all that is good of something, the good ones or the best part
