<ngei> and <mah> written as one word: just as one is used to; {ngeimah bangin} is as usual, as before
<zangh> said twice: go on using something, use it again and again
found after <na> only: {na lengah} is <naleng> with <ah> divided in another place, even in, even at
<kiho> and <sak> written as one word: cause or allow people to talk with one another, put someone in touch with another
a village of the Khuangnung tract in the Tedim area
writing done by hand, or a text written by hand; {khutgelh lai} is a manuscript
<om> and <ciangin> written as one word: when someone is at a place or when something is there
after a verb, said of an action that goes on or is done again and again, as chatting or grumbling; {lu susu} is said of a sleepy person whose head keeps nodding
what makes a person, a people or a teaching different from all others
the muscles and sinews of the body, the seat of its strength; often paired with <thagui>
<gah> and <hoih> written as one word: good fruit, mostly of the good results of a way of life
dealings and traffic between people, villages or countries
<tawi> and <in> written as one word: holding or carrying something in the hand while doing something else
a bishop of the Roman Catholic Church, <siadaw> with the ending {-pi}, great
<i> and <phung.2> written as one word: our clan or family line, mostly in {i beh iphung}
stay on at a place or on the way longer than needed, be held up there
regard oneself as good at something or act as if one were, <kisiam> with <sak>
roll or tie several things into one, and of speech gather several points into one
<na> and <teel> written as one word: either you choose, or with the narrative <na> before the verb, chose or elected
<om>, <lo> and <hi> written as one word: there is not, it does not exist
<a> and <zote> written as one word: those who have finished or passed something, or those who won
the marker <in> written together with the prefix {ki-} of the verb that follows: {inki nei} is {in kinei}
in a firm and lasting way, often paired with <kiptak>
<zui> and <siam> written as one word: be good at following a leader, a rule or a custom

expressive word after a word for a colour or for light and dark: faintly, dimly so; {khuavak philhphelh} is the first faint light of dawn, {khuamial philhphelh} is dusk, and {puang philhphelh} is dull grey
the Houthis, an armed Shia movement of <Yemen> that fights the government of that country
<limci>, good, with <tak> written as one word: very good, excellent, said of an event or a result
a city in the state of <Iowa> in the United States, where a Zomi community lives
Fort Worth, a city in Texas in the United States near <Dallas>, written as one word
<na>, your, and <pasal>, husband, written as one word: your husband
<nuphal> with <pa> for a man: a man who is related to the speaker by marriage as nuphal, by the lexicon the husband of the sister of the wife; the sentences do not show the exact relation
the low, hot country along the rivers and to the south, where crops ripen early, as against <Zogam>, the cool high country
<hong> and <leng>, fly, written as one word: come flying, fly this way, of a bird, a swarm or an aeroplane and its passengers; {lung hongleng} is come to feel lonely
<kum>, year, with <sum>, money: money paid once a year, as the yearly dues of a member or the yearly fee for a service
in {kumsum hun}, the year of the budget of a government, the financial year
steps or a ladder for going up and down, as against a lift
<lo>, not, and <zawin> written as one word, mostly as {hi lozawin}: it is not that, but rather what follows

terms: merely/only as far as/no more than
definition: <ciang>, as far as, and <lel>, only, written as one word after a noun phrase: no further than that, merely that
expressive word after a verb for something done lightly and again and again: of rain, drizzling, as {guah zu supsup}; of people, talking low among themselves, as {kiho supsup}
tell someone plainly that he is wrong in order to set him right; named together with <hilh>, teach
a district of the city of <Seremban> in Malaysia
<i>, we, and <kalsuan>, step, written as one word: we go forward, our going forward
<sum>, money, with <nu>, mother: used in the pair {sumnu sumpa}, money of every kind, wealth, as something sought, earned or asked for in a blessing
<sum>, money, with <pa>, father: the second half of the pair {sumnu sumpa}, money of every kind, wealth; see <sumnu>
<hong> and <zuan>, head for, written as one word: come heading for a place or a person
<khuapih> and <tuipih> written as one word: the people of the same town or village, named after the relatives and acquaintances of a person
<zu>, liquor, and <zuak>, sell, written as one word: sell liquor, the selling of liquor; {zuzuak na} is a place where liquor is sold and {zuzuak nu} is a woman who sells it
expressive word after a word for smiling or for warmth: {nui hieuhiau} is smile softly and {lum hieuhiau} is mildly warm; perhaps the same word as <hiauhiau>
<manpha>, valuable, with <tak> written as one word: very valuable; {manphatak in} is in a way that has worth, to good purpose
poetic word of songs, made of a song word for mother and <sung>, inside; used in {tunsung khat pan piang}, born of one womb, said of the Zomi as one family
<Zotual>, native Zo, and <lai>, writing, written as one word: the native Zo script of Pau Cin Hau, also called {Laipian lai}
<ki> with <phual>, camp: have one's base or home in a place, said of a people, a church body or an armed group
<thei>, can, and the linking <a> written as one word: it can be so, and
<kipawlkhawm>, unite, and <in> written as one word: joining together, as one body
<gam>, land, with <nei>, have: one who owns land or to whom a territory belongs; before a noun, land-owning; of a people, having a land of its own
<kong>, I to you, and <sam>, invite, written as one word: I or we invite you, the closing words of an invitation
<suaktatak>, freely, and <in> written as one word: freely, without hindrance
<a> and <vawh> written as one word: he sows or what he sows, of seed; with <min>, the name he gives
<tawm>, little, and <bei>, be used up, written as one word: little is spent, it costs little; {sum tawmbei zaw} is cost less money
<hi> and <mahtaleh> written as one word: although it is so; after a clause it means even though, and at the start of a sentence however
<giak>, stay the night, with the noun suffix {-na}: the place where one stays for the night, such as a hotel or a house; the same as <giahna>
<kai>, pull, said twice: keep pulling or leading along; {nakpheh khau tawh kaikai} is lead along by a nose rope, said of those who control others
put one's signature to an agreement, a treaty or an order; {limkaai gamte} are the countries that have signed
<kilawh>, be contagious, with <sawn>, onward: of an illness, be passed on from one person to another
<hutkhiat>, rescue, with the noun suffix {-na}: the act or work of rescuing; {hutkhiatna nasem} are rescue workers
<kum> and <tawp> written as one word: the end of the year; {kumtawp exam} is the final examination of the school year
word of songs and stories for <ngasa>, fish; {limnga bang} is like a fish
a large meeting of a church body or association, held in a host village, the same as <khawmpi>
<a> and <huamna> written as one word: its scope, all that it covers or takes in
child's word for <nu>, mother, also said by a mother of herself to her child; it is also a pet name of women
<Mon> with the plural <te>: the Mon people of lower Myanmar
<ong>, here a spelling of <hong>, written as one word with <piang>: come about, arise; with <khia>, be born
<hong> and <panpih> written as one word: help or support us, come and help
level land, a plain; in songs {pupa gamzang} is the land of the forefathers

terms: of one stock/of the same kind/one
definition: of one seed or kind, with <khat>, one: of the same stock or origin, mostly in the pair {cikhat sakhat}, of one stock and one flesh
<ka> and <kam> written as one word: my mouth
a town in <Norway> where Zomi live
<ong>, here a spelling of <hong>, written as one word with <lut>: come in, enter
fit together fully with something, which is marked by <tawh>: agree with it, be in harmony with it
<bang>, what, written as one word with the <na> that stands before the verb: {bangna ci hiam} is what did he say, and with a you subject, what do you
a city in <England>

terms: how it is not/the fact of not being
definition: <loh> and <zia> written as one word after a verb or describing word: the way in which something is not so, as {hoih lohzia}, how it is not good
a Zomi village, with an old and a new settlement
<diakdiak> with the plural <te>, after a noun: those ones in particular, above all the ones named
<Thahdo> with the plural <te>: the Thadou people
passive of <minvawh>, give a name: be given a name, be called; the name stands before <ci-in> or <tawh>
<ka> and <neulai> written as one word: my childhood; {kaneulai-in} is when I was small
a <tau>, platform, built high: a raised stand from which one watches a field, makes announcements or looks out over a place
<aa> and <leh> written as one word after a verb: if that is so, if it happens
<leng>, fly, with the plural <te>: the ones that fly or drift through the air; in {zin le lengte} it means guests and visitors
<nungak>, young woman, with <pi>, great: a grown woman who has stayed unmarried past the usual age
a city in <Florida>, United States
business and the economy, and economics as a school subject
a city in <Ohio>, United States

definition: <deih>, want, and <dandan>, just as, written as one word after the one who wants: exactly as that person wishes, usually followed by <in>
<la>, song, and <dang>, other, written as one word: other songs; in the pair {thudang ladang} it only echoes <thudang> and the whole means other matters, this and that
the Paite word for that and <ziak>, reason, written as one word and followed by <in>: for that reason; found in writing close to Paite, where Tedim Zolai has <tuaziak>
<i>, we, and <neek>, eat, written as one word: we eat, or that which we eat
stand by a person or a people as one's own before others and bear the shame with them; mostly negated as {daipih ngam lo}, not dare to own, be ashamed to be seen with; paired with <zumpih>
<it>, love, and <man>, because, written as one word and often followed by <in>: because someone loves
<bei>, be used up, with a second part that is not clear: of money or time, go into something and be gone, often of spending that goes on or brings little
<mawtaw>, car, and <lam>, way, written as one word: a road for motor vehicles
village in Mizoram, India, where speakers of Tedim live
<na>, your, and <tanu>, daughter, written as one word; {nata natanu} is your sons and daughters
a measure of distance, one eighth of a mile, <tai>; the number follows it
expressive word placed after a verb or a describing word for something that looks large, full or flourishing, as wide sleeves, ripe red fruit or people who are well off
<vaai>, affair, with the plural <te>, in writing that doubles long vowels; the same writing with a capital, {Vaaite}, is the people of India, named beside the Burmans and the Westerners
<Hakha> with the plural <te>: the Chin people of Hakha
a stream in the Tedim area, {Phil} with <lui>, stream; it meets the Tuimi stream at Philka
a village named Bukpi, one in the Muallum area of Tedim and one among the Paite of India; without a capital, {sum bukpi} is a large shop or main place of trade
<CNF> with the plural <te>: the people of the Chin National Front
a branch of the <Gualnam> clan, written after the name of a person
<ciampel>, break a promise, and <lo>, not, written as one word: keeping one's word, never going back on a promise
<inn>, house, and <sian>, clean: in customary law the animal or payment that is due for cleansing a house or household after an offence
<keek>, push out a border, with the noun suffix <na>: the widening of a territory or taking over of what belongs to others; {gam keekna} is colonization and {gamgi keekna} the pushing out of a border
village in the Falam area of Chin State
old village of the Sihzang people near Pimpih in the Tedim area
<kigawmkhawm>, join together, with the noun suffix <na>: the coming together of peoples or groups into one
<inn>, house, and <kawm>, wall or gap, written as one word: the walls of a house, or the narrow space beside and between houses
former village in the Lailo area of Tedim, founded in 1891
<kim>, all, and <ding>, will, written as one word after a verb: that all should do it, or that it be done in full
<pian>, come into being, and <dan>, manner, written as one word: the form or shape a thing has, and the way something came about or happened
<zaih>, photograph or film, with <te>: the pictures or videos that someone took, or the people who take them
sentence-final form of speech, {ka hi ve} run together: the speaker says with emphasis that he is the one who does or did what the verb before it says
<bang>, what, and <sa>, meat, written as one word: what kind of meat; the same spelling also occurs in songs and as a place name in Malaysia
word of songs, used with <khawl>, keep company, in its several spellings: being close together with a dear one; apart from the place name Umbang in the Khasi hills

terms: miss very much/love dearly/long for greatly
definition: <ngaih>, long for, and <luat>, very much, written as one word, mostly before <man> or <manin>: miss or love someone greatly
<nih> and <gel> written as one word: the two together, both of them, mostly in songs and poems
the time of youth when a person is in bloom and at full strength, a word of songs and poems
<zin> and <lai> written as one word: the time when someone is travelling or visiting a place, while on a journey
greet a person on meeting, also the word of greeting itself, as in {Kum Thak Cibai}, New Year greetings; given beside <nohset> for the same act
playing games of chance for money, named with drinking and smoking as a habit that spoils life; also the verb
in freedom, without hindrance or fear, mostly as {zalentak in}
what is in regular or everyday use, and so also a habit that someone keeps; from <zattang>, common use, and <zang>, use

terms: to be able to read/so that it can be read
definition: <simtheih> and <ding> written as one word: for someone to be able to read, mostly as {simtheihding in}, so that it can be read
the living of a teaching or word in one's own life, putting it into practice, set against only saying it
<la>, song, and <tawh>, with, written as one word: with or by a song; {latawh kisai} is concerning songs
<lasa> and <siam> written as one word: one who is good at singing, a singer of note
feel uneasy or accused within oneself and so hold back or take a thing as aimed at oneself, paired with {kisuangtak}; {kaunei kisungsia} is a proverb
<neih>, have, and <teh>, when, written as one word: when one has; {hun neihteh} is when there is time
<na>, you, and <nget>, ask for, written as one word: you ask for or apply for; {thu nanget} is you pray

terms: be fond of/cherish/be loath to leave
definition: be so attached to a person, place or thing that one is unwilling to part with it; {khiatlah huai} is dear, hard to leave
<vaihawm> and <pawl> written as one word: the group that manages or decides the affairs of an organisation, a committee or management team
<hunlap> and <in> written as one word, mostly as {a hunlapin}: in time, at the proper time

terms: pray for you/ask on your behalf
definition: <kong> and <ngetsak> written as one word: I or we pray for you, mostly as {thu kongngetsak hi} at the end of a message of sympathy or thanks
the passing of news between people, communication; {nisim thukizaakna} is a newspaper
<a> and <leen> written as one word: who holds, said of one who holds a post, {panmun aleen}; in one article it is <a> with <leen> fly, when they fly
placed after a verb: although that is so, granted that, before a clause that says something in spite of it
<tung> and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word: arrived, reached, came upon
<ado> and <ding> written as one word: to fight against, that which is to be fought; {adoding in} is in order to fight
make things the same as one another, bring into one form, as spelling, speech or opinions
<ihmu> and <lo> written as one word: not sleep, without sleeping; {ihmulo liangin} is going even without sleep
the state of being free, and the freedoms a person is entitled to: {mihing zaleenna} is human rights; given beside <suahtakna>
<a> and <kiniamkhiat> written as one word: the one who is humble, or he humbled himself; {akiniamkhiat pen} is the most humble
village in the Kalay area of Myanmar where Zomi live, also called Sawbua
the hair that grows at the eye, from <mit>, eye, and <mul>, hair: the eyelashes, and in several articles the eyebrows
<gil> and <sunga> written as one word: that is inside the belly or the womb
<na> and <khen> written as one word: divided or classified, with <na> the particle of earlier action, or you divide, with <na> you; {thu nakhen} is judge a case
<hong> and <ging> written as one word: a sound, a phone or a report rings out or is heard
<kong> and <pai> written as one word: I come to you, I have come here
<a> and <dung> written as one word: its length, the long side, paired with <avai> or {a vai}, its width
Arlington in Virginia, across the Potomac from Washington, known for its national cemetery; also a city in Texas and part of other names
<tu>, grandchild, <leh>, and, and <tate>, children, written as one word: the generations that come after, descendants
<a>, <tha> and <haat> written as one word: it is strong; {athahaat nading} is so that it may be strong
<muh> and <hak> written as one word: hard to find or to see, seldom met with
<koi> and <tak> written as one word: exactly where, at what place
placed after a describing word to strengthen it: {tang zitzet} is perfectly straight, and {kang zitzet} is pure white
<min>, name, with <khum>, put in: enter a name in a list, register, as refugees with the UN or guests on arriving at a meeting; the noun is <minkhumna>
<zon>, seek, with <tawm>, on one's own: look for or get a thing by one's own effort, or only when the need comes; before a noun, self-found
<cing>, be full, and <pan>, begin, written as one word after a number of years or months: have only just completed that length of time
<i> and <za>, hear, written as one word: we hear, we have heard, often closing a report after <cih>
<bawng>, cattle, with <buk>, shed: the shed where cattle are kept, often said of the place where Jesus was born

terms: go round and round/drift about/sway to and fro
definition: <kivei> said twice: keep moving round or to and fro without getting anywhere, of people, of a thing passed round, and of years going by
<neubawl>, belittle, with the noun suffix <na>: treating a person or a people as small, often paired with <simmawhna>
heat cooked food again, glossed in a word list as <sasak> and <lumsak>
of feelings or people, stir up and set going again, as anger, a quarrel or the public
<veng>, quarter of a town or village, with {-pi}, great: a main or large quarter, and part of the name of one, as in {Murlen Vengpi}
said by a writer who sets a matter aside as not known to him, often after <bel> and followed by <in> or <maw>: who knows, that I cannot tell
<a> and <omteh> written as one word: when or whenever someone or something is there or is in a state

terms: put up for the night/lodge/let stay overnight
definition: <giak>, spend the night, with the causative <sak>: give someone a place to sleep for the night, or make someone sleep in a place
<lo>, hill field, with <hal>, burn: set fire to the cut and dried growth of a field before sowing, and the season or work of doing so
<sehkholh>, appoint beforehand, with the noun suffix <na>: in teaching about God predestination, in other writing an arrangement or allocation made in advance
<hihtuak> and the sentence-final <hi> written as one word at the end of a statement: it seems that it is so

terms: be united as one/be one body/unite
definition: <kilom>, gathered in a mass, and <khat>, one, written as one word: be or become a single group
<bang>, like, and <bel>, as for, written as one word after a noun or a number: picks out one case among others, as for this one, such a one as
said after <khamul>, beard, of a thick untrimmed beard, in news items a way of naming bearded militants
<a> and <leinuam> written as one word: the one or the ones who want to buy
<nget>, ask for, and <loh>, not, written as one word: not asked for; {man ngetloh in} is without asking payment, free of charge
<uut>, want, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not want to, be unwilling
freedom, the state of being free, in political writing often paired with <suahtakna>
<nawn>, carry, with the noun suffix <na>: the moving of goods from place to place, mostly as {van nawnna}
after <zun>, urine, or <ek>, excrement: the passing of urine or stool, or the vessel or spot used for it

terms: a certain amount/to some extent/a fair degree

name used in songs for the village of <Saizang>, as <Dimtui> is for Tedim, mostly as {Saitui vangkhua}
word of songs and poems for the heart or mind, where plain speech has <lungsim>
<kikhen>, be divided or part from one another, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not separated, staying together
<a> and <cihtak> written as one word: the faithful one, he or they are faithful; {acihtak lo} is the unfaithful
a Zomi village; written after the name of a person it shows the home village
<neih>, have, and <ten>, the plural with the marker of the doer, written as one word: the people who have or own a thing, as subject of what follows; {inn neihten} is the house owners
<zeek>, manage, and <siam>, skilled, written as one word: know how to handle money, time or goods so that they go far
<a> and <kikhum> written as one word: he is shut in or imprisoned, the one imprisoned; of a tape or a song, is recorded

terms: in order to be able/in order to overcome
definition: <zawh>, be able or overcome, and <nading>, in order to, written as one word after a verb: so that one can do it, so as to win
<a> and <zaak>, the form of <za>, hear, used before <ciangin>, written as one word: he or she heard, what he heard
<a> and <tote>, masters, written as one word: the masters or lords that someone serves

second half of the pair {aktui aktak}, eggs and chickens, the things brought to someone as a gift, as tribute or as a bribe; not seen apart from <aktui>
<zun>, tend and build up, with the noun suffix <na>: looking after a land, a people or a language so that it thrives; another spelling of <zuunna>
found as {ahike'h}, a contraction of {ahih kei leh}: or, or else, if not
<khit> and <nung> written as one word: after something is done or over
<mi> and <tung> written as one word: on or upon a person or other people, with <panin> from others

<mawkmawk> and <lo> written as one word: no ordinary one, not just any, also not merely or idly
the overhanging edge of the roof of a house and the sheltered space under it
<bek> and <tak> written as one word: just at the moment of, as soon as, at the very time
<na> and <ma> written as one word: in front of you, the way ahead of you
<pil> and <loh> written as one word: not being wise or learned, and the fact of not being so
particle after a verb, mostly in {ta teu zongin}, even though it may indeed be so

of a road, be laid out or built along a line
<ci> and <ciat> written as one word: each one says, everyone calls it so
<hih> and <ci> written as one word, mostly as {hihci bangin}: in this way, as follows
<neih> and <dan> written as one word: the way something is had, held or conducted
let something drag on, put it off, keep someone waiting
a city in the United States

terms: our future/what lies ahead of us
definition: <i> and <mailam> written as one word: our future, the time ahead of us
plural of <thumaan>: those who are truthful, upright or righteous

terms: want to amend/want to improve/want to repair
definition: <puah> and <nop> written as one word: wish to mend, amend or improve something, also what one wishes to amend
exclamation of praise to God, also in {Halleluijah lapi}, the Hallelujah Chorus
a people of Meghalaya in north-east India, whose main town is Tura
<seh> and <hi> written as one word: reckon or count something as, also assign or appoint someone
a Zomi village in Chin State, Myanmar
<ih> and <nuntak> written as one word: we live, with <na> our life
<a> and <buk> written as one word: he or they take shelter, stay somewhere for a time as a refuge
<tawp> and <ah> written as one word: at the end of something, in the end
plural of <melhoih>: those who are good-looking, also after a noun as in {nungak melhoihte}, beautiful girls
second half of a pair after <tatdan> or <omdan>: ways and manners, how one behaves or how one is
the words of a song, as against its tune
<sep>, do, and <sin>, learn, as one word: learn by doing, carry out in practice what has been taught

<kam>, speech, with <dam>, slow and gentle: speaking softly and calmly, not in anger, often paired with <kamnem>; {kamdam in} is in a gentle voice

<kithuah>, join or accompany, with <khop>, together: be or work together with someone, come together as one
<kiom>, people are, and <lo>, not, written as one word: among people there is none, mostly after <kuamah>, nobody
<a> and <lemlo> written as one word: what is not convenient or does not work out; also as a noun, something that goes wrong
<a> and <zaknop> written as one word, mostly as {azaknop huai}: that is pleasant or interesting to hear
<gel>, plan, with <khawm>, together, written as one word: think out and decide a matter jointly
<kawm>, wall, with <zawl>, bar: the horizontal timber of the wall of a house, on which things are hung or fastened

definition: <a> and <cihteh> written as one word after the word that is explained: when one says this, what is meant is
<leeng>, fly, with <phei>, across: fly on to another place, or rush over to someone as if flying
<veeng>, <leh> and <paam> written as one word: the neighbours and the people living all around
<ka>, I, and <ko>, express, written as one word after <lungdam> or <lungdamna>: I or we express thanks

<pom>, hold fast, with <pih>, together with: take up and hold to a name, a view or a cause along with others, accept it as one's own

found in the pair {sumzon paizonna}, earning money and making a living: going about to seek a livelihood
<i>, our, and <sanggam> written as one word: our brothers and sisters, said of kindred peoples and of fellow believers

<gualh>, arrange, with <zia>, manner: the way things are set in order, as the letters and words of writing or the places of people in a household

<i>, we, and <sim>, read, written as one word: we read, mostly before <ciangin>, when we read
<lai>, still or at the time of, with the emphatic <mah>, written as one word: still so even now, or just as at that time; the same spelling also stands for {lai mah}, the writing itself

<taksa>, body, with <lam>, side, written as one word: what concerns the body, set against <khalam>, the spiritual side
what falls to a person or a group as theirs: a share or a role, and in present-day writing a right, as in {mihing tanvo}, human rights
<lek>, translate, and <khia>, out, written as one word: turn a text out of another language
<theih>, know or be able, and <man>, because, written as one word: because one knows, and after a verb because one is able to

put up a fence round a place to keep animals or harm out, also written {dai kai}; as a figure, guard one's life
<gam>, <leh> and <lei> written as one word: the country and its soil, the homeland

<khang> grow with <pha> good: grow well and strong; with <sak>, make something thrive, nourish it
<khang> generation with <pha> good: a generation of people who grow up together and do well
<mansuah> lose with the prefix <ki>: be lost, or lose what is one's own
<leen.2> hold with <cip> firmly: take hold of and keep in one's grip, said of a person, a thing or power
<muan> trust and <pen.2> most written as one word: trusted most, the one trusted most; often paired as {muanpen suanpen}, the one most relied upon
movement in Malaysia for clean and fair elections, known for its street rallies
<gan> animal with <ta> child: the animals that a household keeps; paired with <ganpi> as {ganpi ganta}, livestock great and small, and with {huangvulh}, kept in a pen

definition: <theisiam> understand with the prefix <ki>: understand and bear with each other; at the end of a notice it asks the reader to be understanding
used in the saying {tangtel sihtan bang}, like an earthworm in torment: said of one who writhes, shrinks or is stirred up at once when touched by a word or deed
town in the west of the state of Manipur in India, on the railway line planned from India to Myanmar

terms: mention at all/speak of at all
definition: <gen> say and the emphatic <vet> written as one word, used with a negative: {genvet om lo} and {genvet kullo} are not even worth mentioning, let alone, out of the question
<nem> soft with the endearing ending {-no}: gentle and sweet, said of words and of the voice, mostly in songs as {tongdam nemno}, gentle words; also a personal name
<za.3> hundred with <cin.1> be completed, after <kum> year: a full hundred years; {Kum Zacin Pawipi} is a centenary celebration; also a part of personal names
<tui> water with <huan.3> cook: cook food in plain water without frying, of vegetables, meat, fish or maize
<zat> use and <lo> not written as one word: not use, without using; {lim zatlo} is not use much
<a> and <sinna> written as one word: where or what someone studies, the learning of a thing; {asinna dan in} is as a trial, tentatively
township of the city of Yangon in Myanmar
<kaang.1> white with the ending {-pi}, great, used in names: {Tui Kaangpi} is the Chindwin River, and {Inn Kaangpi} is the White House of the United States
<a> and <haat> written as one word: that is strong, the strong one; of flying or running, fast
a government rest house of colonial times, kept by a caretaker and standing at stages along the road, as at Tedim and Phatzang; later a landmark and the name of a place
<tung> arrive and <masa.3> first written as one word: arrive before others, or come to a place first of all

terms: to crack down on/to strike/to crush
definition: <zial> and <ding> written as one word, in news of war and unrest: in order to strike at an enemy or armed group and put it down; <zial.1> roll up is used here of rounding up and crushing
<neusak> make small with the prefix <ki>: make oneself small, in size or in standing; set against <kiliansak>, make oneself great
placed after a verb or after <tu> now: only just, at this very point and not before, often with surprise or reproach; {tu phingphing} is right now of all times
<mawk> and <lo> written as one word after a verb: not do a thing carelessly or without reason; in a question with <ding> it asks whether a thing is not surely so
<i> and <kicih.1> written as one word: that we are called or call ourselves, as in {Zomi ikicih}, our being called Zomi
<a> and <kial.2> written as one word, mostly after <gil> belly: {gil akial} is the belly is hungry; {akial} alone is the one who is hungry
Burmese dish of pickled tea leaves mixed with other tasty things; <laphet> is the tea leaf
<a> and <banna> written as one word, in the pair {atun abanna}, where someone or something has arrived and got to: {atun abanna kitheilo} is whereabouts unknown, gone without trace
a period of supervised work that a student or trainee does to gain experience
a villager called up to carry loads from one village to the next for soldiers, officials or travellers, and this duty itself; {taiban pai} is go as a porter
<hin.1> live with <dan> manner: how a person or a people live
style of popular music with rapping, and the youth fashion that goes with it
<tual> local with <lai> writing: the writing of one's own people; {Mang Tuallai} was the first name of the Roman-letter Zolai that Cope made in 1913
<na.3> and <zuan> written as one word: headed for a place, in an account of the past
<na.3> and <teeng> written as one word: lived or settled in a place, in an account of the past; also written <nateng.2>
<dawi> spirit and <thoih> appease written as one word: make offerings to the spirits to turn away sickness and harm, as in the old religion before Christianity; also the practice itself
<siksak.1> cover the cost and <lo> not written as one word: an insurer or other payer does not bear a cost
<ngah> get and <teh.4> when written as one word: when someone gets or has something, as in {hun ka ngahteh}, when I have time; said to a person, {ngahteh} with <teh.5> is you have got
<va> and <kuan> written as one word: go off to work, to the field or to war
<i> and <tuah> written as one word: we meet with, we come upon, said of hardship and events
<i> and <beh> written as one word: our clan
the chief town of the Garo Hills in Meghalaya, India; in news of Burma the same spelling is the title Thura before a name
the ancient city of Tyre on the sea coast, as one article spells it
being able to learn something, and the place or means by which it can be learned
<sum> and <donna> written as one word: the collecting of money given for a cause
<kilamdang> and <lo> written as one word: not differ, be no different, often after <tawh>
<nem> and <tuam> written as one word: become lighter or less as a result, said of expense and of a longing heart
<ih> and <minam> written as one word: our people

terms: not rely on/not take pride in
definition: <suang> and <lo> written as one word: not lean on something as strength or as a ground for pride
<sahkhua>, society, a term of one group of writers, with <lam>: on the side of society, social
<kilam> and <te> written as one word: the ones that are built, said of houses
<tawn> said twice: keep going along a path; with <lamlam> and {diangdiang} it is said of one who merely drifts along
<zu> and <khum> written as one word: sweet rice beer, the best of the beer, named beside {salim}, the tastiest meat
the black soot on a cooking pot or left by smoke; {belmang zut}, smear with soot, is also said for bringing shame on someone
<kei> and <lam> written as one word: my side, toward me
<upa> with the suffix <pi>, great: the chief elder or head of a people or an organisation

terms: as much as possible/as many as possible
definition: <a> and <hitheizah> written as one word: as much or as many as can be
<ih> and <pian> written as one word: we are born, our being born
the prefix <ki> and <na.4>: people are ill, there is sickness, set against <kicidam>; with <sak> hurt or grieve, and of people hurt one another
<khua> and <lian> written as one word: a large town or village
of a bird, sit on the eggs in the nest until they hatch
rule over a land, said of the British taking the hills under their government; a word of the Mizo side
<thupi> and <seh> written as one word: count something as important
<pau> and <zat> written as one word: the language or way of speaking that someone uses
placed after a verb to stress it: indeed, for sure; before <hangin> or <napi>, though it is indeed so
<kithuah> and <khopna> written as one word: keeping company and doing things together
found in {khuaisah zu}, the beer that is carried when the bees are taken at the Khuado feast; what the word says apart from <khuai>, bee, is not settled
the capital city of Turkey
a people of the Falam area and their chief village, who made war on the Tedim side in the 1800s
<sum> and <bang> written as one word: {sumbang zah} is how much money, and {sumbang mah} with a negative is no money at all
the Thado people, <Thahdo>, with the plural <te>
<cihdaan> and <te> written as one word, placed after a list or a quoted statement: things of that kind, and the like
a person of the colonial power, said of the British
{suan leh khaak}, descendant and offshoot, with the plural <te>: all the later generations of a person or people
<i> and <dawn> written as one word: we drink
<it> with the suffix <pih>: love someone along with another; {itpih dahpihna} is sympathy and condolence
<kilam> and <thak> written as one word: newly built
found after <gii> and <gamgi>, boundary: the setting or drawing of a boundary or limit
placed after a verb: doing it quietly and at ease, without stir
<i> and <kisak> written as one word, placed after a describing word: that we think ourselves to be so, as in {thupi ikisak}, we think ourselves great
<vai>, matter, with <siang>, clean: the matter is cleared, a thing is settled with no more trouble, or is the simple way out
<khua>, weather, with <sia>, bad: bad or stormy weather, set against <khuapha>, fair weather
a spirit of the old belief, named beside <khuapha>; {khuasia meide} is the ghost light seen at night, also called {khuahaang meide}
<gal>, war, and <lai>, time, written as one word: the time of a war, after its name as in {Japan gallai}, during the Japanese war
the particle <na> and <kigelh> written as one word: it is found written, it stands written, said of a text that is quoted
<gal>, war, and <ma>, before, written as one word: the time before a war, mostly {Japan galma}, before the Japanese war
of the ground or a hard thing: break open in cracks; a few writers also spell <khang>, generation, this way
a village in the Lamka area of Manipur, India
<neu>, small, with <lawm>, friend: a friend since one was little, a close old friend
<nei> and <laai> written as one word: still have, have yet
the rule of the old religion that after a sacrifice the household or the whole village stays at home and keeps from work, hunting and visits; {zeh tang} is keep it; compare <zehtan>
a blade that a man carries, named with <thal>, bow, and held in dances; in songs {namtem hiam} is the sharp blade; a word list gives it as <temta>
the flag of a country, a state or an organisation, glossed flag by its writer; compare <dialpi>
<ka> and <zon> written as one word: I seek, that I seek, also of working to get a living
noun of <kigawmkik>: the joining again of a people or a country that was divided
<a> and <kitukalh> written as one word: that conflict, the ones at odds, as in {akitukalh thu}, a matter in dispute
a German airline, one of whose aircraft crashed in France in March 2015
<tuk> and <thum> written as one word: three tuk, the size of a grown pig, as in {vok tukthum}; also a grade of fine in customary law reckoned in such pigs
a Zomi group and its dialect, counted among the Paite dialects
<van>, goods, with <sai>, shop: a shop that sells goods
a village of the Kalay area, also called Ciingpikot
a former village of the Tedim area, burned by British troops about 1890, after which its people moved on to Singmual
a garrison town in Shan State, Myanmar, where army officers are trained
a township of Yangon, named in life stories for its high schools
<Zomi> and <minamni> written as one word: the national day of the Zomi, kept on 20 February
in {Khuado sakholh}, a gift given at the <Khuado> festival and carried home; among the Zomi in Japan a yearly gift of money to a chosen man and woman; by its parts perhaps a gift of meat

terms: in order/in neat rows/one after another
definition: placed after a verb such as <gual> or <kigual>: set out neatly in order, one after another without a gap
<midang> and <a> written as one word: what belongs to another person, that of others, set against <ei a>, our own
<ai> and <taangin> written as one word, the same as {aitang in}: placed after the name of a person or group, in its name and as its representative
<na> and <lau> written as one word: you are afraid, or with the <na> of an earlier event, they were afraid

terms: closed at the bottom/blocked at the end
definition: <taw>, bottom, and <bing>, be closed: with no opening at the lower end; in the folk tale of children whose bottom is closed, and of the end of a river where it joins another; also the name of the village in that tale
<gui>, vine, and <khau>, rope: the long trailing stem of a creeper; in songs {guikhau bang zam} is spread out like a vine, of longing that reaches a far land
<uh>, the marker of a plural subject, and the question word <hia> written as one word: closes a question about what several people do or think
what people look forward to or rely on for the future; the articles use it where <lametna> also stands
<a> and <phuan> written as one word: the one who sets up, mostly as {aphuan khia}, who founded an organisation or church, and {aphuan te}, the founders; of a drink, that foams
holding back among other people, not daring to speak or come forward; {mi zahkai} is a shy person
<kim>, here a spelling of <kiim>, and <bang> written as one word: placed after a number or amount to show that it is an estimate
<bek> and the sentence-final <hi> written as one word: it is only that; {bekhi lo} is not only
<baih>, easy, and <loh>, not, written as one word: the form of <baihlo> used before words such as <dan>, <ding> and <zia>, as in {a baihloh dan}, how hard it is
mourning for the dead, and a time or day set apart to remember them, as {suunna hun} and {suunna ni}
<i>, we, and <cihleh> written as one word: if we say or ask, taking up what was just said as a condition or a question
<Zotung> with the plural <te>: the Zotung, people of that Chin group
placed after a noun or a time: up to and including it, even that; {tuni tanpha} is up to today
<a> and <hual> written as one word: the wave, as in {ahual thum veina}, the third wave, or of thread and cotton, that is rolled or wound
<van>, goods, and <neih>, own: the things a person owns
<kilawm> and the sentence-final <hi> written as one word: after <leh> it seems so, it looks as if; after <ding> it is fitting to do

terms: be more convenient/be made easier/go better
definition: <lem>, be convenient, with <tuam>, all the more: become easier or more convenient because of something
<hanciam>, strive, with the linking <a> written as one word: placed before a verb, doing it with effort, as in {hanciama sep}, work hard
word of surprise or reproach: after a noun or verb, that it should be this of all things or that someone should do such a thing; alone, a call of reproach to a person
feel uneasy toward others over what one receives, owes or has done; {kisuanlah huai} is embarrassing, and {kisuanlah nading om lo} is there is nothing to feel bad about
be late or left behind others; {kiziakai sak} is hold back, delay
<phu>, push against, with <suak>, through: press on through a difficulty until one is past it
<pawllut>, be a member, with the noun suffix <na>: being a member of an organisation, and the fee paid for it
<kamlet>, interpreter, with the plural <te>
<setzung>, factory, and <ah> written as one word: in or at a factory
<a> and a second part written as one word, where the second part is the long spelling of <hai>, foolish, and not <haii>, greedy: one who is foolish, being foolish
<i>, we, and <lam>, build, written as one word: we build, as in {inn ilam}; in {ilam en} it is the first part of {i lamen}, we hope, divided wrongly
the act of inviting someone or calling on them to join, close to <zotna>; in {pum zawtna} of the dictionary the same spelling is paralysis

terms: can often/tend to/from time to time
definition: <thei>, able, and <zeel>, repeatedly, written as one word: placed after a verb, it can happen or is done from time to time
<i>, we, and <muan>, trust, written as one word: we trust, or before <ahi> and a name, the one we trust
<mei>, fire or electric light, and <lam>, side: the field of electric power, as a trade and as a government department; the dictionary also has it for the tail end of an aircraft
placed after a noun or phrase to single it out against what might be expected: it is this one rather, this one indeed; found in northern dialect writing
<ci>, say, and <diam>, the question word, written as one word: after <i> or <ih>, shall we call it, said when the speaker tries out a name for something
<suak>, become, and <lel>, merely, written as one word: come to be nothing more than
ancient city of Asia Minor where the church council of AD 451 met, {Chalcedon Khawmpi}

terms: I declare to you/we make known/express
definition: <kong>, I to you, and <pulaak> written as one word: I or we make known to you, common in notices of thanks and condolence
<bawl>, make, with <hoih>, good: mend a thing or make it better, said of roads, cars and buildings and also of a life or a relationship
a blood-sucking worm that lives in streams and gets into the nose of people and cattle; {liit dawk} is a saying about one who will not let go
a thing worn hanging round the neck, such as a scarf, the stole of a priest or the strap of an identity card
the particle <na> and <do> written as one word: fought, fight back; with <zin>, guest, receive or host
<lak>, take, with <pih>: get a document or a thing on behalf of someone; {pan lakpih} is take part together with
<nei> and <khinzo> written as one word: have already, already had
<khentat>, decide, with the ending {-sa}: already decided, what has been settled beforehand
the bones that are left of a dead person or animal
<uh> and <ciang> written as one word after a verb: when they, at the time they
<tun> and <phet> written as one word: just on arriving, the moment one arrives, followed by <in>
<na> and <phuak> written as one word: composed a song, or you shall name
<suan> and <leh> written as one word, in the pair {suanleh khak}, descendants
<ka> and <thu> written as one word: my word; {kathu ngetna} is my prayer, my request
<inn>, house, with <sim>, every: each house in turn, every household
a small lamp that burns oil with a wick

terms: a little while ago/recently/a little later
definition: <den>, a while ago, with <deuh>, somewhat: a short while back; {a dendeuh ciangin} is a little later
<kiam> and <lo> written as one word: does not grow less, without lessening
<neu> and <nono> written as one word: small, said of several things that are each small
<gelh> and <lo> written as one word: does not write, not written
<khawm> and the plural marker <uh> written as one word after a verb: they do it together
<hong> written together with the first part of <vaikhak> or <vaihawm>: {hongvai khak} is instructs us, and {hongvai hawm} is arranges for us
<ciamnuih> with the prefix {ki-}: joke and tease one another in fun; also be mocked or fooled
the noun of <kigualh>: the order in which people or things are set out, a list of names in turn
<en>, look, and <ni>, let us, written as one word: let us look at, let us consider
<hi> and <napin> written as one word: although it is so, the same as <hinapi>
<gam>, land, with <ciam>, promise: the land that God promised to Israel, Canaan
<van>, goods, with <lui>, old: used or old things, and the old objects that are kept in a museum
imitates the pounding of the heart in fear, said with <ci>: {dip in pukpuk ci} is the heart pounds; also the name of a dull sound in tales
<hilai> and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word: it is still so, it still remains so
<kikup> with its last part said twice: go on talking a matter over together
<kim>, all or fully, with the particle <ta>, now, written as one word: all of them by now, now complete
<nuihzak>, laugh, with the ending {-huai}, worth doing: that makes one laugh, amusing or absurd
a measured plot of land that is sold as one unit
<a> and <hua>, hate, written as one word: one who hates, hating
<tuam>, separate, with <din>, stand: take a separate stand from others, be on its own; in grammar, of a word that stands by itself
describes rain that falls or water that sounds without a break, after <zu>, fall, and <ging>, sound
<tha>, strength, with <hoih>, good: having a strong and healthy body
placed after the name of a land or state: the whole area that it takes in, within its bounds; found in articles written in the Paite way, compare <huam>
<ahih> and <lai>, time or still, written as one word: while it is or was, at the time when it was still, followed by <in>, <pekin> or <takin>
<leng>, fly, and <a> written as one word: flew and, flying; in a few sentences it is the conditional <leng> with <a>
a part of Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, known for its shopping mall and its police station
<sial>, mithun, and <khat> written as one word: one mithun, as an offering, a payment or a price
in songs, the north or the upper side, paired with {khangciang}, the south; in prose the same letters are mostly the end of a verb in {-sak} followed by <ciang>
<zang>, use, and <sa> written as one word: having used a thing, or one who already uses it
<na> and <mat> written as one word: you catch, what you catch; in a report of the past <na> is the particle and the whole means caught
be mixed together with something else so that the two are no longer apart
<lawi> and <giat> written as one word: eight buffaloes, a customary payment or ransom reckoned in buffaloes
<a> and <kihta> written as one word: who fears, the one who fears, mostly of fearing God
be twisted or wound, of a thing that is bent round or wrung into shape; in one sentence it is said of two people who accuse each other
what a wrong brings on the one who did it, used in {mawhlawh tawi}, bear the blame or the punishment
<maw> and <leh> written as one word at the end of an exclamation: can it be, is it so then, said in wonder or protest
a greeting of the morning, used beside {sunpha} and {nitakpha}
the place or the end that one is heading for
<i> and <teel> written as one word: we choose, what we have chosen
<gam> and <pha> written as one word: a good land, or the land is good and fertile
<tak> and <cing> written as one word after a verb: worthy of the action or fit for it, as {etteh takcing}, worthy to be imitated
<a> and <ol> written as one word: it is easy, easily; the same letters are also the name of an internet company in addresses
the Pawi, the people of the Falam side, as enemies in war, and the wars fought with them; the first part is the name of the people, not the word for a feast, and <gal> is enemy or war

<ding> and <ka> written as one word: the marker of what is to come followed by the first person marker of the next verb, as in {ding ka hi hiam}, shall I; in one article {Dingka} is quoted as the Burmese word for a coin
<hong> and <zawh> written as one word: conquer or overcome, seen from the side of the speaker or of the place spoken of
<kizep> and <zia> written as one word: the way people dress and adorn themselves, fashion

terms: care about/attend to/take an interest in
definition: <kin> and <pih> written as one word: be concerned about a matter together with or for someone, take it up as one's own
<bil>, ear, and <dawh>, hold out, written as one word: give ear, listen with attention
the rays of the sun, the light and heat that reach the earth from it
the finishing of a course of study, and the level of schooling that a person has completed
<pat> and <pih> written as one word: begin a work together with others or for them, be among those who start it
<mipihte> with the subject marker <in> shortened and written as one word: one's own people, as the doers of the action
<i> and <pumpi> written as one word: our body
<lukhu> and <nelkai> written as one word: the cap worn at graduation, and so a degree of a university
plural of <micimawh>: people in want or distress who need help, in the news often those who suffer from war
in writing about Buddhism, the teaching of a Buddha and the age in which it lasts
a village of the Tedim area in Chin State, Myanmar
<a> and <liangko> written as one word: his or her shoulder
<cin> and <lo> written as one word: not reaching the full amount, not enough for the need, not up to what is required
<la>, <sa> and <ding> written as one word: to sing songs, in order to sing
<muh> said twice: see again and again, or whatever one sees, as in {ih zakzak, ih muhmuh}, what we keep hearing and seeing
the open floor inside a house or building, where guests sit and where people lie down to sleep
<sang>, school, and <pai>, go, written as one word: go to school, the going to school
<ipsung> and <ah> written as one word: in or into the pocket or bag
without having to pay, one writer explains it with English free; also with <in> or <a> after it
mostly with <loh>, not: {gitneih loh in} and {gitneih loh laitakin} mean unexpectedly, when one did not expect it
<kumsial> and <in> written as one word: every year
<diamdiam> and the plural <te> written as one word, after a verb with <ki>: those who do it to one another in a kindly way, as in {kilui diamdiamte}, people who share with one another
<thei> and <diam> written as one word at the end of a question: can it be done, would one be able to
<luan> and <khop> written as one word, the form of <luangkhawm> used before words such as <ding>, <nading> and <theih>: flow together, and so of a people, come together as one
