definition: <ahoih> and <khom> written as one word: a fairly good amount or number of something, as of votes or seats
<ka> and <muhna> written as one word: what I saw, what I observed, often in the heading of a report
<phi> and <dingte> written as one word: those who are going to sit an interview or a test

terms: observe a taboo/keep a rest day/abstain
definition: in the old religion and custom, keep a set day or time on which people stay in and refrain from work, going out or meeting others

terms: way of suffering/way of feeling/how one is affected
definition: <thuak> and <zia> written as one word: the way a person bears or is affected by something, also the way of feeling
<hong> and <laam> written as one word, mostly in songs: comes dancing, dances this way

terms: in the arms/in the lap/in the bosom
definition: <ang> and <sungah> written as one word: in the arms, in the lap or at the breast of someone
island country in the Indian Ocean, east of Africa, a British colony in the time of the first missionaries
<pha>, <lam> and <manawh> written as one word: heading toward what is good, said of change and progress for the better
word of songs and speeches for the Zomi as the beloved children of Zo, one person or the whole people
<ki>, one another, with <phak>, reach, and the noun suffix <na>: the reaching of one another, mostly paired with <kikawmna> or <kikawm> for travel and contact between places and peoples
placed with a measure: square, of area, as in {tai patle}, square miles, and {pi 100 patle}, a hundred feet each way; also the distance around
city in the state of Uttar Pradesh in northern India, seat of a university

terms: servant/errand runner/one at the bidding of others
definition: a person whom others send here and there and use for their tasks, a servant who does as told; also as the name of such work
first part of {zih ziah}, the word <zihziah> written as two words, placed after a verb: in great numbers, all over the place
move along smoothly without effort, as on a level road or riding in a car, often with <hialhial>
<baihtak> and <in> written as one word: easily, without trouble
<ki>, one another, with <elna>, malice: ill will and envy between people, named beside <kihuat>, hating one another
<ta> and <dihdih> written as one word after a verb, of something that happens on the spot and unexpectedly, as in {nausuak tadihdih}, give birth there and then
<lung>, mind, with <geel>, plan, mostly in songs and headings: what the mind thinks out, a thought or plan; also as a verb, think over
<a> and <masuan> written as one word: what he or they are heading for, the way ahead or the future of someone

terms: likewise/in the same way/just like that
definition: <tua> and <mahbang> written as one word, mostly followed by <in>: in that same way, likewise
<hi>, be, and <ngeilo>, never, written as one word: is never, has never been
a wild game bird of the hills that lives on the ground and is hunted, named beside <vasa> of other kinds

terms: take on a visit/visit with/bring along to visit
definition: <hawh> and <pih> written as one word: go on a visit together with someone, take or bring someone along to see a place or a person
Burmese word for a person who follows a trade or calling, seen only in {nainganyee tamaa}, politician
<telsiam>, understand well, with the suffix <pih>: understand someone or his situation with sympathy, make allowance for
the very top of something high, such as a tower, a dome or a mountain
<peuhmah> and <ding> written as one word after a verb: will or should do so in any case, without choosing; mostly denied, as in {peuhmahding hilo}, it is not something to be done just anyhow
one of the older spellings of the name Zo, and the name by which the Asho Chin of the plains call themselves
<holim>, chat, with its last syllable doubled: go on chatting at ease
<van>, sky, with <khawh>, stab: piercing the sky, said of a very tall building; {vankhawh inn} is a skyscraper

terms: inside of a bowl/inside of a box
definition: <kuang> and <sung> written as one word: in the bowl or trough, and also inside a box, as in {mee kuangsung}, in the ballot box
<leii>, bridge, with <pi>, great, written as one word: a large bridge
the length of a mountain ridge, placed after the name of the range, as in {Sialkal tangdung}, the Sialkal range
what is done for pleasure, amusement or a social celebration
<len>, hold, with <suak>, on: go on holding an office, a post or power
<len>, fly, with <suak>, on: fly straight on to a further place
<a> and <bawlkhiatna> written as one word: the putting out of a statement or study by a body, as in {Statement abawlkhiatna ah}, in the statement that they issued
a large monkey of the kinds nearest to man, an ape
<mo> and <hoih> written as one word: a daughter-in-law who is good to her husband's family
<kei> and <guak> written as one word: I alone, I by myself, without anyone else
<a> and <sing> written as one word: the tree or the wood of something; {asing asuang} is every tree and stone of a place
a year of school, followed by its number, as in {danh 10}, the tenth standard
<hong> and <si> written as one word: he died, said from the side of those left behind, and of Christ who died for us
<anlak>, harvest, with <pawi>, festival: a feast held at harvest, used of Thanksgiving, the Chinese mid-autumn festival and the Jewish feast of harvest
<tual>, native, with <thah>, kill: the killing of a person of the same community, murder
<kong> and <ngetpih> written as one word: I or we pray with you or on your behalf, a closing formula of condolence notices
<lungdam>, joy, with <pawi>, festival: a festival of rejoicing or thanksgiving, also said of Christmas
the place where people have settled or taken shelter, whether refugees, armed groups or a lodger
lead from the front, guide and take charge of people or of a work
<tem> and <bang> written as one word in songs and poetry: like a knife; {tembang kuah} is to keep something close and hold it dear, as a knife is carried at the side
<lam>, dance, with <tual>, open space: the ground where the village dances
<ziak> and <a> written as one word after a noun or clause: because of, on account of; frequent in texts written in the Paite manner
<mal>, north, with <lam>, side, written as one word: the north, the northern side
<guan> and <ding> written as one word: will give, put in or assign, as in {nasep guanding}, will give work
<kim>, all, and the negative <loh> written as one word after a verb, before words such as <hang> and <man>: not in every case, not all of them
old spelling of Qin, the Chinese ruling house and its ruler, given as one of the written forms of the name Chin

terms: go on using/keep using/continue to use
definition: <zang>, use, with <to>, onward, written as one word: go on using from then on
<tuat>, reckon, with <dan>, way: how something is counted or estimated, and the school subject arithmetic

terms: wherever one is/every place of residence
definition: <omna>, place of being, with its last syllable doubled: each and every place where someone or something is, as in {Zomite omnana-ah}, wherever the Zomi are
a kind of passenger bus that runs between towns such as Kalay and Tedim, apparently the Burmese word for a vehicle closed in with glass
<lei>, buy, and the linking <in> written as one word: buying, having bought, before the verb that follows
<sai>, shop or stall, and <ah> written as one word: at the shop that sells the thing named before it
descriptive word placed after a verb for something that dribbles, is smeared or lies about in a mess, often followed by <den>
<tulai> and <a> written as one word: of the present time, today's, before a noun
what a speaker or writer keeps speaking about most, in {genbel in nei}, make something one's main theme, keep stressing it
the state of being of one mind and living together in harmony, often paired with <kipumkhatna>, unity
<lei>, here a bridge, and <khat>, one, written as one word: a bridge or flyover
<tuam>, separate, and <neih>, have, written as one word: have something separate or of one's own
the English plural of <Hacker>, used with <te>: people who break into computer systems and accounts
<ciat>, each, and <a> written as one word: each one separately, placed after the word it applies to
<hong> and <paikik> written as one word: come back to where the speaker or the story is
<tua>, that, and <kiim>, around, written as one word: the area around the place just mentioned, often with <ah>
a rank of junior commissioned officer in the army of British India and Burma, below subedar, the rank named in the life stories of Zomi soldiers
a village in the south of Manipur near the border of Mizoram, where Christian mission work in southern Manipur began in 1910
placed after a verb: to some degree, more or less, not fully or exactly so
<puah>, repair or amend, with <nopna>, the wish to: the wish to put something right, or to amend a law or constitution
the capital city of Libya
<gua>, bamboo, with <pum>, whole or round: a whole length of bamboo, used as a pole, a stick or a surface to carve on
<gamtat> and <luheek> written as one word: the way a person acts and carries himself
word of songs and fine writing, also said <muikhua>: the weather or the times, mostly of the dark, sad or lonesome side, as in {khimkhua zing}, darkness falls
<a> and <sapna> written as one word: his, her or their calling or inviting of someone, the invitation
word of songs and poetry for <tung>, arrive: come to be at another place
deal with a matter or a dispute until it is cleared up, with <vaan>, oversee: settle it, solve it
<hong> and <ho> written as one word: talk to the speaker or the person addressed, also by telephone; {hongho pih} is speak with
a person or the people of the <Sihzang> group of the Zomi
money collected or contributed for a cause, as a church collection or a share of the cost; {sumdon phuang} is announce a collection
go round from place to place, with <vak>, go about; mostly in {vakkawn sia}, an itinerant preacher or travelling evangelist
<siam>, skilled, and <kul>, must, written as one word: it takes skill, one has to be good at the thing named before it
a single grain of <mim>, millet, named with <taangtang> in the story of Thangho and Liando, who shared even one grain between them
<na>, your, and <pu>, grandfather, written as one word
form of <zakhang> used before words such as <nading>, <ciang> and <loh>, and as a noun beside <minthan>, fame: be raised in rank, promotion
a flat piece or cake of food, counted as {pheel khat}, one piece; compare <phel>, piece
descriptive word placed after a verb of falling such as <puk> or <kia>: going right over or right down; after <sang>, tall, it pictures a tall lanky figure

terms: in such places as/and the like
definition: <khong> and <ah> written as one word, after a noun of place: in that and places like it, in such things as
<nei> doubled and written as one word: go on having or holding something, time after time
<kisin> and <tawm> written as one word: learn or practise a thing on one's own, not be born knowing it
<buang> and <ah> written as one word, after <lo>: {lo buangah} is except for, apart from
<meet> and <zaw> written as one word: bring more profit or be the better bargain, often after <sangin>, than
<deih> and the linking <a> written as one word: wanting it, and
<tel> and <sawm> written as one word: make an effort to understand
<angtang> and <in> written as one word: being proud of someone or something, with pride
<hilh> and <zia> written as one word: the way something is taught, what someone teaches

terms: until reaching/as far as/all the way to
definition: <tun> and <dong> written as one word: until one arrives at the place or point named before it
<kisam> and the superlative <pen> written as one word: needed above all else
<hau> and <ding> written as one word: will be rich, going to be rich
<gam> and <lutang> written as one word: the head of a country, its president or prime minister

terms: as for me/I for my part
definition: <ken> and the topic particle <bel> written as one word: as for me, setting the speaker against others
<lup> and <man> written as one word, after <zato>: the charge for lying in hospital as a patient
<tamzaw> and <lo> written as one word, after <sang>: not more than the amount named
<thadah> and the causative <sak> written as one word: take away someone's will to do a thing, make lazy
<daai> and <tak> written as one word, mostly with <in>: quietly, in silence, as a country keeping silence in mourning
<kisam> and <teng> written as one word: everything that is needed for a purpose
the chat service of Google, used together with Gmail
of two people, often husband and wife: quarrel with each other in angry words
<a> and <khom> written as one word: what lasts or is enough for a length of time
<i> and <hun> written as one word: our time, the time that we have or that comes to us
<hetlo> and the sentence ending <hi> written as one word: closes a strong negative statement, is not so at all
<tua> and the topic particle <bel> written as one word: as for that, that on the other hand
hollow or spongy inside, as a dried gourd; of words, thought or playing, empty and without substance

terms: look toward from afar/look forward to/gaze at
definition: look out toward something far off in place or time, as a distant land or a hoped for day; common in songs
a session in which a teacher goes through a subject with those who attend, as a training for ministers or leaders
<thupi> and <zia> written as one word: how important or great something is
<zak> and <loh> written as one word: not hearing, used before a following word or in a dependent clause
<tung> and <zong> written as one word: either to or upon someone as well, or also arrive
<khuam> and <bang> written as one word, in songs and with <kho> or <phuh>, plant: like a house post set in the ground, of love or a home firmly established
<ih> and <biak> written as one word, before a name of God: whom we worship
form of <thatlum>, kill outright, used before <ding>, <khit> and other following words
a newly coined Zolai term for sociology, the study of society
<gal>, enemy, with <man>, seize: in the old customs a man who has taken an enemy in war, named together with {saman}, one who has taken game, as entitled to honours
<lei> and <bang> written as one word, mostly in songs: like the earth or ground, as in {leibang liing}, shake like the earth
<i> and <theihna> written as one word: our knowledge, and with <dingin> so that we may know
<khai>, hang, with <gah>, fruit: the fruit and produce that trees and plants bear
the soft spot on the top of a baby's head where the skull bones have not yet joined, and that place on the crown
of the eyes, the nose or the passing of urine: blocked or closed up so that it does not open or flow
a make of motorcycle sold in Myanmar, and the company of that name
<nadong> and <in> written as one word, after a noun: even that, going as far as that

a large wild bovine counted as game beside {zaangsial}, the gaur, <ngal> and <vom> in the old hunting rules, and in a folk tale an animal that is given and led home on a rope; the exact animal is not certain
a people of Zomi tradition: one account gives the name to those who first came out at the Lailun cave and called themselves Lai, and in the folk tale of Neino they are the rivals of Nantal
small in number or amount, used almost always with a negative: {tawmsan lo} and {tawmsan kei} are not few, not a little, considerable
<cil.3>, beginning, and <lai.4>, time, written as one word after a verb or verbal noun and mostly followed by <a> or <in>: at the time when something first begins or has just happened
expressive word placed after a verb: in a slack, sheepish or half-hearted way, without resolve, as in {thukim heihai}, just go along with it, and {en heihai}, stand looking on
<mi>, another person, and <zi>, wife, written as one word, also written {mi' zi}: the wife of another man, in rules against adultery
<singpuak>, carry firewood, with the noun ending {-na}; said after <lokho> or <lokhawh> as {lokhawh singpuakna}, farming and wood carrying, the daily work of village life
a box made of paper or card, and in the dictionary data a case in which paper and writing things are kept; set against <singkuang>, a wooden coffin, in a sentence about burial
word of songs and festive speech, said with <um>, here sit around a dish: {laikuang um} is eat together from one dish, feast together, as <ankuang> is said in plain speech
<na.3> and <tam>, many, written as one word: there are many of them, mostly as {natam mahmah}, very many

<taak.2>, worthy, and <in> written as one word after a verb: in a way that is worthy of what is named; other uses of the spelling, after <ding> and after a noun with <khat>, are not understood and are not described
<pom>, hold, and <kip>, firm, written as one word: hold firmly to a belief, a custom or a name and not let it go
<aki> and <suut>, go through point by point, written as one word: what is traced or examined, it is examined
a town and township on the Chindwin river in Sagaing Region, Myanmar

<khiat>, out, the form of <khia> after a verb, and <ni>, day, written as one word: the day on which the action named is done, as {vote khiatni}, polling day, {pai khiatni}, the day of leaving, and {pian khiatni}, the day something came into being
<dau.2>, be faint, with the causing <sak>, written as one word: make something faint or weak, as love, closeness or the sense of being one people

terms: way of naming/way of composing/naming custom
definition: <phuah>, give a name or compose, and <dan>, way, written as one word: the way names are given, as in {min phuahdan}, or the way a song is composed

terms: the day after tomorrow/in two days
definition: <thai>, the day after tomorrow, and <ciang> written as one word, often paired with <zingciang>, tomorrow: {zingciang thaiciang} is tomorrow and the day after, the days to come
<nop>, here the form of <nuam>, pleasant, and <lo>, not, written as one word: not pleasant, uncomfortable, and of the mind unhappy
<inn>, house, and <sing>, wood, written as one word: wood for building a house, set beside <ansing>, firewood

a word that one writer calls new to Tedim Zolai and that Paite writers use after a verb for fitting or going well; the writer explains it as a healthy body, good looks and strength together, and also as a stroke of good luck
<at.3>, write, and <dan>, way, written as one word: how a name or a language is written, its spelling, the same as <gelhdan>; once also the way of cutting, from <at.2>
<Vaiphei> with the plural <te>: the Vaiphei as a people, a Zo group now mostly of Manipur

terms: in the situation/in the position/in the place of
definition: <dinmun> with the ending {-a}, in or of, written as one word: in the situation or position named before it, the same as <dinmunah>; {tu dinmuna} is as things now stand
<aklui>, rooster, with <pi.3>, big: a full-grown cock, the one that crows in the morning and that a household kills for a guest
word of songs, from <gual.2>, companion, and <ngaih.2>, beloved: the friends and companions a person loves and longs for

<dot>, ask, with <pi.3>, chief, said after <thu> as {thu dotpi}: the one who is asked for advice, an adviser, written as one word <thudotpi>; after <hong> it is a verb form, the chief thing that was asked
a former Zo village by the Tuigo stream in the old stories of the Tedim area, also called Tampi Khuataw; written without a capital the same letters are also {suan zo}, be able to step
<a> and <saan.3>, accept, written as one word with a long vowel: he accepts or receives, what is accepted, as in {khasum asaan}, the pay he received; the same as <asan.2>

terms: as much as possible/as far as/just enough
definition: <khop.2>, enough, said twice and written as one word after a verb: to the full extent of it; {ei zawh khopkhop} is as much as we are able, and {hihtheih khopkhop} as far as one can do
<dot>, ask, and <leh.3>, when, written as one word after a quoted question: when he asked, on being asked
<ih>, our, with <nu>, mother, written as one word, mostly paired with <ihpa>: our mother and father, our parents
a trained health worker who mixes and gives out medicines and treats the sick, often in places where there is no doctor
<kei>, not, and <lehang>, if we, written as one word after a verb: if we do not
use something wrongly, carelessly or too freely, as money, words or the name of God

terms: be fed by hand/feed each other
definition: have a piece of food put into the mouth by another, or put pieces of meat into each other's mouths as a sign of affection at a feast
the killing of a mithun at a feast, a main event of a feast of merit
a people of Assam in the north-east of India
said of the heat of the sun with <in> before <sa>, hot: {ni satpi in sa} is the sun is scorching hot
plural of <guipi>: the main lines or basic principles of a belief, a history or a custom
word of song language for a promise or vow, especially between lovers or friends
<bulphuh> and <a> written as one word after a noun: taking it as the basis, based on it
the one who owns or has a thing, from <nei> with the ending {-tu}, the doer
that one has earned by work, mostly after <tha>, strength: {tha lawhsa} is what one has earned by one's own labour
that has already been called or said aloud, of words
<ni> and <masa> written as one word: the first day, as of the week or of a meeting
go round a place together with someone as the guide, on foot or by vehicle
<a> and <khenkhen> written as one word: divided up, each one apart, the separate ones
<na>, the marker of an earlier action, and <zo> written as one word: won, or finished and completed
use money, food, water or the like carefully and in small amounts
an airline company of Taiwan
<nua>, behind, with <lam>, side: the side left behind, said of the family a married woman comes from, set against the family she has married into
the side of the woman, as the family of the bride in marriage custom or the female line of kin
<khaih>, strain, with <sa>, already done: strained, of rice beer drawn off clear, as {zu khaihsa}
<a> and <lemloh> written as one word: that it is not convenient or does not work out
a degree of a college or university, named after the cap worn at graduation, <lukhu>
quick to weep, crying easily
a kind of traditional Zomi cloth or blanket, also {tanghciing puan} and {tanghciing puanpi}, given as a gift of honour
the dress or woven cloth that belongs to a people
go on growing or advancing, of a person, a life or understanding
the part of a river, land or house that lies above or to the north, and on from there
<ka> and <thah> written as one word in songs of boasting: what I have killed
<kawl>, Burmese, and <min>, name, written as one word: a personal name in the Burmese language, as against a Zomi name
<thutuak>, be of one mind, with the noun ending <na>; used with <ki> as {ki thutuakna}, the same as <kithutuakna>: being in agreement with one another
<tap>, take the name of, and <sak> written as one word: give a child or a group the name of someone, by custom the name of a grandparent
<gil>, belly, and <vun>, skin, written as one word: the skin of the belly, said to hurt from much laughing, {gilvun na liangin nui}, and to be stretched tight after a big meal, {gilvun kikang}
<lak>, take, with <ki> and <pih>: get or take something for or together with someone, as a document from an office, a photograph with a person, or the harvest of a neighbour, {an lak}
<ngaih>, loud, and <zaw>, more, written as one word: louder, more resounding, and of a name or wording, sounding better to the ear
sentence ending of lively written style, <hi> with an added <si>, often after <lah>: states with feeling that a thing is surely so or cannot be helped
<nin>, rubbish, and <bawm>, basket, written as one word: a container for rubbish

terms: be unable to reach/fall short of/be no match for
definition: <phak>, reach, with <lah>, be unable to: not be able to come up to someone or something; mostly denied, {i phaklah ding omlo} is there is nothing beyond our reach
<ngai>, listen, and <thei>, able, written as one word: be able to listen; with <ki> as {ki ngaithei}, can be listened to
<lai>, the place or time, and <pan>, from, written as one word: after <tua> or <hih>, from that point on; after a span of years, since; after the name of a language, from its writing
<tek>, each, and the emphatic <mah> written as one word, after a noun or pronoun: each one alike, every one of them
<tel>, understand, and <semsem>, more and more, written as one word
the time when a person is small; {ka neusen lawmpa} is my childhood friend and {neusen aa kipan} is from childhood on
<tungnung>, upper, and <zaw>, more, written as one word: higher up, or higher in rank and worth than another
word of songs and elevated style for a young unmarried woman; {siamsin liapal} is a girl student
<ngilh>, forget, with the prefix <ki>: forget each other, or be forgotten; in songs of parting as {kingilh kei ni}, let us not forget each other
word of songs and love letters for the scent of a beloved person, with <nam>, smell, as in {ngaih gimsi nam}, smell the scent of the beloved
the place where roads, directions or people run into one another, and the dealings of a people with others
the word of the Paite and Zou spelling for a leader, in Tedim writing <makai>

terms: want to tell/wish to say/have a message for
definition: <vaikhak>, instruct or send word, and <nop>, want, written as one word: what one wishes to tell or leave as a message, asked at the close of an interview as {vaikhaknop na nei hia}
<na> and <guan>, put into or bestow, written as one word: you put in, as an address into a form; or with the particle <na> of telling, gave, bestowed
<khang>, increase, and <thei>, able, written as one word
<zawk>, more, and <deuh>, somewhat, written as one word after a describing word or verb: {a tawm zawkdeuh} is a little less

terms: to prevent/to shield from/to ward off
definition: <dal>, prevent or shield, and <ding> written as one word: in order to prevent, or what is to keep something off; {nisa dalding} is to keep off the heat of the sun
<madawk>, foremost, with the noun ending <na>: being out in front of others, the lead a person, group or country has, also the wish to be first
<khat>, one, and <lam>, side or direction, written as one word: one side or direction, and of two the other one
<phal>, permit, and <sak> written as one word: give someone leave to do a thing, grant a request
<ong>, another spelling of the particle <hong>, and <hawh>, visit, written as one word: come to visit, of guests and of readers who come to a website
<a> and <pangkhawm> written as one word, after <ma>: {ma apangkhawm} is {a mapang khawm}, who work for a cause together, see <mapang>
<kal>, kidney, with <na>, be ill: illness of the kidneys
<na> and <pha>, reach, written as one word: you reached an age or a place; or with the particle <na> of telling, came to a number or amount
<muh>, get, and <zah>, amount, written as one word: the amount one gets; {sum muhzah} is income
<pasal>, man, and <pha>, good, written as one word: a man of courage and worth, a hero; in hunting stories, the hunters
<phawk>, remember, and <lai>, still, written as one word
<len>, hold, and <khawm>, together, written as one word: hold on to a thing together, hold two things or two offices at once, or hold things together so that they do not fall apart

terms: be able to lead/manage to lead
definition: <makaih>, lead, and <zo>, be able to, written as one word
word of songs for the haze that draws across the sky at the turn from the rains to the dry season, said with <kai>; compare <meilum>
<dung>, along, and <suk>, down, written as one word after the name of a town, valley or border: all along it, through the whole stretch of it
<sim> and <pah> written as one word: read something at once, without delay

terms: be scattered and lost/be dissipated/be squandered
definition: be scattered about and lost, said of a people among other peoples and of money, often beside <mangthang>, {thelthang sak} is squander or make away with
noun of <khaak>, send or hold out: the sending of money, a message or a missile, or what is sent, {mangpha khaakna} is a farewell
<sum> and <zeek> written as one word: manage or budget money, also used as a noun, the managing of money or a budget
<thu> and <sinsakna> written as one word: the teaching of a subject, a training or workshop given to people
<mengmeng> and <in> written as one word, after a verb: do it quickly, at once
doubled form of <dawk>, come out, placed after a verb: the action comes out or shows itself, openly or again and again, as in {khuadak dawkdawk}, peep out to look
the print of the fingers pressed on paper or a machine as proof of who one is, {khutmek ding} is to have the fingerprints taken
<i> and <tu> written as one word: our grandchild, our grandchildren, often paired with <ita>, our children
noun of <etsat>: the feeling of loathing or despising someone, often named beside <muhdahna>
<na> and <kha> written as one word: your soul, your spirit
<na> and <din> written as one word: you stand, {nadin mun} is the place where you stand, your position
word of songs and elevated speech for a young unmarried man, paired with <lia>, maiden
<akuul> and <leh> written as one word: if it is necessary, and in {akuulleh akuulloh}, whether it is necessary or not
<lel>, <ding> and <hi> written as one word at the end of a sentence: will merely, will just do so
<a>, <seem> and <ding> written as one word: who will serve in an office, will do the work of
<hi> and <sang> written as one word, before a describing word with <zaw>: than this, more than it is now
<thu> and <hong> written as one word: <thu>, word or news, followed by the particle <hong> that belongs to the next verb, as in {thuhong zasak}, bring word to me
a country of south-eastern Europe
the minerals in food that the body needs, named beside <vitamin>
<kha>, spirit, with <nin>, unclean: an evil spirit, set against {Khasiangtho}, the Holy Spirit
the way people keep company and deal with one another, <kikholh> with <zia>, manner
a city in the east of Ukraine
a river of the Chin Hills, the upper course of the Kaladan, also met as a personal name
<tal>, male, with {-pi}, great, written after the name of an animal: a full-grown male, as in {bawng talpi}, a bull, and {sazuk talpi}, a stag
<zeek> and <khia> written as one word: give out money or goods in a managed way for a purpose
<uh> and <hiam> written as one word at the end of a question whose subject is plural, as in {na hi uhiam}, are you
<vaihawm> and <khia> written as one word: plan a matter out and bring it about
<ngaihsut> and <teh> written as one word: when I, we or one think about it
caring for the good of others and giving help or work without seeking gain, from <phatuam>, benefit, and <ngai>, {phatuamngai pawl} is a charitable or volunteer group
<pil>, learned, with <ciim>, sensible: having knowledge and good sense, {pilciim na} is such knowledge, {mi pilciim} an intelligent person
careful over every small thing in work or in the use of goods, and of a report, detailed
<na> and <dawng> written as one word: with the particle <na.3> of an action told of, answered, replied, and with the pronoun <na.1>, you answer
noun of <kitelcian>: being sure or clearly informed of something, {gupkhiatna ngah kitelcianna} is assurance of salvation
<Tonzang> and <ah> written as one word: in, at or to the town of Tonzang
<la> and <sinna> written as one word: the practising of songs, a singing rehearsal
first part of the name Buenos Aires, the capital of Argentina
second part of the name Buenos Aires, the capital of Argentina
<ak>, chicken, with <mul>, feather: a feather of a fowl
the koala, a tree-living animal found only in Australia
<muk>, lip, with <mul>, hair: the hair on the upper lip, named together with <khamul>, beard
a people of southern China; one article connects the origin of the Zomi with them

terms: be able to improve/manage to repair
definition: <puah> and <zo> written as one word: be able to repair, tend or put right
put the blame for something on a person or thing, speak of them as guilty
the English grammar term, used in writing about the grammar and spelling of Zolai
<ngak> and <siam> written as one word: be good at waiting, wait patiently
<theih> and <ta> written as one word after a verb: the thing can now be done, has become possible; alone, know it now
<nop> and <zah> written as one word after a verb: the amount that one wishes to do or give
<om> and <bek> written as one word: there is only that, or be simply so
the Mass, the main service of worship of the Catholic church; the Latin name missa
<i> and <pian> written as one word: we are born, our being born

terms: things not known/what one does not know
definition: <theihloh> with the plural <te>: the things that one does not know
the counting of all the people of a country
<ka> and <sanggam> written as one word: my brother or my sister

terms: on the business of/for the cause of/in the matter of
definition: <vai> and <in> written as one word after a noun: on the business of, for the cause of or as a matter of what is named
of a people or group: having many members, the opposite of <citawm>; in other sentences the same letters are {ci tam}, would say, at the end of a question
<vingveng> with the ending {-a}, after a verb of going, running or carrying: setting straight off, and then what follows is done
<om> and <ten> written as one word: those who are in a place or state, as the doers of the action

terms: all those that are more/those mostly
definition: <deuh> and <teng> written as one word after a describing word or a name: all the ones that are more so, or the group that is mostly of the kind named
<hai> and <zaw> written as one word: more foolish
the life that a person lives, its course and condition; {lei nunkhua} is life on earth
<galkap> and <mangpipa> written as one word: the man at the head of the armed forces
<i> and <pan> written as one word: we begin; after <ma>, front, we take up the work and strive, as {ma i pan}
<kikheek> with the noun ending {-na}: an exchanging between two sides, as {thautang kikheekna}, an exchange of fire; also a change of place or post
<la>, take, and the particle <ta> written as one word: has now taken, or with <ding> is now to be taken; {kiciamna lata} is has taken the oath

terms: serve as a dish/give to eat with
definition: give someone a food as <meh>, the dish that goes with the meal, or prepare it for them

terms: look around at one another/look about
definition: <ki> and <khuadak> written as one word: look around, at one another or in wonder and uncertainty
<tom> and <gen> written as one word: say in few words; {tomgen leng} is to put it briefly
<kham>, drunk, said twice, after <zu> or <zuu>, strong drink: get drunk again and again; a few sentences have it after <khen>, divide, of splitting again and again
<zun>, tend, said twice and paired with <puahpuah>: go on tending a language, a people or a land and putting it in order
the particle <hong>, spelled without its first letter, and <zin>, travel, written as one word: come here on a visit or journey
<hawl> said twice: go on driving a vehicle, or keep driving a person or an animal away
<i> and <pianna> written as one word: our birth or origin; {ipianna nu le pa} is the parents who gave us birth

terms: eat with/share a meal with/dine with
definition: <an>, food, and <nekpih> written as one word: eat a meal together with someone, take someone to a meal
<pate>, fathers, and the marker <in> of the doer written as one word, seen in {nu le patein}, the parents as the ones who act
<ki> and <tawldam> written as one word: one gets rest or relief from tiredness or strain
<lo>, field, and <hoih>, good, written as one word, mostly in the pair {innhoih lohoih}, a fine house and good fields, said of property and wealth
<meileng>, train, with the plural <te>
<ngen>, ask for, and the linking <a> written as one word: asking for something and then; {khutdawh ngena} is by begging
placed after a verb such as <pau>, speak, or <ci>, say: doing it carelessly or to no purpose, just going on doing it
a supporter of <Zomism>, the movement for the name and unity of the <Zomi>; a coinage on the English pattern used in political essays
<sahang>, tiger or wild beast, with <no>, young: the cub of a tiger
a substance in food that protects the cells of the body from damage
<phawk>, remember, with <pha>, reach: bring something fully to mind, be well aware of it
descriptive word placed after a word such as <neu>, small, <niam>, low, or <tol>, bald, picturing a thing as very small, shrunken or bare
poetic word for <gal>, enemy, used in songs; one article glosses it as {i galte}, our enemies
a means of crossing a river where there is no bridge, on which people are carried and hauled across; a dictionary has {khau kawn} for a hank of rope
<zaang>, plain or flat ground, and <ah>, at or on, written as one word: on the plain, on a flat place such as a flat roof
<na> and <ngai>, listen, written as one word: you listen, in a command {nangai un}, listen; also with the particle <na> of an action going on at that place or time, was listening
having a big belly; from <gil>, belly
<unau>, siblings, with the noun ending {-na}: being brothers, mostly as {ki unauna}, brotherhood among people
<a> and <vaaihawm> written as one word: he plans or arranges, the one who plans, what is planned
<a> and <kantel> written as one word: he or they investigate, the one who inquires into a matter thoroughly
<a> and <kullo> written as one word, placed after a verb: there is no need to do it, that which need not be done
the Tedim name of Rih Dil, a natural lake west of Tedim by the Tiau river on the border of Chin State and Mizoram, called {Lih bual} or {Lih Dil}

terms: I am good at/I know how
definition: <ka>, I, and <siam>, skilled, written as one word: I am good at it, I know it well; {kasiam tawp in} is as best I can
<om>, be, and <toto>, more and more, written as one word: there goes on being more of it, it keeps happening

<lel>, merely, and <lo> written as one word after a verb, before <ding> or in a question: it would simply be so, would it not; in one sentence it may instead be <lel>, be defeated, with <lo>, not give way
the pool at Tedim from whose glittering water the town is said to have its name; also called {Tuidim}
<Saizang> with the plural <te>: the people of Saizang and the group that speaks the Saizang dialect
a village named in the early history of the Tedim area
<vai>, matter, and <lianpi>, great, written as one word: a very weighty affair of a people or community
a kind of pot or jar, named among the pots for rice beer, {zu beeltung}; its size and shape are not settled
in news of war, a bomb dropped from the air, with <khia>, drop
<lunglut>, be interested, and <lo>, not, written as one word
<hong> and <theih>, the form of <thei>, know, written as one word: come to know, or know us; <hong> shows that the action comes toward the speaker
<ciamteh>, note, with <huai>, worthy of: worth noting or remembering

terms: in order to be able/so as to manage
definition: <zawh>, be able, and <nang>, short for <nading>, written as one word after a verb: so that it can be done

terms: want to attend/want to go to
definition: <kah>, attend, and <nuam>, want, written as one word: wish to attend a school; {President kahnuam} is one who wants to run for president
<se> and <hi> written as one word at the end of a statement, giving it emphasis: indeed, really
<hel>, mix, with <zau>, spread wide: mix different things or people together, mix one matter up with another
<ciim>, sensible or clear, with the comparative <zaw>: wiser, of the mind clearer and sharper
<thumuh>, insight, with <siamna>, skill: the ability to see into matters and understand them
<kamtuam>, a strange tongue, with <pau>, speak: speaking in tongues in church, also speech in a language the hearer does not understand
<taimang>, run away, with <pa>, man: the one who ran away; {tapa taimangpa} is the prodigal son of the parable
<a> and <kaal> written as one word: the week, as in {akaal nihna}, the second week, or with {-ah} the time or space in between
according to law, official, also the field of law; a form built on <upadi>, law, in the writing of one author who glosses it official
<ziau>, lightly or at once, and <lo>, not, written as one word after a verb: the action is not done simply, quickly or easily
<sawm>, ten, and <val>, exceed, written as one word: ten or more, some tens
<a> and <kiciam> written as one word: who vowed or promised, what was agreed, as in {akiciam ni}, the day agreed on
<i>, our, and <mai>, the front or the time ahead, written as one word: before us, our future, mostly with <lam>
<phuah>, give a name, and <zia>, way, written as one word: the way names are made up and given, used after <min>, name
<niam>, low, and <lua>, too much, written as one word: too low in place, level or standing
<taam>, stay, and <suak>, right through, written as one word: stay on in a place for good instead of going back
<sang>, school, and <huang>, enclosure, written as one word: the grounds of a school or university
take something without the owner knowing, quietly take out or steal; <la>, take, with <sim>, here secretly
<et>, look at, and <khak>, happen to, written as one word: come to look at or watch something, with or without meaning to
placed after a verb: the action is kept up steadily and without turning aside, as {en tengtang}, look fixedly
<sin>, learn, and <pah>, at once, written as one word: set about learning something straight away

terms: make compete/hold a contest/set against each other
definition: <kidem>, compete, with the causative <sak>, written as one word: have people or things compete for something
<ngah>, get, and <phet>, just, written as one word and followed by <in>: the moment something is received or caught
of a sight, drawing the eye and pleasant to look at; <mit>, eye, with <tai>, run
a clan or people that is small, short of members or not fully grown as a people, set against {namzau}, a widespread one; known from the old saying {namtom hauh leh tuita khan}

found only in {tuita khan}, growth that shoots up fast and does not last because it has no firm base, as in the old saying {namtom hauh leh tuita khan}; what the word names by itself is not clear from the articles

of termites, bite a way open through the ground; in the saying {phulum phul nading leikha in petlet}, the termites bite the way open for the winged termites to swarm out, said of those who prepare the way for others
<zawl>, sweetheart, with <hel>, court: the evening visits of a young man to a girl he seeks to win, the old custom of courting
<kimang>, be of use, and <thei>, able, written as one word: that can be used, that can be said of something, or that keeps and lasts
<ka>, my, and <cihnopna>, meaning, written as one word: what I mean to say
a blow on the cheek with the open hand, also the act of slapping someone; <pang>, here the cheek, with <bet>, slap
<tup>, aim, <leh>, and, <ngiim>, intend, written as one word: the aims and intentions of a person or an organisation
<mai>, just or simply, and <lo>, not, written as one word after a verb and before <dia> or {ding hiam}: a guess that expects agreement, will it not just be so
<mee>, vote, with the counting word <tang>, written as one word: a single vote, the votes cast for someone
<a> and <moi>, young, written as one word: young, the young one; {amoi pen} is the youngest and {amoi aham} young and old

terms: want too much/be too eager/long for
definition: <ut>, want, and <lua>, too much or very, written as one word: want something very much or too much
<kisin>, practise, and <khol>, beforehand, written as one word: practise or train ahead of the time of need
<lungkim>, be pleased, with the comparative <zaw>, written as one word: be more pleased or more satisfied
<sial>, the mithun, with <lu>, head: the head or skull of a mithun killed at a feast, kept in the house as a sign of the feasts given under the old religion
word of song language for <lutang>, the head; in prose once also the principal of a sum of money
at a later and unhurried time, by and by; once also gently, of a light blow; compare <damdam>, slowly
<midang> and the marker <in> written as one word: another person or other people as the one who acts

terms: go one's own way/stand apart/be divided
definition: keep apart from the others and act on one's own instead of working together, said of people and leaders who split a group; {mi-tangpeek} is used as a reproach for such a person
<thubaih>, an easy matter, and <lo>, not, written as one word: it is no easy matter, hard to do
<sa>, game, and <kap>, shoot, written as one word: shoot wild animals, hunt with a gun; also the one who shoots the animal
town and sub-division in the <Champhai> district of <Mizoram>, India
poetic word for a song that is sung, used in songs and song titles, mostly with <awi>, sing, as {zaideih awi}
of <Nigeria>, a person of Nigeria; the English word, used before words such as <gammi>, citizen
after a verb, of something white or bright that stands out clearly to the eye: {kang viuviau} is gleaming white
<zangsiam>, use well, with the plural <te>: those who make good use of a thing, of time or of a skill
<thuhilh>, teach, and <khial>, wrongly, written as one word: teach what is false; before {syate}, teachers, it describes false teachers
make something narrow or small in its reach, said of the mind, of a view and of the scope of a work; set against <liansak>, make large
<angsung>, one's own good, and <thei>, know, written as one word: knowing only one's own interest, selfish; also a selfish person
a stream on the road to <Tuizang> village in the Tedim area, crossed by a bridge; written small, {tuikai} is also said of a water tap
one single piece of something, as one strand of hair; with <zong> and a negative it means not even one, nothing at all

<zom>, continue or join, with the plural <te>: those who come next or carry on, and those joined to one another, as {laigui zomte}, kin of one navel cord; with a capital some writers use it for <Zomite>
literary word for people who are not one's own, other peoples; {siingdang eng lo} is envying no others
<i>, our, and <sepna>, work, written as one word: the work that we do
<ann>, food, and <lim>, tasty, written as one word: food that tastes good, a fine meal
show fondness to one another by touch, play and teasing, said of lovers and spouses and also of friends who are at ease with each other
one of the traditional kinds of Zo song with its own tune, named in lists beside <latung> and <zawlla>
<tun>, arrive, and <ciil>, first, written as one word: the time when one first arrives; {ka tunciil} is when I first arrived
<tualthat>, murder, with <pa> marking a man: the man who has killed someone
<Khazih>, Christ, and <mite>, people, written as one word: the people of Christ, Christians
poetic word for <gamsa>, wild animals that are hunted, used in songs
<kiteh>, be measured, and <lo>, not, written as one word: with <tawh>, is not measured or judged by something
in {inn lusi}, house by house, every household of a village; with a capital, Lusi is also a spelling of <Lusei>, the Lushai
the stretch of wild land and its cover where game is driven in a communal hunt; {sataang hawl} is drive the game from it and {sataang hal} is burn it
<um>, gourd, dried and cut as a ladle or bowl for scooping and serving soup and water
<don> said twice, mostly as {gal dondon}: keep looking out from afar for someone who is to come, wait for with longing
<thatang>, bodily strength, with the plural <te>: the strength and energy people have to give
a country in the south-east of <Africa>
stop what one is doing or stop on the way in order to rest; {khawlnga lo} is without a break
<manlang>, quick, with <sak>, make: make something go or happen faster
the hornbill, <phualva>, named as the bird of the Zo country; it mates for life and is the emblem of the Zomi, standing for love and faithfulness

terms: will not come/will not go/will not flow
definition: <pai>, go or come, and <loding>, will not, written as one word; {tui pailoding} is the water will not run
town in <Selangor>, <Malaysia>, known for its immigration detention camp, {Semunyih Camp}, where refugees were held
<vak>, go about, and the negative <loh> written as one word: not going out or about
<i>, our, and <maban> written as one word: what lies ahead of us, the rest of our course
form of <kivua>, <vuak> with the prefix <ki>: hit one another or be hit; also used as a noun, a beating
<thupibawl> with the prefix <ki>: be treated as important, or treat one another as important
<nungtolh> with the noun suffix {-na}: a going backward, the decline of a country or a falling back in faith
placed after a verb: holding to what one has said or wants and not giving way
descriptive word placed after a verb of speaking or doing: the action goes on easily and without pause, as in {phun siausiau}, keep grumbling
<an>, food, and <bang>, like, written as one word; in songs and poetic style {anbang it} is to love as one loves food, dearly
the particle <na> and <tai>, run, written as one word: ran or was running, said of someone other than the hearer
word of songs and elevated style, used as {holung kum} and before <kikum>: {holung kum} is talk a matter over, take counsel together

terms: worth keeping/to be kept/to be guarded
definition: <kep>, keep, with <huai>, worthy of: that should be kept and looked after
<khangto> with the noun suffix {-na}: the progress or development of a country or people
<ka>, I, and <kan>, ask or look into, written as one word
word of songs and poetic style for <gamla>, far; {gam vangla} is a distant land

terms: manage in full/be fully able/be fully content
definition: <kim>, all or fully, with <zo>, be able, written as one word: manage to do something in full or for everyone; {lung a kimzo} is the heart is fully content
<et>, look at, with <khialh>, wrongly, and the noun suffix {-na}: seeing a person or matter wrongly, and the ill feeling between people that comes of it; as {ki-etkhialhna} it is mutual
the particle <hong> and <en>, look, written as one word: look toward the speaker, or come and look
<i>, our, and <lawmte>, friends, written as one word; also said of the peoples around one's own, our peers
<kipawlna> with <pi>, great: a large or chief organisation, as the United Nations
a Zomi clan of the Tedim area, found among others at Khuasak, whose name is also borne as a surname
the fastener with two rows of teeth that opens and closes clothes and bags; {sik zit} is a metal zip
written where <zin>, travel, is expected, after <khual> or the name of a country: go on a journey

terms: be seen at once/be noticed right away
definition: <kimu>, be seen, with <pah>, at once, written as one word
<gam>, land, with <kip>, firm: a land or territory that a people or a village holds securely as its own
<khang>, generation, and <tampi>, many, written as one word
<zato> and <lam> written as one word: to the hospital, as in {zatolam kipuak}, be taken to hospital, or the field of medicine
a worker of the lowest rank in a government office or other body, who keeps watch and runs errands
<zek> with the emphatic <mah> written as one word, after a describing word or a word of time: to a fair degree; {nungkum zekmah in} is only last year or so
<mangngilh>, forget, with the causative <sak>: cause someone to forget
village in Mizoram, India, near the border with Chin State, where Zomi live
<phut>, set up, with the plural <te> written as one word: those who founded a church or an organisation
<pau>, language, and the marker <in> written as one word: in or by means of a language
<lungnuam>, be glad, and <pen>, most, written as one word
what a person or a meeting decides; {thupukna bawl} is make a decision or pass a resolution
<a> and <khangcing> written as one word: one that is mature or fully developed, or it grows to maturity
descriptive word placed after a verb of moving or sounding: the action goes on steadily or in a body, as people streaming toward a place; probably the word <nainai>
<ne>, eat, and <khin>, already, written as one word: have already eaten, eat something up
<zong>, also, and <tawh>, with, written as one word: with this one as well, even with
<siam>, skilled, with <tuam>, apart: skilled beyond others, and as a noun a special skill or a person who has one
<gamuk>, government, and <pawl>, group, written as one word: the body of those who govern a country or a state
<ni>, day, and <ta> written as one word after a date or the name of a day: that day, the day of

terms: hundred baskets of millet/great millet harvest
definition: a harvest of a hundred baskets of <mim>, millet, for which a man holds a feast of honour, named together with <taangza>
<a> and <lunggulhna> written as one word: his, her or their longing, what they wish for
<thu>, news, with <kizaksak>, inform one another, and the noun ending {-na}: the making known of news, an announcement, also a paper or record that carries it
<lamsang>, raise up, and <in> written as one word: lifting up, raising to a higher standing
<lam>, side or way, and <sangin>, than, written as one word: more than in the matter of, rather than in the way of
<ngah>, get, and <huai> written as one word: such that one gets something from it, {tha ngahhuai} is strengthening, {thupha ngahhuai} is a source of blessing
Sadar Hills, a hill area of Manipur in India
<sik>, step on, and <khak>, happen to, written as one word: happen to step on something, the form of <sikkha> used before <ding>
<kiim>, around, and <vial>, encircle, written as one word: go all the way round a place, or running all round it
the front of the leg between the knee and the ankle, {ngaltaak guh} is the shin bone; compare <ngaltak>
used in the pair {lamdung lamvai}, along the roads and byways, wherever one happens to be going
<thu>, news, and <zaksak>, make known, written as one word: tell people a piece of news, announce
<koi>, where, and <lak> written as one word, mostly with <ah>: where on earth, in a question or exclamation that expects the answer nowhere
<ba>, owe, with the prefix {ki-}: be in debt to someone, and of a sum, be still owed; {lei kiba} is owe a debt
used in the pair {nisa khasa}, the heat of sun and moon: the burning heat a person is exposed to out of doors
<neih>, have, and <kim>, every, written as one word: every one of them has it, have in every place
<ih>, we, and <dah>, grieve, written as one word: we are sad, we mourn
a state in the west of India
<kisak>, get ready, and <kholhna>, doing in advance, written as one word: getting ready beforehand
<meh>, the dish eaten with rice, with <kuang>, bowl: the bowl that curry or stew is served in, also a bowlful of it
know a person or thing by its marks, take note of it as such; one book of words explains <sansaat>, estimate, with it
come to have the mind of an owner of the house, be as much at ease as in one's own home; of a people or a faith, become settled in a place
noun of {kithuzaaktuah}, let one another hear news, compare <kithuzak>: communication among people by paper, radio or internet, and the information passed on
<ding> and <sang>, than, written as one word after a verb: rather than doing it, instead of doing it
<pi>, <leh> and <pu> written as one word: grandmother and grandfather, and so the forefathers
<lei>, buy, and <nuamte>, those who want, written as one word: the people who wish to buy something
<muh>, see, and <thak>, new, written as one word: something newly seen or found out
Saint Helena, an island in the South Atlantic Ocean
a state in the east of India, now named Odisha; in lists also its people
<phuh> and <ding> written as one word: to found or set up a church, an organisation or a country, what is to be founded
placed after a verb of what a group does: pictures many people doing it together and without stopping, as {nek khawm zaihzaih}, eating together
<zaih>, photograph, said twice, after <man> or <maan>, picture: take one photograph after another
<makaihsiam>, lead well, with the noun ending {-na}: the ability to lead people well
<hong>, here marking us as the object, and <uk>, rule, written as one word: rule over us, the one who rules us
<tan>, school class, with <nih>, two, written as one word: the second class of primary school, and the school reader of that class, above <tankhat>

terms: neighbour below/lower side of the house
definition: the house or people on the lower side of one's own, and the ground below the house; {innsak innkhang} together are the neighbours on every side
<ka> and <kap>, weep, written as one word: I weep, I cried
<ka> and <kap>, shoot, written as one word: I shoot, and with <uh> we shoot, in reports of fighting
descriptive word after a verb, mostly as {niang nuang}: in a slack, drooping or listless way
<pawl>, group, and <tuamtuam>, various, written as one word: the various groups, parties or denominations
<kizaksak>, inform one another, with the noun ending {-na}: the making known of news, an announcement, mostly as {thu kizaksakna}
<nau>, younger sibling, with <sung>, written as one word and used after {usung} or {u sung}: {usung nausung} is among elder and younger siblings, the circle of brothers, sisters and near kin
placed after a verb of sitting, staying or eating, often after <khawm>: of several people gathered close together in one place; near in use to <liailiai>, of which it may be a spelling
<a> and <sumh>, suffer loss, written as one word: the one who loses, what is lost
the English grammar term used in Zolai writing about language: a word of doing or being
<nungsang> with <in> written as one word, placed at the end of a clause, often after <khit>, or after a year: after, now that
<thuzuih>, following a teaching, with the noun ending {-na}: obedience, and the practice of a faith as distinct from its belief, <upna>
<naupang>, child, and <teng>, all, written as one word: all the children, the whole group of children or pupils
<ci>, say, and <kawm>, while, written as one word and mostly followed by <in>: while saying this, saying so and at the same time doing something else
<thuhilh>, preach, with {sya}, teacher, and the plural <te>, written as one word: those who preach and teach in the churches

terms: be planned for/be arranged for/be provided
definition: passive of <gelsak>, plan for someone, with the prefix {ki-}: be planned or arranged for someone, often after <hong> or <ong>, for us or for you
<kha>, moon, and <vak>, light, written as one word: the light of the moon, a night when the moon shines
<khuang>, crow, said twice: of roosters, crow repeatedly, as at daybreak; in songs a sign that it is time to wake
descriptive word after a verb or describing word such as <zam> or <gawng>: of a body, a neck, limbs or a tree that looks long, thin and stretched out
<a> and <thuap>, layer or patch, written as one word: what is laid on top of another; said twice, {athuap athuap}, layer upon layer, wave after wave
a village of Myanmar, given in news reports as the home village of Zomi people
of wood, smooth to the touch, rubbed or planed smooth, as {nawt ngil}, rub smooth
Lenggeng in Malaysia, site of an immigration detention camp, {Lengeng Camp}, named in reports about Zomi refugees
the noun ending {-na} and <ah> written as one word apart from the verb: in or at the doing of it, as {laivuan naah}, in the examinations; usually written {-na ah} or {-nah}
go right through something, as rays through cloth or the body; also see through a thing, after <muh>, and go beyond or past someone
the emphatic <vet> said twice with <lo>, not, written as one word: placed after a verb, not in the least, and after <ngei>, never once; stronger than <vetlo>
<kim>, every, and <phial>, almost, written as one word: placed after a noun or verb, nearly all of them, almost everywhere or in full
<deih>, want, and the particle <ta> of a change that has come, written as one word: now want, have come to want; {deih in deihta kei leh} is whether one wants it or not
<na>, your, and <zun>, urine, written as one word: in the old words for driving out a spirit, {nazun namsia}, your urine stinks
the particle <na> of an earlier action and <zun>, tend, written as one word: tended and built up in former times, paired with <puah>
<hibang>, like this, with the plural <te>, written as one word: things or people of this kind
<kisia>, be ruined, with the plural <te>, written as one word: the houses, bridges or towns that have been damaged; after <tawh>, those who have fallen out with someone
a number of things or beings gathered into one mass, as a heap of stones, a cluster of illnesses or a host of soldiers
<kik>, again, and <teh>, when, written as one word after a verb: when it is done again, as {ngaihsut kikteh}, when one thinks it over again
<kham>, be satisfied, and <tak> written as one word: eating or drinking as much as one wants
<nei>, have, and <khollo>, not much, written as one word: have little or none of something, or go without having arranged it

<khat>, one, and <lo>, not, written as one word after a noun: not of one and the same place or direction, so apart or different; {heina khatlo} is a phrase of songs for people who have gone separate ways
<angtang>, be proud, with <sak>, cause: make someone proud of what he or she is; {ki-angtangsak} is feel proud of oneself
<a> and <kilahna> written as one word: where someone was examined, of a clinic or hospital; also that by which something is shown

terms: compete with one another/vie/try to outdo
definition: <kidem>, compete, with <bawl>: keep trying to outdo one another, as in buying things or in getting ahead on the road
<kitawp>, resign, with the noun suffix {-na}: the act of leaving a post or office
<kitawp>, kiss one another, with the noun suffix {-na}: kissing
English exam with the noun suffix {-na}: an examination at school or university, also the testing of blood
<silh>, wear, and <loh>, not, written as one word, mostly before <ding>: not putting on a garment
<giak>, spend the night, and <suak>, on, written as one word: stay on and sleep at the place one has come to
become full and soft: of soaked grain, swell; of a person or a thing, fill out and grow; of cold hands or tired muscles, loosen and soften
word of songs and poetic speech, {pal}, fence, with <bang>, like: used with <nan>, withstand, of holding off an enemy or a longing as a fence does
become wakeful and lively again after sleep, faintness or illness; {halh sak} is refresh; the same spelling is the second part of <singhalh>, reserved forest, also written {sing halh}
a pot with a spout in which water for tea is boiled or tea is served
the place where a person, a people or an animal lives and moves about, from <tual>, open ground, and <lenna>
<khanglui>, people of former generations, and <ten.2>, the plural with the marker of the doer, written as one word: the forebears as the ones who said or did something
<zawl>, sweetheart or friend, <lui>, old, and the plural <te> written as one word: those one used to court, or friends of earlier days
<hunnuam>, a pleasant time, with the plural <te>: happy times, mostly those remembered
placed after a verb, often with <laitak>: the action is still going on
<a> written as one word with <toii>, short or narrow, the opposite of <zaii>, wide: of time, short; of a mind or a view, narrow
<seem>, here a spelling of <sem>, more, and <leh>, if, written as one word after a verb or describing word: the more something is so, with the result in the clause that follows
<seem>, work or serve, and <leh>, if, written as one word: if or when someone does a work or serves in an office
the papers a person holds, such as identity and registration documents, from <lai>, writing, and <tawi>, hold; a different {laitawi} occurs in an old song with <ton>
<thunget>, pray, and <khopna>, doing together, written as one word: a time when people pray together
<hunzat>, spending time, and <khopna>, doing together, written as one word: a time spent together, also a gathering held with a visitor or for someone who has died
<hawi>, leave alone, with <ki>: be left in place and not removed, as plants left to grow, hair left uncut, a bees' nest kept for later or a place still open for someone
<bah>, be exhausted, with <sak>, cause: take away the strength of a person or hold back a thing such as progress
the highest and coldest zone of the hills, where crops ripen late
<khuat>, dig up, with <ki>: be dug out of or into the ground, as potatoes or a tunnel; with <khia>, of knowledge, be dug out
<khuat>, scratch, with <ki>: scratch one's own body; {eima angsung ciat kikhuat} is each scratching his own bosom, each looking after himself alone
<a> and <kiciamna> written as one word: the promise or agreement that was made, their vow
expressive word placed after a describing word: of ground or a thing, soft and damp; of clothes or a dirty person, limp and shabby
<peem>, live as an incomer, with <khia>, out: leave the home place or country to settle elsewhere
